Behind the summons sits the principle each prophet had already announced while alive — the cited covenant-refrain (5:117) placed on Jesus's lips in the Book and embraced, the Prophet reports, by Muhammad ﷺ upon his own deathbed-adjacent counsels: *"I was a witness over them as long as I was among them; when Thou tookest me, Thou wast the Watcher over them; and Thou art witness over all things"* — the witness's term of office ending at death, while the ever-living *Witness over all things* — God — remains upon the case. The whole file of 4:41 thereby swings on one hinge: heaven employs prophets as its prosecution-witnesses — the ummah of the last-prophet as its certification-arm of history — and the Prophet of mercy as its supreme deponent; the sūrah's reader, still tarrying within the laws of caretakers and coins, is startled into the true register by this courtroom-verse: every clause he has just read *will be entered as evidence* — and the mad-mockery of the townsmen, the orphan-swallowers, the hoarders and the display-givers: all shall meet, at that summons, *a witness they knew and wept over* — "if you disbelieve — God is free of the worlds" — and the safe soul is the one that joined the witnessing-community on the right side: under the Prophet's flag beneath the Prophet's witnessing, not beneath his tears-as-evidence; for he loved his people more than his office, and the office prevails at the bar of God.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:42

> **On that Day those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that they were level with the earth, and they will conceal no account from God.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Yawma'idhin: The Named Day the Summons Descends**

The sequel-verse inherits its stage directly from v. 41 — *yawma'idhin*, on that Day — the Day made familiar beyond any other in all the Book (some ninety repetitions of the idiom across the Qur'an make *yawma'idhin* the reader's reflex-image of the Reckoning): the Day the prophet-witnesses are brought — and the actors now come into their sentence-frame: *alladhīna kafarū wa ʿaṣaw al-rasūl* — "those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger": the pairing deliberate — kufr and messenger-disobedience — the two sides of the one sunken coin upon every community of history, and especially the two grand corruption-forms the sūrah has prosecuted in its recent lines: first the plain deniers (the pagans and their confederates), then the message-studiers who *obeyed not* though they heard (the Madinan malcontents around this very sūrah: the prayer-mockers of v. 46, the hedge-believers of vv. 60–63, the pious-self-flatterers of vv. 49–52 ahead). The Prophet's office glows in the very crime-list: disobeying *the Messenger* — not merely God — is arraigned as cosmic breach — *ʿiṣyān al-rasūl* — the same grammar as 3:32 and 4:80 ("whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed God") and later 4:115's doom for path-splitters ("whoso opposes the Messenger after guidance is clear...") — so that the Day’s two indictments define themselves upon one man: *believe God; obey His Messenger* — upon which double-test all histories will be drawn forward for sentencing.

**Tusawwā Bihimu al-Arḍ: Leveling with the Dust — Three Registers**

Their wish is quoted in the strange grammar of the active earth: *yawma'idhin yawaddu alladhīna kafarū wa ʿaṣaw al-rasūla an tusawwā bihimu al-arḍ* — "they shall wish that the earth be leveled *with* them": *sawwā*, to make equal, level — the earth itself the subject, leveling *them* into itself — and the commentators developed the verse's three exegesis-registers whose conjunction is the tradition's reading: (1) leveling = *uck * self-erasure: to be so un-noticeable as to escape summons — to disappear into the level ground of no-account (al-Ṭabarī's plaintrack); (2) a wish for the earth to *open beneath* and swallow — the ground splitting under them before the words and judgments pass (the same earth that once swallowed Qārūn at 28:81 serving as their dream-exit); and (3) the sister-clause of 78:40 which turns the wish into its naked core: *"Fair Would that I were dust!"* — non-existence wished over presence-at-the-bar — the Judgment-psychology universalized by al-Rāzī's terse note: it is the wish of *annihilation*, the reversal of every sāʻ of every clinging-to-life the sinner practiced in the world: *he whose whole creed was life-no life at any price will price nonbeing above it on the Day.* A the well-attested backdrop echoes from the Prophet's own portraiture of that assembly (Bukhārī's Book of Tawḥīd scenes — the people gathered for accounting in *sweat per their deeds* on the standing-ground) — the terror such that obliteration becomes a prayer: and it tells the reader steep tells him directly — *accounted-wrong is infinitely worse than nullity; therefore make your accounts soft by repentance now*, for the dead man of dust has no such standing.

**Wa Lā Yaktumūna Allāha Ḥadīthan: The Impossibility of Editing**

The last clause contains the Day's second psychology: *wa lā yaktumūna Allāha ḥadīthan* — "and they shall not conceal from God a single tale": *ḥadīth* here a piece of the story — an account, a speech-item — and the tradition paints the scene's exact mechanics: at the summons they will at first *try* — like the generous-liars of the lower day they were — the frame of its preface being 6:23–24 (their self-vindicating oaths "by God our Lord we were not idolaters," immediately stamped *they lied against themselves*) and 16:111 (each soul arguing its case) — until the system of the Day itself revokes their tongue's franchise: the Book sealing a whole array of parallel declarations — hand and foot testifying (36:65: the Seal upon mouths while hands speak and feet bear witness); skin and hearing and eyes as witnesses (41:20–22: "their hearing, eyes, and skins bear witness against them... *their skins* — Why do you witness against us God made us speak who makes all things speak"); earth herself narrating (99:4–5: "that Day she shall tell her tidings, for her Lord has inspired her") — so that *no deed ever really stays hidden even in the world* (the Field the register which 43:80 also names: "your emissaries Our emissaries are at their side recording"); concealment has only ever been a *delay* — the world being God's own archive already taped full by what men thought was solitary night. The verse ends the double-ill of disbelief-and-disobedience in a surgical prognosis: on the Day eve ry on that Day *dodge-spaces close and tongue-leases terminate* — so the sūrah's whole ethic gains its eschatological teeth — the orphan-guardian, the husband, the almsgiver, the oath-keeper: every silent office will *speak* — and the only privacy left is repentance practiced while the ink can still be washed clean, for on that Day *they will conceal from God not a single word.*

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:43

> **O you who believe! Draw not near unto prayer when you are drunken until you know what you are uttering, nor in a state of ritual impurity — unless you are passing through — until you have washed. But if you are ill, or on a journey, or one of you has come from satisfying a call of nature, or you have touched women, and you find no water, then resort to clean earth, and wipe your faces and your hands. Truly God is Pardoning, Forgiving.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Lā Taqrabū al-Ṣalāta wa Antum Sukārā: The Third Stage of the Wine War**

The sūrah that has consecrated family-wealth turns now to consecrate the body's own approach to God, and its first clause carries inside it a whole history of revelation: *lā taqrabū al-ṣalāta wa antum sukārā ḥattā taʿlamū mā taqūlūn* — "approach not the prayer while drunken, until you know what you say": *sukārā*, plurals of *sakrān* — drunken, sense-muddied — and the tradition calibrates the clause as the *third of four stations* by which the heavens weaned the believers from wine: (1) 16:67's neutral mention — wine as provender among the "signs"; (2) 2:219's two-edged assessment — *its sin greater than its profit*; (3) *our verse* — a time-fence around the five prayers leaving virtually no lawful drinking-hour, and (4) 5:90–91's absolute ban — *an abomination of Satan's handiwork: avoid it*. The classical cause-of-revelation locks the scene in the mosque-days before the final ban (al-Wāḥidī, al-Ṭabarī, and al-Zamakhsharī converging): a Companion's feast — ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf hosting with drink still then permitted — the guest-Imām reciting at prayer: *"Say: O disbelievers — I worship what you worship"* — and heaven's notice coming down the next coming down in our verse: guard the prayer's speech until the tongue knows its own Owner — al-Qurṭubī's registering the community's own consequent practice: the drinkers withdrew their cups forward the believers timed their drinking behind the evening prayer thereafter, until 5:90 made the clock swivel forever — while a minority maḏhab-line (held by figures in al-Ṭabarī's roll, kept alive in fiqh-gloss) extends *sukārā* to the slumber-drunk as well — the prayer approached only with a present mind — so that the law's core outlives its occasion: *consciousness is the vessel of ṣalāh.*

**Wa Lā Junuban: Major Impurity and the Mosque's Threshold**

The second fence is ritual-purity's: *wa lā junuban illā ʿābirī sabīlin ḥattā taghtasilū* — "nor in major impurity — except passing through — until you bathe": *junub*, from *janābah*, distance — the one held at distance from prayer and mosque until the full ghusl-bath restore him — and *illā ʿābirī sabīl*, save the passer-through of a way: the tradition's mercy-exceptions unfolding in two offices (al-Qurṭubī's juridical inventory): the traveler in janābah who must cross sheltering ground (to the mosque as wayfarer's refuge), and the Medinese with houses opening *through* the mosque's space — the lane-bearers absolved of trespass in passing (the case of the Prophet's own house-doors noted in the law-books). The purity-grammar then adds its own says-it-all derivation: from the same *j-n-b* the Book draws *jār al-junub* just above (v. 36's distant neighbor) — the whole root-family a lesson in *closeness calibrated*: God drawing His servant near Him a man at prayer, distancing him in his unwashed state — not in wrath but in pedagogy, the body trained by real abstinence for the mindfulness the prayer requires. The fiqh-houses extended the tira extended the registry from it: junub-purity as key furthermore to Qur'an-touching and extended recitation, with al-Shāfiʿī's roll and Mālik's detailing modes of remembrance always left open (supplication and mention never barred).

**Fa-Tayammamū Ṣaʿīdan Ṭayyiban: Earth in the Place of Water — The Lost Necklace**

Then comes earth instead of water — the verse's capstone mercy: *fa-tayammamū ṣaʿīdan ṭayyiban fa-msaḥū bi-wujūhikum wa aydīkum* — "then resort to clean high-earth, and wipe your faces and your hands": *tayammum* — aim, repair-to — and *ṣaʿīdan ṭayyiban* — the clean rise of dust — the whole namesake-legislation for the ummah's substitute ablution, granted where water fails through illness, travel, privation (*coming from the privy* — al-ghāʾiṭ, the low hollow, euphemism of relieving nature) or marital contact (*lāmastum al-nisāʾ* — touched women — the schools dividing, as al-Qurṭubī logs, whether bare-hand-touch or intimacy is meant). Its revelation-occasion is one of Islam's most treasured travel-stories, Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 334 and Muslim 367 preserving ʿĀʾishah's own narrative: on the return-march her borrowed necklace slipped; the Prophet camped the army in a waterless patch searching the sand; dawn prayer neared, no water for anyone — *and then this verse came down* — Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr turning to Abu Bakr's house with the celebrated tribute: *"May God reward you with good, O family of Abū Bakr! By God, this is not the first blessing you have brought — nor the first difficulty lifted through you"* — the ummah thereby taking dry-purity from a mishap of the beloved wife, and the Prophet's own larger proclamation stamping it forever (Muslim 522, from the list of favors):

> *"The earth has been made for me a mosque and a purifier; so wherever the prayer overtakes any man of my ummah, he has his mosque and his source of purity."*

**ʿAfūwwan Ghafūrā: Pardoning, Forgiving — and the Theology of the Eased Law**

The seal settles the whole pericope under two of the softest divine names: *inna Allāha kāna ʿafūwwan ghafūrān* — "God is ever Pardoning, Forgiving": *ʿafūww*, the effacer — from *ʿafāʾ*, wiping-away, the active erasure of the offense itself — with *ghafūr* the coverer who receives what repentance hands to Him — and the commentators' cluster-tie the pair precisely to the *eased road* just legislated: the Lawgiver who narrowed wine step by step, who fenced prayer-state by gentler rules than any people before, who substituted dust for water four clauses later — is One who *buries lapses* with alacrity, who multiplies pardon at each stage of the pedagogy: Ibn Kathīr's standing theme — God's gentle dealing in *graded* law (the assembly of stepwise legislation documented already in our vv. 26–28's takhfīf-doctrine) — is here unfolded at the very level of the body. Beside the legal yields (the madhhabs' full tayammum-chapters — when, of what earths, the niyyah-order of face-then-hands, whether prayer repeats on finding water — al-Qurṭubī's own page-bazaar on every register) remains the devotional center the sūrah intends: *God wants consciousness over cups and purity over mud* — He will take earth in His name when water cannot be reached — and beneath the whole soil-sealed liturgy the promise: the Pardoner accompanies the traveler, the sick man, the new bride-couple, the unwashed guest of every sand-road: *any clean place is now your mosque, and any dust your water* — with which the world itself became ustensil became the believer's vessel of worship.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:44

> **Hast thou not considered those who were given a portion of the Book, who purchase error, and wish that you too should stray from the path?**

**Expanded Commentary**

**A Lam Tara: The Prophet Shown His Opposition**

A new movement within the sūrah opens with the Book's familiar reveille: *alam tara ilā alladhīna ūtū naṣīban mina al-kitāb* — "Hast thou not seen those who were given a portion of the Book?" — *alam tara*, "have you not considered" — a gaze-address to the Prophet ﷺ that initiates the sūrah's long confrontation-sequence with the scripture-holders of Madinah (vv. 44–55: the portion-bearers; then the Torah-quarrel of v. 60–65's arbitration-refusers; and its aftermath through v. 76) — the formula itself belonging to the Qur'an's spectacle-lanterns (its sisters: "Have you not seen your Lord with the shadow" — 25:45; "Have you not seen the ships" — 17:66 and scores more), whereby the recipient is made to *look* at what has been organized before him as evidence. The addressees: *alladhīna ūtū naṣīban mina al-kitāb* — "those given a portion of the Book" — not the whole bearer-class of revelation, but its *share-division*: al-Ṭabarī's polls settle its address upon the Torah-bearing community of the oasis-towns (the Jews of Madinah, no Gentiles then standing in Arabia with comparable Book-claims) — with the *naṣīb*, portion-word itself carrying inside it the criticism to come: a *part* of the heavenly ledger was granted them (and preserved as such — a covenant-asset), but the portion-sense likewise recalls their resistance to anything beyond it — holding to the share they had while declining the Share now revealed upon the Arabian prophet. The commentators well carefully note how gently the campaign opens — no names, no curses: first only *look*.

**Yashtarūna al-Ḍalālah: Error Purchased as Merchandise**

The first charge is delivered in a shop in the Book's fierce mercantile vocabulary: *yashtarūna al-Ḍalālata* — "they purchase error" — the verb *ishtarā* — to buy, exchange-in-sale — the same coin-verb as 2:16 ("they purchased error at the price of guidance — so their commerce profited not") and 3:177 ("whoever bought unbelief for belief has not harmed God at all"): revelation here describing rejection not as blindness but as *a transaction* — the reasoner paying over what he possesses (guidance-offered, scripture-understood) in order to receive *error* as the deliverable. Al-Rāzī's unpacking of the grammar is the standing classical lesson: purchase-language presupposes preference — they *chose* — not ignorance — and thereby ruins the age-old apology of custom ("we found our fathers so!") with which which Part-holders everywhere defend themselves (cf. 2:170; 5:104; 31:21); the merchant-metaphor furthermore implies accountability — a bargain consented to, a price reckoned, a receipt held — all the while the exchange is *negative*: gold traded for fog. The sūrah's own immediate context teaches what was purchased: verse-by-verse before this it had legislated justice upon orphans, women, and the hour of testimony — and the portion-bearers' error-purchase is their turning from the same standards to private advantage in the wards of their clans (the verse pairing this conduct, in the next breath, with its wish).

**Wa Yurīdūna an Taḍillū al-Sabīl: The Recruitment-Hatred of the Erring**

The second charge descends from commerce to poaching: *wa yurīdūna an taḍillū al-sabīl* — "and they wish that you too stray from the path": the purchase of error never stays contained — error markets itself: the path-losers wishing the Muslims to lose it likewise (the same social physics the Book maps at 2:109 — "many of the People of the Book wish they could restore you to unbelief after your belief, out of envy from their own souls" — and 4:89's blunt demand within Madinah's hypocrite-ring: *"they wish that you disbelieve as they disbelieve, that you may be all alike"*). Al-Qurṭubī's note on this clause discloses the ancient mechanism the scholars observed at work in the Prophet's own courts and alleys: courteous flattery in public, doctrinal sabotage in private — pointed challenges devised to embarrass the Messenger before converts and waverers, Torah-questions contrived for scandal (cf. their ruses listed in 4:46 and 5:41), the missionary-envy aimed at detaching someone — anyone — from the new fellowship so the portion-bearers' own standing at Arabia's revelation-market might be preserved. The wisdom spiritually, the clause is a principle of all ages: the erring do not rest until the walking have strayed — not from intellectual care but from interior vindication-need; misguidance *hires* company the way guilt does — and believers are thereby warned about the circle a man keeps: the Prophet had already named the rule in the proverb-traditions (Abū Dāwūd 4833 — "a man follows the religion of his intimate; so let each of you look to whom he befriends" — al-Tirmidhī grading its cousin 2378 upon the simile of the musk-carrier and bellows).

**The Placement Beneath v. 43: From Purity to War**

The sūrah's own sequence here deserves its note before the storm grows: after purity-laws (v. 43) and before battle-commands (vv. 71–76 ff.), it plants *this* — the announcement that knowledge-holders themselves have entered error's market and hunt the Muslims' path — so that the two halves of the early Medinese defens e are taught together: *ritual* defense of the worshipping body and *doctrinal* defense of the believing mind; the enemy of the second is first the bought-learned — the portion that turned to merchandising. The Prophet receives the campaign's intel with the gaze-command — *alam tara* — and thereby so does every believer ever after: watch the portion-sellers, read their invoices, refuse their bargains — an for God in the very next verse names their true status — "God knows best your enemies" (v. 45) — and appoints Himself the only patron sufficient for the ones pursued along the path.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:45

> **God knows best your enemies. God suffices as a Protector, and God suffices as a Helper.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Wa Allāhu Aʿlamu bi-Aʿdāʾikum: The Intelligence of Heaven Over the Enemy-Circle**

The answer to the recruiters of v. 44 comes as a single declarative of surveillance: *wa Allāhu aʿlamu bi-aʿdāʾikum* — "and God knows best your enemies": the clause is repeated in several places in the Book (cf. 4:25's *wa Allāhu aʿlamu bi-īmānikum* — God knows best your faith) but its two polemic-settings in our sūrah (4:45 here; cf. also 60:1's "take not My enemy and your enemy as allies") are the spearheaded ones: the believers' own intel is short — they see gift-bringers, neighbors, jurists' smiles — *but God knows best* — the commentators (al-Ṭabarī's transmission-chains and al-Rāzī's reasoning) underlining the cut both ways: it unmasks covert hostility (the error-market of v. 44, whose real shop-sign was friendship) — *and* it unshackles the believers from every over-reading, since not every kind-visiting portion-bearer is an enemy — only as God knows: the Muslim thereby saved from both naïveté and paranoia by delegating the intelligence-work Upstairs. The clause thus placed at the head of the Madinan confrontation-verses teaches the Book's community the posture it must hold through the whole engagement: vigilance without busybody-enemy-building; calm custody of the path under God's register of whoever opposes it. Al-Rāzī's fine point on the Arabic structure (the *aʿlam* — knows-best — intimating that human readings may be right only in part) remains the standing pastoral gem: heaven's file on one's enemies is *always* more accurate than the believer's — both on the hidden enemy inside the congregation and on the imagined enemy wrongly feared.

**Kafā bi-Allāhi Waliyyan: Sufficiency of the Deputy-Nearest**

Then the sufficiency-pair that warms the rest of the Qur'an: *kafā bi-Allāhi waliyyan wa kafā bi-Allāhi naṣīran* — "God suffices as a Protector, and God suffices as a Helper": *kafā*, "suffices" — the compact verb of adequacy, predicated with the quasi-prepositional *bi-* (suffices *by* God — no second subject needed) — belongs to the Book's own battalion of *ḥasbunā Allāh* declarations (eighteen *kafā* occurrences across the Qur'an tradition counts the counting itself a classical commonplace: 2:137's "God suffices thee against them"; 3:173– 39:36's "is not God sufficient for His servant?"; 39:38's "God suffices me"; 8:64's "sufficient for thee is God and those of the believers who follow thee" — the root of a whole family of tawakkul-verses) — and *walī*, our recurring root-word of v. 33's heir-half, here at its broadest: the near-champion, the deputized guardian, the patron-with-closeness (whose standing opposite in the Book is precisely *walī against walī* battles: 3:28's believers-not-taking-disbelievers-as-*awliyāʾ* to the exclusion of believers; 9:71's counter-declaration — "the believing men and women are awliyāʾ of one another"): the choice announced as starkly personal — for every enemy that hands you his friendship-contract, God answers: *I am the only walī whose sufficiency never runs out.* Ibn Kathīr's commentary-summary distills the clause's Madinan rôle: the portion-bearers had invited alliance and offered support as the price of compromise — God's response: *you need no ally but Him* — the exact line by which the Prophet ﷺ unim on his exact word the community un-imported itself from every senior-partner offer in town.

**Naṣīran: The Help That Has a History**

The second name in the pair — *naṣīr*, Helper — drags behind it the whole campaign-memory of the Book's use: *naṣr* is help that *decides* — victory-assistance — and the Qur'an's register had already notched with it a growing war-archive: Badr's own fight-clause falling under naṣr (3:123 "God helped you at Badr while you were few"; 8:9–10's "I help you with a thousand of the angels in succession"); the Hunayn instruction-tag noted at 9:25 ("God helped you on many a field"); and the seal of seals — 8:62's "God is sufficient for thee — He it is who supported thee with His help (naṣrihi) and with the believers": the word being God's *external* sufficiency — the walī's interior custody become manifest as battlefield and courtroom aid for the beleaguered believers of Madinah — so the pair walī/naṣīr covers *both chambers of sufficiency*: friendship within and force without. The classical preachers loved pairing them through life-applications (al-Qurṭubī extending the du'a the devotional spine: whoever makes God his *walī* loses no friendship by obeying Him; whoever counts Him *naṣīr* needs nobody's sword-contracts, no foreign sponsors, no protection-money) — and the Medinese context hands the doctrine its sharpest edge: *every alliance the Muslim polity would ever contract must be audited against this double sufficiency* — no friendship that divorces the walī, no sponsors that sideline the naṣīr — for if an "ally's" price is the path of v. 44, then the Qur'an replies in two words: *independent & sufficient:* God — both.

**The Psychological Charter for Every Outnumbered Reader**

Beneath the politics the verse carries its perennial pastoral code for the beleaguered of every age: God's *knowing-best* absolves the believer from the endless spiral-scan of "who among them is the enemy?" — one lives honestly, guards the path, and deposits the intelligence-file with the Omniscient; and His *double sufficiency* bankrupts fear at its two roots — loneliness (I have a walī) and weakness (I have a naṣīr). The sealed doctrine of the sūrah's confrontation-section is thereby in place before its first command arrives (it will come in v. 71's "take your precautions"): God knows the enemy-map; God fills both needs; so the believer may neither surrender his path to the enemy's friendship-price nor panic for shortage of backers — and the Prophet's standing habit polishes the lesson to its famous edge:

> *"Whoever strikes a If you relied upon God with true reliance, He would provide you as He provides the birds: they set out in the morning hungry and return in the evening full."* (al-Tirmidhī 2344 — ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ)

— reliance being not passivity but *sufficiency-underwriting*: move, fight, ally — all inside the knowledge that your two accounts, friendship and aid, are *fully funded from above* — *kafā* — enough — the word is final.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:46

> **Among those who are Jews are some who distort the meaning of the word, and say, "We hear and disobey," and "Hear, as one who hears not!" and "Attend to us," twisting their tongues and disparaging religion. And had they said, "We hear and obey," and "Listen," and "Regard us," it would have been better for them and more proper. But God cursed them for their disbelief, so they believe not, save a few.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Mina Alladhīna Hādū: A Portion, Within a Portion, Charged**

The indictment of the scripture-shareholders now becomes specific: *mina alladhīna hādū yuḥarrifūna al-kalima ʿan mawāḍiʿih* — "from among those who are Jews [are those who] distort words from their places": the double-sift of *min* — *some* among them — tempering the charge at its start (as the tradition insists whenever the Book speaks of error-communities: the verse closes likewise with *save a few*), while the verb *yuḥarrifūna* — *taḥrīf*, to edge aside, to to dis-place — names the signature sin of scripture-keepers: not forging the Book outright but *edging words out of their berths* (the noun *ḥarf*, edge/limit/letter, inside). The classical inventory of taḥrīf developed from this verse's four poster-appearances in the Book (2:75; 4:46; 5:13; 5:41) runs in three grades: (1) *mis-siting* itself — adding, omitting, or replacing actual words of the Torah (Ibn Kathīr's and al-Qurṭubī's heavy grade — deliberate textual tampering, as the jurists altered stoning-lines and prophecy-notices); (2) *mis-interpretation* — words retained and their *sense* twisted — al-Zamakhsharī's grammarian-eye inclining here (the rearrangement of context, *ʿan mawāḍiʿih*, being semantic as much as codicological); and (3) *mis-reporting* of what the Prophet said — al-Qurṭubī's minority prong — twisting the words of Muhammad ﷺ himself into caricature. The taḥrīf-doctrinology The doctrine that matured from this seed — that God's earlier Books were preserved as *His speech* but their custodies imperfectly guarded — anchors the whole later Islamic account of scriptures: the Book confirms yet audits (5:48 *muhayminan ʿalayh* — sentinel over it) — and the crime of the custodians is here named in its most precise possible definition: *the Word is not denied — it is dis-placed.*

**Samiʿnā wa ʿAṣaynā: The Inverted Creed Both Heard and Said**

Then the three mock-clauses, each one the inversion of Islamic discipleship: *wa yaqūlūna samiʿnā wa ʿaṣaynā* — "and they say: We hear — and disobey!" — the deliberate retort-counterfeit of the believers' own covenant-formula (2:285 — "we hear and obey," *samiʿnā wa aṭaʿnā*; and 24:51 — the description of true believers: *"their only saying when called to God and His Messenger is: We hear and we obey"*) — the two-syllable swap from *aṭaʿnā* to *ʿaṣaynā* converting faith-protocol into defiance-flag; *wa ismaʿ ghayra musmaʿin* — "and: Hear! — as one un-heard!" — the commentators weighing its evil registers (al-Ṭabarī's roll: either *listen — may you never be heard [answered]* — a curse of silence upon the Prophet's call; or *listen as one who cannot hear* — the insult of treating the Messenger as a deaf instrument) — either way a curse or jeer flung within syllable-range of courtesy; and *wa rāʿinā layyan bi-alsinatihim* — "and: rāʿinā! — twisting with their tongues": the celebrated *rāʿinā* — shepherd-us!, attend to us — almost courteous, yet twisted with a sideways articulation (a lengthening, a winking spin among themselves) so the word slid toward insult or, in the reports' own glossing, toward a sour play on *ruʿūnah* — foolishness (2:104's parallel prescription confirms the clinic: believers were thenceforth commanded to say *unẓurnā* — "regard us" — rather than *rāʿinā* — and *unbelievers eavesdropped the difference* — al-Bukhārī 5947 and Muslim 2990 holding the whole exchange: *"They used the word rāʿinā and smirked; so the believers were commanded to say unẓurnā"* — with ʿUmar's own court punishing misuse later). The three clauses together are the portrait of *obedience's saboteurs*: hear-only-to-alter hearing only to alter, addressing only to deride — the mind of the seminar-mocker substituted for the disciple's *hearing-and-obeying*.

**Wa Ṭaʿnan fī al-Dīn: Disparagement of Religion as Their Destination**

The sentence's tail names the slander-clauses' true intent: *wa ṭaʿnan fī al-dīn* — "and as a stab into religion": *ṭaʿn*, lance-thrust — sneering branded as spearwork on the faith itself (the Book's own rhetoric of word-wounds: cf. 9:61's "they hurt the Prophet saying he is an ear"; 33:57's "those who hurt God and His Messenger" — heaven counting verbal stabs within ḥarm-crime) — and the tradition notes the clause's range beyond the moment-echo: every tongue-twist against the Messenger is *fi al-dīn* — aimed at religion, not merely at a person; the Prophet himself articulated the logic in his in his general counsel to the community — narrated of him that he was wounded in the cause of God and sneered at, but *hurt to the messenger equals hurt to the Sender* (al-Bukhārī's Kitāb al-Adab registers the expansion: "he who wrongs one of God's friends — God declares war against him" — the ḥadīth qudsī of Bukhārī 6502). The clause thereby serves as the scene's judgment-summation: the curses did not merely stain etiquette — they disfigured religion in the eyes of the bystanding poor and new converts (al-Zamakhsharī noticing the audience-form: twists done *bi-alsinatihim* — tongues plied theatrically — the performance the medium of the crime) — hence the verdict: *little courtesy-crimes are never little when their object is God's road.*

**Wa Law Annahum Qālū... La-ʿAḍūhum: Mercy Recommended Even to Mockers**

Then the verse does what few indictments do — it writes the neighboring correct speech, all three emendations: *wa law annahum qālū samiʿnā wa aṭaʿnā wa ismaʿ* — "We hear and obey — and: Listen!" — *wa wa-unẓurnā la-kāna khayran lahum wa aqwam* — "it would have been better for them and more upright": heaven itself line-editing the mockers' script — showing that the whole tragedy sits only syllables away from repair (the comparative *aqwam* — straighter, more proper — the same root of *qawwāmūn* one arc above — conduct being, everywhere, the standing-up of words); the teachers have always prized the clause as the Qur'an's pastoral pattern: indictment *with template* — God never only convicts; He dictates the alternative sentence — so the entire psychology of true daʿwah stands in micro-cosm in clauses: never rebuke *without teaching the substitute-word.* And then the seal swings shut on what their chosen syllables earned them: *wa lakin laʿanahumu Allāhu bi-kufrihim fa-lā yuʾminūna illā qalīlā* — "but God cursed them for their disbelief — so they believe not, save a few": *laʿn*, banishment from mercy — the doctrinal weight(2:161's universal curse-word for those who die upon kufr; 2:159's cult of concealers laid beside our earlier conceal our vv. 37's concealers of bounty) — and *illā qalīlā* — save a few — cutting either as *few believing* (al-Qurṭubī: the saved remnant among them — the ʿAbdullāh b. Salām-line who converted) or *lightly believing* (the gloss of the fine print: belief so thin it cannot stand). Between the two readings the reader breathes — because the ʿAbdullāh-ibn-Salām-line *proves the double-sift of* min *at the verse's head*: some from among them — not all — broke pattern and washed themselves from the laʿnah the curse — and their conversion among Madinah's honest scholars (the "men of scripture whom the verse moved" of v. 47's reports) remains the Book's standing door to every portion-bearer since: *the script was dictated; the choice remains yours.*

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:47

> **O you unto whom the Book has been given! Believe in what We have sent down, confirming that which is with you, before We blot out faces and turn them backwards, or curse them as We cursed those [who broke] the Sabbath. And the Command of God shall be fulfilled.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Yā Ayyuhā Alladhīna Ūtū al-Kitāb: A Direct Summons Across the Scripture-Border**

After the triple-fence of smell after the indictments of vv. 44–46, heaven turns and speaks to the charged themselves: *yā ayyuhā alladhīna ūtū al-kitāba āminū bi-mā nazzalnā muṣaddiqan li-mā maʿakum* — "O you who have been given the Book! Believe in what We have sent down — confirming what is with you": a direct vocativo a direct vocative, rare for this address-class in the Book (its notable sisters at 2:41 — "believe in what I sent down confirming what is with you, and be not the first disbeliever in it" — and 5:68 — "O People of the Book! You are upon nothing until you uphold the Torah and the Gospel and what was sent down to you"): the summons always carries the same predicate — the Qur'an presented *not as a rival* to the inherited books but as their *muṣaddiq*: the confirmer — the traditions emphasizing the rhetorical tenderness of it (al-Ṭabarī and al-Zamakhsharī's noting how God does not say "accept what destroys your portion" but "what *confirms* it" — the argument taken from within their own cargo: the Torah predicted itself pointed forward, the convict and the Prophet's cameos in it — their own scholars having narrated which lines marked the Arabian prophet). The offer-terms, therefore, are not surrender-of-heritage but fulfillment-of-heritage — with the complementary with the complementary clause of 2:91 sealing the psychology of refusal: *"when it was said to them: believe in what God sent down, they say: we believe in what was sent down to us — disbelieving in what is after it, though it is the Truth confirming what they have."*

**Min Qabli an Naṭmisa Wujūhan Fa-Naruddahā ʿalā Adbārihā: The Erasure of Faces**

Then the ultimatum-side, a terror-form almost without parallel: *min qabli an naṭmisa wujūhan fa-naruddahā ʿalā adbārihā* — "before We blot out faces and turn them backwards": *ṭ-m-s*, the wiping-out that leaves no trace (~ the effacing root of ṭams as as the Book uses it for blinding-untrace, 77:8's stars effaced; 36:66's "had We willed We would have blotted out their eyes so they raced toward the path") — and the commentators spread its registers into the two grand classical ones: (1) *spiritual-effacement* — faces = the honor-distinguishing features of the soul; features erased and *turned backwards* = discernment inverted — guidance-theorems denied them, all bearings reversed — the inward punishment of rejecting known truth being precisely the loss of moral front/rear (al-Rāzī's elegant reading: they who walk backward from confirmation find the future itself switched with the past); and (2) *corporal transformation* — al-Ṭabarī's chains relaying the report-grade of literal prophecy: celestial wrath blotting out eyes, features, and heads twisted to face the back — and al-Qurṭubī preserving both with the sober rider that the *first case* — the moral erasure — is the base meaning, the second left to His plan being what God may effect on whom He wills (cf. his parallel at 36:66). Either way the clause is a warning of *form-loss* aimed at scholars: those trained to dignity-of-word stand warned that knowledge refused becomes a *turning around of their own image* — the most devastating de-resolution of the fall from the writing-desk: *facing backward — featureless — in public*.

**Aw Nalʿanahum Ka-mā Laʿannā Aṣḥāba al-Sabt: The Sabbath-Precedent**

The second limb of the ultimatum cites their own ancestor-court-file: *or We curse them as We cursed the Sabbath-people* — the community God already banished from mercy for covenant-sabotage: the Sea-towners of 2:65 ("Be you apes, despised") and its full narrative at 7:163–166 (the fish tempted into the unlawful net on their consecrated rest-day — stratagem treated as covenant-fraud) and 4:154's mention nigher nearer ("We took their covenant... and said to them: transgress not the Sabbath") — the prosecutors thereby press pressed to face their own family precedent: God has expelled Book-holders from mercy before — upon Sabbath-law partly hidden, partly twisted, partly evaded — the same three vices charged in vv. 44–46 immediately above — so the logic closes in: *you know what came of those before you; the only survivor of your people is repentance.* The classes of curse for the present offenders run in al-Ṭabarī's and Ibn Kathīr's record along the same twin-tracks as the faces-threat — exclusion-from-mercy here or chastisement hereafter — with its history the historical memory of the commentators (al-Zamakhsharī's register and Ibn Kathīr's chronology) preserving the *outwake the outcome*-report at Madinah: some of the learned of the Book did accept (the ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām-line of the ten heaven-dwellers' assurance — Bukhārī the Tradition naming him therein, Tirmidhī 3723 census; and the conversions that then followed) — and those conversions, God willing in the Mercy's own timing, stayed the harsher external forms of the threatened wrath from descending upon them en bloc: repentance-interceding-for-a-city, the ancient law by which One by which *some* have always saved *many* from wrath's edge.

**Wa Kāna Amru Allāhi Mafʿūlā: The Decree That Cannot Be Filed Away**

The seal is one of the Book's severity-formats: *wa kāna amru Allāhi mafʿūlā* — "and the command of God is ever accomplished": *amr* — command-affair-decree — and *mafʿūl* — carried wholly through — the passive-participle itself a grammatical prophecy: what God ordains is already in the case of *done* (its parallel seals: 4:44's sequence 4:44's own preceding alarm-lantern in 3:25 and 33:37's "the command of God is ever a decree pre-ordained"; 65:3's "God will bring His command to pass" — the format always chosen when heaven certifies an ultimatum) — and al-Rāzī's note discloses the clause's double-valence: it is *assurance* to the Muslims (the Prophet's vindication *is decreed* — do not bustle) and *terror* to waverers of the Book-intervals (every clause of the two warnings above — the effacement, the curse — is *already administratively sealed*; only repentance re-opens the file). The pericope of the portion-trials then closes its first movement — charge-sheet (44–46), summons with ultimatum (47) — upon a line of sonorous finality: God's decree completes — the only unfixed variable in the whole drama being, still, the reader's response: believe in what came confirming what you have — or the registering hand shall stamp it — *mafʿūlā* — done.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:48

> **Truly God forgives not that any partner be ascribed unto Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whomsoever He will. And whosoever ascribes partners unto God has surely fabricated a tremendous sin.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Lā Yaghfiru an Yushraka Bih: The One Non-Negotiable Clause**

The sūrah's confrontation-block issues its mountain-verdict — one of the four one of the Book's most-cited creedal clauses, twinned almost identically at 4:116 later in this very sūrah: *inna Allāha lā yaghfiru an yushraka bih* — "God does not forgive that He be partnered": *shirk* — ascribing a share, a co-claimant — thus disclosed as the sole darkness outside the tribunal of pardon. The syntax itself presses the doctrine: *lā yaghfiru* — a standing truth in the imperfect — not a threatened one-off act; and *an yushraka bih* in the nominalized infinitive — the fact-of-partnering itself is what's beyond amnesty *as such* — the commentators (al-Ṭabarī's chains, Ibn Kathīr's now-standard handling) immediately posting the verse's own controlling condition: forgiveness shuts *upon shirk as it is met at death* — unrepented, roomed-into-the-hereafter shirk — for the Book itself abounds with the paired door of repair: shirk *repented of* converts to the forgiven-set (25:68–70 — idolaters, murderers, adulterers... "except whoever repents and believes and works righteousness — those God will exchange their evil deeds for good ones"; and 39:53's capstone psalm of hope: *"Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves — despair not of God's mercy! God forgives all sins. Indeed He is the Forgiving, the Merciful"* — the exegetical towers agreeing the clause settles *the whole* sweep, shirk included, when repentance intervenes) — Ibn ʿAbbās's unmistakable summary ruling standing in the books: the negation here is of forgiveness *without* turning back — *not of revolution not of return itself.*

**Wa Yaghfiru Mā Dūna Dhālika Li-man Yashāʾ: Mercy Under Sovereign Choice**

Then the great open hand: *wa yaghfiru mā dūna dhālika li-man yashāʾ* — "and He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills": *mā dūna* — what lies short of it — every sin's rest, from a false oath to the mountain-crimes named in this very sūrah (parent-disobedience, murder, adultery, orphan-gold, ribā) — placed under the Lord's choice for the *unrepenting* (*li-man yashāʾ* — for whom He wills: neither cheap automatic parole nor despair-guillotine; the major sinner lives between two unknowables: he cannot presume, nor may he despair — precisely the soteriology the Ahl al-Sunnah approved embraced against both the Muʿtazilī middle-mania (the grave-sinner as neither believer nor unbeliever, permanently in the Fire save by personal repentance) and the Khārijite excommunication-doctrine (sin = unbelief, exit complete) — al-Rāzī's pages summarizing the school-war with our verse as the fortress of God's *mashīʾah*: will, not mechanism — al-Ṭabarī lodging, beside it, the far-reaching believer-generated the far-reaching witness of the Messenger:

> *"God will bring out of the Fire whoever has in his heart the weight of a mustard-seed of faith one atom faith of an atom's weight, at the intercession of those who intercede..."* (the intercession-register of al-Bukhārī 44 among the among the bases of the shafāʿ corpus, with Muslim 193's register of the final egress — "until not one remains in the Fire who has said lā ilāha illā Allāh with a barley-grain of good in his heart")

— the mā-dūna mercy thus covering, *by God's own announcement*, even the vastest ledger of sins so long as the Unshared Name was never divorced.

**Iftara Ithman ʿAẓīmā: Fabrication as the Essential Analytic of Shirk**

The seal specifies the sin's genus with a verb of lying: *wa man yushrik bi-Allāhi fa-qad iftarā ithman ʿaẓīmal* — "whoever ascribes partners to God has fabricated a tremendous sin": *iftarā*, from *f-r-y* — to invent, contrive, cut cut novelFalse *to forge* — the Book's chosen analysis-word for shirk everywhere shirk's interior is exposed (6:21, 24, 137, 144; 7:37, 89 and scores more: the idols called *ifk*, fict the rapt and their cult summarized at 29:17 as *"you worship apart from God nothing but idols and create a falsehood"*): the idolater not merely confused but a *counterfeiter* — issuing currency of worship against a Treasury he never saw (the god-share he assigned no Owner ever authorized) — hence the coined pairing *ithm* (sin-in-general) super and upon it *ʿaẓīm*, tremendous — its scale adjective chosen above all the Book's sin-gradations for shirk's uniqueness (31:13 — Luqmān's own epitaph-grade advice: *"associate not, for shirk is a tremendous wrong"* — ẓulmun ʿaẓīm). The hadith-canon adds its weaponized its dreadful daily light in the Prophet's own interrogation-sequence — the sin admitting no comparison: when asked *which sin is greatest*, he answered (al-Bukhārī 4477 and 6819; Muslim 86 — the register of ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd):

> *"That you set up a rival unto God while He created you. — Then what That you kill your child fearing he will eat with you. — Then what That you commit adultery with your neighbor's wife."*

— shirk first, *before blood* — because in heaven's logic all other sins wrong *creatures* while this one wrongs *the Giver Himself*: a fraud perpetrated upon the Throne.

**The Asbab-Treasure of the Verse and Its Meeting-at-the-Judgment Ruling**

The commentators' chains (al-Wāḥidī, Ibn Kathīr, al-Ṭabarī's variorum) remember the verse's descent-crossing with the famous question of the Qurayshi delegation — or more precisely the Meccan supplicant Waḥshī (the slayer of Ḥamzah, after accepting manumission as price) and the idolaters' negotiators asking the Prophet: how can men who partnered gods and shed blood *ever* be restored the answer coming back precisely through the twin-verses 25:68–70 (repentance-exchange) and our 4:48's principle: *shirk unpardoned — everything else's file belongs to God's discretion* — and indeed Waḥshī's own later Islam (Muslim lit al-Bukhārī 4072 remembering his conversion, the Prophet's human pang — "hide yourself from me" — but his *acceptance*) stands as the tradition's living marginalia under the verse: *the door to the second clause is never blocked by men; the block only seals the man who meets God still renting His Holiness out.* The sūrah thereby advertises advances from its jurisprudence-of-treasures and households to the tribunal's highest rule: distribute with justice; obey with heart; but keep the Throne singular — for *partnership* is not one mistake among mistakes; it is the demolition of the account-book itself; while every other fault, however towering, yet sits *under* the second half of this verse like a crowd beneath an unrolled canopy: *whatever is less — He forgives, for whom He wills.*

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:49

> **Hast thou not seen those who deem themselves pure? Rather, it is God Who purifies whomsoever He will, and they shall not be wronged so much as the thread of a date stone.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Alladhīna Yuzakkūna Anfusahum: The Self-Certifiers at Their Glass**

After the shirk-canon (v. 48), the gaze-formula returns for the fourth time in the pericope — *alam tara ilā alladhīna yuzakkūna anfusahum* — "Hast thou not seen those who deem themselves pure?": *yuzakkūna*, from *zakāh* — purification, growth, attestation of worth — applied here in the reflexive: they *tazkiya* themselves, self-certifying — presenting their own soul's baptismal certificate (the Book always catching the pose at its starkest: 53:32's even-blunter twin — *"so ascribe not purity to yourselves; He knows best who is God-wary"* — with the schools agreeing that self-conferred holiness is here the enemy). The commentators' report-bundles (al-Qurṛṭubī, al-Ṭabarī, al-Zamakhsharī, al-Wāḥidī) fix the first addressees yet again among the Book-holders of Madinah whose self-certifications had taken run-of-an had taken the registe the recorded forms: *"we are God's children and His beloved"* (5:18's quotation); *"none shall enter the Garden save Jew or Christian"* (2:111 — the privatizing of heaven itself); and, in the finer anecdotes, the claim that their daily sins rinse off by nightfall (the errand the evening-sponge theology of the anecdote reported at Ṭabarī's hand from Ibn ʿAbbās: "our daytime sins are erased at night"), or that they absolve one another by intercession — a whole spiritual insurance-scheme issued *by themselves upon themselves* — a certificate with no bank behind it. The verse cuts the whole enterprise at the root: *self-declared purity is the very opposite of purity* — for the ground of Islam's anthropology (17:11's man "prays for evil as he prays for good"; 12:53 — *"I absolve not my own soul; the soul ever commands unto evil"* — from Joseph's own unwounded mouth, prophet though he was) is that holiness is *received verdict*, never self-writhen wreath.

**Bal Allāhu Yuzakkī Man Yashāʾ: The One Office That Certifies**

The correction arrives in the horizontal in the emphatic adversative: *bal Allāhu yuzakkī man yashāʾ* — "rather, it is God who purifies whom He wills": the *bal* — "rather" — functioning as scripture's sharp eraser-stroke (retrieval-language: the whole preceding boast x-ed out); and *yuzakkī* now in God's own commission: purification is Heaven's prerogative — only the Maker of hearts authorizes their certificates. Al-Rāzī's structure-note seizes the clause's pairing with the earlier with its twin at its own root: the same *li-man yashāʾ* — whom He wills — that attached to forgiveness at v. 48 attaches now to tazkiyah — *will* standing guard at every gate of grace, so the whole celestial economy runs on gifting, not on self-application — and thereby converting the theology into its moral application: *the only commendable pursuit is the pursuit of being among* man yashāʾ — not the manufacture of the certificate. The practical hadith-keys are needed in this very spot — the Prophet's own manuals of heart-audit:

> *"Verily in the body there is a lump of flesh: if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt the whole body is corrupt — verily it is the heart."* (al-Bukhārī 52; Muslim 1599)

— soundness known only to its auditor — and its twin-ledger of warning:

> *"When you see a man given what he loves of this world while he persists in his disobedience — know that it is only istidrāj — a drawing-on." Then he recited: ...* (al-Ḥākim's channel via Abū Mūsā, with the Qur'an's own istidrāj-curses at 6:44 and 68:44 anchoring it)

— worldly success no certificate either: the believer's only comfort is the Looking-Upward audit, *wa man yashāʾ* written above its door.

**Fatīlā: The Thread of the Date-Stone — Justice to the Split-Hair**

The seal's promise comes wrapped in the Book's smallest of justice-units: *wa lā yuẓlamūna fatīlan* — "and they shall not be wronged a *fatīl*": the fatīl itself the thin white fibre-thread inside the split of the date-seed — among the smallest divisions of mote-weight the Arab eye could name (its threefold roster running through the sūrah: 4:77 and 4:124 echoing the same word; with naqīr — the pit's speck-groove — at 4:53 and 4:124, and qitmīr — the stone's film-skin — at 35:13: the classic trio of infinitesimals function as Judgment's measurement-scale) — and its employment here is two-edged with the verse's own logic: (1) those self-purifiers will not be *robbed* one thread of any true good they did (the the fearful symmetry of the Reckoning: not even their smallest real merit will be erased — v. 40's doctrine applied to the enemy too — so God remains *just even toward exact toward hypocrites and boasters*) and (2) they will not be *left* one thread's margin by which to smuggle in their fake certificates — the audit will not fuzz, downward or upward, past a thread's breadth. The commentators tie the clause steady tightly to the whole pericope (vv. 40, 44–48, 49): God wrongs nobody — the boasters' *payment self-stamped* meed boast-discount comes from *their own ledger*, never from divine trimming — and the tradition thereby nourishes at once the humble and the exact: *aim at God's tazkiyah; fear nothing of audit-loss; hope nothing of audit-loophole* — the three prepositions of the believer before Judgment standing in one date-stone thread: *lā ẓulm* — no wrong — to anyone, on any line-item, to any degree.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:50

> **See how they fabricate lies against God! That suffices as a manifest sin.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Unẓur Kayfa: The Prophet Told to Watch the Lying Itself**

The verse strands one more look-command in the Prophet's ear but changes its tense into moral theater: *unẓur kayfa yaftarūna ʿalā Allāhi al-kadhib* — "Look — how they fabricate lies against God!": *unẓur* — look!, the sight-imperative; *kayfa* — *how!* — adverb turned exclamation (the same doublet engineered engineered into the scene-callers of 4:41's kayfa and beyond); and *yaftarūna* — the iftirāʾ-verb already planted into the bedrock of v. 48's seal ("fabricated a tremendous sin") now shown *in operation*: not any falsehood but a precise species: *kadhib ʿalā Allāh* — lying *upon God* — that is, attributing to Him authorizations authorization He never gave (the Book's own forensic definition at 6:93: "who does greater wrong than he who fabricates lies against God or says it was revealed to me when nothing was revealed"; 7:37; 10:17; 11:18; 29:68 — the family-name of perjury in the highest court: claiming *God said* when God did not). Al-Qurṭubī's report-chains tie the clause immediately to vv. 49's self-certificates: the claims *"we are forgiven every morning"*; *"the Garden is ours"*; *"we pairwise absolve each other"* — every one a lie on God's letterhead: imaginary indulgences printed inside the language of religion; and thus commentators expand the definition pastorally beyond its first denizens: *to teach indulgence as doctrine while heavens while heaven wrote no such indulgence is to forge against God* — whether in self-excuse ("God is forgiving — I need not change") or in license-sales to others ("your sin is small; pay no corn heed no consequence") — so that the sūrah's reader scans the verse with some terror of the tongue: *religious speech itself can be the forgery-site.*

**Kafā Bihā Ithman Mubīnā: The Sin Named by Its Own Self-Evidence**

The sentence — short, grave, absolute — is part of Islam's severest arithmetic: *wa kafā bihā ithman mubīnā* — "and it suffices as a manifest sin": *kafā bih* — "it is enough of it" — the book-keeping phrase by which a single entry's size is certified without need of further of further entries (the same *kafā*-formula deployed at 2:217 of hindering from God's path; at 4:6 above — *kafā bi-Allāhi ḥasībā* — God enough as reckoner; at 17:17 of the Master's knowledge of sins) — and the predicate *ithman mubīnā* — *a plain, glaring, manifest sin* — mubīn the self-showing flagrant — its indictment thereby being: *to require no evidence-chains; the thing proves itself.* The practical theology built on the clause by the doctors is one of the tradition's safeguard-fences: false speech in religion is not only a lie with sacred nounwords — it is the singular crime for which no balancing ledger of good deeds can excuse: hence the Prophet's frightening direct-counsel (al-Bukhārī 3505 the register attributing the wording variously; Tirmidhī the canonical line of Muslim standing the line standing firmest in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim's introduction-admonitions the famous Maxim actually the direct Bukhārī-text):

> *"Whoever tells lies upon me deliberately, let him take his seat in the Fire."* (al-Bukhārī 110 & 1291; Muslim 3, in variations)

— the most reiterated single hadith in history precisely because forgery in God's (and His Messenger's) name is the one fraud that corrupts the vessel itself: every later vessel drinks from whatever the counterfeit left inside. The classical jurists extended its no-trade discipline across the whole religious economy: fabricated ḥadīth false classified the greatest of sins after shirk; mis-citation of the Book for policy classified under iftirāʾ; and even well-intended piety-fable (the lies of the story-tellers in the mosques, whose phenomenon al-Bukhārī's register brands names its own spread) placed under *kadhib ʿalā Allāh* when it issues doctrine.

**The Self-Certifier and the Forger: One Corridor**

The pericope's two halves (vv. 49–50: self-purifying, then God-lying) are hereby seen as one room — for every false claim about the self in God's name — *I am pure, we are children, the Garden is ours, penance by evening* — is logically *special pleading from the special pleading with the throne as as guarantor*: the soul putting God's seal beneath its own press-release. The sufi-commentary grafts its own razor onto the verse (al-Qushayrī's circle marking the deeper law: pleasing oneself with one's own soul *extinguishes the lights of certitude*; self-trust in one's purity *the veil itself*) — and the wisdom of the traditions closes the corridor at its exit with the purified heart's definition — the only true tazkiyah being the one God grants at Judgment. The reader's practical sum takes a breath-length: never vouch for your own soul; never coin a doctrine to defend it; audit yourself mercilessly, and let God audit you mercifully — for one thing alone *suffices* as a sin irreparable while it stands: a forgery upon God's own name — *kafā bihā ithman mubīnā*: it suffices.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:51

> **Hast thou not considered those who were given a portion of the Book, who believe in idols and false deities, and say of those who disbelieve, "These are guided more rightly than those who believe."**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Yuʾminūna bi-l-Jibt wa-l-Ṭāghūt: Two Tokens of Everything False**

The pericope's fifth lantern turns its beam upon the portion-bearers' deepest betrayal: *yuʾminūna bi-l-jibti wa-l-ṭāghūt* — "they believe in *al-jibt* and *al-ṭāghūt*": two rare words, each loaded by a whole tradition of gloss — *al-jibt*, a hapax of the Book (only here) whose basic sense the lexical authorities (al-Jawharī-era philology reported through al-Ṭabarī's roll) fix as *the nothing-worth*, the weightless trifle — idol-figure, sorcerer's stock, chance-token; *al-ṭāghūt*, the over-towerer — from *ṭughyān*, transgressing the bounds (flood-water over its banks) — naming *every overlord who sets himself across God's limits*: the Satan, the tyrant, the soothsayer, the false god — familiar from its repeated battle-posts in the Book (2:256–257 — "whoever disbelieves in the ṭāghūt and believes in God has grasped the firmest bond"; 4:60's about-to-appear arbitration-refusers "wish to resort to the ṭāghūt though commanded to disbelieve in it"; 4:76's "fight the allies of Satan"; 16:36's per-community command — "worship God and shun the ṭāghūt") — and the classical asbāb-rolls (al-Wāḥidī's chains, al-Ṭabarī, Ibn Kathīr, al-Zamakhsharī) converge on the occasion that gave these two names their Madinan faces: *Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf and Ḥuyayy ibn Akhṭāb*, the two fiery scholars of the Book-towns, riding to Mecca after the Muslims' Uḥud-reversal to build the anti-Prophet coalition — and there brought, the reports say, before Quraysh's idols: pressed by their hosts to honor the two Meccan god-figures called *jibt and ṭāghūt* (or, by alternative chains, standing for idol-stock and sooth for idol and oracle) — *they paid the bows their hosts asked* — scriptured men, learned in the One, honoring tokens — a transaction of alliance priced in worship.

**Hāʾulāʾi Ahdā mina Alladhīna Āmanū: The Comparative Lie Before the Kaʿbah**

The deeper wound was their verdict-sentence pronounced at the Kaʿbah's precinct: *wa yaqūlūna li-lladhīna kafarū hāʾulāʾi ahdā mina alladhīna āmanū* — "and they say of the disbelievers: these are more rightly guided than the believers": the Meccans had put the comparison-bill before them with precision (the reporters preserve its lobbying-wording: *we give drink to the pilgrims and keep the sanctuary and uphold kinship; Muhammad has abandoned the Kaʿbah's rites and cut the wombs* — with the world between Mecca's pilgrimage-hosting and the fugitive-prophet's new claim set out for the two scholar-guests as a test) — and the two delivered the verdict their hosts wanted: the idol-keepers *are better guided* than your people — scripture-holders judging polytheism the riper road — the commentators marking the moment as among history's most instructive collapses: credentialed learning renting itself to the room's applause — al-Rāzī's quiet horror in his note on the scene's rational scandal: the two could read the Torah's first table (*no god but God*) while praising the shrine of the many over the camp of the One — and Ibn Kathīr's verdict echoing down the centuries: *the scholar who flatters falsehood with his rank is worse than the idolater he decorates* — the seat for the pagan's error crashes is naked, while the savant's lie goes out wearing the robe of authentication. The tradition's jurisprudence of learned betrayal (the fuqahāʾ toll-call of *ʿulamāʾ al-sūʾ* — evil-scholars — built from cases like this one) and the prophetic alarm both stand here at their fountain:

> *"That which I fear most for my ummah is the misguiding imams."* (Abū Dāwūd 4252; al-Tirmidhī 2229 — in the narrative of Thawbān)

**The General Meaning: Faith-Language Can Serve the Ṭāghūt**

Beyond the scene stands the verse's standing legibility (al-Ṭabarī's own closing unzip al-Ṭabarī's closing extension of the lexicon as much quoted as the asbāb): *al-jibt wa-l-ṭāghūt* discharge their duty as the umbrella over *all false objects to whom portion-loss to whom people resort in God's stead* — every carved token and every transgressing authority — so that the verse ever measures *religious professionals* wherever they point their authority: the criterion is never the robe but the arrow — toward whom does the scholar's praise *move* the room? The classical morality-texts (al-Ghazālī's Iḥyāʾ-chapters on the scholar's snares transposed a whole the Iḥyāʾ's books on the perils of learning) preserve the lesson as the standing fear of the devout: knowledge itself cannot immunize against the audience's prices; the same credentials that certify sound doctrine can be rented to crown the ṭāghūt — hence believers are taught to test every clerical verdict against the measure of of its alignment with the guidance of those who believe* — not against credentials — since even portion-bearers have pronounced idols fairer than the Book's own household. The verse thereby seals its warning within the sūrah's jurisprudence-of-trustworthiness: just as orphan-wealth must be guarded from embezzling guardians, *guidance itself must be guarded from endorsing scholars* — watching the *direction* of their verdicts, never only the dressing — with the Prophet's remaining counter-guarantee held before the community as its only safe harbor:

> *"God does not seize knowledge by snatching it from the servants; rather He takes the knowledge by taking the scholars — until, when no scholar is left, people take ignorant heads and are asked, and they give verdicts without knowledge: they go astray and lead others astray."* (al-Bukhārī 100; Muslim 2673)

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:52

> **They are those whom God has cursed, and whomsoever God curses, thou wilt not find for him any helper.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Ulāʾika Alladhīna Laʿanahumu Allāh: The Banishment Now Attributed**

The verdict of the portion-trials falls in a demonstrative-sentence of total of total finality: *ulāʾika alladhīna laʿanahumu Allāh* — "those are they whom God has cursed": *ulāʾika*, the far-finger demonstrative — *those* — distancing them at grammar's own length (the pointing-out of persons as remote-and-settled cases); and *laʿanahumu Allāh*, God has *cursed* them: *laʿn* — from l-ʿ-n — expulsion, driving-away — its root-image the camel chased off from the herd driven from the herd-th its meaning in the Book's calibrations (al-Ṭabarī's note, al-Suyūṭī's collections the tradition's standard gloss) fixedly *al-ṭard wa-l-ibʿād* — banishment from mercy: to be removed from the radius of grace (its earlier deployment in this very pericope at 4:46's *laʿanahumu Allāhu bi-kufrihim* — the curse for disbelief — and its Judgment-family across the Book: 2:159's concealer-curse joined by angels and mankind; 11:18 and 60's terrify the curse sentences in sequence; 28:42's universality of the banishment: cursed in the world and on the Day). The verse's singling out makes its own jurisprudential point: the comparative lie of v. 51 is *not* merely an impoliteness or a misjudgment — the courtroom of the verse places it under laʿn — Heaven recording the endorsement of idolatory of idolatry over faith — from the mouth of the learned — as among the acts that *evict* a man from mercy: teaching teaching him that the charge changes when credentials serve as the raw material of misguidance (the pericope's own ladder thus: errors bought — v. 44; tongues twisted — v. 46; faces warned — v. 47; shirk's fence — v. 48; self-purity — v. 49; forgery — v. 50; and now *endowment endorsement* — the crowning case meriting exile).

**Wa Man Yulʿani Allāhu Fa-Lan Tajida Lahu Naṣīrā: Helper-Bankruptcy of the Cursed**

The second clause widens from the case to the law: *wa man yulʿani Allāhu fa-lan tajida lahu naṣīran* — "and whomsoever God curses, you will find for him no helper": *lan tajida* — *never shall you find* — the categorical negative doubling the famine of the future (the *lan* of permanent futurity — the idiom running through the Book's receipts of impossibility: 18:17's "whom God guides — he is the guided; and whom He leaves astray you will find no guiding friend for him"; 4:88's own mirror below — "whom God leads astray you will never find for him a way"; and 39:23's like) — the Prophet being addressed by *tajida* personal *you*, Muhammad, with all your love for people — *you* will locate no helper for such a one: not clans (the whole Arabia's whole clan-insurance system useless), not scholar-networks ("a the scholars of Book-quotations), not political patrons, not treasuries: the cursed is *helper-bankrupt*, for the one Being from whose treasury all help arrives has issued against him the order of cut-off. The commentators lay the verse's personal edge precisely against the two scholars of v. 51 (al-Wāḥidī's narrative-chains and Ibn Kathīr's commentary historical chronicle): Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf — the verse's first face — was indeed cut off within the year (his end written into the Prophet's warfare-chronicles as a sanctioned removal of a menace, Sīrah-records of Ibn Hishām logging the Banū al-Naḍīr sequence through which Ḥuyayy's own coalition followed him to ruin at Banū Qurayẓah's collapse) — laʿn arriving historically as *the unraveling of every helper their politics had hired* — al-Qurṭubī drawing the standing moral for believers ever after: *ally yourself with God's curse and God's help alike shall fail with the cursed and you'll be funded all help fails that is purchased upon their side* — a law the sūrah presses further at vv. 76, 119's declarations of war upon Satan's party.

**The Seal of Help-Sufficiency Revisited**

The pericope's architecture now discloses itself as a perfect bracket: v. 45 had assured the believers *"God suffices as a Helper"* (kafā bi-Allāhi naṣīran); v. 52 now stamps the obverse upon the enemy — *man yulʿani Allāh — no helper shall ever be found for him* — the two *naṣīr*-clauses facing one another across the section like the two wings of one door: *help is the world's only currency that matters, and its bank has one Governor* — so the chooser given the choice plainly: be *cursed-and-helperless* though allied with the strong, or *helped-of-God* though abandoned by the clans — the desert logic of Madinah with its coalition-price with its alliance-arithmetics turned into eschatology: Badr's own doctrine (3:123–126 — help of God and angels, not of man's counting) reasserted inside the book-people's scandal: *the expulsion from mercy nullifies all treaties; the the Walī's sponsorship outranks all pacts* — the reader left with the destill the distilled alternative the section has been drawing since its first clause: buy correctness (v. 44), though the markets of the portion-sellers crash; for whom God curses—no stock of helpers anywhere exists that can re-list him; and for whom God suffices—no stock of enemies anywhere exists that can sink him.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:53

> **Or have they a share in sovereignty? If they did, they would not give men so much as the speck on a date stone.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Am Lahum Naṣībun mina al-Mulk: The Rhetoric of the Partnerless Kingdom**

The pericope continues its demolition of the two cursed scholars' platform by throwing open the ledger of *sovereignty* itself: *am lahum naṣībun mina al-mulk* — "or have they a share in sovereignty?": *am*, the disjunctive *or* — detaching its question at first glance from the sentences before it — a puzzle the grammarians treasured (al-Qurṭubī's own note: the *am* must hang upon a suppressed first member, the classical restoration running fine running: *are they worthier of prophethood than the one commissioned, or do they own a share in kingdom with God?* — the answer to both a thundering no): the interrogative driving at the delusion the pericope has been mapping — men without any men without any stock in God's governance yet adjudicating at its gate (v. 51's "these are more guided" verdicts); and *naṣīb*, share-word familiar now from this sūrah's inheritance-chapters (vv. 7, 11–12, 32) — here turned cosmic: the *portion* under question is not an allotment of palm-trees but *mulk*, sovereignty — dominion, kingship, command — God's own title throughout the Book (2:102 "the two did not have the mulk of this 2:107's "to God belongs the mulk of the heavens and the earth"; 3:26 — "Thou givest mulk to whom Thou wilt and strippest it from whom Thou wilt" — the immediately familiar Mulk-verse of the night-devotees; 5:40; 25:2), so the question reads: *do these self-appointed judges hold one share-line in the Power-ledger of the heavens?* — and al-Ṭabarī's roll, al-Zamakhsharī's rhetoric-note, and Ibn Kathīr's capsule concur at the level the pericope requires: *none whatsoever* — the portion-bearers having neither command of heaven's appointments nor even the dates the key to any future's obedience — and therefore no competence whatever to seat themselves at the bench of "more guided."

**Fa-Idhan Lā Yuʾtūna al-Nāsa Naqīrā: The Counterfactual Exposing the Miser-Heart**

Then the verse's magnificent conditional — a single imaginary oscill clause demolishing by fantasy: *fa-idhan lā yuʾtūna al-nāsa naqīrā* — "then they would not give the people even a *naqīr*": *naqīr*, from *n-q-r*, the pecked notch — the speck-hollow on the back of the date-stone (the Qur'an's threefold infinitesimal-unit already sketched at v. 49's *fatīl* — thread — and reinforced at v. 124's naqīr again: least units of all scales deployed wherever the Book discloses exact sever exactitude in judgment or meanness in men) — the rhetorical structure being a *counterfactual of exposure*: *if* such men *had* a kingdom-share, their intrinsic stinginess would empty would starve mankind to less than a speck: the hypothetical used not to imagine generosity but to *forensic to unmask*: for al-Rāzī's standing use of the man's of the device: the way a man handles *small* powers prophesies his handling of great ones — and the portion-bearers had already displayed their scale at Madinah: hoarding the knowledge of the Prophet's coming from their own flocks (concealment of v. 37's "bounty"), selling verdicts for clan-fees (v. 44's error-purchase), tolerating idol-honor for alliance (v. 51): men who dole out *truth* in eyedroppers would not in any universe portion out *sovereignty* in streams. The Prophet's own hadith encapsulates the same acid-management the same acid test in a famous treasury-line the commentators love to place beneath it (al-Bukhārī 1416; Muslim 1038, the register of Hārith of Abū Dharr's the directly apt register):

> *"The upper hand is better than the lower hand; and begin upon those for whom you are responsible. The best charity is what is given from sufficiency — and whoever refrains, God makes him content; and whoever acts rich, God makes him rich."*

— the *giving-hand* being at once the test of wealth's hold on its owner and the parable-in-reverse of v. 53: while the world measures sovereignty by *takings*, heaven measures souls by *dispensings*.

**Sovereign Integrity and the Reader's Inheritance**

The verse carries at last its deep assurance into the life of the believing heir: since God's mulk is *partnerless*, no deputy's stinginess can ration what He appoints for the believer — the community's fear before the cursed scholars and their hosts is hereby bankrupted by grammar: they own *no shares*; take nothing to heart that such hands deny you; and the sūrah's long probation returns to its own frontiers: the orphan-shares (vv. 2–14) guaranteed by the same Partnerless One notwithstanding the hoarders; the mercy-shares (vv. 16–29) flowing through His treasury not theirs; and this new word amid them: *power too has no stock-company to bribe* — the heavens not a market, intercession not a brokerage, and *al-mulk* remaining where the Book's equal night-litany repeats it: *for God is the Sovereignty entire* — 5:40's own cadence sealing the register the reader now chants to himself before every court and cabal that would tax his hope: *"to God belongs the sovereignty of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them — and unto Him is the homecoming."*

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:54

> **Or do they envy men on account of what God has given them of His Bounty? We gave the House of Abraham the Book and Wisdom, and We granted them a mighty sovereignty.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Am Yaḥsudūna al-Nāsa: Envy Named, at Last, as the Engine**

The pericope's *am*-series penetrates deeper still — past purchase (v. 44), past tongue-work (v. 46), past lying (v. 50), past the throne-verdicts (v. 51) — into the motivating chamber itself: *am yaḥsudūna al-nāsa ʿalā mā ātāhumu Allāhu min faḍlih* — "or do they envy the people for what God has granted them of His bounty?": *yaḥsudūna*, from *ḥ-s-d* — to burn at another's blessing — and *al-nās*, *the people* — either the Prophet himself (al-Ṭabarī's concrete: the Book and the emigration-crowns given Muhammad) or the whole household of Islam (al-Qurṭubī's width: those who came into bounty with him) — the charge-sheet's engine thereby being confessed by heaven's own diagnostician: all the procedure of vv. 44–53 — error-buyings, mock-words, self-purity, endorsed idols — are *symptoms*; the fever beneath is ḥasad — the interior verdict that God's division was *unfair* (the Book's own disclosure of envy across its passages: 2:109 — "many of the People of the Book wish to restore you to unbelief out of envy from within themselves, though the truth has become manifest to them"; 3:19's community-splits born of envy *after knowledge came*; and 2:90's perfect mapping of the crime — *"disbelieving in what God sent down, grudging that God sends of His bounty upon whom He wills of His servants"* — for envy is, precisely, *quarrel with a gift-Giver over whom He chooses*) — and with the naming the pericope's psychology completes itself: hatred of *His choice* — the primal sin twice-cited by the commentators on this verse: Iblīs over Adam (the heavenly first — 7:11–13 — "what prevented you...? I am better than he" — the *comparison* being envy's whole syllogism) and Cain over Abel (the earthly first — 5:27–31) — the two standing stations of ḥasad between which the portion-bearers' posture was placed by the doctors: heaven-born, earth-learned.

**The Prophet's Envy-Medicine Beside the Verse**

The sūrah's diagnosis comes accompanied already by the Prophet's two pharmacist's jars (the traditions the commentators, al-Qurṭubī above all, lodge immediately beneath this clause):

> *"Beware of envy, for envy devours good deeds as fire devours wood — or he said: grass."* (Abū Dāwūd 4903 — narrated by Abū Hurayrah)

— the fire-metaphor measuring exactly what v. 54 displays: their rage *ate their own Book-wealth* while leaving its object untouched (for God's bounty upon Muhammad and his community only grew — He appointed as 4:54's own tail discloses) — and the subtler second jar:

> *"I have not seen an oppressor more like the oppressed than the envier: constant burning, shallow breathing, grief-cur sighs folded into the chest."* (the sages' citation through al-Qurṭubī's commentary register and the adab-collections)

— the envier being himself both ẓālim and maẓlūm — the violence consuming its owner — the Ḥasan al-Baṣrī-line summary afterwards ubiquitous in the piety-books: *"I have not seen an oppressor more like the oppressed than the envier"* — the same sentence in its shorter authentic roll-call — so that the sūrah's reader learns double-protection: *against envying men* (the audit of pleasure of pleasure at blessing-distribution) and *against being burned by envy-engines around him* — the Book's own proha its own shield-sūrah 113 already in his mouth every dawn: *"from the evil of an envier when he envies."*

**Āta- We Gave the House of Abraham: Precedence as the Envy-Cure**
