The argument's answer arrives as a devastating precedent: *fa-qad ātaynā āla Ibrāhīma al-kitāba wa al-ḥikmata wa ātaynāhum mulkan ʿaẓīmā* — "We gave Abraham's House the Book and the Wisdom, and granted them a tremendous sovereignty": the syntax weights its own anaphora — *ātaynā*... *wa ātaynāhum* — We gave... and We gave them — heaven *reciting its record* against the grudgers: (1) *the Book* — the scrolls of Abraham (87:19 — "the scrolls of Abraham and Moses") and the great dispensations of the house thereafter (Torah, Psalms, Gospel in their line); (2) *the Wisdom (al-ḥikmah)* — inspiration never book-bound: judgment's light behind the written word (the pair kitāb/ḥikmah becoming the Book's own repeated formula for prophet-treas for prophets' equipment: 2:231, 3:48, 4:113 below for Muhammad himself, 62:2); and (3) *a mighty mulk* — the kingdom-line of David and Solomon (vast estate and temple — the wealth-kings whose empires their own people had gloried in) — the whole clause disclosing heaven's logic: *your objection to bounty given Quresh Quraysh has no legs* — God's freedom in distribution is Abraham-anchored, David-anchored, Solomon-anchored — one unbroken record of *outsize gift* — so to burn now over a prophet raised from Ishmael's line (who stands inside Abraham's house! — 2:125–129, 14:37's own landing of the Sacred House's prayer): is either to disown the family-file or to pretend the Father saw wrongly — al-Zamakhsharī's razor adding the worldly counterstroke for the envious of the Prophet's many marriages (33:50's exemption): the clause's own House-argument rebuts even that, since David and Solomon of their *own* house had wives beyond counting. The Shiʿi tradition (citing Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq through al-Ṭabrisī's roll) extends the clause's "men" to the Prophet's *family* — imāmah granted as bounty — the Sunni which the broadest reading already holds inside itself: *bounty-envy in every generation indicts the same ancient disease* — refusing what God gives whom He wills — the medicine forever the same: *count not another's gifts; audit your own ingratitude* — for the House of Abraham's file shows: when God appoints, He appoints on a scale that outlasts the sul the sul outlasts the sun of every envier.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:55

> **Among them are those who believe in him, and among them are those who turn away from him. And Hell suffices as a blazing flame!**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Fa-Minhum Man Yuʾminu Bih: The House Divides Itself**

The pericope closes its judgment-arc with an unsparing division-table: *fa-minhum man yuʾminu bih wa minhum man yaṣuddu ʿanh* — "among them are those who believe in him, and among them are those who turn away from him": the two-fold *minhum* — some of them... and some of them — heaven itself performing the census of a community split by the Prophet's arrival (the two pronoun-investigations the commentators run: *bih* — "in him" — either in the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and his message (the majority, al-Rāzī-logic al-Ṭabarī and al-Qurṭubī's roll: him = the one provisioned with bounty in v. 54) — with the wider reading taking it as *in it* — the Qur'an (al-Qurṭubī's note) — or even *in Abraham*, the House of v. 54 turned itself into the sift of the city — al-Zamakhsharī's alternate) — and *yaṣuddu* — *ṣadd ʿan* — to turn away from, to bar oneself (and others) from — the same ṣ-d-d root of the path-blocker's stubbornness that runs through the Book's portraits of obstinacy (2:217's hindering from God's way; 3:99, 6:126 7:45, 8:47, 34:32 — barring others also from the path they have refused) — the two camps therefore being: the portion-bearers who confirmed and the portion-bearers who entrenched. The historical census the tradition invariably consults: the first column contains the converts of Madinah — ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām and his circle (the tradition's exemplar of the scholar who crossed, Tirmidhī 3723's heaven-roll registering him among the ten assured) — and with them the second-class the second column: the Kaʿb-Huyayy line of v. 51 and the entrenched of the three Book-tribes — the verse thereby *explaining* what the previous verses had threatened: the ultimatum of v. 47 (blotting of faces) never descended en masse because the *first column came over* — repentance and conversion diverting the threat, in line with the tradition's global law (8:33 — "God would not punish them while you are among them; nor while they seek forgiveness" — and the standing prophetic dictum that general chastisement lifts where repentance spreads among a people).

**Wa Kafā bi-Jahannama Saʿīrā: The Sufficiency of What Remains**

For the second column the clause is terrible in its economy: *wa kafā bi-jahannama saʿīrā* — "and Hell suffices as a blazing flame": *kafā* — the sufficiency-verb already met twice in the pericope as comfort (*God suffices as Helper*, v. 45; *the sin suffices as evidence*, v. 50) — now deployed as terror: Hell *is enough* — no further sentence-items need stacking; *saʿīr* — from *s-ʿ-r*, to kindle, stoke — the active blazing Furnace (used of Hell in precisely this sufficing-mold at seventeen at its many stations: 25:55 cf. 25:11 the word runs 4:10 earlier in our own sūrah — *they shall enter a blazing flame* — 4:30, 17:8's *saʿīrā* for "We have prepared for the wrongdoers", 48:13's ident 76:4, and beyond) — and what the commentators make of the clause's calm definiteness is its very horror: not threat-crescendo but *closure* — the turners-away's file stamped with a line-item that stands alone: al-Ṭabarī's record of its function — the postponed count those who refused to confirm are *held to the Hereafter's sentence-book*, their worldly doom (v. 47's) deferred but never dropped — the kafā-construction declaring the storage-receipt complete: *no further punishment scheduled — because Hell suffices.*

**The Column-Question for Every Subsequent Reader**

The pericope's long address to the Book-holders therefore ends where it began (v. 47's summons *āminū bi-mā nazzalnā* — believe in what We sent down): the choice modeled — and the choice remains open — as the tradition consistently reads the whole trial-sequence: *portion-bearer* is not a fixed caste-title but a standing option the world offers every day (the envelope of lineage helps nothing; the record of confirmation alone counts — the very doctrine 49:13 places at its summit: *"the most noble of you before God is the most God-wary of you"*) — for every reader inherits both columns' possibilities: God's bounty given — and then the pivot: *confirm it or fortify against Him* — with the two *minhum* columns running open until the meeting, and the saʿīr-sufficiency standby waiting upon the turners: the Scripture having meanwhile already disposed the escape-clause at every door: repentance reroutes a man from the second column *before* the account is locked — even from the very center of obstinacy. Ibn ʿAbbās's The old exegetical note preserves the fiber of it in the unexpected conversion-tales of the scene (men like Mukhayrīq — the scholar of Banū al-Naḍīr who bequeathed his estate to the Prophet and died fighting with Muslims at Uḥud — a single crossing Column recorded in the biographies) — the whole pericope's code as delivered through v. 55: *the columns are open; the record lies with Him; repent before the receipt is drawn* — for the Furnace alone suffices to finish whatever column a man settles in.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:56

> **Those who disbelieve in Our signs, We shall surely cause them to burn in a Fire. As often as their skins are consumed, We shall replace them with other skins, that they may taste the punishment. Truly God is Mighty, Wise.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Sa-Nuṣlīhim Nārā: Fire-Admission in the First-Person Future**

The pericope moves from the sufficiency-receipt of Hell (v. 55) into a single, unblinking mechanism of its execution: *inna alladhīna kafarū bi-āyātinā sawfa nuṣlīhim nārā* — "verily those who disbelieve in Our signs — We shall make them burn in a Fire": *kafarū bi-āyātinā* — disbelieved *in Our signs* — the object precise for the pericope: the book-holders and the mockers who heard *and knowingly refused the delivered evidence* (not mere pagans by birth and unawares — the Book's sharpened kufr is the one *vis-à-vis* received signs); *sawfa* — the deferred-certain future (the particle of distance-yet-irrevocability; as the sages note: in human promises distance may soften, in divine decree it *only loads*); and *nuṣlīhim* — We shall roast we shall make them *arrive into the fire* — from the same ṣ-l-y root heard at 4:30's *fa-sawfa nuṣlīhi nāran* — the first-person plural of majestic agency making admission no accident of nature but the King's own decree *executed by His hand* — al-Rāzī's note catching the procedure: God will not send them there as a sheriff sends a prisoner; He will *convey* them — attendance adduced by sovereignty itself — the court no longer speaking of punishment as a policy but as a personal act of the Remembered.

**Kullamā Naḍijat Julūduhum: The Endless Reroasting**

Then the measure of torment disclosed through the body: *kullamā naḍijat julūduhum baddalnāhum julūdan ghayrahā* — "as often as their skins are roasted through, We shall exchange them for other skins": *kullamā* — *every time that* — the temporal formula of unending recurrence (its series across the Book always opening into endlessness: 22:22's expulsion-and-return-loop — "every time they wish to leave it from grief they are returned into it"; 36:57 the same *kullamā* of fruit-signing at 2:25 too); *naḍijat* — roasted, cooked-through — the flesh-word used nowhere else in the Book — *julūd*, skins, the organ of sensation (the body's own boundary of feel — the dermis where pain and shame both register) — and *baddalnāhum julūdan ghayrahā* — We *replace* — substitution of another skin for the consumed one: the classical discussions at this point organized themselves into the two readings al-Ṭabarī and al-Qurṭubī bequeath: (1) *somatic resurrection continuous*: genuine skins, sensation restored — the reading the Tradition had already pinned in the famous debate between the Prophet and the Meccan questioners — reported in the transmitted registers as the verse’s occasion-class: the scene stands among the most instructive of the sources — Ubayy ibn Khalaf the Meccan sneering at resurrection ("will my Lord really revive us when we are bones and fragments?") and the Prophet answering that He can do more; the answer converging here: *He who created them the first time* — and (2) the second register (al-Ṭabarī's register, cited in al-Qurṭubī's own pages): the *pitch-garments* of 14:50 — their faces covered by Fire, their clothes made of pitch — being consumed and replaced round the real body beneath — a garment-of-flame reading that softens nothing of the horror, only changes its textile — the tradition concluding across both: *recurring in kind, unbroken in time* — al-Rāzī's metaphysical aside being thereby made useful: the changing of *attributes* (skins) around an *essence* (the punished self) — the sufferer abideth, his rind his surface replenished — eschatology teaching plainly what it needn't teaching by sheer anatomy: *whoever demanded literal proof of torture's machinery has been answered in literal anatomy; whoever feared it as metaphor may read the metaphor — for both the depth is the same: never-endingness.*

**Li-Yadhūqū al-ʿAdhāb: Taste as the Purposed Instrument**

The clause of purpose seals the machinery with the Book's favorite eschatological verb: *li-yadhūqū al-ʿadhāb* — "so that they may *taste* the punishment": *dhāqa*, to taste — the Qur'an's selected apparatus for experience-not-news (the verb family running through dozens of verdicts — 4:57's own contrast arriving the very next verse at 44:56's "they shall not taste death therein beyond the first death"; 3:106's whitening-and-blackening faces; 8:50's "taste the punishment of the Burning") — and the choice of *tasting* is doctrinal, as al-Rāzī's page insists: punishment is not *information* but *felt* — the skin being replaced precisely *because* tasting holds it — the organs exchanged for nothing but renewal of the taste-circuit: the wisdom shown as education-in-reverse: *in the world, taste was the locus of choosing; on That Day taste becomes the locus of serving the sentence.*

**Inna Allāha Kāna ʿAzīzan Ḥakīmā: Might and Wisdom Above the Furnace**

The seal pairs its two attributes with the pericope's own specific geometry: *inna Allāha kāna ʿazīzan ḥakīman* — "God is Mighty, Wise": *ʿazīz* — the Invincible — answering the reader's involuntary wince (*can such power really?*): yes — ʿazīz — nothing stands between His decree and its skins; *ḥakīm* — the Wise — answering the theological recoil (is endlessness itself just?): yes — ḥakīm — His wisdom has calibrated eternity with the offense — and the commentators' note for the pairing is the sūrah's now-consistent doctrine: after every severity-clause the two attributes reappear (4:17, 26, 30's pattern of *ʿalīm ḥakīm* pairs) to keep terror from collapsing into arbitrariness and mercy from collapsing into permissiveness. With v. 56 the portion-trials find their furnace-door — and v. 57 immediately throws open the opposite garden-gates: the Two Abodes set facing one another (as is the Book's perpetual manner) — skin-taste answered by shade-cool by shade-taste; the reader suspended in between, still free to choose — *and that suspension is the only unsealed page in the entire register*.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:57

> **But for those who believe and perform righteous deeds, We shall cause them to enter Gardens with rivers running below, abiding therein forever. There they shall have spouses made pure, and We shall cause them to enter plenteous shade.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Wa Alladhīna Āmanū — the Door Swung Opposite**

Heaven's arithmetic of the furnace is answered in the Book's perpetual twin-habit with its garden-clause: *wa alladhīna āmanū wa ʿamilū al-ṣāliḥāti sanudkhiluhum jannātin tajrī min taḥtihā al-anhāru khālidīna fīhā abadā* — "and those who believe and work righteous deeds — We shall cause them to enter Gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever": the syntax deliberately mirrors the whole Qur'an's twin-engine (belief *and* works — the twin-condition that runs from the Fātiḥah's gate straight through every gate to every estate of the Hereafter — never one alone: cf. the countersignature at 2:25, 2:82, 4:122 below, 18:107, 25:70's repentance-exchange): deeds married to trust; trust proven by deeds. *Sanudkhiluhum* — We *cause them to enter* — the same first-person agency of v. 56 reversed for bliss (the commentators noting the courtesy-architecture: God Himself admits both cases, though to opposite addresses); *jannāt*, gardens, in the common plural (its stations exhaustive richly catalogued in the Tradition — Firdaws the highest; ʿAdn the Abode of residence; Naʿīm of Delight; Maʾwā of Refuge); *tajrī min taḥtihā al-anhār* — rivers running *beneath them* — the grade-bene the superlative courtesy-image of mastery (rivers *underneath* — their water-subjects, al-Ṭabarī style: not scenery to visit but estates to own — the hadith of the four rivers — 76:6–18's fountains named: Kafūr for God's own cupbearers, Salsabīl, Tasnīm for those brought near — Muslim 2830's with the famous river of al-Kawthar as the Prophet's own announced stream in the Garden, Muslim 400); *khālidīna fīhā abadā* — abiding forever — *combined* eternity-doublet (kh-l-d inside, abadan appended — the doublet for emphasis al-Zamakhsharī explains at such joins: *dwelling* mortgaged to *endlessness* — no lease, no move, no sunset-clause on bliss): everything the fire-quarters lacked — release-turnings, its *kullamā*-loop of skin-replacements — answered here by a *kullamā* of a different disposition (its counter its own loop-resident at 2:25: *every time they are provisioned therefrom and say: this is what we were provisioned before — and they are brought its like*).

**Lahum Fīhā Azwājun Muṭahharah: The Purified Consorts**

The next item upon the estate-list is the companionship-crown: *wa lahum fīhā azwājun muṭahharatun* — "therein they shall have purified spouses": *azwāj* — spouses, consorts — a word faithful to the Book's whole married theology (wherever the Garden is fully described the consorts attend — 2:25's *purified spouses*, 3:15's *purified spouses*, 4:57 here, and its decoration at 56:36–38's chamber-nymphs, 37:48–49's restrained-eyed companions, 55:56, 72–74's untouched ones) — and the adjective *muṭahharah* — purified — the ṭ-h-r root of cleanness, delivering the commentators into the delighted delicacy of their ritual-books: purified of every imperfection the world's companions could carry — of menses and childbirth-soilings (al-Qurṭubī's listing); of excretions and of secretions; of bad temper and wrangling; of envy, resentment, and the jarring of married-life the sūrah itself legislated against at vv. 19, 34–35, 128–130 — so that the adjective is at once *hygienic and characterological*: the sūrah's own household-crisis trios answered by a heaven where every shadow of home has been rinsed away. The Prophet's hadith already supplied the harmony-module corroborating the adjective (al-Bukhārī 3251; Muslim 2834 — from Abū Hurayrah's register of the believers' garden-architecture): *"their hearts shall be as the heart of one man; there is neither rancor nor hatred among them"* (al-Bukhārī 3249–50 and the parallel registers of Muslim) — one-heart companionship as the inside-matching of *muṭahharah*: spousal purity and communal single-heartedness both calibrated to the sūrah's recurrent dream — the Home perfected — with the sufi-readers' prism (al-Qushayrī's line of comment) seeing even the consorts' company as the whole heart's *transparency*, purified finally of the body's dividers — the veils of the old clay.

**Wa Nudkhiluhum Ẓillan Ẓalīlā: The Plenteous Shade — Closing of the Aridity**

The final item is a single doubled word: *wa nudkhiluhum ẓillan ẓalīlā* — "and We cause them to enter shade abundant": *ẓill*, shade; *ẓalīl*, its adjective-intensity — vast, spreading, plenteous (33 the tawālur the tradition glossing: a shade extending as far as the eye's range — extending forever — the report-classes expanding the shade-metaphors of the Garden into canopy-horses of the Tradition — the shade-tree of Ṭūbā beneath which a rider could ride a century without escaping its shade — the hadith-file of the Blessed Tree (Tirmidhī 3283 — with Ḥakīm's amplifications) standing nearest hand in the commentators' page) — the desert-born image chosen to crown the entire promise: *after the furnace, shade* — the Book's own closing arithmetic of the pericope — skin-fire replaced by skin-shade. And the received tradition (al-Ṭabarī, Ibn Kathīr) had always loved to fold v. 56–57's pair into its eschatology of *reciprocity*: beginnings reversed, *bodies* reversed, *consorts* reversed, *covers* reversed (skins consumed ↔ canopies spread): for the Garden even the air-side of architecture is mercy-climate: no sun-dart, no skin-burn — *a world built for dwelling* — khālidīna fīhā abadā — the fire-verse's nowhere answered by the garden-verse's everywhere — the pericope's twin-gates now both standing open in print — with the reader still poised in the unsealed middle: *choose; the admission-office answers to āmanū wa ʿamilū al-ṣāliḥāt alone.*

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:58

> **God commands you to return trusts to their rightful owners and, if you judge between men, to do so with justice. Excellent indeed is the instruction God gives you. Truly God is Hearing, Seeing.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Inna Allāha Yaʾmurukum an Tuʾaddū al-Amānāti ilā Ahlihā: The Great Mandate of Return**

The sūrah opens its celebrated authority-block (vv. 58–70) with the verse that became the charter-text of Islamic governance and ethics alike: *inna Allāha yaʾmurukum an tuʾaddū al-amānāti ilā ahlihā* — "God commands you to deliver trusts to their people": *amānah*, from the root of *amn* — security — the deposit that makes its keeper safe-guarded by conscience: the word's classical breadth spanning (1) *literal deposits* — goods, moneys, documents, borrowings, findings (al-Qurṛṭubī's jurists counting every species of custody: wadīʿah safekeeping, ʿāriyah borrowings, laqṭ findings, securities of every stamp; with the direct contrast the Book already drew at 3:75 — some People of the Book "if you trust them with a single dinar they will not return it" — dishonesty in trust being itself the marker of unfaith); (2) *offices and authorities* — the reading Ibn Kathīr and al-Ṭabarī's chains hold alongside (every delegated charge being an amānah toward its beneficiaries), and (3) *all religious obligations* — prayer, fast, the soul itself — Ibn Kathīr's note the shared gloss of the early masters: everything God charged man with is a trust, down to the tongues and bellies and organs of the body (36:65's hand-and-foot testimony corroborating). The revelation-occasion the historians never fail to retell — for it is the most beautiful *return* in Islam's annals — the conquest-day at the Kaʿbah (Bukhārī 2498 traceable register; al-Wāḥidī, al-Ṭabarī, and Ibn Kathīr's narrative weave): the Prophet took the sanctuary's key from ʿUthmān ibn Ṭalḥah — hereditary keeper by Quraysh-treaty; al-ʿAbbās, his uncle, standing ready with the petition for its transfer to the Hashimite line of custodianship; and the Prophet, opening his hand, handing back the key with the verse descending upon his hand: *"Deliver trusts to their people"* — returning custodianship to the family that had *earned* it by centuries of office — ʿUthmān accepting Islam upon the justice that reached him past the conqueror's own kin: the single deed that settled forever the law of Islam upon delegated offices: *merit and custodianship outrank nearness, even the Prophet's own family* — mercy and anti-nepotism sealed in one key.

**Wa Idhā Ḥakamtum Bayna al-Nāsi an Taḥkumū bi-l-ʿAdl: The Judicial Pair**

Directly upon the trust-command rides its brother: *wa idhā ḥakamtum bayna al-nāsi an taḥkumū bi-l-ʿadl* — "and when you judge between people, judge with justice": the conditional *idhā* — *when* — reads as normative whenever-adjudication (fiqh-books counting the verse among the foundations of qadāʾ-discipline — al-Qurṭubī's extended ruling-chapters flowing from it: competence preconditions, evidence-standards, even sentence-formality) — and *bi-l-ʿadl* — with equity — the mid-justice the Qur'an's favorite among its justice-words (its sister *qisṭ* — apportioned equity — running at 4:135 below and 5:42's domains) — the command's reach deliberately universalized by the commentators past judges to *every seat of decision*: parent over children, shepherd over flock, husband adjudicating wife-grievances, a man ruling upon *himself in his own weighing* (al-Qurṭubī's beautiful extension: each man is a judge between his outward and inward selves), with the corresponding hadith's terrors and joys both built upon the office (Muslim 1716, from the justice-triad traditions: *"the just shall be upon pulpits of light with God — those who are just in their judgments, their families, and whatsoever they are put in charge of"*) — and its counter-terror lodged in the disobedience-books as one of the seven shaded — standing in al-Bukhārī 680's roster — *"a just ruler"* — the first of the seven, because no human action spreads further into both worlds.

**Inna Allāha Niʿimmā Yaʿiẓukum Bih: The Excellent Counsel — and the Two Attributes Guarding It**

The verse's middle-seam — *inna Allāha niʿimmā yaʿiẓukum bih* — "excellent indeed is what God admonishes you with": the Book's own doxology inserted mid-command (*niʿimma* — how excellent! — the exclamatory form that stamps the instruction itself as grace, not burden — the same insert-habit as 16:90's *God commands justice and excellence...* — the twin-verse whose minbar-mandate echoes at every sermon of Islam — and 4:58's own standing sermon-right beside it in the preacher's libraries; the *yaʿiẓukum* — He admonishes you — making legislation itself pastoral: authority-law wrapped inside *ʿiẓah*, counsel — as though governance were admonishment before decree) — and the seal brings its two justice-attributes: *inna Allāha kāna samīʿan baṣīran* — "Hearing, Seeing": *samīʿ* — All-Hearing — interrogatories, oaths, depositions, whispers inside chambers: *baṣīr* — All-Seeing — the tilted scale that no camera catches, the trustee's private hand, the judge's private prejudice: the commentators across the register noting the deliberate doublet's guard-posts upon both halves of the verse: the Hearer of grievance-words stands behind the deposit-holder; the Seer of courtroom-gestures stands behind the magistrate — hence the generalization tradition-wide: the verse became, in caliphal-era edicts and mosque reading alike, *the* standing command-sentence of state-ethics (ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb's famous judicial instruction to Abū Mūsā ringing with it; and every khaṭīb's framing ever since) — whereby the authority-block opens: *power is a deposit; office is a custody; God watches the ledger through two attributes that no appeal-court can fool: the Ear and the Eye.*

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:59

> **O you who believe! Obey God and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you. And if you differ among yourselves concerning any matter, refer it to God and the Messenger, if you believe in God and the Last Day. That is better, and fairer in outcome.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Aṭīʿū Allāha wa Aṭīʿū al-Rasūla wa Ulī al-Amri Minkum: The Threefold Obedience Joined**

The authority-block's second verse mounts its tripod of command: *aṭīʿū Allāha wa aṭīʿū al-rasūla wa ulī al-amri minkum* — "obey God, and obey the Messenger, and those in authority among you": the grammar itself is the first exegetical lesson: for among the three imperatives the first verb is *repeated* before "the Messenger" but *not* repeated before "those in authority" (the third party being carried by the same verb-breath as the Messenger's — obedience below still linked, never free-standing) — al-Rāzī's celebrated point-from-syntax plus the tradition's ḥadīth ladder beside it: the saying of Ibn ʿUmar's chain in al-Bukhārī 2955 & 2957 and Muslim 1835 lodging the office-structure: *"whoever obeys the commander appointed by me has obeyed me, and whoever obeys me has obeyed God"* — the ascending stair of authority in Islam being always *derivation*, the sultan never sovereign by nature (the exact concept the Book engraved nine verses later at 4:80 — *"whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed God"*) — and the identity-file of *ulī al-amr* — "those of the command among you" — the classical discussions dividing their registers into several complementary seats: (1) *military commanders* appointed by the Prophet (the celebrated occasion in Ṭabarī, al-Wāḥidī, Ibn Kathīr: ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir granting amnesty over the head of commander Khālid ibn al-Walīd, dispute taken to the Prophet, the Prophet *upholding the amnesty but disciplining the bypass* — obedience to the chain; mercy of a soldier honored); (2) *the scholars* — al-Qurṭubī's school reading: those learned in Qur'an and Sunnah who transmit command-through-knowledge (the standing principle: scholars obeyed *as commissioned interpreters*, not as sources); (3) *the rulers* properly so-called — with ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib's decisive proviso, born within sight of v. 58: *only those who deliver the trusts and judge justly* — obedience being tethered to the discharge of the trust it obeys (the juristous condition running thence through the madhhabs' ethic of revolt (al-Ghazālī's third later manuals: no rebellion for worldly grievance alone, *yet* the Qur'anic ceiling never lifted: "no obedience to the created in disobedience to the Creator" — Aḥmad's register 1052, and Bukhārī 7257's "no obedience in a sin"). The tripod thus stands *calibrated*: God supreme; Messenger deputy; ulu'l-amr bounded by the first two — civil peace purchased without civil absolutism.

**Fa-In Tanāzaʿtum fī Shayʾin Fa-Ruddūhu ilā Allāhi wa-l-Rasūl: The Referral-Court of God and Messenger**

The disobedience-cap is immediately wrapped in the adjudication-clause — the verse's supreme legal-contribution: *fa-in tanāzaʿtum fī shayʾin fa-ruddūhu ilā Allāhi wa-l-rasūli in kuntum tuʾminūna bi-Allāhi wa-l-yawmi al-ākhir* — "and if you differ concerning anything, refer it to God and the Messenger — if you believe in God and the Last Day": *tanāzaʿtum* — dispute-withdrawing — contention as mutual withdrawal of assent; *ruddūhu* — *return it* — the same r-d-d root as v. 58's "deliver" — the jurisprudential correspondence deliberate (trusts *delivered back* to owners; disputes *returned back* to God and Messenger: authority-block delivering both account-types to their true owners); with the conditional — *if you believe* — making recourse itself the litmus of faith (foreshadowing v. 65's oath: *"they will not believe until they make thee judge..."*) — the madhhabs thereafter erecting upon the clause the entire architecture of *referral-sources*: Qur'an (God's speech), Sunnah (the Messenger's enacted will) — and upon their two referral organs the long discipline of ijtihād, qiyās, and derivation (al-Shāfiʿī's Bay his Risālah claiming our verse among Islam's uṣūl landmarks: every legal question answered in God-Messenger terms either directly or by inference — this being exactly al-Qurṭubī's cited reconciliation with v. 83's *referral to those in authority among them*: scholars' office exists only *within* God-Messenger bracketing).

**Dhālika Khayrun wa Aḥsanu Taʾwīlā: Better, Lovelier as Interpreted End**

The seal closes with the Book's own measuring of legal morality: *dhālika khayrun wa aḥsanu taʾwīlan* — "that is better and more beautiful in its issue": *khayr* — sheer goodness; *aḥsan taʾwīlan* — fairer in *what it returns to* (taʾwīl from āla/yaʾūlu — to return-come-home — the ending a thing returns to, hence *interpretation* as arriving at the matter's true home) — al-Rāzī's two-level observation being the tradition's permanent gem at this clause: God's referrals are better both *here* (social peace; clean adjudication; innocence secured) and *there* (outcome issue the *return* on That Day a fair home) — with the creed-condition folded into the clause itself (*if you believe in God and the Last Day*: eschatology underwriting jurisprudence — the subjected the subject's heart agreeing to be ruled by what judges beyond appeal) — and the verse thus delivers the ummah its civil constitution in one breath: hierarchical obedience reverse-flowing upon referral; offices legitimate only inside trust-delivery; disputes solvable only by returning to the sources; and the Last Day standing behind every arbitration-book as the audit wherein opinions all *come home* — *aḥsanu taʾwīlan* — loveliest of all destinations.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:60

> **Hast thou not seen those who claim that they believe in that which was sent down unto thee and in that which was sent down before thee, desiring to seek judgment from the ṭāghūt, although they were commanded not to believe in it? But Satan desires to lead them far astray.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Yazʿumūna Annahum Āmanū: Claim as Currency**

The authority-block, having built the tripod of obedience (v. 59 — God, Messenger, ulū al-amr), now surfaces its saboteurs under the Book's special gaze-command: *alam tara ilā alladhīna yazʿumūna annahum āmanū bi-mā unzila ilayka wa mā unzila min qablik* — "Hast thou not seen those who *claim* to believe in what was sent down to thee and in what was sent down before?": *yazʿumūna* — they claim — *zaʿm* being the Qur'an's chosen verb for assertions unweighed (its assembly-line of claimants running from the pagans' genealogy from their God-kinship claims at 37:150 to v. 62's upcoming oath-claims; al-Rāzī's note every time: *zaʿm* never certifies; it merely relays) — the class here disclosed being the Madinan *hypocrites* (munāfiqūn): outward confession, inward refusal — their asbāb-portrait the tradition preserves with a court-case made famous (al-Tirmidhī's transmission through al-Ḥasan's channel from Ibn ʿAbbās; al-Wāḥidī's and al-Ṭabarī's similar rolls): a dispute broke between *a believing Jew* — the litigant with a case too strong to lose — and *a hypocrite* among the ostensibly Muslim (the named cast varying among reports: Mughīrah Ḥuyayy-side a man of Banū al-Naḍīr's orbit the hypocrite in any register): the Jew demanded the Prophet's arbitration; the hypocrite steered toward the kāhin — the soothsayer of Juhaynah set up for such cases in Medina's pagan-adjacent milieu (Ibn Sayyād in one chain; a Jewish in another, a rabbinical tribune): the believer the dispute landed at the Prophet's gate, and heaven judged the epidemic: *for someone to profess the whole testimony-belief in *every* revelation — Torah, Gospel, and Muhammad's Book — and still bypass God's appointed tribunal for Satan's outpost (a soothsayer's tent! a clan-broker's palm-court!) — exposes the claim as currency of convenience only*.

**Yurīdūna an Yataḥākamū ilā al-Ṭāghūt: The Second Ṭāghūt within Nine Verses**

The desire-word indicts as soon as it is uttered: *yurīdūna an yataḥākamū ilā al-ṭāghūti wa qad umirū an yakfurū bih* — "they desire to seek judgment from the ṭāghūt, though they were commanded to disbelieve in it": *yataḥākamū ilā* — the litigant's reflexive — *to take their mutual case unto* — and the illative *wa qad* — *though they had been commanded* — making the betrayal of covenant the heel-fragile the covenant's very first term: *the receipt of revelation carries the explicit instruction to disbelieve in the ṭāghūt* (2:256's exact pairing — *"whoever disbelieves in the ṭāghūt and believes in God has grasped the firmest bond"* — with 16:36's identical cousin: *worship God and shun the ṭāghūt*) — and *ṭāghūt* here gathering all its accumulated load (from 4:51's idol-pair nine from 4:51 above its meaning-theaters: idols, soothsayers, sorcerers, satanic proxy-authorities, and — by the juristic extension that became Islam's constitutional vocabulary — *any authority that substitutes its own ordinance for God's* — the following piety-tradition making no mince: Imām Mālik's dictum style the maximaries the fuqahāʾ's named formula — *al-ḥukm bi-ghayri mā anzala Allāh* — ruling against what God sent down — seeking judgment elsewhere being *functional* worship of that elsewhere). ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb's famous definition-answer stands at the register's head: asked what the ṭāghūt was, he said (Tirmidhī-fre reported through the the register of his Companions' responses: "the ṭāghūt is the devil" — and, in the wording of his companions: *everything worshipped beside God* — judgments by other lights being its adjudicative mode).

**Wa Yurīdu al-Shayṭānu an Yuḍillahum Ḍalālan Baʿīdā: Distance as Satan's Aim**

The verse's third term discloses the true litigant behind the rival tribunals: *wa yurīdu al-shayṭānu an yuḍillahum ḍalālan baʿīdā* — "while Satan desires to lead them into a far misguidance": *ḍalālan baʿīdā* — astrayness *remote* — distance-adjective chosen on purpose (the commentators' question-note — why *far* answered in two registers: far *from God's law* — distance in standards; and far *from return* — distance in repentance, since each bypass of the Prophet's court digs the trench deeper: al-Rāzī's al-Rāzī's counsel here belongs to his finest psychology: a man may begin by outsourcing one quarrel to a soothsayer and end by building his whole faith upon counterfeit altars: ḍalāl *increases in its own direction*; and 4:119's Satan's self-confession later in this very sūrah — *"I will surely command them, and they will alter God's creation"* — standing behind the arbitration-abstacle: every alternative tribunal is Satan's *creed-workshop* — the slow replacement of judgment by counterfeit until the name is all that remains of the claim). The believer's safeguard against this drift is the very anchor the verse presupposes — *yakfurū bih*: to *disbelieve in* the ṭāghūt — unbelief, the Book's own paradox, as a positive required act (the sages' aphorism multiplying from this root: *faith's first pillar is refusals* — one rejects idols *into* God; so every court of appeal's legitimacy tests sound the same: *where does the decision come home to — God's ordinance, or the ṭāghūt's convenience?* — the boundary line not between ancient and modern tribunals but between judgment that fears God and judgment that serves appetite) — and the pericope's cinematic next its next frames (vv. 61–63) march the hypocrites through the remaining diagnostic: the invitation answered by turning away (v. 61), the misfortune met with oath-theater (v. 62), and heaven's triage — turn aside, admonish, and speak into their souls (v. 63): three stations of pastoral triage standing beneath one indictment — *the zaʿm-claim collapses upon the first tribunal-choice.*

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:61

> **And when it is said unto them, "Come to what God has sent down and to the Messenger," thou seest the hypocrites turn away from thee with aversion.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Wa Idhā Qīla Lahum Taʿālaw: The Simple Invitation**

The diagnostic of the pretender-class proceeds to its simplest test — the open invitation: *wa idhā qīla lahum taʿālaw ilā mā anzala Allāhu wa ilā al-rasūl* — "and when it is said unto them: Come — to what God has sent down, and to the Messenger!": *taʿālaw* — the summoning imperative, from *ʿalā* — to rise to — *come up unto* — the verb carrying itself the dignity of the destination (the invitations of the Book are always an ascent — to prayer, to the war, to God) — and its contents states states the twofold referral in shortened form: God's sending-down (the text) and His Messenger (the living instance and judge) — the protocol of v. 59's *ruddūhu ilā Allāhi wa-l-rasūl* here field-tested: nothing more complicated is asked of the claimants than to walk up and stand before the revealed ordinance and its bearer. Al-Qurṭubī's jurisprudence finds in the clause itself the ummah's permanent court-summons value — the simple call being all that is ever due as the measure: the Prophet needed no procedural no procedural bodywork — a *come to God and the Messenger* sufficed to flush every counterfeit: and the lawyers noted for all later history the value of refusing the *simple* call: one may wrangle over complicated bills, but to be called *to the Book and the man* — and to turn — is a deed that no apologetics can re-texture: *evasion itself arraigns*.

**Raʾayta al-Munāfiqīna: The Witnessing-Seal of Hypocrisy**

The scene's proof arrives as sight endorsed to the Prophet: *raʾayta al-munāfiqīna yaṣuddūna ʿanka ṣudūdan* — "thou seest the hypocrites turning away from thee — a turning": three chairs in one clause: (1) *raʾayta* — *thou sawest* — hypocrisy passing from suspicion into witnessed conduct (its definition passing thereby from interior-state to track-record: the Prophet is not authorized is authorized to *see* it by what his eyes verify — the classical scholars' standing caution: only conduct condemns, no heart-guesswork admits an accusation to stand — with the hadith-sieve of ʿUmar's famous quandary: only God knows hearts, but *behavior is ours to judge*); (2) *al-munāfiqīna* — the hypocrites — the noun now named openly, extracted from n-f-q — the gerbil's the rodent's two-doored burrow (nāfiqāʾ: the tunnel with two exits — the desert-weasel that keeps an alternate door — the perfect organic emblem of the double-exit religion) — with the whole Surah al-Munāfiqūn (63) ahead as their full portrait-book; (3) *yaṣuddūna ʿanka ṣudūdan* — turning away from thee *a turning*: the cognate-accusative amplifying into spectacle — their turn is noted their turn is a full, flagrant, total turning (the verbal-noun doubling in Arabic for stamped excellence-of-act: the turning is *thorough*: no half-shoulder, no excused absence: the whole back). Ibn Kathīr's register at the clause records the two practical lessons the salaf drew: (a) that fidelity is *measured by response to the summons*, not by presence at sermons, so the believer's daily audit is likewise *the speed of his coming*; and (b) that the Prophet (and by extension every daʿwah-voice) was told to *watch conduct* — not to blast hearts with verdicts — pastoral method guarded by heaven itself — the cosmos-eyes the eye of the Prophet acting as the ummah's own audit-lens, the seen avoided, the unseen left to God.

**The Two Invitations and One Response**

The pericope thus builds its double-portrait of the trial that never fails (v. 60: they *desire* ṭāghūt-arbitration; v. 61: they *turn from* God-and-Messenger's invitation): the same two verbs pulled into exact opposition: *yurīdūna* — they wish — versus *yaṣuddūna* — they turn — willing and walking agreeing with each other against their claim (the claim of *īmān*) — and the sages' summary their summary-dictum that became classic precisely from this pair: *whoever claims discipleship yet shuns the *taʿālaw* of God and His Messenger tests as a munāfiq by the very test his own feet administer* — while the in the corresponding teaching on the *Messenger's* side completing the symmetry just below (4:64's *"We sent no messenger save to be obeyed by God's leave"* — the office's warrant making the community's walk the measure) — so that vv. 60–61 are the sūrah's mirrored doors: hypocrite-behavior on one side, prophet-authority on the other, and between them the standing referral — *to God and the Messenger* — upon which the next verse puts the hypocrites' Last-Day oath-theater (v. 62), upon which the verse after that dispatches the pastoral triage (v. 63): turn aside, admonish, speak the word that pierces their souls — *for the Prophet is judge of conduct, God of hearts, and the sign stands static at the gate: come up — to the sending-down and to the Messenger.*

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:62

> **Then how will it be when calamity befalls them for what their own hands have sent forward, and they come to thee swearing by God, "We meant naught but virtue and harmony"?**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Muṣībatun Bi-mā Qaddamat Aydīhim: Calamity as the Follow-Up Bill**

The verse opens with the Book's cinematic asking again — *fa-kayfa idhā aṣābathum muṣībatun bi-mā qaddamat aydīhim* — "how then shall it be, when a calamity befalls them for what their own hands have forwarded?": *fa-kayfa* — *and how!* — the same how-horror frame of 4:41 (its scene-projection power: the reader made to face the future-scene before it can be prepared); *muṣībah* — calamity — from *ṣ-w-b*, a striking that lands on its mark — and the causative formula *bi-mā qaddamat aydīhim* — *for what their hands sent forward* — rehearsal of Islam's plain account-theology (42:30 — "whatever strikes you of calamity — it is by what your own hands earned; and He pardons much"; together with the paired warnings at 2:195's "spend in the way of God and cast not yourselves by your own hands into destruction" and the broader engine-verse of earthly causality at 13:11 — *God changes not a people's state until they change what is in themselves*): every misfortune that overtakes such claimants is heaven-posted — its postage printed *on the hand* — not randomly assigned, not unjustly mailed. The commentators' reports of its first fabric: the calamity the two disputants of v. 60 invited by their ṭāghūt-tribunal (al-Qurṛṭubī and Ibn Kathīr recounting that in the hypocrite's case the sent-forward deeds were the double-act itself — false piety by day, private mockeries of the Prophet's judgment-benches by night — with the *muṣībah* then arriving either as exposure at Madinah (the turning-back of v. 61 made public) or — in the commentators' wider frame — as the reverses through which God kept testing their masks (al-Wāḥidī's broader chain reading the affliction as any trial that uncovers the ṭāghūt-petitioner's true balance).

**Thumma Jāʾūka Yuḥlifūna bi-Allāh: Oaths in Allah's Own Name Built Upon Rubble**

Then the theater-response that heaven strips with one clause: *thumma jāʾūka yuḥlifūna bi-Allāh in aradnā illā iḥsānan wa tawfīqā* — "then they come to thee, swearing by God: We intended naught but virtue and harmony": the oath-in-Allah's-name — *yuḥlifūna bi-Allāh* — the ultimate legal tender of the oaths-market, spent upon the counterfeit merchandise of *niYYah-claims*: "we meant only iḥsān and tawfīq" — iḥsān, redemptive good; tawfīq, concord — heaven quoting their own self-insurance vocabulary (the word-doublet iḥsān/tawfīq chosen deliberately as the two big piety-flags of sūrah of the sūrah's own vocabulary — iḥsān back at vv. 36's conduct-compass; tawfīq at v. 35's arbitration-success — counterfeiters always borrowing the true mint's paper) — and the commentators' asbāb-rolls (Ibn ʿAbbās's chain through Mujāhid and al-Ḥasan in al-Wāḥidī and al-Ṭabarī) record its office-context with telling fineness: the hypocrite litigant and his fellows — caught between the Qur'an's condemning verse and the Muslims' knowing looks — came *early-morning to the Prophet* rehearsing their salve-oaths: "We sought no quarrel with the Believers; we only went to the soothsayer for iḥsān and conciliation" — the form thereafter etched into the literature of fake repentance: *good-feelings speech covering bad conduct* (the tradition's categories classifying such excusal as *muḍārabah* — diplomatic trim — among the nifāq-marks the Prophet's own short-creed listed (Bukhārī 33, Muslim 59 — *"the signs of the hypocrite are three: when he speaks he lies; when he promises he breaks; when he receives a trust he betrays."*)

**The Soul-Audit's Bottom Line Within the Calamity**

The pastoral and theological latitude of the clause runs several streets at once for every generation: (1) *oaths certify nothing beyond oaths* — God's name can be rented by unbelievers; the practical jurisprudence of Islam thereafter never admitting oath-denial alone as discharge of evidence — the fiqh the courtroom traditions weighting conduct, prior record, and circumstance — oath being the gate-pillar but never the whole bridge (cf. the Prophet's teaching that the sworn perjured claimant may discharge his guilt in the court while the truthful unsworn party stands convicted by it — the standing warning of al-Bukhārī's Kitāb al-Aymān, nos. 2510, 2680); (2) *intentions are audited by heaven independently of invocations* — they may lie even in the syllable iḥsān; the doctrine of niyyah remains the believer's own interior court, as the founding hadith stands forever (Bukhārī 1 — *actions are by intentions*) — so a false iḥsān-claim is not good-intentionedness but *added perjury*; and (3) *disaster is God's diagnostic-exposure instrument*: the sages summarized: tribulations scatter masks before hearts — al-Rāzī's phrasing of this verse among his most arresting — calamity unveiling the claim's base-metals, and *God in His mercy sometimes withholding calamity* (deferred to the Hereafter) and sometimes sending it (exposure now means repentance still possible): the believer is trained therefore to meet his own misfortunes in the inverse manner of the perjurer — first with confession of what his hands forwarded, then with repentance, never with the oath-theater of clean-hands denial; for the calamity of the false swearer by God's name is the very largest class of forward-sending (cf. al-Bukhārī 6546 — the *ghamūs*, immersing oaths that sink their holders into the Fire) — and the Prophet here is left by heaven awaiting the next verse's pastoral triage: God knows their hearts — so *you* stand clear, warn without rancor, and speak the depth-word that might yet save them.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:63

> **They are those of whom God knows what is in their hearts. So turn away from them, admonish them, and speak to them a word that reaches to their souls.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Ulāʾika Alladhīna Yaʿlamu Allāhu Mā fī Qulūbihim: The Formal Transfer of the Heart-Files**

Against all the oath-theater heaven now moves its own judge's gavel: *ulāʾika alladhīna yaʿlamu Allāhu mā fī qulūbihim* — "those are they of whom God knows what is in their hearts": *ulāʾika* — the remote demonstrative again (the far-pointing of set-and-settled cases, as at 4:52's *"those are they whom God cursed"*) — and the clause form itself one of Islam's most consequential: God *knows* — the whole thing ending there, as the doctors of the tradition noted: where mere human authority must seek further proof, God's file closes at *yaʿlamu* — knowledge itself being verdict enough for the One who is both Witness and Judge (its duplicates as bolts closing a door: cf. 3:119's "God knows what is in the breasts", 5:7's "God knows what the breasts conceal", 50:16's "We know what his soul whispers", and — territorially closest — 9:47's "God knows the liars") — al-Rāzī's note on the formulation emphasizing additionally the brutal exactitude of the grammars: knowledge attaches itself to *mā fī qulūbihim* — what IS in their hearts — present-continuative: the ongoing pump the ongoing counterfeit-mechanism still running beneath the oath-syllables — so the clause is not merely retrospective (God *recorded* their lie) but live (God *sees* their inner file still updating now).

**Fa-Aʿriḍ ʿAnhum: The Turning-Away — Dismissal, Not Neglect**

Then three pastoral verbs delivered to the Prophet in sequence — and the tradition has always treasured their order (the school of balāghah rhapsodizing on the sequence as gradation of mercy): the first is *fa-aʿriḍ ʿanhum* — "so turn away from them": ʿ-r-ḍ, to turn aside from — the counsel of dignified *procedural* dismissal: close the case-by-case wrangling; do not sit at the ear of their oaths-market; withdraw the privilege of your adjudicative attention (Ibn Kathīr's register: neither punishment nor expulsion — a *with-holding of engagement* sanctioned by heaven — the same posture the Prophet was commanded respecting the obstinate elsewhere: 5:42's "if they come to thee, judge between them or turn aside"; 68:44's "leave Me and those who cry lies"; 73:10's "bear patiently what they say, and part from them graciously — *hijran jamīlan*") — teaching thereafter every believer in the saboteur's path: *disengagement is the first pastoral act* — not every court not every debate need be attended; some quarrels are fed by reply — the Book's own *ʿirāḍ* doctrine later matured into the Prophet's standing teaching at Muslim 57 and Bukhārī 6018: *"let him speak good or keep silent"* — the believer's withdrawal from the liar-circuit being itself course one of daʿwah-ethics.

**Wa-ʿIẓhum wa Qul Lahum fī Anfusihim Qawlan Balīghan: Admonition and the Depth-Word**

The second and third verbs ascend where the first withdraws: *wa-ʿiẓhum* — "and admonish them": w-ʿ-ẓ — the composite counsel-word (already met at 4:34's first nushūz-step *ʿiẓūhunna*) — heart-channeling of knowledge toward reform: not information-only but *admonition* — knowledge aimed at the will (the sages' definition of waʿẓ: *an exhortation that softens the heart toward obedience* — al-Zamakhsharī's elegant gloss: it is counsel *with a warning-element and a promise-element fused*) — and *wa qul lahum fī anfusihim qawlan balīghan* — "and speak to them, touching their souls, a word that reaches": *fī anfusihim* — *into their selves/souls* — the talking aimed not at their ears but their *insides* — debated philologically the two classic grammatical readings al-Ṭabarī weighs: either *their* souls (speak into their interiors) or *thy* soul (speak from the depth of thine own self into theirs — the authentic voice-union — chiefly the majority favoring *their*, with the second reading furnishing the pastor's own posture) — and *qawlan balīghan* — a *far-reaching*, *penetrating* word — from b-l-g, to arrive at destination: the word perfected of its conveyance — hitting the target of the heart (a phrase that entered Arabic rhetoric permanently as the title-word of eloquence-teaching itself — *balāghah*, the science of arriving, taking its name-flag from this single concatenation — with al-Jāḥiẓ's tradition remembering that the Prophet's own speech was its definition — *jawāmiʿ al-kalim* — the comprehensive few-words that arrive where many-words cannot) — the triage thereby complete: *withdrawal* (from their theater), *admonition* (through their ears), *soul-word* (into their interior) — in ascending degrees of directness: estranged from the performance, but not abandoning the souls — heaven never permitting its Prophet to write off the audience's heart as unreachable, since the education of the soul is the daʿwah's last task: *turn away from their poison; prescribe their cure.*

**The House-Teacher's Whole Syllabus in One Verse**

The pericope's architecture reveals itself at last as the sūrah's textbook of pastor-and-judge psychology: v. 60 diagnoses (claims scale claims contrasted with tribunal-choice), v. 61 witnesses (the invitation and the turning), v. 62 strips the excuse (calamity → oath-theater), v. 63 transfers the heart-file and ordains the response: *turn away, admonish, speak into the soul* — and the entire pedagogic pattern has ever since governed how Muslims address the pious-dissembling class: no heart-assassinations (only God audits), no rubber-stamping of oaths (only conduct verifies), and no despair of hearts either (the depth-word still possible) — with the counter-case standing across in the purest of the Prophet's own records to show the road home: the men of the Aws-Khazraj who at Uḥud's eve wavered like the hypocrites and then *repented* — their names entering later the roster of the people of the Garden — hypocrisy in the Book being always a *present-tense* condition, never a species: *mā fī qulūbihim* can still change — and until it does, the believer's standing orders at the gate of the double-speakers remain the three verbs alone: *aʿriḍ — iʿiẓ — wa qul qawlan balīghan.*

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:64

> **We sent no messenger, save that he should be obeyed by God's Leave. If, when they had wronged themselves, they had but come to thee and sought forgiveness of God, and the Messenger had sought forgiveness for them, they would surely have found God Relenting, Merciful.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Wa Mā Arsalnā min Rasūlin illā Li-Yuṭāʿa bi-Idhni Allāh: Prophets Sent for Obedience Alone**

The pericope now plants the warrant beneath the whole tribunal-obligation: *wa mā arsalnā min rasūlin illā li-yuṭāʿa bi-idhni Allāh* — "We sent no messenger except to be obeyed, by God's leave": the absolute *mā... illā* — *none... except* — universalizing the commission across the prophetic corps (the commentators' broad note: from the earliest warner to the Seal — each one dispatched *for obedience*, his authority never private property but God's franchise — *bi-idhni Allāh*, by God's leave) — and the two classical readings the kalām-masters developed on the clause are both permanently indexed to our verse: (1) the Muʿtazilite emphasis — God *wills the messengers be obeyed by all*; none is ever misguided *by divine intent against them* — the verse proving heaven's goodwill toward every audience (their reading setting it alongside the hadith-famous their distinctive defense of human choice); and (2) the Ashʿarite reading — al-Rāzī's own celebrated use: *bi-idhni Allāh* — by God's leave — is the operative governor — obedience and disobedience alike occur within His encompassing decree, none slipping past His idhn — so the very warrant itself equals proof of the Sovereignty-of-leave (the school fight here being over who authors the *walking*, never over whose command the messengers carry — both houses agreeing on the latter absolutely) — the pastoral yield of the clause outlasting the school-grammar: in every age God's appointed guidance is *obediently receivable*; the bypass of the Prophet's court (v. 60's ṭāghūt-litigants) thereby stands measured against the whole architecture: to skirt *this* Messenger is to skirt the universal covenant of messenger-ship itself.

**Wa Law Annahum Idh Ẓalamū Anfusahum: The Counterfactual of the Door Left Open**

Then comes the verse that the entire tradition has treasured as the charter of prophetic intercession for sinners: *wa law annahum idh ẓalamū anfusahum jāʾūka fa-istaghfarū Allāha wa-staghfara lahumu al-rasūlu la-wajadū Allāha tawwāban raḥīman* — "and if, when they wronged themselves, they had but come to thee, sought God's forgiveness, and the Messenger sought forgiveness for them — they would have found God Relenting, Merciful": the *law* — *had they...* — a counterfactual of yearning (the same tender subjunctive-conditional the Book uses when holding open roads not taken: the door not closed even to the ṭāghūt-litigants — had they come, forgiveness *would have* issued — ṭab heaven lamenting the missed appointment, not celebrating their loss) — and the triple choreography of the scene: the wrongers *come to the Prophet* (admission of guilt at the living court); the wrongers *seek God's forgiveness* (their own istighfār — direct address to God); and then *the Messenger seeks forgiveness for them* (his ku his intercession completing the double-appeal of the weak party by himself and by the sanctioned patron) — find with the verdict certain: *la-wajadū* — they would surely have found — tawwāb, the Ever-Returner — raḥīm, Ever-Merciful. The doctrine sequenced here is the ummah's standing istighfār-triangle: person to Prophet, person to God, Prophet for person — with the reverse-side gospel preserved in its sister-cases the commentators always line up beside it (9:80 — "seek forgiveness for them or seek it not — if you seek seventy times God will not forgive them"; 63:6 — "it is alike for them whether you seek forgiveness or not"; 9:113 — "it is not for the Prophet and the believers to seek forgiveness for the polytheists, even if near of kin" — the intercession conditional upon the *repentant approach* itself, never a limitless blank check) — so that al-Rāzī's capsule stands: *the Prophet's prayers open only the doors the runners themselves run to.*

**The Station at His Grave and the Verse's Living Afterlife**

Upon our verse stands one of the most cherished devotional practices and theological conversations of Islam at once. The famous accounts in the transmitted registers (the maghāzī and āthār channels, with Ibn Kathīr's citation through Ibn ʿAsākir's chains) preserve the community's memory of this verse at work: the well-known story-report, transmitted through Mālik al-Dār's anecdote, tells of a needy man coming to the Prophet's grave in Madinah and praying the clause's own formula: "My Lord, I have wronged myself; You said: *if they came to thee and sought forgiveness...* — so I have come to Thy Prophet" — and receiving the answer in a dream: *forgiven*. The report's chains have been graded and criticized in the technical books, yet it is beloved of the devotional community, serving ever since as the verse's living pronunciation-guide: the dead Prophet in the believers' heart never exited his intercessory office (its law underwritten by the authentic the authentic proclamation of the Prophet's ongoing life in his grave — Muslim's reports of the prophets greeting each other alive in the night-journey, Muslim 237, and Bukhārī's multiple prophetic-life attestations) — with the scholarly boundary-lines the doctors guarded at equal strength: the verse's *coming* remains the sinner's own motion, its *istighfār* his own lips, its Messenger-intercession God's own gift of agency — not magical proximity but covenant fidelity — tawwāban raḥīman sealing the door as always-open *only to the seeker* — and the last word the Book leaves lying at the perjurer's feet being precisely this verse's kindness: *had they but come... they would have found* — the pericope's oath-theater answered not by a stake but by a road-sign — a road that every reader this day may still walk.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:65

> **But no, by thy Lord, they will not believe until they have made thee the judge between them in their disputes, and find no resistance in their souls to what thou hast decreed, and surrender with full submission.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Fa-Lā wa Rabbika Lā Yuʾminūna: The Oath Denying the Claim**

At the threshold of the verse heaven does what it does what it does in rare and heart-stopping solemnity — an oath by *the Prophet's own Lord*, sworn upon a negation of claims: *fa-lā wa rabbika lā yuʾminūna* — "nay, by thy Lord — they do not believe!": *fa-lā wa rabbika* — nay — by thy Lord! — the oath-formula addressing *Muhammad* in God's own mouth — an honor-grammar without peer (al-Rāzī's note trembling at it: God swearing *by* Himself but invoking the *kinship-of-lordship* — "thy Lord" — coupling His name to His Prophet's name in a single possessive phrase — the commentators never tired of noting the honor embedded in the form: sworn-truth addressed to no one else in quite this directed diction); and the negative absolute *lā yuʾminūna* — *they do not believe* — delivering the sharpest possible creed-vet creed-verdict upon the tribunal-bypassers of vv. 60–63: professed, pulpit-sitting, congregation-standing Muslims whose *īmān* heaven here flatly refuses until three conditions complete. The verse thereby builds for Islam its its belief*-conditions hierarchy: verbal confession is insufficient without this tripartite act — the tradition citing at its head the Prophet's own operational triad upon exactly this standard (al-Bukhārī 15; Muslim 43 — from Anas: *"None of you believes until I am dearer to him than his father, his child, and all mankind"* — love as the believer's true warrant, and 4:65 giving its *legal substrate*: acceptance of the Prophet's arbitration).

**Ḥattā Yuḥakkimūka fīmā Shajara Baynahum: The First Condition — Referral**

Condition one: *ḥatta yuḥakkimūka fīmā shajara baynahum* — "until they make thee judge in what branches out between them": *yuḥakkimū* — installing him *ḥakam* — judgment-maker; *shajara* — from the same sh-j-r of branches and trees — the dispute being *what grows entangled* (the beautiful root-image the philologists cleanse prize: disagreement as branches *overlapping into one another* — the case knotted — made for a judge to trim) — and the asbāb-occasion the tradition hands over with the verse's name written upon a water-course (al-Ṭabarī, al-Wāḥidī, and Ibn Kathīr's register): al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām and an Anṣārī neighbor of Banū Umayyah's palm-water line the two quarreling over the dividing of an irrigation rill from the shared highland flow; the Prophet ruled: *"irrigate first, O Zubayr, then send the water to your neighbor"* — a rule favoring the cousin — and the Anṣārī, stung, said: *"Because he is your aunt's son?"* — the side-remark heaven answered with our oath-verse — the Prophet's face darkening so the watery worldly so the public remembered the day as one of Islam's creed-crises: even a good, wronged-wrongless even a lawful cause is lost by grudging against the Messenger's gavel (the school-exegetes taking the occasion as secondary-probation secondary but illustrative: the verse's creed-logic stands universal — thus al-Ṭabarī's superscription of it over all rulings-refusals anywhere).

**Thumma Lā Yajidū fī Anfusihim Ḥarajan Mimmā Qaḍayta: The Second Condition — Interior Clearance**

Condition two — the hardest ever set for any court-order: *thumma lā yajidū fī anfusihim ḥarajan mimmā qaḍayta* — "then they find in their souls no tightness at what thou hast decreed": *ḥaraj* — constriction — the same word of breast-anguish the Book deploys against every inward resistance (6:125 — "He makes his breast tight (ḥarajan ḍayyiqan) as though climbing into the sky"; 33:36's exact sister — "it is not for a believing man or woman — when God and His Messenger have decided a matter — to have any choice in their affair") — the condition carrying belief *past compliance into interiority*: the disputant must receive the ruling *without chest-squeezing* — the tradition's saints commenting with memorable directness: outward bowing is servitude forced; the believer's distinct sign is *broad-chestedness under decree* (the hadith-testimony of its rarity and glory: Bukhārī 21 — *"the whole ummah will enter the Garden save those who refuse — What is refusal, Messenger of God Whoever obeys me will enter the Garden, and whoever refuses me has refused"*) — while al-Rāzī's theology raises the clause into the definition-of-faith debates: *ruling-acceptance without soul-tightness is the Qur'an's own operationalization of īmān* — head, heart, and chest all voting one way — the comparison with 33:36 sealing the sum total in every Muslim jurist's ethical canon thereafter: *no belief whatever until God's and His Messenger's decrees beat upon empty upon open rooms within.*

**Wa Yusallimū Taslīmān: The Third Condition — Total Handover**

Condition three — the cognate-accusative of completion: *wa yusallimū taslīman* — "and they surrender with full surrender": *yusallimū* — from the s-l-m of Islam itself — hand-over, consign; *taslīman* — the verbal noun — absolutely, unreservedly: the tree the triad then standing as Islam's hierarchical its creed-architecture before the ancient before every dispute-machine of history: referral (the case *goes* to the Prophet), interior release (the chest *opens* beneath the verdict), full consignment (the self *ignores executes* hand-over) — with the sufi-grammar finding all three stages telescoped forever into the single word *islām* — submission as end-station of arbitration (the early saying-books preserve ʿAlī's distilled gloss: *submission is Islam's *the nub the core the soul of Islam is þed the delivering-up of the outcome to the Prophet's decrees*) — and the pastoral-moral yield of 4:65 has ever since rung in the mufti's, husband's, and qāḍī's ears alike: *any* grudge against any established judgment of the Messenger's Sunnah is nothing less than a creed-issue — the believer's daily practice meaning being the folding of his preferences beneath the delivered rule — chest at ease, face at peace, step in obedience — until *taslīm* becomes instinct, and the proof of the profession stands not upon his statements but upon his comportment beneath the verdict: *by thy Lord — they believe not, until.*

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:66

> **And had We prescribed for them, "Lay down your lives" or "Leave your homes," they would not have done so, save a few. And had they done what they were exhorted to do, it would have been better for them, and a stronger confirmation.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Wa Law Annā Katabnā ʿAlayhim Ani Uqtulū Anfusakum: The Test-Command That Was Never Given**

The verdict of v. 65 (no belief until the triple submission) deepens into a staggering counterfactual: *wa law annā katabnā ʿalayhim ani uqtulū anfusakum awi ukhrujū min diyārikum mā faʿalūhu illā qalīlun minhum* — "and had We prescribed for them — lay down your lives, or leave your homes — they would not have done so, save a few": *katabnā ʿalayhim* — written upon them — the covenant-verb of imposed ordinance; and then two ancient test-phrases in the imperative plural: *uqtulū anfusakum* — slay yourselves — the exact commanded form the Book *has* employed before upon a covenant-holders' mass — at 2:54, Moses to his people after the golden calf: *"your Maker has commanded you: slay yourselves"* — a command taken by the Muslim doctors as *mortification of the corrupt self* as much as corporal death — with the second clause *awi ukhrujū min diyārikum* — *or leave your homes* — the exodus-command borne by every prophet-emigration in history (Abraham's, Lot's, Moses's, and — freshest — the Muslims' own hijrah: the willing emptying of Mecca that built Madinah, its cost audited its cost forever printed into the names of the *Muhājirūn* who rose past it: "[they] were driven from their homes and their wealth for the bounty of God" — 2:189 59:8) — the verse's premise thus: *the easy commands at hand — the referral of v. 65 — are nothing alongside what has historically been demanded of God's covenant-people*; and its verdict: the waverers *would not have answered even then*, save a few. Al-Ṭabarī's collection record at the clause traces its the the exegetical twofold: it may be spoken against the hypocrite-class of vv. 60–63 (the two defaulting-litigants and their circle — no hides on the no hides upon the war-commands either, and little stomach for emigrations) or, by the early by the reading toward the earlier scripture-holders of Madinah: the nation whose ancestors were actually commanded both — self-slaying and exodus — and answered in body but not in heart — the counterfactual hanging on both communities' failed files.

**Illā Qalīlun Minhum: The Excepted Few as Standing Law**

The exception riding at the clause's tail — *illā qalīlun minhum* — "save a few of them" — entered the tradition as a doctrine-principle in its own right: in every mass-human test of history, the covenant-answers come through *al-qalīl* — the few (the Book's constant apportioning: 38:24 — "few are they" for those who believe with righteousness; 7:17 — "most of them are not thankful"; 12:103 — "most people, though you desire, are not believers"; 2:246's "when fighting was written upon them they turned back except a few" — the Saul-Talūt narrative it now recalls pat clearly; and 4:46's own earlier *illā qalīlā* — save a few of the portion-bearers who would believe) — al-Rāzī's spiritual-note awaiting attesting the takeaway: the believer never measures truth by headcounts — God's tests always filter the mass down to a band — the "few" functioning across Islamic history as the believers' comfort at every outnumbered hour (the early ummah itself a few against the might of empires — Badr's 313 the standing emblem, 8:9's thousand-angel assist attached; and the Prophet's famous proclamation lending the "few" their future-encouragement for the strange days:

> *"Islam began as something strange, and it shall return to being strange as it began — so give glad tidings to the strangers." They said: Who are the strangers? He said: Those who reform what the people corrupt of my Sunnah.* (Muslim 145; al-Tirmidhī 2629 & 2630 — with his cousin-register)

— the ghurabāʾ-blessing being this verse's own *illā qalīlun* translated into prophecy.

**Wa Law Annahum Faʿalū Mā Yūʿaẓūna Bih: The Better Course They Declined**

The verse's tail swings from counterfactual-refusal to counterfactual-mercy: *wa law annahum faʿalū mā yūʿaẓūna bihi la-kāna khayran lahum wa ashadda tathbītā* — "yet had they done what they were exhorted, it would have been better for them and stronger in establishment": *yūʿaẓūna bihi* — what they are admonished with — pointing back down the pericope to the whole waʿẓ-syllabus (referral to God and Messenger — v. 59; stopping at the summons — v. 61; triple submission — v. 65): had they taken it, two yields stand certified by heaven itself: (1) *khayran lahum* — *better for them* — the undifferent bo absolute goodness spanning worlds (the doctors' division: world's peace now — requited reconciliation Hereafter) and (2) *ashadda tathbītā* — *stronger in confirmation/firmness* — *tathbīt* — from th-b-t, to stand fast — the word whose cognate grammar appears next at v. 68, its standing at the battle-blessings: 3:147's "firm our feet and help us", 8:11's angelic fastening upon Badr's morning ("to make firm therewith your feet"), and 14:27's 14:27 — *"God keeps firm the believers with the firm word in the world's life and in the Hereafter"* — obedience *itself* being read by the clause as the great foot-firmer of faith — not merely morality but *stability-technology*: with each answering of God's call the believer's footing deepens, and with each avoidance it loosens — the whole economics of wavering hearts here reduced to one law of heaven: *advice unenacted becomes disenchantment; advice performed becomes bedrock* — khayran lahum wa ashadda tathbītā — the pericope thereby carrying from the oath-theater of vv. 60–63 to its first loud call of hope: even now — despite the verdict — the admonished road stands open, its two payments still offered: *betterment in this world & the next, firmness in everything in between.*

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:67

> **Then We would surely have granted them, from Our Presence, a great reward,**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Wa Idhan la-Ātaynāhum min Ladunnā Ajran ʿAẓīmā: The Crossways of the Conditional**

The tiniest verse of the pericope — one dependent clause — yet it hangs upon the whole balance of vv. 66–68 as the first of the three then-payments: *wa idhan la-ātaynāhum min ladunnā ajran ʿaẓīmā* — "then would We surely have granted them, from Our Presence, a mighty reward": *wa idhan* — *then, at that* — the apodosis-marker of the entire conditional structure launched in v. 66 ("had they done what they were admonished... then We *would surely have*..."): grammar itself thus carrying the theology — the *la*-of-certainty (*la-ātaynāhum* — We surely would have given) answering the *law* of hypothetical obedience — the mutual-conditions heaven's fidelity being thereby prototyped into its syntax: *if the stride is taken by man, the response is signed by God* — never vice-versa (the sunnah-order everywhere in the Book: 5:9's "God promised"; 24:55's succession-promise; and the classical ḥadīth qudsī which the tradition placed at the pericope's threshold: Bukhārī 7405 & Muslim 2675 — *"I am as My servant thinks of Me; when he remembers Me I am with him... and if he draws near to Me a span I draw near to him a cubit, and if he draws near a cubit I draw near him an arm's length, and if he comes to Me walking I come to him running"* — hurrying down the conditional's own rush into mercy).

**Min Ladunnā: The Ladunnī Signature of the Reward**

Within the clause sits the preposition the tradition has always marked with a bright pin: *min ladunnā* — *from Our own Presence*: the l-d-n adjacency-word — *from beside Us, from Our immediate nearness* — which the Book's readers of reward-theology met already at v. 40 of this very sūrah (the *ajran ʿaẓīman min ladunhu* of its pristine multiplytude its clause there: a good deed multiplied, *then* a great reward *from His Presence*) — al-Rāzī's celebrated distinction at that locus returning here to anchor the whole pericope: there are *two reward-classes* — (1) the *multiplied* payback of deeds themselves, counted, measured, apportioned (the ledger-of-returns, *yuḍāʿifhā*), and (2) the *ladunnī* endowment — the bounty that streams directly from His nearness — which the gnostic commentators associate the commentators associated with goods unshaped by instrumentation: the pleasure of His countenance, the direct rainwater of vision-love-knowledge — al-Rāzī's own phrasing his own image at 4:40's commentary: the first reward for the limbs for limbs' work; the second for *the soul sanctified by light* — bodily happiness versus spiritual happiness — the very categories rekindled now at v. 67: had the waverers obeyed, their *wage* would not be disbursed merely from an account-office but from *ladunnā* — from God's immediate side — the preposition carrying what no arithmetic can: *closeness with the Recompenser built into the recompense*. The Book's other deployments widen the mint: 17:80's "grant me from Your Presence an authority that helps"; 18:10's youths in the cave — "grant us from Your Presence a mercy"; 3:8's — "our Lord, let not our hearts swerve... and grant us from Your Presence a mercy — Thou art the Bestower" — and the treasury the piety-books' summary Al-Ghazālī's register the standard devotion-key of them all: *everything from ladunnā arrives unmediated — such is the promise stood behind the obedience of the small* (the very class contemplated here — the few of v. 66's *illā qalīlun*).

**Ajran ʿAẓīmā — Mighty, Not Measured**

The size-word *ʿaẓīm* — great, mighty — carries into the tiny verse the pericope's entire grandeur of scale: *ajr* — reward-payment — qualified by neither boundary nor breakdown (the commentators' observation at its similar stations: when heaven wishes to *dwarf* a reward it details it; when it wishes to *exalt* it, it writes *ʿaẓīm* and leaves it open — cf. 48:10 — the Hudaybiyyah pledgees promised "a mighty reward"; 33:29 upon the Prophet's wives — "a mighty reward prepared"; and throughout the trading-verses at 4:95, 133, 162, 173 and on) — so that the wavering audience learns the scale of what their one shortcoming of obedience forfeits: *a reward classified as mighty, drawn from the immediate Presence, sealed with heaven's own oath-particle *la-* — the conditional tragedy thus standing in full: all this *would have been* — and the small few who did answer receiving exactly it — though the tradition always keeps the door-half-open where God leaves it: *would have been* is not *never shall be* — any late-claimer may still convert his file into the three then-payments by completing v. 65's triple submission) — and the verse after (v. 68) pours the second payment beside it, the third following at v. 69's companionships-roll: the trinity of *reward from His Presence, guidance on the Path, and the company of the blessed* — a majestic three-line bill for one act of obedience that the reluctant so nearly missed.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:68

> **and We would surely have guided them unto a straight path.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Wa la-Hadaynāhum Ṣirāṭan Mustaqīman: The Second Then-Payment**

The pericope's second heaven-signed apodosis follows immediately upon the reward-promise: *wa la-hadaynāhum ṣirāṭan mustaqīman* — "and We would surely have guided them upon a straight path": *wa la-* — and surely — the lām-of-certainty again (matching v. 67's *la-ātaynāhum* — the conditional ledger pairing its two promises in seamless grammar), and *hadaynāhum* — We guided them — the h-d-y verb-family that holds the Book's entire navigation-engine (guidance as God's own action over hearts: 2:213 — "God guides whom He wills"; 6:82's Abrahamic security-cohort — "those who believe and mix not their belief with wrongdoing — for them is security, and they are guided"; and the fixed principle at 47:17 — "those who follow guidance — He increases them in guidance") — yet calibrated here, as the clause's own logic discloses, as heaven's *response to compliance*: they walked, so they were shown — guidance increasing upon the obedient, the wage of steps already taken, exactly per the hadith-qudsī announcement that anchored v. 67's own commentary (al-Bukhārī 7405 — "if he draws near to Me a span I draw near to him a cubit... and if he comes to Me walking, I come to him running").

**Ṣirāṭan Mustaqīman: The Road-Term of All Roads**

Then the object-phrase the whole ummah carries daily on its tongue — *ṣirāṭan mustaqīman* — the straight path: *ṣirāṭ* — road, crossing-way (its bridge-image made famous at the Resurrection in the hadith-topography: a bridge thinner than a hair and sharper than a sword — cf. al-Bukhārī 6573 and Muslim 183 — yet in its *worldly* employment always the religion's traffic-way) — and *mustaqīm* — from q-w-m, to stand straight — the path without crooks or folds, its vocabulary-cousins all aligning: *istiqāmah*, the believer's own standing-straight — the Prophet's advice given to the man asking for a single counsel that would suffice his whole life:

> *"Say: My Lord is God, then stand straight (qultu rabbi Allāh thumma istaqim)."* (al-Tirmidhī 2410; Muslim 38)
