## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:82

> **Do they not contemplate the Quran? Had it been from other than God, they would surely have found much discrepancy therein.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**A-Fa-Lā Yatadabbarūna al-Qurʾān: Contemplation as Standing Obligation**

After the night-plots clause, heaven turns the beam upon the very text that has just been quoted against the conspirators — and issues the question that built a science: *a-fa-lā yatadabbarūna al-Qurʾāna* — "do they not contemplate the Quran?": *tadabbur*, from d-b-r — to follow behind a thing, to consider its outcomes — to walk toward the back of the words where their consequences grow (the Book's own four stations of the command: 4:82; 23:68; 38:29 — "a Book We sent down to thee, blessed, *that they may contemplate its signs*"; and 47:24 — "Do they not then contemplate the Quran — or are there locks upon their hearts?" — the sister-clause that seals the diagnosis: hearts acquire locks exactly where tadabbur is left off) — the commentators read the question in two directions at once: as challenge to the doubters — had they truly read this Book, which now publishes their own night-schemes within its pages, they would confess its Divine provenance, for it names their secrets — and as standing *obligation upon the believers*: the Recitation is not meant to be merely intoned but entered into understanding — 38:29's blessing tied directly to the very act of pondering. The Prophet's own practice was the lifelong demonstration of the verb — his night-standing with the sūrahs until his feet swelled — and the preserved reports describe his manner of recitation as measured and halted, dwelling upon each clause of mercy or punishment, as in the record of his reading the closing verses of Sūrah al-Nisāʾ's own sister-sūras and pausing at the warnings and promises to press them into supplication (Muslim 772's register of his pondering-style); from this single command grew, in due course, the entire tadabbur-genre of the libraries of Islam — the treatises that taught the world to hear the Book as a living Speaker rather than a museum-text.

**Wa Law Kāna min ʿIndi Ghayri Allāh: The Coherence-Test as Authenticity's Signature**

Then comes the counterfactual that has never stopped serving as an open challenge to humanity: *wa law kāna min ʿindi ghayri Allāhi la-wajadū fīhi ikhtilāfan kathīrā* — "and had it been from other than God, they would have found in it much discrepancy": the logic-spine, as al-Zamakhsharī and al-Rāzī both sharpen it, is not merely *absence of contradiction* but absence of the natural human entropy of speech: any human author composing over twenty-three years — amid war and truce, bereavement and victory, persecution and triumph, hunger and rule — would accumulate *ikhtilāf kathīr*, massive inconsistency: tones shifting, loyalties bending, self-corrections lurching in, factions courted, early positions quietly disowned. Yet the Recitation descends across the most violent biography ever given a messenger — through migration, battlefield defeat, public scandal, famine, and absolute sovereignty — and emerges as *one voice*, one doctrinal geometry: the whole Book resolving always into the same tawḥīd, the same ethic, the same eschatology.

From this verse the proof-method itself was patented into the sciences of Islam: the inimitability doctrine (iʿjāz) with its standing challenge-verses — 2:23 ("then produce a sūrah like it"), 10:38, 11:13, and 17:88:

> *"Say: If mankind and the jinn came together to produce the like of this Quran, they could not produce its like, even if they backed one another"* (17:88)

— and the consistency-theology of 39:23 ("God has sent down the fairest discourse, a Book self-consistent, oft-repeated, at which the skins of those who fear their Lord shiver"). As for the critics' rejoinders — the varied canonical readings (qirāʾāt) and the abrogating and abrogated verses (nāsikh and mansūkh) — the classical frame answers without flinching (al-Ṭabarī's collation carried down by al-Suyūṭī's circles): divergent readings and revealed development are *intended divine pedagogy*, disclosed upon the face of the Book rather than concealed — an honest Book's evolution is stamped and marked in public, which is the very opposite of a forger's method: the pretender would hide revisions; the Prophet instead publicly recited abrogations, announcing changed rulings before the world exactly as the Book records the scoffers' retort — "thou art but a forger!" — precisely at the open management of sequence (16:101).

**The Standing Promise: Tadabbur as Policy for Every Age**

The verse's legacy runs wider than apologetics, as the classical masters long ago taught from it. For the *seeker*: the Book repays deep reading with coherent sight — surface-readers find puzzle after puzzle; tadabbur-workers find convergence — and whenever apparent disagreement arises among verses, the remedy is harmonization, not combat: the Prophet grew visibly angry upon hearing Companions wielding verses against one another in dispute, and warned them:

> *"Nothing destroyed the peoples before you but this."* (al-Bukhārī 2410; Muslim 2666 — the celebrated report on Qur'an-dueling)

— making one verse fight another without a reconciling hermeneutic is *man-made ikhtilāf*, the very flaw the Book demonstrably lacks; the clear verses (muḥkam) govern, and the interwoven (mutashābih) yield to them, per 3:7's architecture. For the *scholar*: al-Qurṛṭubī and al-Rāzī read the clause as the warrant for analogical reasoning (qiyās) and systematic reconciliation — since no contradiction exists, interpretive labor is entrusted with *finding* the seamless reading — the muḥkam-mutashābih structure never being license for two camps at war but a summons to one integrated vision. And for the *ordinary believer*: tadabbur remains daily devotion — the standing antidote to locked hearts being open pages — crowned by the Prophet's promise upon every reader:

> *"The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it."* (al-Bukhārī 5027)

The sūrah's pericope has just displayed, in the night-contrivers of v. 81, what a community looks like when held up against this un-discrepant Light: the Book knows its readers before they know it — and asks them only one open question, permanent in every century, written to every locked heart it finds: *Do you not contemplate the Quran?*

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:83

> **And whenever tidings come unto them, whether of security or fear, they spread it about, whereas had they referred it to the Messenger and to those in authority among them, those of them whose task it is to investigate would have known it. Were it not for God's Bounty toward you, and His Mercy, you would surely have followed Satan, save a few.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Wa Idhā Jāʾahum Amrun mina al-Amni awi al-Khawf Adāʿū Bih: The Rumor-Epidemic Named**

The pericope completes its governance-machinery (trusts at v. 58, authorities at v. 59, referral at v. 83 herein) with its information-law chamber: *wa idhā jāʾahum amrun mina al-amni awi al-khawfi adāʿū bih* — "and whenever some affair comes to them — of security or of fear — they broadcast it": *amr* — an affair, a tiding, a case — the indefinite noun seeded in both directions (security-news *or* fear-news — victory-bulletins and invasion-terror alike); *adāʿū*, from a-d-y-ʿ from *adāʿa* — to scatter abroad, spread wide — the verb of uncontrolled diffusion (its kin word being *dhayāʿ* — waste, scattering-to-nothing — the Quran's chosen sound for rumor-scattering — deliberately chosen, al-Rāzī notes, over mere telling (ikhbār, khabar-news) — broadcasting is *already* a judgment: an undisciplined widening of a datum into the public ear without verifying it — with the Sīrah-background the tradition hands to the verse (al-Wāḥidī's chain, al-Ṭabarī, Ibn Kathīr's forum collation): the terrain being Madinese, where every week saw where detachments marched and returned — and every souk-hour generated lore about them: reports of victory, of massacre, of heroes fallen — quickly sewn into the marketplaces — and — above all — the run-up phase to the *Lesser Badr* rendezvous, when enemy disinformation (an immense Makkan host lies across the road) was pumped into Madinah to freeze the Muslims — the verses' word *al-khawf*, fear-tidings, fitting perfectly the panic-stock the scenario: fear-data bred in the hypocrites' courts and tossed into the believers' streets.

**Wa Law Raddūhu ilā al-Rasūli wa ilā Ulī al-Amri Minhum: The Correct Protocol**

Then the standing counter-rule — one of Islam's institutional marvels: *wa law raddūhu ilā al-rasūli wa ilā ulī al-amri minhum la-ʿalimahu alladhīna yastanbiṭūnahu minhum* — "and had they referred it to the Messenger and to those in authority among them — those of them whose task is to make inquiry — would have known it": referral again (the sūrah's third stitch into the institutional fabric — v. 59's ruddūhu ilā Allāhi wa al-rasūl for disputes; v. 83's raddūhu for *news*) — and its billets articulated: (1) the Messenger (the dir-head the head of state) and (2) *ulū al-amr* — the command-authorities — the commentators' the commentators' reading making this the standing civil-military intelligence service — and (3) the expert-class specialized in the news-file *alladhīna yastanbiṭūnahu* — yastanbiṭ, from n-b-ṭ from *istinbāṭ* — drawing out the water of the sense extracting, deriving, investigating-to-the-bottom (the root-water itself: nabaṭ — the spring's first al-Rāzī's the classical image: the investigator as a well-digger who lifts the payload truth out of the strata) — so that Islam ends up with an inquiry-function legally treasured inside the state: intelligence cleared among those who understand its edges — with al-Rāzī's celebrated jurisprudential red his landmark definition flowing out of it: istinbāṭ is the exact functional role of ijtihād (the qualified derivation-work of the jurists) — this verse being his classical license beside the beside the Muʿādh-hadith base the Prophet's dispatch of Muʿādh to Yemen (Tirmidhī 1327; Abū Dāwūd Abū Dāwūd 3592): *"How will you judge By the Book — and if not present By the Sunnah — and if not present I will practice independent judgment (ajtahidu ra'yī)"* — so the istinbāṭ-class is the same class licensed for juristic derivation: the sulṭān of the mind, the mind of understanding, under the governance of revelation.

**Lawlā Faḍlu Allāhi ʿAlaykum wa Raḥmatuhu: Bounty-and-Mercy as the Community's Immunity**

The verse's seal opens upon its near-miss theology: *law-lā faḍlu Allāhi ʿalaykum wa raḥmatuhu la-ttabaʿtumu al-shayṭāna illā qalīlā* — "were it not for God's bounty upon you — and His mercy — you would have followed Satan, save a few": the sentence scanning the whole rumor-epidemic to its own asymptote end: without God's blessings (twin-named: faḍl — bounty — and raḥmah — mercy — the commentators' twofold gloss sitting into mapping unto God's two gifts: (1) the Prophet and the Qur'an themselves, i.e., the office that *exists* to be referred to, and (2) the sustaining of the believers by by victories and gradual disentanglement) — the whole ummah with its camp-noise and market-noise would have drifted after the Devil — *illā qalīlā* — save a few (the exceptive again — the Book's standing sociological-statistical realism — everywhere — from 4:66's qalīlun minhum through 4:46 to here: the immune band, tiny yet real, whom God kept unbought from guile) — the seal thereby tying v. 83 into the sūrah's pastoral covenant its covenant-grammar: God pays His community with both *faḍl* and *raḥmah*, granting the institutional machinery (referred authorities, expert-diggers) that keeps it from Satan-slam drifting — with the teachers’ summary passed down the centuries: communities die first not of wrong belief but of *information-disorder* — so God planted the Prophet so God planted right handling of reports into the religion itself — *verify, refer, investigate: then broadcast* — a law as fresh in every century's rumor storm as it was beside the wells of Badr al-Ṣughrā.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:84

> **So fight in the way of God. Thou art accountable only for thyself, and urge on the believers. It may be that God will restrain the might of the disbelievers, for God is stronger in might and more severe in punishment.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Fa-Qātil fī Sabīli Allāh: The Command Single-Minded**

After the rumor-diagnostics of v. 83, the command comes down to the Prophet directly — stripped to its essence: *fa-qātil fī sabīli Allāh* — "so fight thou in the way of God" — the command addressed in the singular-second-person (the Book's grammar-shifted its honor-grammar: the *qātil* singular riding singular addressed context: where the ummah was addressed collectively at v. 71, here the Prophet alone — meaning: the war-responsibility falls on him whether or not the timid mass follows — the classical use of this verse being among the most famous in all Islam's biographical inheritance: the asbāb-chronicles of the *Lesser Badr* mission (al-Tabarī coll collations, al-Wāḥidī and al-Rāzī's registers) delivering the verse's field-paraphrase its very spark: after Uḥud's wound, Abū Sufyān proposed a return engagement for the following year at Badr; when the date neared, disinformation was pumped into Madinah about the *immensity of the Makkan muster* (v. 83's rumor-wave) — whereupon most of the Madinese shrank back — and the Prophet declared the covenant his answer preserved as one of the glories of the Sīrah:

> *"By Him in Whose hand is my soul — I shall go out, even if alone!"* (recorded across the tafsīr asbāb-register on this verse, by al-Ṭabarī's and al-Wāḥidī's chains)

— and he set out with only seventy riders — and found the Makkans had themselves had themselves shrunk from the rendezvous — a a demonstration of the very promise the rest of the verse makes: morale-theater victories belong to the soldier who obeys irrespective of the crowd.

**Lā Tukallafu illā Nafsak: The Soul-Accountonomy**

The second clause releases the Prophet from hostage-taking from the militia's consent: *lā tukallafu illā nafsak* — "thou art accountable only for thyself": *tukallafu* — burden-accountability — from k-l-f, the weighing of duty — news both sobering and freeing: your war-duty does not wait upon quorum (the commentators tracing this freedom-clause to its Sīrah-sisters: Moses's own declaration of the "I have no power save for myself and my brother" — 5:25; and the Book’s parallel license to the Prophet at 24:54 — "if you obey him, you shall be rightly guided; and upon the Messenger is only the clear delivery") — the sentence thereby erecting the standing liberating-theology at the heart of Islamic command doctrine: *the leader's accountability is personal, never contingent on the crowd's* — truth carried by one man does not die of loneliness (its counter-views expressed forever at the prophets' own moments: Noah's Noah's ceaseless night-a day-and-night call with its handful; Lot's solitary table household-band; Moses at the well's at the sea's brink — *"Nay! My Lord is with me — He will guide me"* — 26:62) — and the Prophet's seventy-maker seventy-man ride sealing it into the Sīrah: go, if none goes with you (with the immediately-following clause then restoring then adding the second arm — *wa ḥarriḍi al-muʾminīn* — yet *urge on the believers* — loneliness-of-duty being no license for exasperation: the Prophet both walks alone when he must *and* never ceases wakening the rest — ḥarriḍ — urge, stir, inflame — from ḥ-r-ḍ's from the root of incitement itself — the verb of mobilization, matched by heaven's own promise that the exhortation works through time: vant victory sits behind *urging*, not behind headcounts).

**ʿAsā Allāhu an Yakuffa Baʾsa Alladhīna Kafarū: Might Restrained from Above**

Then the promise — the sentence the Sīrah of the Lesser Badr worked out before the commentators' eyes: *ʿasā Allāhu an yakuffa baʾsa alladhīna kafarū* — "it may be that God will restrain the might of the unbelievers": *ʿasā* — perhaps, may-be — the commentators unanimous that with God *ʿasā* carries *certainty* (the Book's honorific economy — "perhaps" in God's mouth = *promise-tailored promise in royal understatement*: cf. 17:79's "it may be that your Lord will raise you to a praised station" — known-certain in advance) — *yakuffa*, restrain, hold back (from k-f-f itself: the palm-withdrawal word — used by God through the Book wherever a war’s storm-wave is recalled — 4:77's own *kuffū aydiyakum* of the Meccan-quiet era) — *baʾsa* — might, striking-power, war-fury — and the fulfillment-record the historians write beside it: Abū Sufyān's own host, pumped-up Advertised advertised into Madinah as gigantic, itself withdrew withdrew at the appointed sheikh at the appointed rendezvous under the logistical under the drought-pressure and the terror of the Prophet's advance: restraint accomplished by *non-collision* — God not requiring not always restraining might by arms but sometimes by *withdrawal* itself — baʾs evaporating before battle could start (with the hadith's own summary of the Lesser Badr outcome preserved in the campaign-roll simply: the doubled blood-value the outcome's standing signification booked in the tafsīr-lines as the proof of ʿasā-victory) — and the seal locks the axiom locks the axiom in place: *wa Allāhu ashaddu baʾsan wa ashaddu tankīlā* — "God is stronger in might and more severe in retribution": *baʾs* matched to the enemy's baʾs — with *tankīl* — from n-k-l — exemplary deterrent punishment — heaven's two two attributes of force set against disbelieving might forever — the sūrah's war-block hence commissioned at last in its own grammar: fight as if you were alone; urge as if you were followed; know that the might above yours and theirs both is God's — and that He may restrain their storm without a single stroke struck, when the commander stands fast.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:85

> **Whosoever intercedes for a good cause shall receive a share of it; and whosoever intercedes for an evil cause shall share in its burden; and God is Sustainer of all things.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Man Yashfaʿ Shafāʿatan Ḥasanatan: The Intercessor's Share-Law**

The battle-and-governance pericope suddenly opens into a general social law — one of the ummah's most recited formulas of communal ethics: *man yashfaʿu shafāʿatan ḥasanatan yakun lahu naṣībun minhā* — "whoever intercedes a good intercession shall have for himself a share of it": *yashfaʿu* — from sh-f-ʿ — to pair, double, yoke-to (its root-image being *joining another's plea to one's own* — advocacy as partnership: the intercessor adding his weight onto the case-cass onto another's case); *shafāʿatan ḥasanatan* — a good advocacy — named with the Book's standard beauty-adjective; and the promise: *naṣībun minhā* — a share *from it* (the inheritance-word again — v. 7's far naṣīb familiar from the sūrah's own estate-chapters — now turned moral: advocacy itself earns a *bequest* from the cause advanced) — al-Qurṛṭubī's register the doctors' elaboration at once: the intercessor's share is not cut *from* the principal's reward but granted fresh from God in *parallel* (the hadith-capsule lodging it:

> *"Whoever guides to good has the like of the reward of its doer, without that diminishing from the doer's own reward aught; and whoever guides to evil has the like of the burden of its doer, without that diminishing from his burden aught."* (Muslim 2674 — Kitāb al-ʿIlm; with Tirmidhī's cousins 2670 & 2671)

— reward flowing *twice*, without siphoning: the divine economy no zero-sum ledger).

**Wa Man Yashfaʿ Shafāʿatan Sayyiʾatan Yakun Lahu Kiflun Minhā: The Counter-Share**

Then the mirror — and its vocabulary shifts from naṣīb to something heavier: *wa man yashfaʿu shafāʿatan sayyiʾatan yakun lahu kiflun minhā* — "and whoever intercedes an evil intercession shall have for himself a *kifl* of it": *sayyiʾah* — evil — and *kifl* — portion, burden-lot — from k-f-l — to be answerable-for, to carry liability (the commentators noting the deliberate word-swap: for good, a *naṣīb* — free gift-share; for evil, a *kifl* — weight of responsibility, kafālah-cognate — the man legally morally bonded to what he boosted: the guarantor-syntax of sin) — and al-Rāzī's note seizes the moral architecture: advocacy is *agency-multiplied* — the advocator who stands behind a deed shares in every downstream consequence the deed begets (cf. the hadith Max the celebrated Muslim 1017 — *"whoever makes a good precedent in Islam has its reward and the reward of those who work by it after him... and whoever makes an evil precedent has its burden and the burden of those who work by it after him"*) — the battlefield-face of the doctrine at hand in the asbāb-roll (al-Ṭabarī's and al-Rāzī's collations): those who *promoted* the marching — equipping contingents, arguing men forward, loaning mounts to the fighters — being *shufaʿāʾ ḥasanah-*intercessors, whose share of each detachment's wages was certified by heaven; and from the other bench — those whispering-out the marching those who dissuaded Madinese from answering the Prophet's muster-call (vv. 72, 83's tarriers and rumor-mon the fear-mongers) — being the *kifl*-intercessors of evil, bearing their cut of every missed obligation their discouragement spawned — with the classical application-rules drawn from the verse standing to this day in qānūn in Islamic legal-ethical lore: aid a plaintiff's just case — earn a share of the judgment's good; defend the wrong man knowing his wrong — bond yourself to his to his entire liability.

**Wa Kāna Allāhu ʿalā Kulli Shayʾin Muqītā: Muqīt — Nourisher-Watcher Over All**

The seal names its rarest attribute-token of the sūrah: *wa kāna Allāhu ʿalā kulli shayʾin muqītan* — "God is Sustainer of all things": *muqītab muqīt* — from a-w-t from q-w-t — provision of food-strength — the commentators' glà the commentators' array of glosses fixing its triplet: (1) *Nourisher* — He who metes every being's sustenance-exact, down to the down to the grain beneath the stone (11:6's "no moving creature is there upon the earth but that God provides its sustenance"); (2) *Powerful/Capable* — muqtadir — over all things; (3) *Witness-Preserver* — ḥafīẓ — watching everything for its accounting — the word's four occurrences across the Book sealing its rare-stra its select deployment (here; 33:58 cf. its three cousins: count: 4:85 plus its resisters standing main suf: its companions across the Revelation being likewise divine-self-testimonies of providential trusteeship) — and the reason the seal belongs exactly to v. 85 is disclosed by the tradition at once: *the keeper of the share-and-burden ledgers must be the One who supplies all things* — for only the universal Nourisher can grant rewards without robbing the original earners (the naṣīb is fresh mint after fresh mint — sent down like rain — and the kifl is weighed out with the same precision) — so the morality-r so the ethical doctrine inherits its ground: be an intercessor — in the family, in the war-camp, before the king, between quarreling spouses, at every desk of every administration — and only ever measure *whose case what you push upon whom*: shafāʿah is a currency God mints twice — and the good advocate joins the ranks of the few of whom the Prophet reported his glad tidings about reported across the Sahīh his standing hope-proclamation (Muslim 2636's register of the celebrated parallel: *"the best charity? no — *the best of people are those most beneficial to people"*) — with God's own muqīt-attributes standing over their ledgers forever.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:86

> **And when you are offered a greeting, respond with a greeting that is better, or return it; surely God takes account of all things.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Wa Idhā Ḥuyyītum bi-Taḥiyyatin Fa-Ḥayyū bi-Aḥsana Minhā: The Greeting-Protocol of Heaven**

The sūrah's communal-ethics chamber opens with a verse that became the charter of Muslim convivial law: *wa idhā ḥuyyītum bi-taḥiyyatin fa-ḥayyū bi-aḥsana minhā aw ruddūhā* — "and when you are greeted with a greeting — respond with a better one, or return it": *taḥiyyah*, greeting — from ḥ-y-y — to live, and thence the wish *may you live* — the oldest benediction-family of the Semitic languages the comment-lineage reminding that taḥiyyah means originally *life-salutations* — the peace-greeting *al-salāmu ʿalaykum* being its Islamic patent-form — and the twin imperative-options unleashing their doctrine: (1) *bi-aḥsana minhā* — with better than it — the excellence-track: return with *more* (the hadith-canon demonstrates the ladder beautifully in the model progression of the Sunan registers: a man greets: *al-salāmu ʿalaykum*; a second answers better: *wa ʿalayka al-salāmu wa raḥmatu Allāh*; a third crowns it: *wa ʿalaykum al-salāmu wa raḥmatu Allāhi wa barakātuh* — peace, and mercy, and blessings (cf. Abū Dāwūd 5231 and al-Tirmidhī’s Adab-registers) — the Prophet’s own standing commentary upon the exchange being the model-form of the aḥsan-bidding, with al-Bukhārī’s and Muslim’s rolls sealing its affection-engine in the settling clause: *"you shall not enter the Garden until you believe — and you shall not believe until you love one another. Shall I guide you to something by which you shall love one another? Spread the salām among you."* (Muslim 54, Kitāb al-Īmān))); and (2) *aw ruddūhā* — *or return it* — the equality-track: equal return as a matter of right (the fiqh-doctrine issuing straight from the verse's disjunction: better-return = recommended; equal-return = obligatory — al-Qurṛṭubī and Ibn Kathīr's standing rule — failing to answer a salām being unlawful, even when the greeter is lowly, or lowly and unloved in the commentators' own note of its binding character upon believer to believer).

**The Salām as Islam's Social Covenant**

The commentators then unfold the verse's hidden architecture — that its center is not etiquette but *theology of peace*: al-salām returning forever inside Islam's covenant-locations: God's own name *al-Salām* — the Peace — 59:23; the Garden's entry-word being salām (50:34 — "enter it in peace — that is the Day of Eternity"; 56:25-26 — "they hear no ill speech nor lie — only a saying: peace, peace!"; 14:23 — "their greeting therein: peace!"; 36:58) — archangels greeting at the gates (13:23-24); and the Prophet commissioned by heaven to make it the Muslims' standing counter-signature in the world — with the whole structure reaching its plenary summit its plenary in the duodec in the standing admonition-roll of the practices of the rightly ordered heart (Bukhārī's own Abū ʿUmāmah collected in the Adab-books of Bukhārī abiding-members the famous verse the famous Boy the Prophet's own uniform practice of salām to *everyone he passed* — old and young, known and unknown) — protocolized into the universal ethics of the ummah (al-Bukhārī 6232; Muslim 2160–62): greet the known and the unknown alike; begin with the standing to the seated, the rider to the walker, the few to the many, the young to the old — the peace-verse thus becoming the ummah’s oldest social software: its encounter-codes designed to load every meeting with mercy — and the Prophet’s clear law revealing its hidden counter-weight: every cold shoulder toward a salām contradicts the verse-born covenant outright*.

**Inna Allāha Kāna ʿalā Kulli Shayʾin Ḥasībā: The Auditor of Greetings**

The attribute-seal twines the verse's seal closes its covenant with its own heaven-watch: *inna Allāha kāna ʿalā kulli shayʾin ḥasīban* — "God surely is a Reckoner over all things": *ḥasīb* — accounter-tracker — from h-s-b — the counter of everything counted (with its standing honors 4:6's *kafā bi-Allāhi ḥasībā* above — and the sufficiency-inflection at 4:81's wakīl/70's ʿalīm/45's aʿlamu — the pericope's audit-attr audit-attributes triangulating together in the seal-cluster) — here assigned specifically over *greetings*: heaven weighing even the "salāmu ʿalaykum" on its ledger — peace-return being no small coin: the hadith-tradition at the the widely-recited allocation-system of aḥsan-return (cf. the standing tip Tirmidhī's own register of Tirmidhī 2689 — greeting-response weights certified in the hadith-books) — while beyond arithmetic the attribute plays its silent pastoral role: men may well where men might count blessings-currency as beneath their stature, the Auditor's ledger never does — the smallest peace-offering between two passers-by is filed in the Book that forgets nothing (99:7-8's atom-weight again) — and the whole sūrah thereby moves from battle-holds into everyday covenant — vv. 85-86 constituting the ummah's two coming two operating protocols of commun of civic grace: intercede for good; greet with peace; know that *both directions of human speech — the plea and the salutation — are banked with God* — so that the believer greets *every soul* with the peace of a man whose Auditor is Ḥasīb, and advances *every case* with the advocacy of a man whose Nourisher is Muqīt.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:87

> **God, there is no god but He. He will surely gather you all unto the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt. And who is truer than God in speech?**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Allāhu Lā Ilāha illā Hū: The Creed-Anchor Amid the Laws**

Between the peace-protocol of v. 86 and the two-party verdict-battle of v. 88, the sūrah plants its bald creed-obelisk: *Allāh — lā ilāha illā hū* — "God — there is no god but He": the kalimah placed in absolute form, the detached pronoun carrying the whole of Divinity in this its most compressed formulation (its family-station across the Book, in the same emphatic arrangement: 2:255's Āyat al-Kursī opening; 3:2; 3:18's like attestation of oneness in the selfsame early-Madinan tract) — and the structure-critics note its function here: the sūrah's long string of communal duties and battle-decrees pauses for one breath — and resumes after — as though heaven itself breathed once through the law-text — recalling every reader from secondary matters to the First Thing, the One God — before descending into the hypocrite-verdicts, where men *talk* of God endlessly without knowing Him. Al-Rāzī's small precision catches the theology in the word-order: *Allāh* first, as the proper noun; then the entire monotheistic sentence is reduced to a pronoun — the whole of Divinity stated by *He* alone, no predicates added — huwiyya-language in its purest formulation: everything else in existence is describable by titles; Him — by *He*.

**La-Yajmaʿannakum ilā Yawmi al-Qiyāmati Lā Rayba Fīh: The Gathering Oath**

Then the resurrection-oath — doubled-emphatic: *la-yajmaʿannakum ilā yawmi al-qiyāmati lā rayba fīh* — "He will surely gather you unto the Day of Resurrection, wherein is no doubt": *la-yajmaʿannakum*, its grammar loaded with two emphatic particles (the lām of certainty and the doubled nūn of force — the Book's heaviest oath-formula); *jamʿ* — gathering — the resurrection-scene named first by its *assembly-function* (64:9's own title for the Last Day is *yawm al-jamʿ* — the Day of Congregation — its very name drawn from the gathering of every scattered life that ever lived: dust reassembled, bones recalled, souls called down). And *lā rayba fīh* — *no doubt in it*: the Book's standard iron-proofing of the day about which every civilization has postured doubt — its family of attestations running across the Revelation: 3:9 — "Our Lord, Thou wilt gather mankind on a day wherein is no doubt"; 3:25; 18:21; 22:7; 40:59 — the deliberate pattern being (in the tradition's standing observation) that heaven reattests *the Day of no-doubt* upon passage after passage of the Book precisely because *rayb* — doubt of it — is the deep solvent of religious seriousness: without the Day, orphans' gold is safe food, battles are avoidable forever, oaths are ornamental; and indeed 45:32's bitter retrospective seal shows the dissolution at its purest: when they are told *God's promise is true — and the Hour — no doubt in it*, they answer: "we know not what the Hour is — we think it but conjecture; and we are not convinced." And the sūrah of household-honesty needs the creed-anchor exactly so: an ummah being taught to pay blood-money and hold treaty-lines must know there *is* an Audit, or law becomes a mere matter of who is watching — whereas with the Day of lā rayb, every clause of this sūrah writes itself upon an eternal ledger automatically.

**Wa Man Aṣdaqu mina Allāhi Ḥadīthan: The Rhetoric-Seal of Truth**

Then the clinching question — one of the Book's most perfect pen-bows: *wa man aṣdaqu mina Allāhi ḥadīthan* — "and who is more truthful than God in speech?": *man* — who — driving the comparative to its absolute, the interrogative form carrying the force of a universal negation — *no one* is a truer speaker; *aṣdaq* — truer — from ṣ-d-q's own trunk: *ṣidq* — truth-being and true-speech — the same root-region as *ṣiddīqūn* in v. 69's blessed cohort and as the Muslim's standing charge upon his own tongue; *ḥadīthan* — *in speech-statement* — the accusative of manner — the whole clause striking at the root of the dark-chamber of vv. 81–83, the sūrah's hypocrite-paragraphs: men may be part-liars in their councils, their oaths, their excuses — while God's *ḥadīth* stands over all. Its twin-stamp comes below in the sūrah itself at 4:122 — *wa man aṣdaqu mina Allāhi qīlan* — (the commentators among the balāgha-school parsing the two rhetorical words: ḥadīth as the conveyed tiding, qīl as the utterance-form — both absolutized beyond all competitors); and the standing doctrine the kalām-masters drew from the pair runs to the roots: God's revelation is truth *not only in fact but in kind* (6:115's summation: "None can alter His words — and He is the Hearer, the Knower"; 18:27: "recite what has been revealed to thee of the Book of thy Lord — none can change His words"). The verse thereby welds v. 82's coherence-challenge to v. 87's truth-guarantee: He is One; He will gather every soul at the Day of no-doubt; and no speech anywhere compares to His for truth. Upon that plinth the entire hypocrite-file of the verses immediately following (vv. 88–90) conducts its business — the sūrah's creed-grammar being nothing less than: *since He is One, and will assemble, and speaks true — all those fear-oaths, secret cabals, double-sidings and rumor-games stand already convicted before the Day of lā rayb* — and the believer answers in the closing-language of the devout: *ṣadaqta* — "Thou didst speak true" — every prayer thereafter recited with this seal's full weight, every worldly obligation assessed under the Day's audit, and nothing beneath its archway running any escape.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:88

> **What is with you that you are [divided into] two groups concerning the hypocrites, when God Himself has cast them back for that which they have earned? Do you seek to guide those whom God has led astray? Whomsoever God leads astray, thou wilt not find a way for him.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Fa-Mā Lakum fī al-Munāfiqīna Fi'atayn: The Believers' Debated Hypocrite-File**

The sūrah's governance chamber opens its tightest hypocrite-court with a courtroom question: *fa-mā lakum fī al-munāfiqīna fi'atayn* — "what is with you — that you are divided into two parties concerning the hypocrites?": *fi'atayn* — two factions (the Book choosing the body-of-men word deliberately, to emphasize the *dual-party* split inside Madinah itself — the believers' community dividing *within its own walls* over how to judge the half-committed: the Sīrah-background the commentators preserve in their asbāb-roll (al-Ṭabarī's collation; al-Wāḥidī; Ibn Kathīr's summary) tells of a band of professing Muslims — said variously to be certain Medinans who set out with the Prophet for Uḥud but then withdrew back to Madinah (the same band indicted at 3:167 with their hollow excuse — *"had we known there would be fighting, we would have followed you"* — the words of men who weigh devotion on odds) — or, on the more common asbāb-line, a band of Makkans who had claimed Islam, came to Madinah, then departed under pleas and excuses and settled again among the idolaters — leaving behind them the question of their final disposition) — and the Companions themselves divided between two camps: one party calling for stern judgment upon the deserters; another urging that they be left alone in patience — whereupon heaven intervened in the debate itself. The verse's stinging diagnostic: *your division into two parties about them is already a mark upon you* — the question of blatant treachery had drifted from clear covenant-assessment into *partisan camps arguing over hypocrites* — a sign of how deeply the fence-sitting contagion can work inward through a community's gates, not by changing beliefs but by *paralyzing verdicts*. With al-Qurṛṭubī's and al-Rāzī's master-point: the question rebukes not the *discussion* but the *two-grouping itself* — judgment upon daylight-manifest treachery should require no faction (the covenant's criteria are already drawn: profess, settle, answer the call, and leave not — and the man who oscillates between the signs is judged by them) — the believers' duty being *verification*, followed by a single verdict — never factional stasis over the manifest.

**Wa Allāhu Arkasahum bimā Kasabū: The Casting-Back as Divine Verdict**

Then the theological center of the verse: *wa Allāhu arkasahum bimā kasabū* — "God Himself has cast them back for that which they have earned": *arkasahum*, from r-k-s — to throw backward, to invert, to cause to return reversed (its Book-kin: the same verb haunting 4:91's own alert three verses below, and used throughout the Revelation only in judgment-settings) — the hypocrites *cast backward by God into the unbelief they had secretly carried all along* — divine inversion as settled judicial sentence. And the causal fire-doctrine the commentators crowd upon the clause: *bimā kasabū* — *for what they acquired* — the inverted status being *earned fruit*, not arbitrary stroke (the Book backing the formula with its standing philosophy of moral harvest: 45:22 — "God created the heavens and the earth in truth, and so that every soul may be recompensed for that which it has earned — and they shall not be wronged"; 16:111 — "the day every soul comes pleading for itself, and every soul is paid in full for what it wrought — and they shall not be wronged") — so heaven's repudiation here is not caprice but *accounting completed*: their profession of faith was already unbelief inside; God merely finalized the verdict which their own works authored — al-Ṭabarī's classical summary: what they were outwardly, they had never believed within; He returned them to the truth of their own inner being, the external sign adjusted at last to the internal fact. Thereby the question answers the two-party debate from above: do not squabble over their state as though it belonged to your competence — God's verdict preceded your councils.

**A-Turīdūna an Tahdū man Aḍalla Allāh: Guidance Denied to the Reverse-Sentenced**

Then the deepest question-clause, closing the file: *a-turīdūna an tahdū man aḍalla Allāh* — "do you seek to guide those whom God has led astray?": the rhetorical impossible — seeking to cancel a judgment the Judge has already handed down (the commentators' settling doctrine — the Ashʿarī school laying its heaviest weight exactly here: *iḍlāl* — leading astray — in the Divine mouth being ultimate, and unanswerable by any creature's hope; with the countering kalām-line at their side — iḍlāl as *sealing-upon-earning* — pairing astrayness with voluntary wrong-work: cf. 28:50 — "who is more astray than he who follows his own whims without guidance from God? — indeed God guides not the wrongdoing folk"; 14:27 — "God leads astray the wrongdoers — and God does what He wills" — the seal enclosing a subject-cohort already defined by its deeds). And the verse's own seal delivers the Book's most quotable build-axiom: *wa man yuḍlili Allāhu fa-lan tajida lahu sabīlā* — "whomsoever God leads astray — thou wilt find for him no way": *sabīl* spelled out as *way-of-access* — road, exit, rescue-route — men being told flatly: God's astray-judgment leaves no road by which *you* can re-guide them — so cease organizing your ummah around their rescue (with its standing twin-seals in the Book — 18:17: "whom God guides is rightly guided; and whom He leads astray, thou wilt find for him no guiding protector"; 7:186: "whom God leads astray has no guide — and He leaves them in their insolence wandering blindly"). And the sūrah's master-precision for the believers then emerges: *the guidance-debate concerning fence-sitters is not yours to fix:* judge actions openly, follow only where God's Word rules, keep covenant-honor with those who stand clear — and never let the half-committed's temperature set Madinah's climate. Verse 88 thus delivers all three arms of the hypocrite-file's governance: the warning against two-party stasis; the verdict-exposition (God inverted them for what they earned); and the pastoral release (leave the astray to their astrayness — you cannot find them a way) — the believers' community emerging *purified by release*: free at last from the fatal burden of trying to carry the half-hearted as if half-heartedness were a faith-and-a-half.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:89

> **They wish that you should disbelieve, even as they disbelieve, that you may be on a level with them. So take them not as protectors till they migrate in the way of God. But if they turn their backs, then seize them and slay them wherever you find them, and take no protector or helper from among them.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Waddū Law Takfurūna kamā Kafarū fa-Takūnūna Sawāʾan: The Equality-of-Misery Wish**

The verdict upon the two-timing band opens with the exposure of their wish: *waddū law takfurūna kamā kafarū fa-takūnūna sawāʾan* — "they wish that you should disbelieve as they disbelieved, that you might be on a level with them": *waddū* — from w-d-d — the wish-verb of longing (its root also giving *wudd* — affection — the commentators remarking that hypocrite-desire dresses itself as tenderness: their wish *for* you reads in their mouths like love of company, ruin-council wearing the mantle of reunion-invitation); *kafarū* — they disbelieved — the verdict finally said outright (the Book through v. 88's inversion now naming what their professions concealed); and *sawāʾ* — *level*, equal rank — the devastation-locus of the whole clause: equality as bait (the standing Quranic psychology of the apostate tempter: the one who has fallen cannot endure the sight of the un-fallen, and so he recruits company for his pit — the Book's fourfold anatomy of this downward-sociology crowding the memory: 33:68-69's damned — "give them a doubled punishment... they say: our Lord, those of jinn and men who led us astray — give them a doubled torment"; 16:86-87's partners hauled in; 37:31-32's "so we led you astray — indeed we ourselves were astray" — the fell-as the leaders' own confession: *we ourselves were astray* — misguiders gloating; even 2:166-8's banding followings splitting apart at the sight of chastisement) — al-Rāzī's diagnostic summarizing the human scene: *envy of equal footing* — the migrant-runaway gazing back at Madinah cannot bear to look up; so his plan becomes engineering how to bring the whole city down to his own floor — and the Book perpetually exposes him at his wish, before his schemes are even built (cf. 68:9 — "they wish that thou wouldst compromise, so they would compromise" — the truce-of-degradation wish running on the identical track).

**Fa-Lā Tattakhidhū Minhum Awliyāʾa Ḥattā Yuhājirū fī Sabīli Allāh: No Walāyah Without Hijrah**

Then the covenant-law riding the exposure: *fa-lā tattakhidhū minhum awliyāʾa ḥattā yuhājirū fī sabīli Allāh* — "so take not from among them protectors, till they migrate in the way of God": *awliyāʾ* — protecting-allies, covenant-friends (the sūrah's third restitching of the prohibition — v. 45's "God knows best your enemies — God suffices as a Walī"; vv. 139/144's cringing vv. 139 and 144's reiterations to come — "do you take the unbelievers as protectors rather than the believers?"; here the condition-clause makes the sūrah's political theology complete: walāyah is *conditional upon total allegiance*) — and the test named: *ḥattā yuhājirū fī sabīli Allāh* — until they migrate in God's path: *hājara* — the full covenant-signature of the first ummah (the Madinan charter-era the first-state phase when Islam's identity and Islam's geography were one — hijrah meaning: house sold, kin forsaken, passport stamped by blood-if-needed — the Book's own plenary portrait of that covenant at 8:72 — "those who believe, and migrate, and strive with their wealth and their selves in the way of God — and those who shelter and help — those are protectors of one another" — the anṣār's own membership-receipt exactly) — the commentators mapping it into the standing Madinan jurisprudence: loyalty to Islam's polity was attested by residence-and-arms, not by formulas on the lips (the moderns' note the standing jurisprudence of the classical canon ra generalizing beyond: the community may accept *professions* as grounds of individual membership, yet *trusted alliance* — office, confidence-food counsel, war-stations — lies committed only upon proved commitment) — and the equity of the test being its *remediable* character: the doorway back is open — migrate, and be in covenant again (cf. 9:117's rewriting reception of the three left behind: repentance being always a standing gate in the Book, even for the once-defected).

**Fa-in Tawallaw fa-Khudhūhum: The Turned-Backs Clause**

Then the sanction — among the strongest-seeming clauses in the sūrah and therefore, in the classical canon, the most carefully fenced: *fa-in tawallaw fa-khudhūhum wa-qtulūhum ḥaythu wajadtumūhum wā lā tattakhidhū minhum walīyyan wa lā naṣīrā* — "but if they turn their backs — then seize them and slay them wherever you find them — and take from among them no protector and no helper": *tawallaw* — turned their backs — the commentators' gloss being uniformly *apostate-enemy reversal* (the man who openly joins the war against the believers — not mere weakness, not mere departure-depression not mere migration-refusal but active belligerency: the asbāb-bands — those who quit Madinah, then fought in the idolater ranks, or robbed who spread the terror-report or harmed the believers — being exactly this category) — *fa-khudhūhum* — seize them — the capture-decret first; *wa-qtulūhum ḥaythu wajadtumūhum* — then the war-slaying decree with its open locative (its parallel-shadow the escape-clause at the war-charging the identical wartime sentence at 4:91 — both lodged strictly in a state-of-war context) — and the second clause restoring the prohibition (wa lā walīyyan wa lā naṣīrā — the covenant-ban twice-stitched: the seal-word *naṣīr* carrying the war-climate with it: no helper-status with enemies) — and the fence around all of it being v. 90's own exception set beside it — the very next verse opening *illā alladhīna yaṣilūna ilā qawmin baynakum wa baynahum mīthāq* — cutting the sword-clause's application to *only those who neither flee to treatypeople, nor lay down arms, nor incline to peace* — so that the sūrah's whole war-canon stands: futility fidelity to Islam's covenant, the right of a two-timer to return, the ban on making allies of enemies — and the sword reserved exactly for the man who meets you on the battlefield — the classical jurists of every century lodging their summaries in the same four-verse block (vv. 89–92 being the standing source-file of the war-law: enemy engagement — peace-rights — accidental-of-believer compensation; the canon thereby kept under one liability: whoever fights you, fight; whoever inclines to peace, incline; whoever wrongs unwittingly, make reparation; everything else, leave to God).

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:90

> **Save those who seek refuge with a people with whom you have a covenant, or those who come to you with hearts reluctant to fight you, or to fight their own people. Had God willed, He could have given them authority over you, and then surely they would have fought you. So if they withdraw from you, and do not fight you, and offer peace, God allows you no way against them.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Illā Alladhīna Yaṣilūna ilā Qawmin Baynakum wa Baynahum Mīthāq: The Treaty-Harbor Exception**

The sword-clause of v. 89 collapses, by God's own hand, at its very rim: *illā alladhīna yaṣilūna ilā qawmin baynakum wa baynahum mīthāq* — "save those who reach a people between whom and you there is a covenant": *yaṣilūna* — from w-ṣ-l — to join, connect, arrive-at (the joining-word chosen deliberately over mere flight — the man *re-anchors himself*: an accession to the covered body); and *mīthāq* — the weighty covenant — from w-th-q — firm-binding trust — the Book's heaviest covenant-noun (its seal-pattern: mīthāq everywhere marks bonds God Himself witnesses — 4:21's marriage-mīthāq — 33:7's prophets' mīthāq — and now the nation-of-madīnah's treaty network) — and the asbāb-knowers telling the Sīrah-application which taught the ummah for all centuries (al-Ṭabarī; al-Wāḥidī): certain retractors of Madinah fled to confederate tribes under treaty with the Prophet (the Khuzāʿah-figures and their like in the standing accounts) — and thereby *re-crossed into immunity by treaty*, not by Islam — the covenant's umbrella sheltering even those beneath it who were themselves outside the ummah: the signature of the emerging polity's covenant order now covering third parties whose contractual friendship extends its own shadow (with the commentators' standing legal point from it: the mīthāq-people acquire war-cover as being *of your covenant* — reaching them = acceding to covenant-security, whoever the refugee is) — the Book thereby building into its war-law the whole asylum-door forever: the man who escapes the believers' sanction by attaching himself to your *friends* becomes untouchable for the friends' sake — not because his own past is pardoned but because *his sanctuary is God's ratified architecture*.

**Aw Jāʾūkum Ḥaṣirat Ṣudūruhum an Yuqātilūkum: The Constricted-Chest Men**

The second safe-conduct is stranger still — God's own profiling of a soul: *aw jāʾūkum ḥaṣirat ṣudūruhum an yuqātilūkum aw yuqātilū qawmahum* — "or those who come to you, their chests constricted against fighting you — or fighting their own people": *ḥaṣirat* — from ḥ-ṣ-r — compressed, narrowed, hemmed-in (the Quranic root of *iḥṣār* — besiegement — and of ḥaṣīr 17:29's "make not thy hand tied to thy neck"; here the inward siege of a conscience) — *ṣudūr* — chests — the Book's seat-of-heart vessel (the soul's chamber where conviction and hesitation wrestle — 3:154's "their own souls whispering: \'we have no share in the affair\'"; 6:125's breast opened-to-Islam vs. narrowed-to-unbelief) — the verse thereby profiling Madinah's strangest war-casualty: a man from that scattered band who comes back *too bridled for war on either side* — too much at war with himself — whose chest speaks: *I will not fight you, and I cannot bear to fight my own kinsmen* either — the middle-man of tribal war, no longer Muslim enough to battle for Madinah nor idolater enough to battle against it — and heaven itself licenses him, in his very paralysis, a protected status: *no war applied against the man whose constricted breast refuses either way* (Ibn Kathīr's summary being the standing interpretation: *"kāfūn" — abstainers — neither with you nor against you; and some of that band indeed belonged to this kind*) — and the entire juristic tradition of Islam's laws-of-war drawing from this clause its standing neutrality-doctrine: the unbelligerent non-citizen, the man in the neutral zone, is *immune in himself*, treaty or no treaty — his own torn breast being its own protected charter.

**Fa-in Iʿtazalūkum fa-Lam Yuqātilūkum wa Alqaw Ilaykumu al-Salam fa-Mā Jaʿala Allāhu Lakum ʿAlayhim Sabīlā: No Way Against the Peace-Inclined**

Then the ending formula — one of the war-law canon's capstone-sentences: *fa-in iʿtazalūkum fa-lam yuqātilūkum wa alqaw ilaykumu al-salam fa-mā jaʿala Allāhu lakum ʿalayhim sabīlā* — "so if they withdraw from you, and fight you not, and cast peace toward you — God assigns you no way against them": three conditions, one after another — *iʿtazala* — withdrawal (they disengage — the step-out-of-war itself); *lam yuqātilūkum* — actual cessation-of-hands (the un-fired side of the line); *wa alqaw ilaykumu al-salm* — they cast *al-salm* — peace, surrender-truce — the peace-token thrown (from s-l-m, the same root-ground as islām and salām both — the Book's word-choice deliberately threading the truce of warring parties into the peace-vocabulary of heaven — war-ending itself as a kind of islām-gesture) — and the verdict: *fa-mā jaʿala Allāhu lakum ʿalayhim sabīlā* — *God appointed for you no way against them*: *sabīl* again — the way-lexicon of the sūrah closing twice in two verses (v. 88's *no way found for the astray*; v. 90's *no way opened against the peace-offerer*) — the possibilities of warfare's last words being simply a legal blockade from above (with its sister-charge the Book's other half-capitol at 8:61 — "and if they incline to peace, incline thou to it, and trust in God" — matching this verse into the standing peace-doctrine) — and the commentators' comprehensive war-canon seals here the sūrah's block: agitators *can be judged*; active enemies *can be fought*; but every gate of exit must stand open throughout — treaty-cover, constricted chests, peace-casting — so that no believer's sword ever reaches the no-fight zones heaven drew around its own people — with al-Qurṛṭubī's summary, never bettered, lodging the whole: *the battle-line is God's, the peace-doors are wider than men's: when men withdraw, withdraw; when they cast peace, gather it — the way-appointer Himself barred every other way.*

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:91

> **You will find others who desire to be secure from you, and secure from their own people, yet whenever they are tempted back to hostility, they are plunged back into it. So if they withdraw not from you, nor offer you peace, nor restrain their hands, then seize them and slay them wheresoever you come upon them. Against these We have given you clear warrant.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**An Yāmanū Minkum wa Yāmanū Qawmahum: The Double-Insurance Men**

The sūrah completes its four-part hypocrite-file (vv. 88–91) with the portrait of its most calculating type: *sa-tajidūna ākharīna yurīdūna an yāmanū minkum wa yāmanū qawmahum* — "thou wilt find others who desire to be secure from you — and secure from their own people": *sa-tajidūna* — taken here by the commentators as *you will find* (the mīm of continued pardon reading with the larger account — the predicate trailing Godward through the occasion-language of the verses just past); and the double-security wish is the diagnostic: safety *from both sides at once* — a man insuring himself with Madinah's covenant and with Quraysh's with his tribe's war-hospitality simultaneously (the classical asbāb-name identifying the cohort through the canonical lines, variously: Makkans who professed before the Prophet then slipped back to the idolaters — al-Ṭabarī; or — as the standing account carries it — the tribes of Asad and Ghaṭafān hovering in the neutral belt of the Arabian war-map, pitching their claim for security with both Madinah and the confederate idolaters at once) — the political anatomy exact: the ure the absolute fence-man, whose security strategy is *universalized neutrality for himself with universalized access to every side* — the man of whom al-Qurṛṭubī writes that his Islam is never open treachery — it is a ceaseless shuttle of excuses, a ceaseless shuttle between fronts.

**Fa-In Lam Yaʿtazilūkum: The Refusal Test and the Clear Warrant**

Then the verdict-clause, reverting directly to the sword-lexicon of v. 89's: *fa-khudhūhum wa-qtulūhum ḥaythu wajadtumūhum* — "seize them and slay them wherever you find them": the twin imperatives — capture, and slay — with the standing lugh note of the mastered tradition attaching them with their classical swordsman-note: *khudh* — from kh-dh — here with its (al-Rāzī's its classical and lughawi tonic — *take* with connotation of taking-by-surprise and with a certain ignominy — not the straight wrestling of open war — and *qatala* — the direct death-dealing verb — against its sister *qātala* of 4:89 and so 4:89's reciprocal struggle — the root distinction Ibn ʿAbbās noted in the tradition (qatala = killing outright; qātala = fought-with — the present verse requiring employing *q-t-l* form I — the strike delivered upon the found — against the fencing-law of 4:89-90 — there being no duel expected now — the court of hypocrisy no battlefield) — *ḥaythu wajadtumūhum* — wheresoever — the locative-latitude handed equal with its sisters (2:191's same war-license, against aggressors; 9:5's against the Qurayshi confederates against the idolater-breachers) — and the seal: *ulāʾikum jaʿalnā lakum ʿalayhim sulṭānan mubīnā* — "against these We have appointed for you a clear warrant": *sulṭān* — authority authorization (the Book's own warrant-vocabulary: sulṭān as reason-permission-license stamped by heaven — 17:33's — "We have given his heir sulṭān — but let him not exceed in slaying" — the twin guard-rail standing beside it: clear warrant *does not* abolish due-hierarchy-limits) — and *mubīn* — clarifying-patent clarifying — seal of plainness set forever against the sophistry of war-law: with the authorizers with the Authorizer in the plural We (the majesty-plural the we of divine power: the warrant-bearing voice of the omnipotent itself, never of private ambitions) — and the constative note of al-Rāzī along with the canonical houses of the canonical line: the sulṭān-mubīn of v. 91 names precisely *dispensation against the twin-insurers* — whose double-security strategy had made them worse than open enemies: open enemies fight you and thereby declare the front; these maneuver *between* fronts — so heaven wrote their exposure from above, and made their double-safety purchase null at law.

**The Soul's Own Asad and Ghaṭafān: Ibn ʿAjībah's Interior Allegory**

The tradition's mystical commentators then lift the whole file inward — Ibn ʿAjībah's typology, standing at the end of the classical line, reading Madinah's warring bands as the believer's inner stations: the v. 89 hypocrite — the man who wishes the faithful down to his own level — corresponding to *al-nafs al-ammārah bi'l-sūʾ* — the soul that commands to evil (12:53's own self description) — the soul-arm that not only fails itself but recruits others toward its fall; the v. 90 constricted-chest — to the soul torn between obedience and rebellion — *not yet delivered into war on either side*; and the v. 91 double-insurer — to the most deceitful faculty of the merely maintaining self: the inner man who propitiates both the discipline of the heart and the demands of habit — securing himself against the *sharʿ's* claims while keeping the world's affect the world's friendship on the side — the double-minded man of whom it is said his dwelling is wavering dust the inner image the Sufis borrowed from this very pericope: the *munāfiq of the breast* must be fought as Madinah fought such men — seize him and slay him wheresoever he is found — no quarter given to the faculty that prostates plays both sovereigns — with the standing rule of interior war mirrored from the civic verse: for the soul-tempter there is soli no standing treaty — every discovered corridor of excuse must be blocked once heaven's warrant is pronounced against it — the sulṭān mubīn of conscience operating through the same unambiguous, plain authorization God first stamped upon the believers at Madinah.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:92

> **It is not for a believer to slay a believer, unless it be in error. Whosoever has slain a believer in error, let him set free a believing slave and pay compensation to the victim's family, unless they remit it in charity. If he belonged to a people at war with you, but was a believer, then a believing slave is to be set free. And if he belonged to a people with whom you have a covenant, let him pay compensation to the victim's family, and let him set free a believing slave. Whosoever finds not [the means], let him fast two consecutive months as a penance from God. God is Knowing, Wise.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Wa Mā Kāna li-Muʾminin an Yaqtula Muʾminan illā Khaṭaʾan: The Believer's Blood a Protected Citadel**

Having regulated war without, the sūrah now walls blood within — with the strongest grammatical construction Arabic can build: *wa mā kāna li-muʾminin an yaqtula muʾminan* — "it is not for a believer to slay a believer": *mā kāna* — it is not, it cannot be, it stands outside the possible — the prohibition conveyed in the ontological register rather than merely the juridical (not "do not kill" but *believer-killing-believer is not among the things that are* — as the commentators put it, the sentence-lines vault the crime out of Islam's own possibility-map: cf. 49:11-12's parallel ontologizing of the ummah's vices — "let not a folk deride a folk"; 4:29's "kill not one another — God is ever Merciful unto you") — with the sole egress-clause immediately attached: *illā khaṭaʾan* — unless by error — *khaṭiʾ* — the miss, the unaimed the unaimed harm (khaṭaʾ vs. ʿamd — error vs. intent — becoming the master-contrast of Islamic penal law at its root) — and the asbāb-lines anchoring the statute in Madinah's ground: al-Ṭabarī and al-Wāḥidī's preservation naming ʿAyyāsh ibn Abī Rabīʿah, the Emigrant, who struck down a man who had once flogged him savagely in Makkah for his Islam — not knowing the man had since emigrated and embraced the faith; and its companion-report of Abū al-Dardāʾ, who struck an enemy at the battle's edge even as the shahādah was rising to his lips — a cautionary tale the tradition carries as the standing warning against killing under battle-doubt (its plenary form at 4:94 below: "say not to him who offers you peace: thou art no believer").

**Man Qatala Muʾminan Khaṭaʾan: The Fourfold Reparation Architecture**

Then the statute itself — Islamic law's standing engine of blood-repair, built in clauses like bricks: *man qatala muʾminan khaṭaʾan fa-taḥrīru raqabatin muʾminatin wa diyatun musallamatun ilā ahlihi illā an yaṣṣaddaqū* — "whosoever slays a believer by error: freeing of a believing neck, and compensation delivered to his family — unless they remit it in charity": (1) *taḥrīru raqabatin muʾminatin* — the freeing of a believing slave — *taḥrīr* from ḥ-r-r — emancipation (the verse's unbearable symmetry noted by every commentator: against one life lost, one life *granted*: the dead goes to God, the bound walks free — expiation designed as creation-symmetrical rebalancing — the Book's other stations of the same institution — 5:89's broken oaths; 58:3-4's ẓihār — all bearing the same economy: Islam's penances do not chastise the wallet; they *restore life to the bound*) — (2) *diyah* — blood-money — handed *to the victim's house* (the canon-fixing at its classical quantum in the fiqh: a hundred camels for a free man among the camel-lands, or a thousand gold dīnārs for the wealthways of the towns — al-Qurṛṭubī and al-Ṭabarī's register — payable across three years from the killer's *ʿāqilah* — his paternal kin-coop i.e., his paternal corps of kin — the remarkable social institution by which the clan shoulders its member's blood-debt, binding the whole tribe against each man's rash stroke) — (3) *illā an yaṣṣaddaqū* — unless the family gives it up in alms — *ṣadaqah*! — (the forgiveness-door, stitched into the homicide-statute itself: charity-transfiguring revenge into ad into a gift (the Book's own parallel sanction of the higher road: 2:178's "whosoever is pardoned by his brother aught, let there be fair following and payment in kindness"; 42:40's "whosoever pardons and makes reconciliation — his wage is upon God"); and (4) the error-grades elaborated by the later canon: accidental vs semi-intent — the heavy-camel the heavy diyah for the semi-intent; the dialectical-only the pure-accidental at its ordinary rate — with the death-of-dhimmī the protected non-Muslim's blood standing in its own rate-structure beneath the beneath classical fiqh's tables (the majority half-pairing versus al-Qurṛṭubī's mapping — with its foundation in the hadith-canon's own extension: "the killer is cut off from inheritance" and the covenant-man's blood parity ruled under treaty-protect the Sunnah itself commanding equal protection for ahl-al-dhimmah on the battlefield's far side of error).

**Fa-Man Lam Yajid fa-Ṣiyāmu Shahrayni Mutatābiʿayn: The Poor Man's Penance**

The statute's final mercy is its floor-clause for the destitute: *fa-man lam yajid fa-ṣiyāmu shahrayni mutatābiʿayn — tawbatan mina Allāh* — "whosoever finds not the means — then the fast of two consecutive months, as a penance from God": *lam yajid* — finds not (he who has neither slave nor camel nor kin-purse) — and the substitute: sixty successive days of fasting (its twin-station: 58:4's ẓihār-penance — and the standing fiqh-note that *consecutiveness* — mutatābiʿayn — is commanded by the verbal adjective itself: a broken sequence begins the count again — repentance requiring the unbroken dailiness of self-discipline, the body trained by the slip by the slip's own span) — *tawbatan* — as repentance — in the accusative of purpose: the fast itself is the tawbah, not a mere platform for it — fasting embodying the inward turning (the prophet's standing root the Prophet's own pairing across the whole discipline: "fasting is a shield" — Bukhārī Bukhārī 1894-5 — here arrayed not for blessing-currency but for *blood-washing*) — and the twin-attributes sealing the statute: *wa kāna Allāhu ʿalīman ḥakīmā* — "God is Knowing, Wise": Knowing — the Intent-Gauge; Wise — the Law-Fashioner (the twin-epithets returning at the sūrah's every legislated turn — vv. 17, 24, 26, 92 — listing the roll-call itself a pedagogy: every statute of this sūrah descends rooted in omniscient-exact knowing plus wise-measured shaping — never arbitrary statute) — and among the lenda among living scholars across centuries the verse has stood as Islam's first cathedral of restorative justice — no the killer of error not the killer by error faces not the sword but the *gift-duty* — a slave walks free, a family receives a kin-transmitted fortune, or the poor man's body fasts two months toward God — bloodshed met not with counter-bloodshed but with *life-restitution by every available instrument of freedom* — the ʿāqilah-system itself being one of the ancient world's earliest collective insurance-pools (prefiguring every modern no-fault compensation fund by thirteen centuries, yet grounded in covenant rather than actuarial table), and the charity-egress being the permanently open portal back to the Mercy that made the believers brothers from the first day.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:93

> **Whosoever slays a believer willfully, his recompense is Hell, abiding therein. God is wroth with him, and curses him, and prepares for him a mighty punishment.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Wa Man Yaqtul Muʾminan Mutaʿammidan: The Willful-Kill Verdict Fire**

After the mercy-arc of the error-killer's reparations, the sūrah's law-canon drops its heaviest single verse — unmatched in the Revelation for accumulated threats in one sentence: *wa man yaqtul muʾminan mutaʿammidan* — "whosoever slays a believer willfully": *mutaʿammidan* — deliberate — from ʿ-m-d — aim, column-intent (the jurists draining the word's forensic fill-in over four centuries: intent read from the instrument of assault — a sword-stroke/spear-stab reading willfulness prima facie; the wooden-cudgel the stick or whip raising the famous borderline-case across the schools — al-Ṭabarī's register of the earliest scholars splitting over whether the stick-kill is ʿamd for qiṣāṣ or quasi-ʿamd for heavy diyah — with the later canon settling the debate case-chamber by case-chamber: weapon-stock weapon-type + site of blow + kin of prior enmity + verbal context, until the Ḥanafī take — weapon-of-cutting = willfulness absolute; club-fire-immolation likewise; casual slap-of-hand seldom so) — then the sentence itself, riding out clause upon clause in a mount in a mounted escalation the tafsīr-canon calls *unparalleled in the Book*: (1) *fa-jazāʾuhu jahannamu khālidan fīhā* — "his recompense is Hell, abiding in it" (2) *wa ghaḍiba Allāhu ʿalayhi* — "God is wroth with him" (3) *wa laʿanahū* — "and He curses him" (4) *wa aʿadda lahu ʿadhāban ʿaẓīmā* — "and prepares for him a mighty chastisement" — al-Rāzī's standing enumeration: no other sin in the entire Revelation receives this quadr this fourfold stacking in one sentence — the number itself being the exclamation-mark: murder of the believer carries the full four-part sentence-roll usually reserved for the capital-offenses of spiritual treason.

**Ghaḍab, Laʿnah, ʿAdhāb ʿAẓīm: Each Threat Layer Unpacked**

The commentators then take each clause one rhetorical tier higher: *ghaḍiba* — wrath — divine anger-in-person, directly elected onto the sinner's account (a wage constrast contrast-drawn across the Book: anger upon a fallible man sticking to his obedience-league is one thing — cf. the fleeting ghaḍab-themes upon the collective — the explicit anchoring of ghaḍab against the named individual being rare and terrible); *laʿanahū* — He curses him — *laʿn* being, in the canon, expulsion-distance from Mercy — the curse spelled out (with the Book's own standing ledger-seal at its matched clause: 11:18's upon injustice-true upon the wrongdoers; 2:161's triple-ben upon those who hid those who hide truth; 3:87's upon apostates each marked by cat-L-N expulsion — the killer-of-believer now individually anchored); and *wa aʿadda lahu ʿadhāban ʿaẓīmā* — a mighty chastisement *pre-fabricated*, waited-upon (ʿaẓīm — mighty — the adjective the sūrah repeatedly reserves for the eschatological torture-scale for apocalyptic weight: v. 37's prepared abaser the prepared debasing punishment; v. 102's its own ahead-clauses; and *aʿadda* — prepared-in-advance — the commentators' note on its ominous cast: the sentence waits ready-built, not jury-too-met; the willful murderer's punishment was set before the deed, like the throne's anti-wearing no — like a drawn sword awaiting the neck).

**Khālidan Fīhā vs the Gate of Repentance: The Classical Great Debate**

Then the verse's greatest legal-theological battleground in all Islam — waged at the headland of fought out across three centuries of commentary with unusual honesty in the sources: does *khālidan fīhā* — abiding eternally — close the gate of repentance from the intentional believer-killer? The positions in order: (1) the Muʿtazilite severity — eternal Fire certain, repentance no escape (their logic: divine threat-statements bind like promises; no exception-footnote in the verse); with their standing hadith-companion in the modality: ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd's narration that the killer the would-be repentant killer flagged in a saying written across two stations a hadith handed down whereby the participant in slaying a believer comes up on the Day with "despair of God's mercy" written on his brow (Zajjāj's registry across the canon, from al-Zajjāj); (2) the jamhūr / majority answer — repentance remains open, *even here* — al-Ṭabarī's leader of the canonical majority citing the twin verse-handles 25:68-71 — the passage that recites the believers-of-mercy as those who "call not upon another god with God, nor slay the soul God has forbidden... yet whosoever does that shall meet a penalty... *save him who repents and believes and works righteousness* — for those God will exchange their evil deeds for good" — the exception clause formally the exception clause most explicitly re-opening the door to the murderer who turns — with 4:116's own general with 4:48+116's only-unforgivable = shirk lemma boxing in severity: no verse may leave a single human sin *absolutely* beyond God's accepted repentance — al-Rāzī sealing it with the kalām axiom: whatever lies beneath tawḥīd-level can be forgiven beneath tawba (cf. Muslim's own hadith-portrait of the hundred-murderer — Bukhārī 3470, Muslim 2766 — who killed ninety-nine souls, then a hundredth — and was *accepted* at last when he turned toward repentance, dying on the road; the Two Measured two angels of mercy and wrath measuring the two towns' span and finding him a hand-span closer to mercy) — the majority's solution riding then upon the precision of *khālid*: (a) abiding *so long as God's threat wills*, not flat eternity; (b) or *for one who dies unrepentant*; (c) or hyperbolic-magnification (mubālagha) to seal the deterrent (the believers are to know the crime's true its true weight — the verse itself being punishment-engineered to barricade the ummah against blood); with (3) al-Thaʿlabī's merciful mediator-scheme: worldly punishment upon the killer in execution for blood-right functions as partial atonement toward the next world (the standing hadīth on it in the Sunan of the two al-Tirmidhī's register — "the punishments of this world expiate the Muslim's account therein therein") — and the verse's balanced closing doctrine thus received through the whole classical line: *willful murder of a believer is the worst human sin after shirk — its threat-structure maximal — and still the gate marked "repentance" stays open beside the gate marked "Hell"* — the two portais the two portals facing one another over every would-be killer in every century, so that no man in rage may plead ignorance of the sentence, and no man in abasement may plead ignorance of the Mercy.

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:94

> **O you who believe, when you journey in the way of God, exercise discernment, and say not to one who offers you peace: "Thou art no believer" — seeking the ephemeral goods of the life of this world; for with God are gains in abundance. Even so were you aforetime, but God was gracious unto you; so exercise discernment; surely God is Aware of whatsoever you do.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Yā Ayyuhā Alladhīna Āmanū Idhā Ḍarabtum fī Sabīli Allāhi fa-Tabayyanū: The Discernment Command of the Road**

The war-canon completes its educe its edifice with the operational rule for borderlines: *yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū idhā ḍarabtum fī sabīli Allāhi fa-tabayyanū* — "O you who believe — when you march in the way of God — discern": *ḍarabtum* — you struck-traveled (ḍ-r-b — the Arabic idiom of road-threshing — the road struck underfoot — the march given archaic physicality) — and *fa-tabayyanū* — *exercise tabayyun* — clarify, verify, distinguish (b-y-n — the word drew down the whole verification-law of Islam: under its from it all the comment-traditions deduce the juridical war-sift — distinguish combatant from surrenderee, treaty-man from hostile, shahādah-bearer from battle-flag man) — from the asbāb-line which the tradition's own preserved the most-accepted report of the occasion being the Companions' foray upon a band of herdsmen i.e., a raiding-E the canonical account (al-Wāḥidī; al-Ṭabarī collations; Ibn Kathīr) of al-Miqdād ibn ʿAmr (or Usāmah ibn Zayd in its sannah in the Sunan's adjacent account): the Muslims overtake a man from the tribes on the way, whose gossip whose flocks he was guarding who, seeing the raid, declares *aslamtu* — "I have submitted" — and is slain notwithstanding by the pursuer, his spoils taken — whereupon the verse descends chastising: he offered you *peace* before your sword — and the seal-history standing as the tradition's own marker: the Prophet's standing rebuke to Usāmah — the hadith-engraved exchange pairing recorded at Bukhārī at Bukhārī at Muslim 96 — "You killed him after he said: *lā ilāha illa Allāh*!" — Usāmah: "It was but the fear-cry of the sword." — The Prophet: *"did you split open his heart — to know whether he said it truly or not?"* — and its echo without date until its second line — *"what will you do with lā ilāha illa Allāh, on the Day of Resurrection, when it comes?"* — Usāmah's own testimony: from that day he resolved never to strike anyone who says lā ilāha illa Allāh Usāmah: I wished I had not become Muslim before that the shock of the report being its own standing canon.

**Lā Taqūlū li-Man Alqā Ilaykumu al-Salāma Lasta Muʾminan Taghtamma bi-Ajn Tabtaghū ʿAraḍa al-Ḥayāti al-Dunyā: Spoil-Motive Invalidates Sword-Reading**

Then the prohibited utterance named: *lā taqūlū li-man alqā ilaykumu al-salāma lasta muʾminan — tabtaghū ʿarada al-ḥayāti al-dunyā* — "say not to him who casts peace toward you: Thou art no believer — pursuing the fleeting stuff of worldly life": *alqā ilaykumu al-salām* — the peace-tossing recur recurring v. 90's affection-root (al-salm — peace-casting) — and the revelation's psychology, one of its keenest dissections of warfare-justification: the slayer who overrides peace-declaration *because spoils await* does not merely make an error — the verse identifies the real engine: *tabtaghū ʿaraḍa al-ḥayāti al-dunyā* — "thou seekest the ephemeral goods of the mundane life": *ʿaraḍ* — ephemera, trade-wares, an article passing in offer (the classical turning of the root across the Book: what lies to hand to be used-up — cf. 8:67's and the worldly doctrines) — the depth-anatomy: booty rewrites the operational diagnosis: if the only evidence you slay him is his flocks and his camel-goods, *you did not verify a threat; you wanted his goods* — the verse erecting the standing prohibition of *motivated verification-failure*: where men define threat with their purse — classic with the Book's standing cousin-law confirming the same engine across the whole canon-family of battle-abuse texts (9:5's treaty-exception clause; 60:8's "God forbids you not those who fought you not in religion"; plus the great canonical import of 4:94 into the law of combatant-safety: al-salām or shahādah uttered at sword-point grants *safety presumptively* — the battle ʿamal the operative presumption shifts: certify later, strike never).

**Fa-ʿinda Allāhi Maghānamu Kathīrah: The Spoils at God's Treasury, Not at Men's Throats**

Against that petty spoil-lust the verse holds up its mirroring counter-treasury: *fa-ʿinda Allāhi maghānam kathīrah* — "with God are gains in abundance": *maghānam* — spoils-plural — from gh-n-m — war-gain-word itself (the Book's own classic term for godly war-boo for warfare spoils — 8:69's "enjoy what you take in ghanīmah as lawful and good"; 8:41's khums-code; and the exact antithesis set out: spoil-eyes drawn down lift the spoil-desire from roadside corpses from roadside flock-keeping — the war-economy the sūrah now draws as exact antithesis: the wealth-fields of heaven's own treasury where gains exist in *plural-abundance* — kathīrah — the plenty hanging from God, whom no raid limits that no raid can corner) — then the sūrah's tender reversal: kadhālika kuntum min qablu fa-manna Allāhu ʿalaykum* — "so were you aforetime — but God was gracious to you": you — the Madinan fighters — were yourselves once like that herdsman — a despised, poor, hidden, weak — Mohammed before the war-booty era, hiding your shahādahs from persecutor-swords in Makkah (cf. the sūrah's own prior memory at v. 75 — the mustaḍʿafūn;
