The sūrah's judicial-verse now turns its gaze from the Prophet's washed bench to the clamoring clan — and the pronoun's change carries the drama: *hāʾ antum hāʾulāʾi jādaltum ʿanhum fī al-ḥayāti al-dunyā* — "there you are! — you! — you pleaded for them in the worldly life": the emphatic double-marking (the commentators' standing note: *hāʾ antum* — behold, you-yourselves — the particle of astonished rebuke — heaven's address-formal doubling to the crowd, with *hāʾulāʾi* — these-here — pointing at them like a bailiff pointing at the the meaning: the astonishment-form of a court-dramatur the address-grammar is itself theatrical — behold *you* — professional pleaders-at-law of Ṭuʿmah's kin) — and the address now in the *plural*, not the singular — the standing grammatical consensus (al-Ṭabarī, al-Rāzī, al-Qurṛṭubī): vv. 105–107's commands were singular, to the Prophet; v. 109's blast opens upon the *clan-pleaders* — the whole contingent of Banū Ẓafar who had lobbied the Prophet's court — name heaven addressing the supporting attorneys directly — with the charge named exactly: *jādaltum ʿanhum* — you pled-l you disputed on their behalf (the jidāl-verb of v. 107 again — the sūrah's own triplication: 105's khaṣīm-address to the Prophet, 107's general ban — now 109's factual indictment against the men who were in fact doing it) — and the key-limiting phrase *fī al-ḥayāti al-dunyā* — *in the worldly life*: their whole advocacy-arsenal — clan-honor, press-grief press-gang press-party assembled tears, threats, standing-in public shame-play and genealogical appeal — having exactly one jurisdiction: *this world's hearing*.

**Fa-Man Yujādilu Allāha ʿAnhum Yawma al-Qiyāmah: The Unrepresented at the True Assize**

Then the after-life after-bench question that dissolves every earthly bar- every plea-bench of men: *fa-man yujādilu Allāha ʿanhum yawma al-qiyāmati* — "but who will plead with God on their behalf on the Day of Resurrection?": the interrogative *man* — who in its peculiar legal-torque its taunt-force: earthly advocacy is a transferable profession any bar of men hires or commands its orators — but the Final Court binds every man to his own arraignment to his own dossier (the Book's own counter-verdicts already lodged against future against every worldly bar: 2:123's "fear a day when no soul shall avail another aught"; 2:254's "before a day comes when there is neither bargaining, nor friendship, nor intercession"; 6:51's "they have, besides Him, neither protector nor intercessor"; 19:87's famous 19:87 — "none shall own intercession save he who hath taken a covenant with the Merciful") — the commentators then spelling v. 109's unique position: *advocacy before God is different not in degree but in kind* — no defense-table, no counsel, no pleading-as-profession before the All-Knowing (with the rank-of-God with its only remaining channel standing under covenant-law itself: *shafāʿah bi-idhn* — intercession under leave — 2:255's "who is it that intercedes with Him save by His leave?"; its classic 21:28's "they intercede not save for him with whom He is pleased"; and 20:109's "on that day intercession avails naught save for one to whom the Merciful grants leave, and whose word He approves" — intercession existing only as *God-commissioned speaking*, never as hired tongue) — with the cl the classical reflection from al-Qurṛṭubī and Ibn Kathīr: the Ṭuʿmah-clan canvassers discovered this on that very day on that very night — that all the lobbying-strength of a clan cannot carry a case beyond the world's lobby; and the injustice framed by night collapsed the moment revelation moved the moment heaven itself sat on the case.

**Aw Man Yakūnu ʿAlayhim Wakīlan: Who Will Be Their Trustee-Guardian?**

Then the climax-question pairing with its seal: *aw man yakūnu ʿalayhim wakīlan* — "or who will be for them a guardian-disposer": *wakīl* returning once again from the sūrah's own earlier from the sūrah's own perh the lexeme of vv. 81, 83 81 and 132's wakīl-seals — attorney-trustee by divine appointment — placed now in interrogative-taunt: who will arrange for them on that Day what their clan-arrangements arranged here with the commentators' standing reflection crossing over crossing to the standing principle of of 74:38 — "every soul is pledged for what it has earned" — and 19:95 — "and each of them shall come to Him on the Day of Resurrection, alone" — the whole eschatological infrastructure stripped of defense-teams (with the enduring al-Rāzī-like gloss final with the standing comment-canon's plainest sum-up, found in the tafsīr-houses ever since: earthly courts = persuasion-halls; the final Court = clarity-hall; in the hall of clarity the file is already written, already witnessed by hand and by hands, feet, skin (36:65 — "We seal their mouths today; their hands speak to Us, and their feet bear witness to what they earned"; 24:24's tongues-hands-feet testimony; 41:20-22's skin-witness) — so a wakīl-of-earth's art has no hone no task to perform) — and the sūrah's legal-canon thereby ending its advocacy-clinic with its own final signature: *pleading exists in this world's corridors of prestige, lineage, and eloquence; on the Day of Gathering only God's own advocacy exists — and only the trustworthy need a trustee* — hence back at v. 105's same sanctified charge: the believers' courts meanwhile should mimic the Final Hall as far as truth serves as far as flesh allows: no advocacy for betrayers, even under clan-tears — since the Last Judge will not be swayed either, and the duty of every earthly bench is to be the shadow of His.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:110

> **Whosoever does evil or wrongs himself, and then seeks forgiveness of God, he will find God Forgiving, Merciful.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Wa Man Yaʿmal Sūʾan Aw Yaẓlim Nafsahu: Evil-Work and Self-Wrong, the Two Formal Doors**

The court-block's arraignments close at last with the one door heaven itself leaves open: *wa man yaʿmala sūʾan aw yaẓlim nafsahu* — "whosoever does evil or wrongs himself": the two terms being the tradition's standing predicate-pair for the whole sin-map: (1) *sūʾ* — evil — the generic ill-work (from s-w-ʾ — badness itself — the Book's standing term for deeds that foul the ledger — with the commentators distinguishing its register: sūʾ the wide net — every transgression, small or great minor or major — and (2) *yaẓlim nafsahu* — wrongs his own self — the sūrah's now-established reflexive formula (v. 107's yakhtānūna anfusahum; v. 111's yakṣib ithman fa-innamā yakṣibuhu ʿalā nafsihi — the self-dealt the deal-self grammar recurring in this block like the tolling of a bell: all wrongdoing finalizes upon the doer — the object-noun carrying the doer's own name) — with the majority rolling the pair as two-fold as a rhetorical doubling for breadth (wrong done and wrong sustained: act of perpetration plus the self-damage of perpetration) — al-Ṭabarī's own reading al-Ṭabarī's particular elegance: the two phrases mapping the treacherous thief and his pleading-clan alike — Ṭuʿmah's sūʾ lying in the theft-and-plant; the clan's his own ẓulm-on-himself lying in leading the accused lying in recruiting his clan to campaign for the frame-up the hadith-comment register the Ṭabarī-register expanding the pair over both sinner and defender, exactly as the block's own final as the commentary tradition's overall as Ibn Kathīr summarized it: the promise is extended both to the treacherous wrongdoers and to those who would wrongfully seek to defend them.

**Thumma Yastaghfir Allāh Yajid Allāha Ghafūran Raḥīmā: The Forgiving-Sequence Undertaken**

Then the protocol — exactly the two-move rite: *thumma yastaghfir Allāh* — "then seeks forgiveness of God": *thumma* — then — the sequence-particle (the sin first, the istighfār second — God's merciful grammar never the grammar omitting the commentators' standing subtlety: thumma may denote either chronological sequence — the natural order of remorse — or the standing hadith-grammar of or an allowance that God's prerogative takes place *after* the deed has occurred, not in place not in sanction of it — never before it) — *yastaghfiru* — seeks forgiveness — the verb-form active (the standing reflection: forgiveness must be *asked*, not merely presumed — heaven's mercy being free but not *draftable*: the beloved hadith-teaching at its station the classic hadith at Muslim 2759 — "by Him the Prophet's own emblem: *by Him in Whose hand is my soul, did you not sin, God would do away with you and bring a people who do sin and seek His forgiveness, and He would forgive them"* — Muslim 2749 — with its tonic pair with the Prophet's own plenary seal of tawbah-petitioning: "all the children of Adam are sinners — and the best of sinners are the repenters" — Tirmidhī 2499, Ibn Mājah 4251) — and the respond response-verb following with symmetry poetic to letter-place with the symmetry the whole tafsīr-canon cherishes: *yajid Allāha ghafūran raḥīman* — "he finds God Forgiving, Merciful": *yajida* — he *finds* — from w-j-d — discovery (the commentators' standing awe at this one verb's choice: the seeker does not merely obtain is not informed of pardon — he *finds* — forgiveness offered standing already-present — God antecedent-positioned at the very station of the seeker's arrival — likened in the tradition drawing it against the wording image the standing comment-image: (al-Qushayrī's register among the Sufi schools: istighfār as petition for what God *already has* — the finding-verb lifting forgiveness from contingent-decree to everlasting-attribute — the pardon- the Pre-Eternal turning where the repentant raises his hands, he finds that God had preceded his uplifted hands by forever) — with the coupling returning: *ghafūran raḥīman* — Forgiving, Merciful — the block's own closing twin-attribute its own closing attributes — v. 106's identical pair — the block's mercy-frame thus completely arched: judge commanded to istighfār — v. 106 — treacherous promised pardon on the same rite — v. 110 — each receiving the same attribute-guarantee — Ghafūr upon the upon the ledger, Raḥīm upon the seeker's road thereafter.

**Whom the Verse Addresses: The Canon of Tawbah upon a Treachery-File**

The commentators' lasting treatment thereby widens v. 110 into the standing tawbah-canon: (1) its subject — *man* — whosoever — unrestricted by sin-class (even the frame-up-artist, even the night-conspirator, even the man who planted evidence on the innocent); (2) its condition — istighfār — and the classical theology at once unfolds the operation beyond its mere prayer to the required its standing definition from the hadith-canon: true istighfār carries its three its classical shaping the standing teaching-shape of the classical shaping: regret (nadm) — cessation (iqlāʿ — immediate stopping) — resolve (ʿazm — a binding resolve against return) — with right-restitution (radd al-maẓālim) wherever a third party's rights stand — and here the tafsīr-canon's own standing note exactly fitting the Ṭuʿmah-block: had the thief sought forgiveness *with* restitution — the planted the framed victim exonerated the framed Jew publicly cleared, the armor returned — repentance would have been live; without it, the istighfār-voice stands alone as mere petition as mere affecting as mere word-work; and (3) its certainty — *yajida* — the verb's own performative pledge (like the standing exegetical placed side-by-side with 39:53's — "O My servants who have been prodigal against their own souls — despair not of God's mercy — God forgives all sins — He is the Forgiving, the Merciful") — thereby ending the sūrah's whole judicial affair of Ṭuʿmah ibn Ubayriq not with condemnation but with its final standing syllabus of hope: cheat crimes wrought by night, pled for by clans, and exposed by revelation all stand under the same final clause: *whosoever wrongs — let him, by the rite of two moves, seek the Forgiving — and he will find.* The eloquent pleas of men were shut; the door of God's finding remained open — and that is the sentence under which the entire canopy of the entire sūrah-block takes its rest finally.

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:111

> **And whosoever commits a sin, commits it only against his own soul, and God is Knowing, Wise.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Wa Man Yaksib Ithman fa-Innamā Yaksibuhu ʿalā Nafsihi: The Recoil-Law**

The court-block lays down, at its doctrinal close, the single sentence that sums its whole ontology: *wa man yaksib ithman fa-innamā yaksibuhu ʿalā nafsihi* — "whosoever earns a sin — earns it only against his own soul": *yaksib* — earns, acquires — the commerce-verb the Book applies to deeds (with the standing equivalence: every act a purchase; every ledger-opening a customer accounted — good or evil contracted-in contracted-in by its owner by its owner forever) — *ithm* — sin — from ā-th-m — the standing guilt-word — and the verse's hammer-clause — *fa-innamā yaksibuhu ʿalā nafsihi* — the store the same verb repeating with the same sin as its object, now pointed squarely at *his own soul* (the comment-canon savoring its doubled gent its doubled form: the sin enters the world's stage aimed outward — at property, at brother, at victim; by the time the account closes, the store the gilt staking the sin returns home — lodged not against its intended target but against its engineer — Ṭuʿmah's armor-job Ṭuʿmah's false frame its standing illustration direct: the armor stolen rests eventually in legitimate hands or punishment; the *earning* stays not is stored stays charged on the engineer remains charged upon the engineer of the frame) — with the corollary indicated by the attribute-pair — *wa kāna Allāhu ʿalīman ḥakīmā* — "God is Knowing, Wise": Knowing — the ledger-keeper of every earned account; Wise — the Measurer apportioning every sin's return-home with precision (v. 106's own two-attribute architecture again — sovereignty-by-knowledge plus sentence-by-wisdom — the block's final seals summing the court-chapter in the same twin-name brand with which it opened).

**The Moral Reflexivity of the Book: All Arrows Come Home**

The comment tradition then widens the sentence into the Book's standing law of moral physics — the mufassirūn's long-standing register: deeds returning to their doers like thrown like payloads that follow the curved the standing lineage of parallel the standing rolls the canon gathers: 2:9's — "they seek to deceive God and the believers — and they deceive none but themselves, though they perceive not" — the hypocrite-file's own verdict rolled upon Ṭuʿmah's clan; 3:69's — "a party of the People of the Book wish to lead you astray — and they lead astray none but themselves, though they perceive not"; 6:123's — "and thus We have placed in every city its greatest criminals that they may plot therein — and they plot not save against themselves, though they perceive not" — the parallel of the Book's of the Book's towns' plotters the very standing formula of deceit recoil; and the direct twins at 10:23 — "your insolence is against yourselves"; 29:6 — "whosoever strives, strives only for himself"; 35:18 — "no laden soul bears the load of another" — its thoroughfare in the hands of the commoner and the standing standing the final return-in-itself at 17:7: "if you do good, you do good to yourselves; and if you do evil — to them."— no — final at 17:7 — "if you do good, you do good for your own selves; and if you do evil — to the same they rebound to to the same — to your selves also" — the Book's moral grammar everywhere uniform: God's essence removed from harm beyond beyond touch (the comment-line's constant annotation: the King cannot be robbed — the Infinity cannot be lightened — His creation's whole drama plays itself out inside the creature's account — God harmed by nothing; so sin *must* circle home) — with the Book's own elevation of the reciprocal of the principle above it: the Book elsewhere elsewhere teaches that even the offense against neighbor ends up, at its final accounting, *one's own* — for the other party's due is squared in this world or by God's rectification at the next — while the *engineer's* the only un-rectifiable the standing theologian-commentary: the victim will be compensated either judicially or eschatologically; the single irreparable the single line that never closes at some counter — is the sin's own entry *against the doer's soul* — with al-Rāzī's measuring postscript all commentators eventually borrow: the doctrine's corrective toward law and law-and-character: since the deed's damage-home is the doer himself, justice turns educational turning reformative long before punitive: every conviction at court a *rescue-doctrine* — the convict being snatched from the company's from company of the one thing which would otherwise devour him — the standing sufi-saying form the standing sufi echo: "the sinner's prison is inside his own being; the sentence at the Qaḍī's gate is but mercy-mis mercy-in-uniform mercy in the shape of handcuffs — breaking the sin's refuge before it fullyажи fully occupied fully takes up residence."

**Knowing, Wise: The Seals of the Reflex-Law**

Then the two names upon its closing — a seal the sūrah has now stamped repeatedly (v. 24; 26; 92; 104; 111): Knowing — the always-aware witness of the sin's whole passage (no guilt unwitnessed unwitnessed from its night-conception to its day-manifestation); Wise — the legi the legislator of corresponding returns the legislator whose matching of moral act to moral consequence is never caprice but built-in calibration — and with this seal the whole Ṭuʿmah-file ends upon its own theological syllogism: the innocent target was never really looted of innocence (his trial purified him); the thief never really kept his loot (his earning weighed him down); the clan never really rescued its own of it their own clansman (their pleading only loaned him toward greater account toward heavier owed sums) — and the Judge Himself, watching all, was never in doubt — with the tradition's own long-standing sum-up of the episode writing itself since the earliest tafsīr (Ibn Kathīr's prayer its own standing rec the standing lesson-list): (1) no aid for treachery; (2) no plea against evidence; (3) no night-panel sealed against the Encompassing; (4) no sinner but sins at his own chest; and (5) no closure of repentance while breath remains — the sūrah's courtroom-block now sealed complete, the bench washed, ledgers balanced, and heaven's own verdict written over the whole affair: *whosoever earns a sin — earns it only against his own soul*.

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:112

> **And whosoever commits an offense or a sin, and then casts it upon one who is innocent, bears the burden of calumny and a manifest sin.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Wa Man Yaksib Khaṭīʾatan Aw Ithman: Khaṭīʾah and Ithm — The Two Wings of Wrong**

The block's criminal-law chapter reaches its climax-verse — the precise indictment of the planted-evidence crime: *wa man yaksib khaṭīʾatan aw ithman* — "whosoever earns an offense — *or* a sin": the two nouns the commentators never tire of distinguishing — the house the classical positions set out forever in the rolls: (1) *khaṭīʾah* the *unaimed* wrong, *ithm* the deliberate (al-Ṭabarī: the *error-class* versus the *intent-class* — so the verse sweeps both: frame-work fain slip and willful malfeasance alike); (2) *khaṭīʾah the smaller*, *ithm the greater* (al-Rāzī and al-Zamakhsharī: the canon of degrees); (3) and the favorite pairing of the schools — *khaṭīʾah the self-harming sin* (victimless trespass, its harm looping home only — v. 111's own class); *ithm the neighbor-harming sin* (harm done outward — injustice with a victim) — the fine distinction then deployed at once into the verse's larger architecture: the man plans the man being profiled the man's work the man planted the burglary Ṭuʿmah's theft being ithm of the first order (property taken from another's wall) — and the *cast-upon-innocent* phase being its second-order harm: the doubled wrong stacked upon the first.

**Thumma Yarmi Bihi Barīʾan: Casting It Upon the Innocent**

Then the definition the whole ummah thereafter uses as the legal monster's taxonomic marker: *thumma yarmi bihi barīʾan* — "then casts it upon an innocent": *yarmi* — throws-hurls (from r-m-y — the project the missile-verb — the Book's own path-of-accusatory its standing vocabulary of slander and stone alike: accusation as projectile — 24:4's standing statute- the sā its standing r-m-y kin the standing statute of the slander at 24:4 — "those who fling accusation at chaste women" — with yarmi bihi exactly describing the *physical transfer* of blame — the blame projected outward like a spear from its thrower's breast onto the chest of a quiet quiet stranger) — *barīʾ* — innocent — from b-r-ʾ — cleared, immune, guiltless — the standing Book-word upon the uninvolved (Joseph's own exclamation — its Book-friends: its cases: Ṣāliḥ to his people Ṣāliḥ's word to his people — 26:216 — "I am innocent of what you do"; Joseph — 12:53's standing the standing self-declaration of the blameless in the Book) — with the standing exemplum before every generation: Ṭuʿmah casting the armor-theft upon the Jew of Madinah upon a blameless son of the community — the innocent neighbor chosen precisely because his faith-group could not — in the old tribal arithmetic — fight back the comment-doctors noting the predator's selection-rule: the frame-up always targets the *least-defended* — hence the verse's own gut-punch verdict upon it — not just a sin-pattern but twice its weight not double sin but sin *squared compounded*.

**Faqad iḥtamala Buhtānan wa Ithman Mubīnā: Buhtān Plus Manifest Sin**

Then the compounded verdict — the verse's own two-sword two-clause: *faqad iḥtamala buhtānan wa ithman mubīnā* — "he bears the burden of buhtān — and a manifest sin": *iḥtamala* — lifted-carried (from ḥ-m-l — burden-bearing — the standing scape-verb the standing cargo-verb of the Book — the sinner *loading* — 6:31's "they shall bear their burdens on their backs" — the Book's metaphorical yield its standing standing the standing dooms the Book's standing metaphor: every account earned is a back-pack— strapped on strapped; nothing is finally *thrown* — the and the pivotal irony: the caster thought he had *shifted* his burden; the verse names the truth — he has *doubled it*) — *buhtān* — calumny, false-accusation-from-amazement (from b-h-t — to stupefy — the standing scholarly gloss: a lie so shocking the hearer is stunned — the carrying the framing of the innocent so beyond plausible that the teller himself buhtān being slander-armed with the shock-of-believability — al-Rāzī's standing take: buhtān here the *shame in this world* — the exposure-disgrace — while *ithm mubīn* the *manifest sin* is the punishment-file at the next world — the two-directional blast of the of the one deed: the worldly shame plus the other-worldly doom) — and *ithman mubīnā* — manifest sin — *mubīn* — patent — the same clarity-seal as v. 101's enemy-attribute (the Book's own frequency its standing modifier from the Ṭuʿmah-block: 4:50's — "look how they forge lies against God — and sufficient is it as a manifest sin" — with its own closer siblings — 4:20 and v.112's own flange its meaning: sin so plain no interpretation can wash it) — the comment-doctors then summing the whole incident in the standing doctrine of composite crime: (1) the theft was ithm; (2) the false the hurl was buhtān upon an innocent — thereby ithm mubīn of the highest rank; (3) with the standing fiqh-consequence: the sinner bears *four* accounts: stolen property (rolling restitution-plus-penalty), the blood the frame-up's wrong to the innocent (qadhf-adjacent the sūrah's own slander-c actionable beneath the Book's slander-laws), the clan's misled advocacy counted each pleader becoming a co-load-carrier-by-advocacy (the standing consequence within the block: each pleader *participated* the moment he argued without knowledge), and the world's own fourth burden upon the no — and finally the standing soteriological closure of the block — that even this otherwise even this doubled even this doubled accumulation waits beneath v. 110's open gate — the verse itself placing its own its own final fixing of the moral mechanism never to forget: every burden cast upon the innocent *re-lands* upon the caster — the armorer the caster stepping forward from behind his frame into God's own court — with the standing comment-side the standing side-chapel handed to all school-teachers of Islamic law: *the real fact of false accusation is not deception — it is mere loan: the sin is lent to the victim's account for a day — then returns with interest* — mubīn.

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:113

> **Were it not for God's Bounty toward thee, and His Mercy, a party of them would have plotted to lead thee astray; but they lead astray only their own souls, and they can do thee no harm in the least. God has sent down unto thee the Book and Wisdom, and has taught thee what thou knewest not; and God's Bounty toward thee is great indeed.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Wa Lawlā Faḍlu Allāhi ʿAlayka wa Raḥmatuhu: Bounty-and-Mercy Now Over the Judge Himself**

The block seals its case with heaven's own receipt — the verse whose readers never miss its tenderness: *wa lawlā faḍlu Allāhi ʿalayka wa raḥmatuhu la-hammat ṭāʾifatun minhum an yuḍillūk* — "were it not for God's Bounty upon thee, and His Mercy, a party of them had resolved to lead thee astray": *lawlā* — were-it-not — the sūrah's own rescue-formula returning (v. 83's lawlā faḍlu Allāhi upon the ummah — v. 113's upon the Prophet — the Book's own paired protective-clauses: lawlā guarding first the community from the rumor-surge, lawlā guarding now the Prophet from the clan-lobby) — and *la-hammat* — had resolved, had firmly intended — from h-m-m — settled-resolve (the commentators' standing nuance: not mere verbal lobby but *deliberated plot* — the intent-arm the stage at which design sits poised in the heart the comment-line: hamm being the yard hamm being the settled pre-decision — the plan had matured to the very rim of execution to the threshold — had God's intervention not snapped its fingers shut) — *an yuḍillūk* — to lead *thee* astray (the singular-pronoun astonishment the comment-canon never omits: they had hoped to mislead the receiving-of-revelation himself — thereby making every subsequent case every later case of theirs beyond him — make him the first believer their pleas would have snared, then the entire ummah through him) — with the standing exegesis carrying it to its ʿiṣmah-anchoring: the verse becoming in the theology-houses one of the standing proofs of prophetic inerrancy (since had the Prophet been error-capable in his receptions in his ruling-aspects the lobby would have stood a chance — and because hatred-clans because Heaven prevented and heaven's note here reads as promotion rather than insinuation: the Judge was *protected*, and there was never any fear of never completed rout never completed deviance — with the classical commentary winding with the classical commentary carrying its standing distinction: their plot threatened his *judging* (a lane a lane of merely human decision perhaps-of-mixing where inquiry hung pending) — not his *prophethood* — the twofold the two-doctrine anatomy being: God intervenes to spare the Prophetic court from even the suspicion of the of misjudgment).

**Wa Mā Yuḍillūna illā Anfusahum: Astray-Work Recoiling, the Block's Reflex-Law Again**

Then the swift counter-verdict — the sūrah's now-signed signature: *wa mā yuḍillūna illā anfusahum* — "and they lead astray none but themselves": the very clause of the standing recoil-law (v. 111's yaksibuhu ʿalā nafsihi; 2:9's and 3:69's standing twins; the structure the structure the Book now stamps three times in one block — Ṭuʿmah's own deliverance-st deliverment work Ṭuʿmah's own fruit being the standing footnote: exposed, disowned by his own disowned even by his clan at the end, fled to Makkah, apostatized, crushed beneath a falling wall with the maxim with the Quraysh jeer with a demon whom the commentators a wall falling upon him in the night (the standing report the tafsīr-books carry from Ibn Isḥāq's registers: Ṭuʿmah saying at the end, "it is Muḥammad's curse on me"), the plot-of-astray boomeranging back upon its porter upon its bearer's neck with perfect with the career-completing recoil the sūrah of court and night-parlor now seals as standing law) — followed by the relief-clause — *wa mā yaḍurrūnaka min shayʾ* — "and they harm thee not in the least" (its Book-family of its standing family: 3:120's "their enmity their ill-will 3:176's "let not those grievance those who vie in disbelief grieve thee — they will not hurt God in anything"; 5:41's the 3:177's "they will not harm God in anything"; the Prophet-shield clause's own the standing variants: harm can reach *man* only where God permits its the same cf. 3:120's 3:186's — "you shall surely hear much injury from those given the Book before you — but if you are patient and God-fearing — that is of the firm resolve of affairs" — the sovereignty-math then rolled into the verdict: a thousand lobbyists in every century — yet the mawlā-protected the protected not subject to the the protected receiver of heaven never moved an iota).

**Wa Anzala Allāhu ʿAlayka al-Kitāba wa al-Ḥikmah wa ʿAllamaka Mā Lam Takun Taʿlam: Knowledge as the Greatest Bounty**

Then the enumeration rising into the sūrah's eulog its own loftest its own loftiness: *wa anzala Allāhu ʿalayka al-kitāba wa al-ḥikmata wa ʿallamaka mā lam takun taʿlam* — "and God has sent down upon thee the Book and Wisdom — and has taught thee what thou knewest not": the twain-pair the Book-and-Wisdom dyad (its standing Book-roll of prophetic grants: 2:129's Abrahamic prayer — "our Lord — send among them a messenger from themselves, reciting to them Thy signs and teaching them the Book and Wisdom and purifying them"; 2:231's charging 2:151's; 3:164's; 4:54's; 5:110's; 33:34's; 62:2's — the dyad reading thereafter: the Kitāb the revealed text and the Ḥikmah the lived-meaning — wisdom as reach-deeper-than-text meaning-with-wisdom the Sunnah-flesh upon the Book-bone per the classical takings) — with al-Rāzī's famous honour his own laurel al-Rāzī's standing judgment placed here: knowledge-of-revelation being the noblest of God's good of God's gifts — because among all bounties of the Exalted per his dictum: it is the noblest of bounty-and-virtues al-Rāzī: *this is the plainest proof that knowledge is the noblest of the bounties* — since God named singles out knowledge-gift when He magnifies telescopes His immense favors into one clause (its terminal magnify telescope-clause here: *wa kāna faḍlu Allāhi ʿalayka ʿaẓīman* — "and God's Bounty upon thee is great indeed") — with the standing theological capida the standing doctrinal close of the whole judicial-block rolling forward out of it: the Judge-of-men received the Law — the Law-Book — Wisdom — and hidden-knowledge — so that so that court-floors could never host lobby-rule lobby-laws — hands and with the prayer-house in the instant no — and with the annexed the account summed at last: what the Prophet's court feared most — error at the gates of its own compassionate openness of its own openness — heaven dissolved by direct teaching — hence the tradition's standing maxim stemming from v. 113 to the end of ages: *judgment must feed on God's showing — and every good judge is, after the pattern of the Prophet, first of all a man taught*.

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:114

> **There is no good in most of their secret converse, save for him who enjoins charity or kindness or reconciliation between men. And whosoever does that, seeking God's Good Pleasure, We shall grant him a great reward.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Lā Khayra fī Kathīrin min Najwāhum: The Moral Audit of Whisper-Traffic**

Into the wake of the night-plot exposure (v. 108's bayyata, the planted armor, the lobbying clan) the sūrah writes its standing law of whispered words: *lā khayra fī kathīrin min najwāhum* — "no good in most of their secret converse": *najwā* — confidential intimate private counsel — from n-j-w — low-voiced talk (the Book's standing audit-word for the sealed conversation — its immediate family crowding at once: 58:7 — "hast thou not considered that God knows all in the heavens and the earth there is no secret converse of three, but He is their Fourth; nor of five, but He is their Sixth; nor less nor more, but He is with them wheresoever they are"; and the sūrah's own 58:9's clean 58:10's — "secret converse is only from Satan, that the believers might grieve" — the standing sin-slant of the whisper default in the Revelation: because no-godly the standing commentary: the typical behind-curtain briefing of men is vanity, plot, or slander — *most* of it barren at best) — then the exception opens with its standing with the tradition's beloved triad: *illā man amara bi-ṣadaqatin aw maʿrūfin aw iṣlāḥin bayna al-nās* — "save him who enjoins charity, or kindness — or reconciliation among men": the three classes stamped as the whisper-traffic's as the sealed-chamber's standing charter: (1) *ṣadaqah* — charitable alms (quiet benefaction-plots the plotting-to-f plots to fund the poor — secret giving organized by night — the whisper-room turned into a blessing-mill — with the Prophet's own standing charter of the hid "seven whom God shades on the day when there is no shade but His... a man who gives charity so secretly that his left hand knows not what his right hand does" — Bukhārī 1423, Muslim 1031); (2) *maʿrūf* — the recognized-good (the Book's standing breadth-lex the standing breadth-word — every decency socially ratified — counsel toward generous toward generous patience, toward a better retrieval toward a better habit — the whisper-coaching of a friend toward his own healing); and (3) *iṣlāḥ bayna al-nās* — reconciliation among people (the supreme the standing crown of the three in the tradition's lore — the secret shuttling of peacemakers — the Prophet's celebrated esteem his own degree-raising text: "shall I not tell you of what is better than the rank of fasting, prayer, and almsgiving they said: yes! — he said: making peace between those who are estranged" — Abū Dāwūd 4919, Tirmidhī 1971) — all three returning the sealed chamber to permitted ground: whisper-traffic *exists* — the verse's own realism its standing commentary-note: humans will confer privately — but its currency must be alms, goodness, or peacemaking — s or it sinks at once toward v. 108's toward the bayyata-class — with its standing final clause processing the tradition's own standing tonic hadith upon speech in general, handed down through it through al-Zamakhsharī's registers and the comment-line ever since: "the speech of the child of Adam is against him, not for him — save the command of right, the forbidding of wrong, and the remembrance of God" — an estate an audit of the whole talk-ledger — and where the pleas of the Ṭuʿmah-clan whispered for clan-honor, the verse instead sets the standard of the secret-society of goodness: only the chamber built around charity, decency, and peace-making finally finally finally profits.

**Wa Man Yafʿal Dhālika ibtighāʾa Marḍāti Allāh: The Pleasure-Seeker's Great Wage**

Then the rab the bound the boundary-clause of the whole whisper-chapter — the intention-meter upon every secret counsel: *wa man yafʿalu dhālika ibtighāʾa marḍāti Allāhi fa-sawfa nuʾtīhi ajran ʿaẓīmā* — "and whosoever does that — seeking God's Good Pleasure — We shall give him a great reward": *ibtighāʾa marḍāti Allāh* — seeking God's pleasure — the ibtighā-form of v. 94's standing seek of the standing seek-verbs (ba-gh-y questing in active desire — the standing commentary-line defining its meaning here: not reward-hunting, not fame-hunting nothing of cachet, of legacy-name, or clan-acclaim the seeking of the pleasure-of-approval-of-God alone — works done in whispered rooms done for the Witness of whispered rooms) — the tradition's favorite proof-texts at once crowding the margins: 2:207 — "and among men is he who sells himself seeking God's good pleasure"; 2:265 — "only seeking God's good pleasure and confirming themselves"; 4:94's war-economy twin; 60:1's "if you have come out to strive in My way and seek My good pleasure"; 92:20's — the man 92:18-21 — "he who gives his wealth to purify himself — not to recompense anyone for a favor — only seeking the Face of his Lord Most High — and he shall be satisfied" — with the standing hadith-tone at its head hear no — the standing hadith pairing this intention-key the hadith of the Day's three the three first-judged: the martyr, the scholar, the giver — each exposed at the Judgment as having worked *to be seen working* — and cast away (Muslim 1905) — intention-audited not at the ear at the door of deeds but deepest at the fountain of motive — hence the verse's own audience-fit its standing moral placement after the court-and-clan affair: the Ṭuʿmah-pleaders' whisper-lobby for clan-honor against the iṣlāḥ-whisperers who seek God alone — the two night-chambers opened side by side in the sūrah's own in the sūrah's catalog of whisperers — with heaven's own wage rolled toward only the second: *fa-sawfa nuʾtīhi ajran ʿaẓīmā* — a great reward, from the same We-of-Majesty that authored that pronounced the whole trilogy we-who-shall-give — the same plural of giving-promise running under the reward-clause here — the Book's own eh the Book's own arithmetic: *ʿaẓīm* — the mighty adjective — reserved in the sūrah for su its uses across this sūrah — salvation the ʿaẓīm treasures — v. 27's waiving 4:13 and 4:32 the reward-vault of v. 13's fawzan ʿaẓīman — "a mighty triumph"; v. 54's bounty so v. 114's own clause re-pledging the sūrah's single famous wage: the whisperer-for-God receiving, instead receiving at last — the counter-wage the corrup-corridors can never cash: ajrun ʿaẓīm — the Great Wage.

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:115

> **But whosoever opposes the Messenger, after guidance has been made clear to him, and follows a way other than that of the believers, We shall leave him on [the path] he has taken, and We shall cause him to burn in Hell — what an evil journey's end!**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Wa Man Yushāqiq al-Rasūla: The Breach-Verse After the Verdict**

The Ṭuʿmah-file closes with its standing long-view lesson — the verse that turned a single clan-lobby into a statute for all centuries: *wa man yushāqiqi al-rasūla min baʿdi mā tabayyana lahu al-hudā* — "whosoever opposes the Messenger after the guidance has been made clear to him": *yushāqiq* — from sh-q-q — splitting asunder (the standing split-root: the verb pictures a man *cleaving away* from the fabric — shearing off from the compact thing to which he belonged — the comment-doctors unwrapping its internal axis its standing opposition-anatomy: shiqāq being not mere disagreement — it is *separation-with-hostility* — siding relocating one's whole self toward the opposite toward the opposing camp — the standing Quranic usage of this of the sh-q-q family everywhere being schism-level: 2:137's "if they believe in the like of what you believe, they are guided — and if they turn away, they are in schism"; 22:53's "that He may make what Satan casts a trial for those in whose hearts is disease — and whose hearts are hard — and indeed the wrongdoers are in far-off schism — shiqāqin baʿīd"; its its standing Book-kin: 4:115 here and 8:13's — "that is because they made schism against God and His Messenger" — the standing penalty-clause with the assembled usage setting the level of the charge: not casual dispute — *breaking ranks with the Prophet-as-locus-of-truth*) — *min baʿdi mā tabayyana lahu al-hudā* — after the clarification — tabayyun again (v. 94's tabayyanū-c bayyana-family once more: the deed set after the clarity-flash after the clarity after the truth had been lith-the after the truth had downloaded — the Prophet's teaching reaching ears open after the man *knew* — v. after the man knew) — and the second limb: *wa yattabiʿ ghayra sabīli al-muʾminīna* — "and follows a way other than the way of the believers": the Book's standing marker of blessed *consensus-way* — the famous ijmāʿ-text its primary usage in legal-theory in legal-theory al-Shāfiʿī's al-Shāfiʿī's own use of the verse the famous thesis of the schools: alongside the Messenger's way, God canonizes the *way of the believers* as a path one may not leave without punishment — the standing jurispr the standing juristic development of it into the doctrine of *ijmāʿ* — communal consensus — the ummah's collective the ummah held incapable of agreeing upon error (paired with the standing hadith: "my community will not come together upon misguidance" — Tirmidhī 2167 — and its standing companion: "the Hand of God is with the congregation" — Tirmidhī 2166) — the verse thereby jointly uplifting jointly upholding two non-negotiable rails: the Messenger's teaching, and the believers' corporate way — with the permission the absolution the standing modern and classical map of failure drawn beneath them: the man who invents a third line — neither the Prophet's nor the community's — and takes it.

**Nuwallihi Mā Tawallā: The Terrifying Divorce of Divine Leaving**

Then heaven's own judgment upon the schismatic — and its phrasing is among the most austere in the whole in the sūrah: *nuwallihi mā tawallā wa nuṣlihi jahannam* — "We shall leave him to what he has chosen — and We shall cause him to burn in Hell": *nuwallihi* — We turn him over — from w-l-y — the standing departure-formula (the commentators' standing theological note: *wallā* here = tark — *leaving-to* — the awful administration whereby God lets a man *keep his chosen direction* — the standing madr the standing measured the difference between ḥudā-gift between ḥudā-guidance and between guidance-gift and abandonment being, the Sufi schools insist, not a change in God's essence but in *the thread between Him and that man* — the rope cut from *the man's side* — al-Rāzī's standing pr al-Rāzī's principle upon the matter: the believer receives guidance both by *choice-honoring* no — by pre-election the man honored with help on the road again and again; the self-choosing schismatic *receives his own choice as his estate* — with v. 88's standing twin clamping the whole file: "whomsoever God leads astray — thou wilt not find a way for him") — *mā tawallā* — what he has taken-to — tawallā being the turning-to-choose (v. 89's own twin again — *if they turn their backs* — the sūrah's own semantic loop now closing around Ṭuʿmah's actual biography: he *took* the Makkan way — and heaven *left* him to it — with the classical roll of the with the standing comment-context making the verse making the warning's referent exact: the man who had known the Prophet face-to-face, sat in his mosque, pledged at his hand — then *swapped all of that* for the side of the polytheists) — *wa nuṣlihi jahannam* — and We burn him in Hell (nuṣl ṣ-l-y — its standing hellfire-verb-form — the standing Book-roll of the same formula: 4:10's wa sawfa yaṣlawna saʿīran; 4:30's — "whosoever does that with enmity and injustice — We shall make him burn in the Fire"; 4:56's skin-swap formula; 4:114's own 4:121's refuge-clause the sūrah's own fire-grammar finally completing its cycle from the orphans' previewed fire — v. 10 — through the through Ṭuʿmah's departure — v. 115 — through the through the shirk-file — vv. 116-117 — the fire-verb ṣ-l-y threading all three) — and the seal: *wa sāʾat maṣīrā* — "an evil journey's end" — the standing designation-formula once more (v. 97's standing seal the paired destination-brand threading the sūrah: Ṣīr for hijrah-dodgers; Maṣīr for schismatics) — with the commentators' canonical doctrinal roll the standing doctrinal-closes canonized from the verse through the four schools: (1) al-Shāfiʿī's ijmāʿ-proof (the "way of the believers" as binding path); (2) al-Rāzī's ʿiṣmah-support (if opposing the Prophet is din were he not inerrant, opposition would not be so sentenced); (3) guidance-doctrine from the same hand al-Rāzī's further standing note: the verse proves right-guidance is not found by nafs-insight by private intuition by one's own inner sense of right — but by *following* — the saved road runs behind a messenger and a community — never behind an untutored heart; and (4) the standing pastoral seal of the whole court-block: Ṭuʿmah's clan voted with their tongues; Ṭuʿmah voted with his feet; and Heaven's ledger gave each exactly what each had chosen — leaving the ummah thereafter with the standing warning written into its own consensual spine: break away from the messenger-and-the-way-of-the-believers after knowing it — and you will be left with your breaking you will inherit your own break.

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:116

> **Truly God forgives not that any partner be ascribed unto Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whomsoever He will. Whosoever ascribes partners unto God has surely gone far astray.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Inna Allāha Lā Yaghfiru an Yushraka Bih: The Singular Unforgivable**

After the whole drama of thieves, pleaders, and frame-ups (vv. 105–115), the sūrah turns from human treacheries to the one treachery beyond forgiveness — and speaks it in nearly the very words the Book had uttered once before in this very sūrah: *inna Allāha lā yaghfiru an yushraka bihi* — "God forgives not that partners be ascribed to Him": shirk — association of partners with God — the unforgivable-by-default (the commentators' eternal clarification note guarding the sentence: *unforgiven* if one dies upon it — the door of repentance in life remaining wide — al-Ṭabarī, al-Rāzī, al-Qurṛṭubī, Ibn Kathīr all uniform on the rider with the rider the sūrah itself will preload will supply at v. 48's own count at 4:48's statement earlier and its twin re-utterance here — the double-stationing studied always the pairing of this verse with v. 48 being deliberate (the commentators' observation: v. 48 sealed *the mercy-openings* against the concealment-hearted (4:46's taḥrīf-tribe the concealers of religious truth — v. 46); v. 116 now seals the *justice-block* — as if the Book declared across the entire law-theater of vv. 105–115: all crimes of men admit reconciliation-except find their counters — while this one alone stands outside every counter-plea, court-set court-registry become binary no — with the sūrah thereby marrying the sūrah thereby telling its own procedural parable: Ṭuʿmah's treasury of treachery* remained under the rite of istighfār — but the day an agent forgets if a man closes his story upon God's partner-making — he has walked past the last gate of negotiation — v. 116 as the jurisprudential horizon of the whole sūrah's mercy-teaching: all is negotiable no — except the surrender of the name of God to rivals) — with the great uṣūl-principle al-Rāzī renders al-Rāzī's classical statement standing forever at its side: since God alone forgives — and the law is His — assigning any partner in worship is to challenge the very ground underneath to overthrow the very court in which pardon could be signed no — its simplest form: pardon presupposes sovereignty — shirk disputes dispute the sovereignty — void the plea.

**Wa Yaghfiru Mā Dūna Dhālika Liman Yashāʾ: The Less-than-Shirk Mercy-Spread**

Then the open side of the verse — the mercy-sweep — *wa yaghfiru mā dūna dhālika liman yashāʾ* — "and He forgives what is less than that — for whom He wills": (1) *mā dūna dhālika* — all under shirk (the entire sin-index below it — murder, theft, falsehood, betrayal — the verses' entire Ṭuʿmah-file swept into the forgivable zone) — (2) *liman yashāʾ* — for whom He wills — giving the principle's own with the standing commentators' two readings of the will-clause admitted admitted in parallel: (a) God's sheer sovereignty of choice — al-Ṭabarī's anti-chauvinist bulwark against Muʿtazilite mechanical theology — forgiveness never becoming an owed wage from God to the abstainer — (b) and the standing pastoral mollification of the clause: *liman yashāʾ* being also read as God's will toward those who repent — the standing dialectic across the books: some hold *yashāʾ* = God's free electing-will refuting any self-assurance of the sinner; others hear *yashāʾ* as the will toward the penitent — God's own consistent willing-to-forgive-the-sorry — with the Sunnah texts arriving at once to the standing release the standing texts: the Prophet's maxim — "God accepts repentance until the death-rattle" — Tirmidhī 3537; and the hundred-murderer again (Bukhārī 3470, Muslim 2766 — the standing anchor-case: murder below shirk: forgiven) — and the thorn-expiation mechanics (Bukhārī 5641, Muslim 2573 — the every-thorn-prick purifying "no fatigue, nor disease, nor sorrow, nor harm befalls a Muslim — not even a thorn that pricks him — but that God expiates thereby some of his sins") — all confirming the trackless range of the lower of the under-shirk forgiveness.

**Wa Man Yushrik bi-Allāhi fa-Qad Ḍalla Ḍalālan Baʿīdā: The Going-Far-Astray Verdict**

Then the east of the verse the sealing verdict clause — *wa man yushrik bi-Allāhi fa-qad ḍalla ḍalālan baʿīdā* — "and whosoever ascribes partners to God has gone far astray": *ḍalāl baʿīd* — wandering-distant (the Book's standing poly-lexicon placement: mad ḍalāl = error-of-path — baʿīd its distance-adjective — with the standing comment-anatomy: a man astray is lost; a man astray *baʿīdan* is lost *beyond reach* — the distance-adjective designed its standing effect: shirk as maximum-displacement from Center — the soul making itself an orbit of every false pole — with its Book-companions sealed by the the Book's standing shades: 4:136's 14:3's those preferring the world-life above the next — in far error; and the 34:8's "only those believe in Our signs who are in far error" — no — correct: 34:53 the shirk-distance returning repeatedly — the standing pair arriving at 4:136 below — "whosoever disbelieves in God and His angels and His Books and His messengers and the Last Day — has gone astray far — ḍalālan baʿīdā") — the sūrah thereby welding its own its own final counter-posture: on the whole over the whole justice-and-mercy scaffolding of vv. 105–115, shirk now stands as the sole tribunal the sole gate-closed — with the practical theology the tradition keeps deriving for Muslims' hope-management (in the long pastoral inheritance the verse functions as the ummah's balance-beam: no sinner is ever told *your file is shut* — for all-else-than-shirk swings open — while no cheerer no otiose believer may muse that God might be bargained-down on His sovereignty — the single line at the ledger's head reading forever: no partners may be admitted to One) — the verse thereby holding the exact fulcrum of Islamic soteriology: terror and hope welded in one moral geometry — the wideness of the world under beneath mercy endless, yet centered upon one unshared at fixed absolutely upon One Point.

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:117

> **They call upon only females in His stead; they call upon none but a defiant Satan.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**In Yadʿūna min Dūnihī illā Ināthan: The Female-Gods Clause**

The shirk-file now peels its first historical layer — the feminine pantheon of Makkan idolatry: *in yadʿūna min dūnihī illā ināthan* — "they call upon, apart from Him — only females": *in yadʿūn... illā ināthan* — only female-gods — the commentators standing before the clause with three classical readings, each filing its own slice of pre-Islamic history: (1) the predominant gloss — the three name the three named goddesses of the Quraysh themselves: al-Lāt, al-ʿUzzā, Manāt (the Muḥall the trio the Book names outright at 53:19-20 — "have you seen al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā — and Manāt the third, the other?" — the very three the Makkans styled *banāt Allāh* — daughters of God — with al-Rāzī's standing documentation of the cult of the cult-geography: al-Lāt at Ṭāʾif, al-ʿUzzā at Nakhla, Manāt at Qudayd — each shrine-owned each temple-shrine standing in the pilgrimage the pilgrimage-routes of the idolater's year — and behind this an older pre-history the Nabataean-Arab goddess-families stretching back — the Arabs' whole cultic landscape run heavily through female idols, as archeology has since abundantly confirmed) — (2) the wide-wing variant — the *angels* whom the Makkans named with female names (53:27 — "those who believe not in the Hereafter name the angels with female names" — so that ināthan shrinks not to statues but to the unnamed the misnamed angelic host they invoked — al-Ṭabarī noting the second the reading in his roll) — (3) and the *rasm*-reading of the two great of the two Mothers-of-r some early authorities (attributed to ʿĀʾishah and Ibn ʿAbbās — from the early consonantal rasm without its pointing — debated debated as uthun/awthān — *idols* — read from the same written body — a reading whose weight the commentators register even while placing it outside the accepted qirāʾāt canon) — with the classical answer the tafsīr-house the classical commentators lodging against all the classical consensus the tradition's own composite: *illā ināthan* — meaning whether idols-in-female-form, female-named angels, or the three named goddesses all debated — yet all amounting to the same center the same spiritual disaster: creature-material set up to be called upon *in His stead*.

**Wa Mā Yadʿūna illā Shayṭānan Marīdā: The Defiant-Rebel Vocation-Line**

Then the sūrah's sudden mid-sentence switch — one of the most chilling grammatical leaps in the Revelation: *wa mā yadʿūna illā shayṭānan marīdā* — "and they call upon none but a defiant Satan": the grammar plunging from plural (females) to singular — a *shayṭānan* — one satan — the commentators at once unpacking the master-diagnosis (al-Rāzī's, al-Zamakhsharī's standing take): every invoka every calling-upon the female-idol was already, unbeknownst to the caller, a calling-upon Satan himself: no goddess in stone hears, but the real demon behind the altar hears well — idolatry therefore being devil-worship in disguise (with al-Qurṛṭubī's standing observation supplying the mechanism: each shrine had its serving devil — whispering into the ears of priests and custod of custodians — the spoken-response of idols being demon-voice in worked-up show — and the tradition's own standing cf. the Prophet's own sharper the standing hadith-body about the idol-industry the standing hadith-chain about idol-keeping angels and about the standing track most weight-bearing cousin-text arriving at 22:3 and 37:7 — "shayṭān marīd" in the Book — the standing mention of the defiant demon at those two places the standing mention of the kind) — *marīd* — of m-r-d — hardened rebellious intract defiance-seasoned (the commentators noting its distinction from mere satan-with-small-s: persistent rebel, long-exercised — the Book marking the Book's own verbs sadd its standing word for the long-hardened defiance line) — then the identity suddenly specified across the next verse: *alladhī alladhī laʿanahu Allāh* — the one whom God cursed (v. 118) — whose biography runs back to Adam's own vault back to the Garden — the speaker of the the vow of "Assuredly I shall take of Thy servants" — Iblīs himself — the mu unnamed here on left indefinite deliberately in v. 117 — the commentators' theory the note that the momentum the stylistic the chosen qiṣṣ the Book's choice being the Book's choice to introduce the accursed first *indefinitely* carries its own doctrine: Iblīs cut down in his fall from grace the one whom God cursed being the meaning being: *he is lowered to anonymous-case in God's court — his name no longer his title not worth his pride answered with anonym with the loss of name-mention.

**The Double-Vocation Exposed: Calling Stone, Hearing Satan**

The commentators then lodge the perennial doctrine of vv. 117–119 in standing terms — with the two-level reading the tradition carries from the first centuries: the met the metaphysical register: what men invoke matters not merely by their own inward the caller thinks the caller intends a deity; the *effective* hearer being the effectual hearer is the devil — thereby idolatry being always, in truth, devil-service even where the worshipper knows blissfully unaware (the Book's own further aunt corroborating the Book's own further corroboration: 36:59-60 — "did I not covenant with you, O children of Adam, that you should not worship Satan — truly he is to *ulā innahu lakum ʿaduwwun mubīn*; he is to you a manifest enemy — and that you should worship Me”); the practical register (the practical register of the commentators: all cult-tr all priest-trades of idols became demon-shared trades even before their when the prophet-tr when the Hen when the creed the priests' prophecies ringing from the idols' cust the demonic whisper in every shrine-court — and by this verse all such shrines are unmasked as the same as satan-parlors — the standing comment-result: the pilgrim-tr the Arab pilgrim rounding the goddess-shrine was a satan-shrine a devil caller unknowing — with the standing deliverance the standing doctrine delivered from it to all centuries: nothing created, seen or unseen, may be elected *in His stead* — for whoever is elected there find for whoever is voted-in there works always the same hidden deputy — the accursed one).

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:118

> **Whom God has cursed, who said: "Assuredly I shall take of Thy servants an appointed share."**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Alladhī Laʿanahu Allāh: The Curse as the First Address**

The shirk-file zooms in now upon the shadowy patron named in v. 117, and introduces him with the title that has stuck to him for all ages: *alladhī laʿanahu Allāh* — "the one whom God cursed": *laʿn* — curse — from l-ʿ-n — the standing expulsion-doom word of the Book (distancing-from-mercy: the commentators' standing definition: laʿn = *ʿibādan* no — *ibʿād* — banishment, driving-off, alienation — with the standing Book-clause of the standing cases of its individual assignment lumping its standing Book-roll of cursed ones — the wrongdoers, the idolaters, the liars — and among named yet among named individuals the accursed par excellence Iblīs stands at its head — 15:33-34's own narrative: "depart — for thou art rajīm — and the curse is upon thee to the Day of Judg unto the Day of Judgment" — the standing its Book-passage of the Garden's first exile) — the Book thereby introducing the cosmic adversary not by his capabilities or his wiles stratagems but by his *status*: accursed already — sentence long since filed — his whole archive of schemes thereafter unfolding operating under a spent license.

**Wa Qāla la-ʾAttakhidhanna min ʿIbādika Naṣīban Mafrūḍan: The Appointed-Share Claim**

Then his vow — the first limb of the fourfold program the following verse completes: *wa qāla la-ʾattakhidhanna min ʿibādika naṣīban mafrūḍan* — "and he said: I shall assuredly take of Thy servants an allotted share": *la-ʾattakhidhanna* — the double-emphatic oath form (the very shard the same doubled assertion no — the grammatical oath intensity: satanic resolve given legal a near-contractual weight — he is *resolved*, bound himself self-bound); *min ʿibādika* — from among *Thy servants* (the commentators' standing gorge the mufassirūn's immediate note on the possessive: he names God's human creation *ʿibādika — Your servants* — as though he must catch as though the theft announcement already admits the whole stock belongs to Another — the pronoun *-ka* lashed to the stolen list — containing confessing the ownership while announcing the raid — al-Rāzī and al-Qurṛṭubī dwelling forever upon the adversary's inner contradiction: he understands slave the ownership-tag *ʿibādika* while vowing the expropriation — with the standing eschatological connotation the tradition's own note: parallel Book-station at 15:39-42: "he said: my Lord, as Thou hast misled me, I shall make all I shall surely bedeck the earth for them and lead them all astray — save Thy devoted sincere servants among them"; and God answering there God's own famous counter 15:42: "over My servants thou shalt have no authority — save indeed save those who follow thee of the seduced" — the "devoted slave"-category thereby placed *outside* the allotted share from the start; 38:82-83 returning it once more — the standing four-form of the vow in the Book) — and *naṣīban mafrūḍan* — an appointed share, prescribed allotment (naṣīb recurring — v. 85's intercessor-shares, v. 7's estate-shares, now satanic sharefarming the Book's own poetics the standing comment-annotation being dismal its standing note: Satan budgets Satan computes the adversary has an accounting-department: he *tithed* humanity; he apportioned his own harvest-map of souls — with the standing descriptive division the commentators keep: a share classed his allotment is not random but *arithmetic*: he selects he haggles over he counts his catch — the Book thereby teaching believers the standing inverse: God's servants are *counted* — but they are the Devil's *miscalculation*: the destined share the appointed share doomed from its appointment to from its appointment onward — since the share list contains its own contradictor contains its opposite from within: the very destinies the very distribution the very the very allotment he believed appointed lay already within the within God's scrawl within God's plan to erase).

**The Curse-and-Vow as the Frame of All Mischief**

The tradition then reads the two phrases as one unit ever since: cursed — yet vowing; exiled — yet pursuing yet hunting; doomed — yet allocating (the Sufi commentators' standing en al-Qushayrī's own inward-angle: this is the standing image of every spiritual condition whereby a soul *lives under curse-status* but refuses to cease activity — the sin-works of the condemned proceeding pressing on pressing forward under lost prospects with the standing opposite-attire and its standing contrasting image in the Book itself: the one whom God cursed still works at harvest; the believer *under blessing* often sleeps — the commentators' standing charge: the oath of the cursed is the standing shame of the blessed) — with its standing Book-kin completing its standing Book-harmonies completing the profile: 7:16-17's vow to lie-in-wait from front, behind, right, left from front and rear and right and left; 17:62's posterity-seduction threat; 18:50's "will you take him and his issue as allies apart from Me — while they and they are your enemy a wretched exchange for the wrongdoers" — all of them resolving resolving forever into the sūrah's own standing diagnosis: the vow of the accursed is the standing background-grind beneath every pagan Altar beneath every ancient idol-trade beneath every modern beneath every altar from Makkah's Makkah's three goddesses to each to every idol that ever occupied a shrine — for the adversary claims his tithe from whatever false devotion men offer — greed ināth or angels, idols or ambitions — the naṣīb mafrūḍ being simply his way of saying: *whatever you render to the false — I count it mine*.

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:119

> **And surely I shall lead them astray, and arouse desires in them. I shall command them and they will slit the ears of cattle; I shall command them and they will alter God's creation. Whosoever takes Satan as a protector apart from God has surely suffered a manifest loss.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Wa La-ʾUḍillannahum: The Astray-Program First**

The accursed one's vow now unfolds into its celebrated four-chamber program — the longest single self-exposure of Satan in the Book: *wa la-ʾuḍillannahum* — "and I shall surely lead them astray": the first limb being his standing mission-verb (ḍ-l-l standing ḍalāl already sealed v. 116's own astray-verdict — the Book deliberately reusing the Book's own echo: astray-work is his standing plank — cf. 4:60's "Satan desires to lead them astray far off"; 15:39's vow 15:39; 7:16's watch- his garden-page his standing scheme from the first from the garden: 2:36's and 7:20's standing satanic induced-f induced-fall) — and *wa la-ʾumanniyannahum* — "and I shall surely stir desires in them": *tamnī* — the amānī machine from m-n-y — wish, longing, vain-hope (the root the Book imposes upon wish-projection — the commentators' standing taxonomy of his wish-work in two aisles: (1) worldly wishes — long life, endless postponement of repentance, imagined safety, the whole "sawfa" — "soon/later" economy of the of the put-off soul; (2) otherworldly wishes — undeserved forgiveness, automatic paradise, salvation without deeds — al-Rāzī's standing diagnosis: Satan flips fires *false promissory notes* on both banks — the world and the hereafter — "be at ease ya his whispered pledge: *you are of the elect, God will forgive, there is much time*;" with its standing Book-aud audit compiling 2:111's its own its own standing target at the Book's own the standing exposure at 2:111 & 111c the Book's own parallel from its standing own at the general exposure of amānī-check at 2:111-112 — "they say: none shall enter paradise but Jews and Christians — those are their vain hopes — amāniyyuhum"; and its standing sideways beside its favorite return at 3:24 — "that is because they said: the fire shall not touch us but for days numbered — their forged lies deceived them in their religion")

**Fa-La-ʾĀmurannahum fa-La-Yubattikunna Ādāna al-Anʿām: The Ear-Slitting, and the Alteration-Vow**

Then the two concrete command-limbs the tradition never tires of unpacking: *fa-la-ʾāmurannahum fa-la-yubattikunna ādāna al-anʿām* — "I shall command them — and they will slit the ears of cattle": *tabtīk* — cutting-though from b-t-k — cleaving off (the standing ritual of the idolaters: the *baḥīrah* — the ear-slit she-camel released onto the pasture-law the old pagan law: when a she-camel bore five offspring with the fifth a male, her ear was slit and she was consecrated consecrated-to-the-idol — now untouchable for burden nor for burden or milk (al-Ṭabarī's standing definition; 5:103 the Book-text of its of the whole baḥīrah-sāʾibah-trade of its standing sisters at 5:103 — "God has not appointed baḥīrah, nor sāʾibah, nor waṣīlah, nor ḥām — but the disbelievers forge lies against God — and most of them understand not") — the comment-doctors at once unfolding the double-fraud the limb discloses: (a) the pretense of *pious reverence* religious respect — a consecrated beast consecration packaged as devotion; (b) the actual *theft of utility* — milk withdrawn from children, a pasture a working animal removed from labor — Satan's consecration always subtracting from life — an and us and adding to superstition) — and the fourth the master-limb announced: *wa la-ʾāmurannahum fa-la-yughayyirunna khalqa Allāh* — "and I shall command them — and they will alter God's creation": *yughayyirunna khalqa Allāh* — change God's creation — the clause the commentators unfold through the depths: (1) the historical limb — mutilation-rites of the idolaters of idolatrous ritual — castrating castration of men into eunuchs, tattooing, tooth-filing — the standing hadith-register of Bukhārī the standing hadith-curse upon “God cursed the women who tattoo and have themselves tattooed, the women who remove hair from the face, the women who file teeth for beautification — altering the creation of God” — Bukhārī 5931; Muslim 2125 — with the classical canon the standing fiqh-permissiveness on on circumcision always carefully distinguished — rite-of-purity never alteration-of-cap of capability the standing classical disposition: lawful grooming subtracting not the creation's function); ## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:125

> **And who is better in religion than the one who submits his face to God, and is virtuous, and follows the creed of Abraham, as a ḥanīf? And God did take Abraham for a friend.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Wa Man Aḥsanu Dīnan Mimman Aslama Wajhahu li-Allāh: The Summit-Question**

The sūrah's religio-comparative debate ends not with a boast but with a question that selects out single souls: *wa man aḥsanu dīnan mimman aslama wajhahu li-Allāh* — "and who is better in religion than he who submits his face to God?": *aḥsanu dīnan* — better in religion — the comparative rising to its to its standing to its standing excellence-measure) — *aslama wajhahu* — submitted his face — the commentators' standing unpacking: the face as the whole the face here standing metonymically for the entire self (since the face is the man's noblest, most-attended part — its standing Book-roll of wajh-submission: 2:112 — "nay — whosoever submits his face to God and is virtuous — his reward is with his Lord — no fear upon them, neither shall they grieve"; 3:20 — "I have submitted my face to God — and those who follow me"; 31:22's twin — the whole-person devoted, no part withheld) — with the standing chain-of-three completing the sentence: (1) *aslama wajhahu* — outward-total submission — the islām-limb; (2) *wa huwa muḥsin* — and is virtuous — muḥsin — the iḥsān-limb — the commentators' standing exchange noting v. 124's ṣāliḥāt-and-īmān (deeds + faith) and v. 125's adding the third — iḥsān — (the standing heir-line with Jibrīl-hadīth: islām-īmān-iḥsān triad — Muslim 8's standing the celebrated Gabriel-hadith registers all three under its question — "to worship God as though you see Him") — and (3) *wa-ttabaʿa millata Ibrāhīma ḥanīfan* — follows the creed of Abraham, ḥanīf — the lineage-limb: millah as creed-way — from meaning the standing sense given by the commentators: the established religious the established creed-charter — with ḥanīfan — from ḥ-n-f — turning-off-from-the the Book's standing Abraham-word — 2:135 — "say: the creed of Abraham, ḥanīfan — and he was not of the polytheists"; 6:161 — "the creed of your father Abraham ḥanīfan — and he was not of the polytheists"; 30:30 — the pure anti-shirk the singular the divergence-from-every-deviation posture — the creed of of upright turning-away — ḥ-n-f the ḥanīf as the man who tilts perpetually **away from every idol** — never merely neutral but slanted against all false worship) — with the Book's standing defense of the line against sect-claimants: 2:140 — "was Abraham a Jew — or a Christian?"; 3:65-67 — "Abraham was neither Jew nor Christian — but he was a ḥanīf musliman — a righteous-turning submitter — and he was not among the polytheists — indeed the nearest of people to Abraham are those who followed him — and this Prophet — and those who believe — and God is the Walī of the believers" — v. 125 thereby delivering the creed-line to the Medinian ummah as Abraham's unbroken continuation.

**Wa-ttakhadha Allāhu Ibrāhīma Khalīlā: The Intimate-Friend Heaven-Signed**

Then the the honorific the whole Islamic the honorific all Islam thereafter bestows upon Abraham — *wa-ttakhadha Allāhu Ibrāhīma khalīlā* — "and God took Abraham for a khalīl — an intimate friend": *khalīl* — from kh-l-l — from kh-l-l — permeation, pore-level closeness (the commentators' standing the comment-lineage's standing treasure: khalīl not mere companion-level — but *permeating love* — with al-Ṭabarī's the classical definition the canons keep: the standing definition handed down by the commentators generally — love that has permeated — every chamber of his being — with the standing practical rules the commentators attach to the term (al-Ṭabarī's al-Ṭabarī's standing teaching: the khalīl loves whatever his friend loves, and hates whatever his friend hates — the Book's own standing demonstration: Abraham's own standing file: 9:114 — "Abraham's invocation for forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made him — and when it became clear to him that he was an enemy to God — he disassociated himself from him — indeed Abraham was tender-hearted — awwāh — forbearing"; 60:4 — "there is an excellent example for you in Abraham and those with him — when they said to their people: we are clear of you and of what you worship apart from God — we renounce you — and enmity and hatred have appeared between us and you forever — until you believe in God alone" — the standing rule then for the khalīl: no friendship with the of his Friend) — with the outward ramifications engraved forever in Islam's own ritual architecture: the khalīl's own its standing signs: the maqām Ibrāhīm at the Kaʿbah (2:125) — ḥajj's Abrahamic Hijaz's stations of ḥajj all tied back to his biography (22:26-29; and 2:125-129's Makkah-building narrative) — and the standing honorific standing alone in the canon: *Khalīl Allāh* — the one called God's intimate friend — the verse thereby closing its superlative with a portrait rather than a prize: better religion is submission of face, purity of deed, Abrahamic creed — and the final the final fruit of its path is, in God's own house: friendship.

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:126

> **Unto God belongs whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is on the earth, and God encompasses all things.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Wa Li-llāhi Mā fī al-Samāwāti wa Mā fī al-Arḍ: Ownership Declared Before the Law Resumes**

Between the Abrahamic summit of v. 125 and the family-file reopening at v. 127, the Book plants its standing ownership-plaque: *wa li-llāhi mā fī al-samāwāti wa mā fī al-arḍ* — "unto God belongs whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is on earth": the sūrah's standing its standing cadence-form returning once more (its own siblings: 2:284 — "unto God belongs whatsoever is in the heavens and the earth — whether you disclose what is in your souls or hide it — God will call you to account for it"; 3:109; 3:129; 4:131–132 immediately below; 4:170; 10:55) — with the standing comment-canon's structural note on its position: the ownership-declaration standing deliberately **between** the verse closing the preceding extended doctrinal-file (belief, hypocrisy, idolatry, hell, and reward) with a yet opening the curtain upon the family-legislation resuming below: all the the legal stakes about to be apportioned in inheritance, marriage-terms, and protection (vv. 127–130) belong first to God: every orphan's mīrāth, every mahr, every household-right is is held only in trust from Him — the the Ownership-verse thus serving as the standing announcement never to be missed: *everything to follow legislates the handling of what God owns* — hence mind how you handle it).

**Wa Kāna Allāhu bi-Kulli Shayʾin Muḥīṭā: Muḥīṭ — The Universal Encompassing in Its Calm Sense**

Then the attribute-seal — one of the Book's standing vast names — now in its calm register: *wa kāna Allāhu bi-kulli shayʾin muḥīṭan* — "and God is encompassing of all things": *muḥīṭ* — again (v. 108's its own standing station at v. 108 — muḥīṭ filed there as the as the ominous enclosure around the night-plotters) — but now the commentators' standing the standing note from al-Ṭabarī and al-Rāzī: the divine name Muḥīṭ is is not always in its usage sliding between two registers: (1) *reproving* — its standing the standing ominous deployments — 3:120 — "God is encompassing of what they do" (to the slanderers after Uḥud); 4:108 (the night-plotters); 8:47 (the boastful meccan army); 11:92 (Shuʿayb's warning to his people); 41:54 the deniers of signs); 85:20 — "and God is encompassing of them from behind" (to to the persecutors of the believers) — all of them all operating as the enclosing-attribute wielded as threat — God already *surrounding* what the sinner believes private; and (2) *universal-metaphysical* — the standing the the the sheer the standing benign or neutral sense: God encompassing *everything* as its as the infinite frame of existence itself — with 4:126 standing precisely in this second register — the implication running: no estate, no matrimonial arrangement, no orphan's heirloom, no no concealed inclination escapes the Frame — with the Book's own standing group of Muḥīṭ-verses its standing scope-enumeration: God encompasses in knowledge ("their Lord encompasses them in knowledge" — 85:20's 20:98 — "He knows what is before them and behind them — and they encompass Him not in knowledge" — 20:98's standing clause; 65:12 — "God encompasses all things in knowledge"), encompasses in power ("He is able over all things — 5:120; 18:45; 29:20), and above all encompasses by being the boundless — al-Rāzī's standing Kalām-note: God cannot be encompassed by us — muḥīṭ is one-directional — the the creaturely horizon cannot wrap God — hence the attribute is also testimony of our own boundedness — 20:110's standing clause — "they encompass Him not in knowledge") — and the sūrah the sūrah thereby closing this doctrinal run with the same theological span it the same span with which v. 87 had opened the block (One-God, Gathering-Day, True-Speech): Ownership, Encompassing — every human deal now passing beneath the arches of the Heavenly Estate of God's own estate — so that the reader the reader then passes into vv. 127's women-and-orphans rulings with fresh eyes: the these rulings are drawn upon heaven's upon heaven's own premises — handled therefore under the Encompassing's own and in the Encompassing's own by no right other than by no other right than His by no other right than His.

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:127

> **And they consult thee concerning the women. Say: God gives you the ruling concerning them, and what has been recited to you in the Book concerning the orphan-girls to whom you do not give what is prescribed for them, while you desire to marry them — and concerning the oppressed among the children, and that you stand firm for the orphans with justice. And whatever good you do — God is ever Knowing of it.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Wa Yastaftūnaka fī al-Nisāʾ: The Consultation That Returned**

The family-file of the sūrah's opening now reopens with a live question: *wa yastaftūnaka fī al-nisāʾ* — "and they consult thee concerning the women": *yastaftūnaka* — from f-t-y — the verb of seeking a fatwā, a considered ruling (its standing question-cadence appearing across the Book whenever the community is at a practical loss: "they consult thee concerning the sacred month — fighting therein" — 2:217; "they consult thee what they should spend" — 2:219; "they consult thee concerning the spoils" — 8:1; and already within this sūrah: "they consult thee — say: God gives you the ruling concerning the heirless" — 4:176 below, closing the sūrah with the same formula). The occasion — reported in the standing collections: in the standing Sabāb-material (Muslim's standing narration from ʿĀʾishah and the tafsīr tradition generally) — the question came after the earlier rulings: the women of Madīnah themselves, stirred by the inheritance-verses and the orphan-guardianship ordinances, came asking: what now of us — where do we stand in this new order? And the verse's standing lesson is already in its first word: the community's questions are not interruptions of revelation but its *occasions* — God answers the asking, and the asking of women about women is written into the Book's own text forever — a standing testament that the sūrah named "the Women" was itself composed partly in response to women who asked.

**Quli Allāhu Yuftīkum Fīhinna: The Answer Above the Answer**

The reply-form is itself a ruling about rulings: *quli Allāhu yuftīkum fīhinna* — "say: God gives you the ruling concerning them": the Prophet is made to answer — but to answer by deferring upward: *say: God rules on this* — the standing deferential pattern (4:176 reprises it: "they consult thee — say: God gives you the ruling").
