The commentators mark the fitna of its exactness: the selective believers sought *distinction* — status, the dignity of the discerning, the middle-position of the judicious — and their prepared wage is *disgrace*: tafrīq answered by tahwīn — they who prided themselves on dividing shall be levelled by shame; they who took a middle-road for dignity arrive at the extreme of humiliation (the standing Book-pattern of punishment-as-mirror: 10:27 — "those who earned evils — the recompense of an evil is its like — and abasement shall cover them"; 2:85's disgrace-wage above). And the double-registry of the verse — v. 150 defining the act, v. 151 defining the actor and the wage — completes in two short verses the Book's standing legislation of assent-integrity: faith is by constitution indivisible; the distinction-maker is by deed a disbeliever; and for disbelief there stands, from the first day, a preparation — humiliation prepared by the same God whose preparation of Gardens the sūrah has already sung (4:57, 4:122): two two prepared destinations, and the difference between them nothing more — and nothing less — than the difference between taking all of the prophecy and refusing any part of it.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:152

> **But those who believe in God and His messengers, and make no distinction between any of them — unto those He shall give their rewards. And God is ever Forgiving, Merciful.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Wa Alladhīna Āmanū bi-llāhi wa Rusulih: The Counter-Registry of the Complete**

The Book turns its face from the distinction-makers to their opposites — the *wa*-adversative swinging the ledger: *wa alladhīna āmanū bi-llāhi wa rusulih* — "but those who believe in God and His messengers": the counter-formula stated first in its standing positive — unqualified, inclusive assent: God *and* His messengers — no parenthesis of exception admitted between the Sender and His sent. The commentators mark the echo-architecture reaching back through the sūrah: v. 136 above had erected the archipelago of faith ("believe in God and His Messenger, and the Book sent down upon His Messenger, and the Book sent down aforetime"); v. 150-151 had charged those who break the archipelago as "disbelievers in truth"; v. 152 now files the island-keepers — those whose assent follows the contiguity entirely given. And the commentators' standing note on register-placement: the chapter of law and hypocrisy ends its doctrinal section precisely here — in creed-completeness stated as reward-worthiness — the sūrah's several audiences (believers, hypocrites, People of the Book) all addressed finally in the same creedal currency: whoever you are, the question is the same — whole faith, or the art of the partial?

**Wa Lam Yufarriqū Bayna Aḥadin Minhum: The Non-Distinction as Creed**

The qualification-clause seals the condition: *wa lam yufarriqū bayna aḥadin minhum* — "and make no distinction between any of them": *aḥadin* — "any one" — the indefinite-singular in a negation carrying the Book's absolute: not one exception — not between God and messenger (v. 150's first severance), not between messenger and messenger (its second): the standing creed-text of 2:285 sounded once more as this verse's own interpretive anthem ("the Messenger believes in what has been sent down to him from his Lord — and the believers: each one believes in God and His angels and His books and His messengers — we make no distinction between any of His messengers — and they say: we hear and we obey — Thy forgiveness, our Lord — and unto Thee is the journeying"); with 2:136 and 3:84 beside it (the standing triad of prophecy-inclusiveness: "say: we believe in God and in what was revealed to us and revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Tribes, and in what was given to Moses and Jesus and the prophets from their Lord — we make no distinction between any of them — and unto Him we submit"). The commentators (al-Rāzī's standing ladder-note) mark that the clause describes not mere non-discrimination but *positive theological posture*: the believer receives prophets as one receives chapters of a single Book — differences of tongues, codes, and eras standing as variety within a unity, never as warrant to strike chapters — 35:24's standing census of mercy ("there is no community but a warner has passed among them"); 10:47; 16:36; 21:7-8 — the testimony of God's wide mercy: no nation left unaddressed, no messenger a rival to another — all witnesses to the one Lord (11:50-60's standing sequence: Hūd among ʿĀd, Ṣāliḥ among Thamūd — each saying "O my people — worship God — you have no god but He").

**Fa-Ulāʾika Sawfa Yuʾtīhim Ujūrahum: The Rewards of the Undivided**

Then the promise-formula in its standing future-form: *fa-ulāʾika sawfa yuʾtīhim ujūrahum* — "unto those He shall give their rewards": *ujūr* — the plural of *ajr* — wages, rewards — pluralized deliberately (the standing note of the language-commentators: the plural registers the multiplicity of what full faith earns — each article believed, each messenger received, each undisputed truth submitting a separate wage-slip) — and *sawfa* — the future-particle with its standing note of solemnity: *shall* — assured but deferred — the reward pledged upon God's own calendar. The standing promise-file of the Book assembles beside it: its register: 4:100 — the emigrant to God "his wage has fallen upon God"; 18:30 — "verily those who believe and do righteous deeds — We shall not waste the wage of him who did good work"; the grand wage-list of 33:35 for the men and women of every virtue; "that God may acquit them of the worst of what they did and pay them their wage with the best of what they used to do"; "theirs is a wage unfailing" — *ajr ghayr mamnūn* — the standing superlative: wages without interruption, reduction, or grudge.

**Wa Kāna Allāhu Ghafūran Raḥīman: The Names Against the Figures of the Ledger**

The verse seals with the sūrah's most familiar Name-pair — *wa kāna Allāhu ghafūran raḥīman* — "and God is ever Forgiving, Merciful": the standing seal of the sūrah's family-file (4:23; 4:24; 4:96; 4:100; 4:106) now sealing the creed-file — and the commentators' standing question — "why Forgiving where the verse describes *success*?" — answers itself: because the promise of reward is issued to humankind *as found*: even the undivided believer arrives freighted with slips and debts; his ujūr rest not on a perfect account but on a Forgiver standing between his ledger and his wage — and even the erstwhile distinction-maker, repenting into wholeness (the dossier's standing exception-pattern — 4:146's repentant hypocrites now mirrored by v. 152's reachable selective believers), finds the door named Ghafūr-Raḥīm already open at the archive of the verdicts. The triad vv. 150–152 thus stands as the sūrah's standing creed-triptych: the distinguished-and-disbelieving (150), the verdict with its prepared wage of disgrace (151), and the undivided with their pending rewards under Forgiveness-Mercy (152) — and the verse-number's own neatness (152 = v. 136's archipelago + the 16 intervening verses of hypocrisy-anatomy) marking how the sūrah's long shadow-section on the false and the partial closes finally in its two gentlest Names — as if the Book, having spoken so long of the basement and the humiliation, would now leave the reader at the doorway of the Forgiving, the Merciful — before turning, in the address to come (v. 153 onward), to the People of the Book with their standing questions and the sūrah's standing answers.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:153

> **The People of the Book ask thee to bring down upon them a Book from heaven. Yet they asked Moses for a greater thing than that, for they said: "Show us God openly" — so the thunderbolt seized them for their wrongdoing. Then they took up the calf, even after the clear proofs had come to them; yet We pardoned that, and We gave Moses a manifest authority.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Yasʾaluka Ahlu al-Kitāb: The Old Question at a New Door**

The final movement of the sūrah opens upon its addressed community with a demand: *yasʾaluka ahlu al-kitābi an tunazzila ʿalayhim kitāban min al-samāʾ* — "the People of the Book ask thee to bring down upon them a Book from heaven": the commentators (al-Ṭabarī's chains; reports naming specific leaders among the Jewish scholars of Madīnah) specify its intended shape: a physical writ — an inscribed tablet or sealed document descending visibly from the sky, akin to the tablets of Moses (28:48's standing parallel: "why was he not given the like of what Moses was given?"; and 17:93's standing Meccan twin from the idolaters: "or thou bring down upon us a book that we may read"). The demand is forensic in costume — "give us documentary proof of prophethood" — but the Book immediately strips the costume by narrating *the same people's precedent*: they had once asked Moses for something *greater* — *fa-qad saʾalū Mūsā akbara min dhālik* — "yet they asked Moses for a greater thing than that": the comparative exposing the demand's rank within their own history of demands: they had already outstripped it — and the greater demand had already shown what such demands are worth as instruments of belief.

**Arinā Allāha Jahrahan: The Demand to See — and the Thunderbolt's Answer**

The greater demand is quoted verbatim: *fa-qālū arinā Allāha jahratan* — "for they said: show us God openly": *jahrahan* — openly, with unveiled eyes (the same root as v. 148's jahr — publicness): vision demanded as the entrance-fee of belief — 2:55's standing twin recounting the explicit condition-currency of the demand: "and when you said: O Moses — we shall never believe thee until we see God openly — whereupon the thunderbolt seized you while you looked on; then We raised you up after your death, that perhaps you might give thanks": the standing sabab-reading (al-Ṭabarī, al-Qurṭubī) locating the petitioners among the seventy elders Moses selected for the covenant-mīqāt — the story in the fullest register at 7:155's seventy ("And Moses chose of his people seventy men for Our appointment") — the elite delegation itself perishing in the demand's own answer: *fa-akhadhathumu al-ṣāʿiqatu bi-ẓulmihim* — "so the thunderbolt seized them for their wrongdoing": *ṣāʿiqah* — the standing punishment-word of the skies (2:55; 41:13 — "warned them of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of ʿĀd and Thamūd"; 41:17; 51:44) — with the causal-clause *bi-ẓulmihim* — "for their wrongdoing" — marking the seizure not as refusal of a lawful wish but 7as verdict upon its arrogance: the demand to see God made not as thirst (Moses' own *arini* at 7:143 — "my Lord — show me, that I may look upon Thee" — answered gently with the mountain's collapse and "thou shalt not see Me") but as ultimatum: *we will not believe until* — the grammar of extortion, not of longing — 2:260's standing counter-case clinched the rule: Abraham's "show me how Thou givest life to the dead" — asked from within belief ("that my heart may be at rest") — was granted without thunder. The commentators gather the standing jurisprudence of the three cases: the desire for vision is of itself neither sin nor right; it is weighed by *intention* — Moses the beloved asking as a lover (answered with pedagogy), Abraham the friend asking for heart's rest (answered with demonstration), the seventy asking as negotiators (answered with the bolt).

**Thumma Ittakhadhū al-ʿIjla: The Golden Calf After the Clear Proofs**

The verse then compresses the standing chronicle of relapse: *thumma ittakhadhū al-ʿijla min baʿdi mā jāʾathumu al-bayyināt* — "then they took up the calf, even after the clear proofs had come to them": the standing calf-file (2:51-54; 2:92-93; 7:148-156; 20:86-97) cited here for its exact pedagogic wedge — *min baʿdi mā jāʾathumu al-bayyināt* — after the clear proofs: al-Ṭabarī's gloss reading the bayyināt as precisely the thunderbolt-and-resurrection itself (they had *seen* — their own bodies dying and being raised — what no demand could make clearer: that the God they must worship is not an object for the eyes); al-Qurṭubī widening the register to the full Moses-miracle inventory (the sea's parting; 17:101's standing nine signs; 28:36). The commentators mark the dark lesson the sūrah intends its Madīnan audience to absorb: spectacular proof does not manufacture faith — a generation that watched thunderbolts and parted seas could still, within weeks, worship a calf cast from earrings: *proof* is God's part; *response* is man's — the demanders of 4:153's present tense being addressed through their own ancestors' file: you ask for a book from heaven? Your fathers received thunder, seas, and tablets — and made a calf.

**Fa-ʿAfawnā ʿan Dhālik: Pardoned — and Authority Confirmed**

Yet the verse descends — astonishingly, after thunderbolt and calf — to the standing note of mercy that the commentators prize as the verse's own portal: *fa-ʿafawnā ʿan dhālika wa ātaynā Mūsā sulṭānan mubīnan* — "yet We pardoned that, and We gave Moses a manifest authority": *ʿafw* — the effacing pardon (v. 149's Name-file immediately above: *ʿafūwwan qadīran* — Pardoning, Powerful — the sūrah's own pairing of pardon-with-power here displayed in history: God pardons the very generation He could justly have erased) — 2:52's standing record of the pardon ("then We pardoned you after that — that perhaps you might give thanks"); and the second half restores the office the rebellion had impugned: *sulṭānan mubīnan* — a manifest authority — glossed two ways in the standing readings (al-Qurṭubī's and al-Ṭabarī's: the proof and powers by which Moses' prophethood stood manifest; al-Zamakhsharī's complementary: the concrete *authority* over the Israelites by which he could command their repentance and enforce the atonement of 2:54 — "then turn to your Maker and slay yourselves" — authority surviving their rebellion: pardoned people, reaffirmed prophet). The verse thereby delivers to its present demanders its folded answer: they demanded a tablet; the verse gives them a history — in which (a) demands for visible proof have already exceeded their present request and been answered with consequences; (b) the proofs given produced — in unrenewed hearts — calves, not belief; (c) pardons, not bolts, form the standing divine default toward those who return; and (d) God's authority rests upon His prophets *regardless of* who demands paperwork — the Book from heaven they seek having in fact already descended: it is the very Book in which their question is recorded — the Qur'ān itself the tunazzila-ʿalayhim kitāban standing fulfilled, the demand answered by the demand's being written into revelation — the standing irony the commentators savor: they asked that a Book be brought down; a Book was being brought down upon them *as they asked*.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:154

> **And We raised the Mount above them for their covenant, and We said to them: "Enter the gate, prostrating," and We said to them: "Transgress not the Sabbath." And We took from them a solemn covenant.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Wa Rafaʿnā Fawqahumu al-Ṭūr: The Mountain Held Over the Treaty**

The covenant-chronicle continues with one of the Book's most majestic pressure-images: *wa rafaʿnā fawqahumu al-ṭūra bi-mīthāqihim* — "and We raised the Mount above them for their covenant": *al-Ṭūr* — the Mount — the Book's standing name for the Sinai-mountain wherever it appears (its register: 2:63; 2:93; 19:52 — "We called to him from the right side of the Mount and brought him near in communion"; 20:80; 28:29; 28:46; 52:1 — "by the Mount"); and the *raising* understood in the standing majority-reading (al-Rāzī gathering the comment-canon) quite literally: God lifted the mountain from its foundation and held it suspended over the Israelites at the covenant-making — with 2:63 its standing twin: "and when We took your covenant and raised the Mount above you: take what We have given you with strength, and remember what is in it — that perhaps you may fear"; and 2:93 adding its standing detail: they took it under the mind's coercion of the hanging mountain ("and it was raised above you as though it were a canopy — and they supposed it was falling upon them — take what We have given you with strength, and hear"). Al-Qurṭubī registers the alternative restraint — the raising as the image of sheer loftness and overwhelm — but the dominant imagination of the tafsīr-tradition keeps the mountain airborne: covenant extracted from a people beneath geology itself made eyelid. The commentators mark the theological point: the miracle-as-treaty-witness — twelve tribes assembled beneath levitated stone — a covenant witnessed not by ink but by the Creator's own suspension of His own physical order — and the sūrah's present audience (the People of the Book in Madīnah covenanting, or refusing to covenant, with the new revelation) reading the file of their fathers: covenants with God were sealed, for them, under a mountain — let no one treat the mīthāq lightly now that it comes by recitation instead of levitation.

**Wa Qulnā Lahumu Udkhulū al-Bāba Sujjadan: The Gate That Required Bowing**

The verse then proceeds to the standing command charged at the covenant's edges: *wa qulnā lahumu udkhulū al-bāba sujjadan* — "and We said to them: enter the gate, prostrating": the standing file at 2:58 and 7:161: "and when it was said to them: dwell in this town and eat of it wheresoever you will, and say: ḥiṭṭah — and enter the gate prostrating — We shall forgive you your offenses — We shall increase the good-doers": the gate-gloss under the standing readings of the commentators being the gate of the promised town (Jericho or Jerusalem in the standing reports — 5:21-23's standing file of the entry-debate) — and the posture demanded at the entry: *sujjad* — prostrate — the entrance to victory dressed as the entrance to worship: the people of God entering their long-promised possession *forehead-down* — conquest-behavior inverted into gratitude: not as raiders claiming a prize but as worshippers acknowledging a gift. The standing callback of the tradition: the chronicled alteration — 2:59; 7:162 — "but the wrongdoers among them substituted a saying other than that which had been said to them — so We sent upon them a scourge from heaven for their wrongdoing": they changed the dictated word *ḥiṭṭah* (unburdening) into mocking parody-forms, and bent the prostration into its own caricature — the entry that was to be prayer becoming farce: the standing lesson of the commentators: the covenant's outward conditions are tests of inward submission; humiliation-postures refused at the gate become punishments delivered from the sky.

**Wa Lā Taʿdū fī al-Sabt: The Sabbath-Order in the Standing File**

And the third command-station: *wa qulnā lahum lā taʿdū fī al-sabt* — "and We said to them: transgress not the Sabbath": *lā taʿdū* — do not commit ʿudwān — transgression-overstepping (its standing paired usage 4:30's — "whoever does that in aggression and injustice — We shall roast him in a blaze") — the Sabbath of the covenant-community being their standing sanctified rest-day, set apart (its standing Book-file: 2:65 — "you well know those of you who transgressed the Sabbath — We said to them: be apes, despised"; 7:163's full Sabbath-file — the town by the sea, the fish appearing on the Sabbath in abundance, absent on other days — and the trawling folk splitting into transgressors, warners, and the saved; 4:47 above's own Sabbath-curse-station; 16:124 — "the Sabbath was only set down upon those who differed concerning it") — the Sabbath-legislation thus read by the commentators not as a timeless universal but as a *covenant-specific* sign: a test-institution marking that community's treaty with God — which is precisely the frame the present verse gives it: ordered in a chain with covenant-mountain and prostrate-gate, all three standing as *terms of the mīthāq*: divine order, worshipful conquest, sanctified time.

**Wa Akhadhnā Minhum Mīthāqan Ghalīẓan: The Covenant in Its Thickness**

The verse seals with the covenant-word at its heaviest registered form: *wa akhadhnā minhum mīthāqan ghalīẓan* — "and We took from them a solemn covenant": *mīthāq* — the standing treaty-word of the Book (its register of covenants: 2:40 — "fulfill My covenant — I shall fulfill your covenant"; 2:83-84; 3:81 — the covenant of the prophets; 5:12; 5:70; 7:169; 33:7 — "and when We took from the prophets their covenant — and from thee, and Noah, and Abraham, and Moses, and Jesus son of Mary — We took from them a solemn covenant — mīthāqan ghalīẓan" — the identical collocation) — with *ghalīẓ* — from gh-l-ẓ — thick, dense, strong: the covenant described by its own materiality — not parchment-thin but load-bearing: a treaty of thickness, because its terms connect heaven's patience to earth's history. The commentators note the standing enumeration compressed in the verse: mountain, gate, Sabbath, all three bound by the single thick covenant — and the standing irony the sūrah then develops immediately in v. 155: the same community whose covenant was of *ghalīẓ* quality broke it in every registered particular — the very next verse naming the breach ("then for their breaking of their covenant..."). The sūrah of covenants — whose entire architecture, from 4:1's standing exordium ("O mankind — fear your Lord") through its marriage-treaties and orphan-trusts, is a sustained jurisprudence of *kept* bonds — here places the standing counter-example at full scale: a community that received every reinforcement heaven could engineer — levitated mountain, dictated entry-posture, sanctified calendar — and still breached: the demonstration the chapter now carries forward against its present Madīnan addressees and every reader since: covenant-breaking is never a failure of the covenant's reinforcement; it is a failure of response — and the thickness of the treaty measures the ruin of those who break it, no less than its security for those who keep.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:155

> **Then, for their breaking of their covenant, and their disbelieving in the signs of God, and their slaying of the prophets without right, and their saying: "Our hearts are uncircumcised" — Nay! God has set a seal upon them for their disbelief, so they believe not, save a few —**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Fa-Bi-Mā Naqḍihim Mīthāqahum: The Indictment Opens With the Breach**

The verse begins mid-sentence — a *fa-* of causation whose promised consequence arrives at v. 160 ("and We forbade them good things that had been lawful") — but which first assembles, in verses 155–157, the standing bill of indictment: *fa-bi-mā naqḍihim mīthāqahum* — "then, for their breaking of their covenant": *naqḍ* — from n-q-ḍ — unravelling, undoing a knitted thing (its standing Book-file: 13:20-25 — "those who break God's covenant after contracting it, and sever what God has commanded to be joined... theirs is the curse"; 16:91-92 — the covenant not to be unspun like the spun thread — "fulfill God's covenant when you covenant"; 2:27's standing opening-file of Sūrah al-Baqarah: the breakers of God's covenant after confirming it) — the *mīthāq* of v. 154 — thick, mountain-witnessed, gate-and-Sabbath structured — undone thread by thread. The standing cross-register of the breach-file: 2:83-85 (the covenant recited — worship God alone, goodness to parents, near kin, orphans, the needy; shed not your blood nor expel one another — then the breach itemized); 5:12-13 (the covenant with the twelve chieftains — "they broke their covenant — so We cursed them and hardened their hearts"); 5:70 — the covenant taken, the messengers sent — "whenever a messenger came to them with what their souls did not desire, some they denied and some they slew."

**Wa Kufr Him bi-Āyāti Allāh: Disbelief in the Signs as Selective Reception**

The second count: *wa kufrihim bi-āyāti Allāh* — "and their disbelieving in the signs of God": *āyāt* — the standing double-unit of revelation (the verse of the Book and the portent in the world — 17:101's standing nine signs; 41:53 — "We shall show them Our signs in the horizons and in themselves") — and al-Ṭabarī's standing gloss localizes the charge's exact shape: they did not disbelieve in *all* signs uniformly; they received Torah-signs and refused what came after — the standing selective-reception already legislated at vv. 150–151 ("we believe in some and disbelieve in some") — this verse historical-documenting what those verses doctrinally define: the refusal of particular revelations (most pointedly Jesus, as v. 157 will detail; and ultimately — sūrah-addressed — Muḥammad) constituting *kufr bi-āyāti Allāh* — disbelief in God's signs *as such*: because the sign belongs to the Sender, partial reception is refusal of the Sender's sovereignty to address.

**Wa Qatlihimu al-Anbiyāʾa Bi-Ghayri Ḥaqq: The Prophet-Killing File**

The third count names the darkest institutional crime in the Book's history of covenant-people: *wa qatlihimu al-anbiyāʾa bi-ghayri ḥaqq* — "and their slaying of the prophets without right": a charge the Book levels repeatedly — and always with the phrase *bi-ghayri al-ḥaqq / bi-ghayri ḥaqq* — "without right" — the jurisprudential precision marking that these were not judicial executions but murders wearing judicial robes (its standing register: 2:61 — "and they slew the prophets without right — that because they disobeyed and used to transgress"; 2:91 — "why did you slay the prophets of God aforetime, if you are believers?"; 3:21 — "those who disbelieve in God's signs and slay the prophets without right and slay those who command justice among men — give them glad tidings of a painful punishment"; 3:112 — "they slew the prophets without right"; 3:181-183 — the standing pair with āyāt and fire-sacrifice taunt; 5:70) — the commentators (al-Ṭabarī's chains naming the conventional cases: Zechariah and John in the standing tafsīr-file; the traditions of the sawn prophet Isaiah in the standing report-literature) treating the count not as a handful of criminal episodes but as an *established culpability-pattern*: the standing rejectionists' terminal argument against inconvenient revelation being — where possible — the elimination of its bearer. And the Book's own structural irony is sharp here: the people of the *Book* — custodians of prophecy's registry — stand charged with homicide against prophecy itself: the archives guarded, the ambassadors killed.

**Wa Qawlihim Qulūbunā Ghulfun: "Our Hearts Are Uncircumcised" — and the Counter-Sealing**

The fourth count quotes their own defense and convicts them by it: *wa qawlihim qulūbunā ghulfun* — "and their saying: our hearts are uncircumcised": *ghulf* — the plural (or collective adjective) of *aghlaf* — uncircumcised, hence in the standing lexical gloss: *covered, sheathed, enwrapped* — the boast reading: our hearts are sheathed against your summons — receptivity refused on surgical grounds. The commentators (al-Ṭabarī's standing pairing with 2:88 — "and they said: our hearts are uncircumcised — nay, God has cursed them for their disbelief — little do they believe") unfold the double-resonance: (1) the literal community-marker: circumcision stood among them as the bodily sign of covenant-membership — so the claim "our hearts are *un*circumcised" exposes the covenant of these speakers as skin-deep — membership marked in flesh but never penetrating to the heart (the standing scriptural echo in their own register: Leviticus' "uncircumcised hearts" and Jeremiah's indictment running in parallel within the prior text-tradition the commentators knew); (2) the psychology of the boast: the sheathing presented as incapacity ("we *cannot* receive") while functioning as policy ("we *will not* receive") — 41:5's standing parallel-exposure of the same stratagem among later hearers ("our hearts are under coverings from what you call us to"). And the Book's answer is the standing verdict-formula of divine sealing: *bal ṭabaʿa Allāhu ʿalayhā bi-kufrihim* — "nay! God has set a seal upon them for their disbelief": *ṭabʿ* — sealing (its standing register: 2:7 — "God has sealed their hearts and their hearing"; 7:100-101; 9:93; 16:108; 30:59; 40:35; 42:24; 63:3) — and the theology of the seal here made deliberately judicial: *bi-kufrihim* — *for / because of* their disbelief — the sealing expressly a *consequence*, not a pre-dawn decree: the standing majority-reading of the commentators that the seal is God's punishment answering human transgression (10:74's standing sequencing — "thus do We seal the hearts of the transgressors") — their chosen unreceptivity ratified from above, the boastful incapacity made, by decree, actual.

**Fa-Lā Yuʾminūna illā Qalīlan: The Few — the Crack in the Seal**

The verse ends with the standing qualification that keeps the indictment from erasing the remnant: *fa-lā yuʾminūna illā qalīlan* — "so they believe not, save a few": with the standing alternative parsing registered by the commentators (al-Rāzī gathering both): *illā qalīlan* may read "save a few" (persons — the ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām-file: members of the community who broke through to belief in the Prophet) or "save a little" (of belief — partial assent remaining: Torah-confessing while refusing later revelation — the 2:88 pattern) — and the sūrah's own development favors the held-open door: v. 136's archipelago commanded belief in *all* the books and prophets; v. 152 rewarded the undivided believers without ethnic carve-out; and the People-of-the-Book movement of the chapter (running to v. 162's own *al-rāsikhūna fī al-ʿilmi minhum... wa al-muʾminūna* — "those firmly rooted in knowledge among them, and the believers, believe in what was sent down to thee") will shortly name the remnant it here excepts — the standing Qur'ānic pattern of indictment-with-exemption (3:110's "among them are believers"; 3:113-115's standing righteous-cohort file among the People of the Book; 3:199 — "among the People of the Book are those who believe in God and in what was sent down to you and what was sent down to them — humble toward God... theirs is their wage with their Lord"). The verse thus performs the standing jurisprudence of collective judgment: the community as covenant-bearer indicted in its institutional counts — breach, selective disbelief, prophet-slaughter, the sheathed-heart boast — and the seal imposed at institutional level ("upon *them*") — while *illā qalīlan* preserves, inside the sealed edifice, the standing window through which individuals always still may climb — the seal upon hearts never being the abolition of the Few but the explanation of their scarcity.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:156

> **And for their disbelief, and their uttering against Mary a tremendous calumny —**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Wa Bi-Kufrihim: Disbelief Named as the Mother-Charge**

The indictment of vv. 155–157 continues its fourth count — transitional and re-foundational: *wa bi-kufrihim* — "and for their disbelief": the bare noun, unqualified by object, functioning as the commentators read it (al-Ṭabarī's chains registering the standing gloss): the root-state beneath all the counted crimes — covenant-breach, sign-refusal, prophet-slaying, the sheathed-heart boast — each an eruption of this single condition. The placement is architectonic: immediately after the sealing ("God has set a seal upon them for their disbelief"), the verse returns to *kufr* as though to say: and for that same disbelief — now consider what it uttered next — leading into the fifth count with the terrible seamlessness of a court record: disbelief does not merely withhold assent; it generates speech — and the speech it generates here is among the worst in the Book's catalog of utterances.

**Wa Qawlihim ʿAlā Maryama Buhtānan ʿAẓīman: The Calumny Against Mary**

The fifth count is quoted, and the Book's own naming of the crime defines its magnitude: *wa qawlihim ʿalā Maryama buhtānan ʿaẓīman* — "and their uttering against Mary a tremendous calumny": *buhtān* — the slander-word already drilled at v. 112 within this sūrah ("whoever earns an offense or sin then casts it upon the innocent has burdened himself with *buhtān* and manifest sin") — the fabricated charge designed to deceive the hearer about its victim — and here qualified by the superlative *ʿaẓīm* — tremendous: a calumny of the first magnitude. The standing comment-canon identifies the charge: the insinuation of indecency against Mary — the virgin mother — when she returned bearing the child Jesus (the standing file at Sūrah Maryam: "then she brought him to her people, carrying him. They said: O Mary — thou hast brought a strange thing — O sister of Aaron — thy father was not an evil man, nor was thy mother unchaste" — 19:27-28 — the insinuation-pointer already in the text; the *slander-form proper* — the explicit accusation of unchastity — recorded in the standing tafsīr-reports as the gist of their rejection: rather than reading the miracle, they read scandal). The commentators mark the calumny's exact theological cost: the miracle of the virgin birth stood deliberately *legible* — the child himself speaking from the cradle in his mother's defense (19:30-33 — "verily I am the servant of God — He has given me the Book and made me a prophet") — yet the calumny-makers preferred the scandal-reading, because the miracle-reading would have obliged them before a prophet: disbelief protecting itself by defaming the evidence's mother. Ibn Kathīr's standing severity locates the count's order: of the possible refusals open to them — doubt, silence, departure — they chose the one that aimed at a woman's honor: kufr not only deaf but armed.

**Maryam al-Batūl in the Book's Own Register: The Lady the Calumny Could Not Reach**

Against the slander the Book has already installed its own standing memorial — and the commentators, commenting v. 156, regularly recite the counter-file as though to answer the calumny perpetually: 3:42 — "the angels said: O Mary — verily God has chosen thee and purified thee and chosen thee above the women of the worlds"; 66:12 — "and Mary daughter of ʿImrān, who guarded her chastity — so We breathed into it of Our Spirit — and she confirmed the words of her Lord and His books — and she was of the obedient"; 3:37 — the Lord's beautiful acceptance of her ("a beautiful acceptance — ḥasan — and reared her a beautiful rearing"); 21:91 — "she who guarded her chastity — We breathed into her of Our Spirit, and made her and her son a sign for the worlds"; 19:16-21 — the annunciation-file complete. Al-Qushayrī's standing classification (noted across the later commentaries) places Mary in the rank of God's waliyyah — His protected friend — and draws the standing two-sided warning the verse's charge embodies: two kinds of people err concerning the saints — those who exaggerate them (in Mary's case, the deifyers — 5:116's standing eschatological arraignment: "O Jesus son of Mary — didst thou say to men: take me and my mother as two gods beside glory be to Thee!") and those who denigrate them — as here: the calumny that would not see the miracle for the scandal. Between the two errors stands the Book's own measurement: mother-of-a-prophet, pure, chosen, sign-carrying — honored forever — while the slanderers' count sits in the indictment of v. 156, payable on the Day the wronged of v. 148's exception-clause receive their full hearing.

**The Standing Lesson of the Buhtān-Counts: Disbelief Needs False Witness**

The verse's compressed charge (six words in Arabic) is framed by the commentators as a standing study in the *speech-economy* of disbelief: truth needs only to be told; error must arm itself — and its weapon of first resort is the fabricated accusation. The sequence of the counts at vv. 155–157 maps the escalation: covenant quietly broken — then signs selectively refused — then inconvenient prophets removed — then the unreceptive heart defended as a surgical fact — then, when even those defenses failed against a speaking infant, the slander of his mother — the final instrument of unbelief being always the honor-charge, because honor-questions are the questions unanswerable by laboratory: Mary could not *prove* a miracle the scandalizers refused to see; she could only be what she was — and God be what He is: and the Book records the standing adjournment of the case: the calumny entered into evidence; the Verdict deferred — vv. 160-161's file (the forbidding of good things once lawful — the standing consequence-clause of this entire indictment) naming the first penalty installment in history, and 4:161's "severe punishment prepared for the disbelievers among them" the standing remainder. The next verse's count — the sixth — will complete the file in its most consequential utterance of all: "we slew the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, the messenger of God" — the boast that the Book will answer with its own fourfold negation, and with the raising that undid it.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:157

> **And for their saying: "We slew the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, the messenger of God" — though they slew him not, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear so unto them. Verily those who differ concerning him are in doubt about him; they have no knowledge of him, but follow only conjecture — and they slew him not for certain —**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Wa Qawlihim Innanā Qatalnā al-Masīḥa: The Boast That Filed Itself as Evidence**

The indictment's sixth count quotes the boast itself: *wa qawlihim innanā qatalnā al-Masīḥa ʿĪsā ibna Maryama rasūla Allāh* — "and for their saying: we slew the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, the messenger of God": the commentators (al-Zamakhsharī's standing gloss leading) read the utterance in its performative register: not a legal confession but a *taunt* — the dismissal of Jesus' prophethood by claiming his judicial disposal: we dealt with your "messenger" as the Law deals with claimants — death by the civic procedure — the same psychology of v. 155's prophet-slaying file now applied to its most famous name. The Book's own framing is exact: four full titles attached to him inside the quoted boast — *al-Masīḥ* (the Messiah — the standing title, its register: 3:45 — "his name is the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary — eminent in this world and the Hereafter, and of those brought near"; 4:171-172; 5:17; 5:72; 5:75; 9:30-31), *ʿĪsā ibna Maryam* (Jesus son of Mary — the matronymic that is itself the Book's standing refutation of the paternity-slanders: named for his mother, as no son of Joseph-narrative ever was in the slanderers' file), and *rasūlu Allāh* (the messenger of God — the Book inside the quotation correcting the boast's estimate of its victim) — the indictment thus quoting its perpetrators at their most self-satisfied, immediately before reversing the claim's factual basis wholesale.

**Wa Mā Qatalūhu wa Mā Ṣalabūhu wa Lākin Shubbiha Lahum: The Fourfold Negation**

Then the Book's famous negation — the only passage addressing the crucifixion-event in the entire Qur'ān: *wa mā qatalūhu wa mā ṣalabūhu wa lākin shubbiha lahum* — "though they slew him not, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear so unto them": *shubbiha* — passive of sh-b-h — resemblance-making: a likeness imposed — and the tradition of interpretation built its standing accounts upon the passive's open agency: the appearance engineered — by God — upon some figure of the arrest-scene. The standing accounts in the comment-canon (al-Ṭabarī's chains, through Ibn Kathīr's and al-Zamakhsharī's collections): (1) the arresting party could not distinguish Jesus among his gathered followers — a divine resemblance cast so that the circle looked alike — and another was taken in his place; (2) the specific report-variants naming a disciple who *volunteered* to assume the likeness and bear the death — sometimes specified as having asked Jesus for "the likeness and the promised companion-rank in Paradise" — and being crucified (i.e., publicly exposed upon the beam — the standing lexical note: ṣalb in the commentators' usage here often post-mortem exposure — matching the verse's order: "slew him not, nor crucified him": slaying first, exposure second) in Jesus' stead; (3) the Wahb ibn Munabbih account-line — the perfidious insider (the Judas-figure of the gospel-file) made to wear the likeness as his treachery's own recompense — betrayer executed in betrayed's image. The commentators' standing note for the record: since *shubbiha lahum* covers the perception of *them* — addressed to the boast-makers but naturally extending to the watching crowd — the appearance ruled the scene for almost everyone present — al-Ṭabarī's standing pastoral clause following: no charge of dishonesty lies upon those Christians who, trusting the dramatic public record of the event, believe the crucifixion occurred — the Book's target throughout being the *boast* and the *rejection*, not the witness of deceived eyes.

**Al-Rāzī's Standing Objection: The Deception-Problem**

The comment-canon also preserves the tradition's own internal audit — and no treatment of this verse is complete without it: al-Rāzī's celebrated objection to the substitution-accounts: if God casts likenesses upon persons such that sensory identification fails, the entire edifice of testimony-based law trembles — marriage-identity, witness-identification, the whole witness-economy of the sharīʿah resting on perceived personhood; the Quran itself builds upon sight its own procedures. Al-Rāzī therefore inclines to readings avoiding mass deception of identity — the standing alternatives gathered in his long discussion: death occurring but not at their hands as claimed (they neither killed nor crucified — the event otherwise than their boast, its appearance interpreted by them in boast-fashion); or the semblance attaching to the mode of Jesus' exit rather than to another's execution. The tradition's standing counter-notice from Ibn Kathīr's register and others: providentially altered perception is not without Book-precedent — 8:43-44 at Badr: "when God showed them to thee in thy dream as few... and when you met, He made them seem few in your eyes and made you seem few in their eyes — that God might accomplish a thing foreordained" — the audience-perception at Badr adjusted on both sides by decree: where the purpose is prophecy's deliverance, the commentary-record judges, the Ruler of perception may adjust the perceived — the disagreement itself being the tradition's standing testimony that the verse's grammar holds its mystery: *shubbiha lahum* states the appearance without inventorying its mechanics.

**Inna Alladhīna Ikhtalafū Fīhi La-Fī Shakkin Minhu: Doubt as the Standing Verdict of Difference**

The sentence then widens from event to epistemology: *inna alladhīna ikhtalafū fīhi la-fī shakkin minhu mā lahum bihi min ʿilmin illā ittibāʿa al-ẓann* — "verily those who differ concerning him are in doubt about him; they have no knowledge of him, but follow only conjecture": the pronoun *fīhi* — "concerning him" — read by its standing double-gloss (al-Zamakhsharī preferring "concerning *it*" — concerning the whole affair): the differing-parties placed by the Book's judicial grammar inside *shakk* — doubt — and *ẓann* — conjecture — the standing Book-epistemology of awe-files (its register of ẓann as the false coin of disputed truth: 4:157's own neighbor 53:23 — "they follow naught but conjecture and what the souls desire"; 6:116 — "if thou obeyest most of those on earth they will mislead thee from God's way — they follow naught but conjecture"; 10:36; 10:66; 45:24's standing would-be cosmology built on conjecture; 53:28 — "they have no knowledge thereof — they follow only conjecture — and conjecture avails naught against truth") — the standing referent of "those who differ" read two ways: the Jewish authorities themselves uncertain whether the execution had truly reached Jesus (al-Ṭabarī's and al-Zamakhsharī's prime reading — the boast's own cover-story already fraying); or, in al-Qurṭubī's register, the later Christian differentiations over the event's nature. The verse's diagnostic here is less about the first century than about the standing epistemology of contested salvation-events: where parties differ over a matter the Book has ruled upon, their difference itself is named the proof of their epistemic station: *lā ʿilm* — no knowledge — only *ittibāʿ al-ẓann* — the following of conjecture — as though conjecture were a guide-dog that could be followed home.

**Wa Mā Qatalūhu Yaqīnan: The Closing Certainty**

The verse doubles its negation into seal: *wa mā qatalūhu yaqīnan* — "and they slew him not for certain": *yaqīnan* — the accusative of emphasis — either as standing certainty-adverb ("certainly did not slay him" — the majority reading: God's *repeated* negation terminating every debate by restating the fact: whatever was done, to whomever, under whatever appearance — they did not slay him) or as the standing idiomatic reading registered in the comment-canon (al-Qurṭubī noting the usage): "they killed it not with certainty" — their *doubt* itself remaining unslain — the uncertainty persisting unrectified beneath the boast: the sentence thereby, on this register, convicting them even internally: the claim-cry "we slew the Messiah" delivered over an inquest their own hearts never closed. Either register terminates at the same standing verdict the Book now springs in the next verse: the entire earthly file — arrest, appearance, execution-scene, boast — overruled by one celestial motion announced with the standing Name-pair of majesty-and-wisdom: *bal rafaʿahu Allāhu ilayh* — "but God raised him unto Himself" — v. 158's own file: the deliverance as divine act, the failure of the boast as divine design — the account of Jesus in the Book closing not on a beam but in an ascent.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:158

> **But God raised him unto Himself; and God is ever Mighty, Wise.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Bal Rafaʿahu Allāhu Ilayh: The Ascent That Overrules the Beam**

The Book closes the crucifixion-file with its counter-event — five words in Arabic that the entire tradition reads as the axis of the Jesus-history: *bal rafaʿahu Allāhu ilayh* — "but God raised him unto Himself": *bal* — "but/rather" — the particle of amendment — cancelling the whole boast-narrative in one corrective stroke (its standing usage: as at 2:88's "nay — God has cursed them..." — the abrupt divine override); *rafaʿa* — to raise: the raising-verb whose selection the commentators mark as a precise technical choice: not *baʿatha* (to resurrect — the standing word for raising *from the dead*, as at 2:56; 19:33's own standing Jesus-file: "peace be upon me the day I was born, and the day I die, and the day I am raised alive — *ubʿathu ḥayyan*" — the resurrection-lexicon there), but *rafaʿa* — the elevation-word that needs no antecedent death — and *ilayh* — "unto Himself" — the destination stated as the Divine Presence itself. The verse joins its standing twin 3:55 as the two-source Qur'ānic foundation of the ascension: "when God said: O Jesus — verily I shall take thee and raise thee unto Myself and purify thee of those who disbelieve" — *mutawaffīka wa rāfiʿuka ilayya* — the commentators noting the twin-verse's double vocabulary (taking + raising) and the present verse's economy (raising, direct) — together establishing the standing doctrine: Jesus ascended to God directly from the earthly scene — the file closing not in a tomb but in the raising.

**The Mortality-Puzzle the Tradition Filed Under This Verse**

The verse's implications set the standing theological inventory, and the commentators unfold them in order: (1) the Book is unwavering that Jesus is *not* divine (5:116's standing arraignment-dialogue; 5:72; 5:75 — "the Messiah son of Mary is but a messenger — messengers have passed away before him — and his mother a truthful woman — they both used to eat food"); (2) therefore, mortal nature attaches to him as to every human messenger ("We did not give them bodies that ate no food — nor were they immortal" — 21:8; 21:34 — "We granted not immortality to any man before thee"); (3) therefore his death is *real but pending* — the tradition locating it after the return at the end of time: the standing eschatology-file (its register in the sunni hadith-collections: the descent of Jesus at the white minaret in Damascus, the slaying of the Dajjāl, the breaking of the cross and the just rule, then death and funeral among the Muslims — its standing registers in Muslim's Ṣaḥīḥ and the Sunan-collections) — Jesus' biography in the standing Muslim account thus running: virgin birth — mission — raising alive to God (this verse) — return — death (19:33's own words) — resurrection with all mankind. Ibn Kathīr's standing note within the exegetical file resolves the apparent double-scene of the last hours: some of his followers witnessed the raising itself and knew he had not died; others witnessed the appearance and believed the Jewish account — the two witness-strata coexisting from the first hour, and the Book adjudicating between them: *bal rafaʿahu Allāh*. And the standing boundary-gloss some commentators add: that "raising" does not logically preclude a *death-and-raising* sequence (2:259's standing hundred-year sleeper, *then* raised — baʿatha) — but the verse's own syntax — negating both slaying and crucifixion, then substituting raising — deploys its weight on the direct-ascension side, where the standing tradition consolidated.

**Wa Kāna Allāhu ʿAzīzan Ḥakīman: Might and Wisdom as the Twin Seals of the Deliverance**

The verse seals with the standing Name-pair that the commentators read as the explanatory signature of the whole affair: *wa kāna Allāhu ʿazīzan ḥakīman* — "and God is ever Mighty, Wise": *ʿazīz* — the Mighty, the Unconquerable (its standing register sealing act-of-power verses across the Book: 2:209; 2:220; 2:228; 3:6; 5:38; 8:10; 8:63; 8:67; 9:40 — "God is Mighty, Wise"; 48:7; 48:19) — the Might specifying *how* the deliverance succeeded: the arresting authorities held the square, the guards, the sentence, the crowd — and the outcome fell entirely outside their writ because Might does not negotiate with jurisdiction: the boast "we slew the Messiah" undone by the attribute "*ʿAzīz*" — One whom no coalition outbids; and *ḥakīm* — the All-Wise — specifying *why* the deliverance took this extraordinary form rather than the ordinary: Wisdom choosing dramaturgy that would instruct all parties forever: the boastful authorities taught that their writ ends at the sky; the watching disciples taught that messengers are delivered by means beyond the visible cordons; the slanderers of Mary answered by the elevation of her son past every earthly tribunal; and the later centuries of theological controversy already ruled upon in advance (5:116's dialogue; 4:171-172 below) — Wisdom engineering an event whose *appearance* would be debated exactly where Wisdom wanted debate to die: in the standing acknowledgment that *no one knows the scene finally except God* — "they have no knowledge of it" (v. 157) — because the event's decisive motion happened in the register where *rafaʿahu Allāhu ilayh* operates: not in the arena of the accusers, but in the vertical direction of the Mighty, the Wise. The Jesus-file of the sūrah thereby closes its first panel (vv. 156–158): calumny answered by exaltation; execution-boast answered by negation; earthly closure answered by heavenly opening — and the sequel the Book immediately legislates: v. 159 — the standing eschatological remainder: "there is not one of the People of the Book but shall surely believe in him before his death" — the raising not being the end of the Jesus-ministry, but its adjournment — to a session where every one of the addressed communities shall at last confess the truth of him, and "on the Day of Resurrection he shall be a witness against them."

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:159

> **And there is not one of the People of the Book but shall surely believe in him before his death; and on the Day of Resurrection he shall be a witness against them.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Wa In min Ahli al-Kitābi illā La-Yuʾminanna Bihi: The Pronoun That Holds Two Deaths**

The Jesus-file's sequel opens with its standing universal — and immediately divides the comment-canon over one possessive pronoun: *wa in min ahli al-kitābi illā la-yuʾminanna bihi qabla mawtih* — "and there is not one of the People of the Book but shall surely believe in him before his death": the oath-weighted formula (*in... illā la-* — "there is none... but that he shall surely...") leaving no exception in its class — every single member of the People of the Book — and the possessive *-hi* of *qabla mawtih* — "before *his* death" — the standing fork: (1) before *Jesus'* death — the reading al-Ṭabarī, Ibn Kathīr, and al-Zamakhsharī consolidate as primary in the register of reports from Ibn ʿAbbās and others: since v. 158 has just established that Jesus was raised alive and has *not yet died*, the verse schedules the universal belief for the era of his return at the end of time — the descent, the Dajjāl-battle, and the file of the standing hadith-register (Muslim's standing register 155 and the Sunan-collections: "by Him in whose hand is my soul — the son of Mary is about to descend among you as a just judge — he shall break the cross, kill the swine, abolish the jizyah, and wealth shall overflow until none accepts it") — at which hour the People of the Book, Jews and Christians alike, "shall surely believe in him" — believing him to be what the Book declares: God's servant and messenger (the standing predicate ambiguity of *yuʾminanna bihi* glossed by the commentators: belief *in* him — in the truth of his prophethood and the truth of his declared status — not adoption of every historical community's doctrine *about* him); the standing quote of Ibn ʿAbbās in the tafsīr-tradition: "before the death of Jesus son of Mary" — the report preserved in the canonical tafsīr-chains beside its own completion ("and on that day, the People of the Book will all believe" — its standing register).

**Qabla Mawtih (II): The Alternative — Belief at the Edge of One's Own Death**

(2) before *each one's own* death — the second standing reading (recorded through the same chains among early authorities including some reports from Ibn ʿAbbās's circle): every individual of the People of the Book, at the approach of his own death-moment — when the veil lifts and the truth of Jesus' status becomes visible in the dying hour’s disclosure — "shall surely believe in him": a belief arriving at the very edge, where — the commentators immediately attach the ancient rule (al-Ṭabarī's and Ibn Kathīr's standing filing: 10:90-91's standing template) — it profits nothing: Pharaoh drowning cried "I believe that there is no god but He in whom the Children of Israel believe — and I am of the submitters" — and the answer was and thou wast aforetime in rebellion" — deathbed-faith classified as sight-of-the-unseen, not faith: *lā yanfaʿu nafsan īmānuhā* at the hour repentance-signs close (4:18; 6:158 — "the day some of thy Lord's signs arrive — a soul's belief shall not avail it, that believed not before"). The commentators generally treat both readings as preserveable truths — the first anchoring the verse in the eschatology of the return (and receiving, in the register of narrations, the stronger chain-support), the second anchoring it in the theology of the deathbed — and many let both stand together: the Book's standing capacity for doubled reference in a single pronoun being, in their reading, not a defect of the verse but its design: the pronoun holding both deaths because both deaths hold the same confession — Jesus will be believed in, universally, either at his return or at every individual's last threshold — each a *qabla mawtih* in its own frame.

**Wa Yawma al-Qiyāmati Yakūnu ʿAlayhim Shahīdan: The Witness-Office of Jesus**

The verse closes with the standing office of the messengers at the Judgment: *wa yawma al-qiyāmati yakūnu ʿalayhim shahīdan* — "and on the Day of Resurrection he shall be a witness *against* them": shahīd — witness — upon (*ʿalā*) them — the standing Book-doctrine that the messengers themselves testify concerning their peoples' reception: 4:41's own standing assembly within this very sūrah ("how shall it be, when We bring from every community a witness, and bring thee as witness against these?"); 16:84; 16:89 — "We shall raise up in every community a witness against them from among themselves — and We bring thee as witness against these"; 39:69 — the standing tribunal-scene; and Jesus' own deposition-text preserved in the Book itself — 5:116-117's standing testimony-record: "O Jesus son of Mary — didst thou say to men: take me and my mother as two gods beside he says: glory be to Thee — it was not for me to say what I had no right to... I said to them naught but what Thou commandest me: worship God, my Lord and your Lord — and I was a witness over them while I abode among them — but when Thou tookest me, Thou wast the Watcher over them — and Thou art Witness of all things" — the witness-content thereby specified by the Book in advance of the Day: twofold — *for* the truth (he delivered the message of servanthood-worship) and *against* both deviations that the sūrah's own dossier records: the claim of his divinity made by those who exaggerated (the 4:171-172 file just below: "the Messiah son of Mary was but a messenger... believe in God and His messengers and say not: Three"; 5:72-74; 9:30-31), and the denial of his prophethood by those who boasted his execution (v. 157's own indictment). The standing comment-canon thus reads v. 159 as the eschatological summation of the whole Jesus-dossier of the sūrah: raised (158), believed-in ultimately and universally (159a), and installed as standing witness at the Trial (159b) — the person over whom the two communities divided becoming, in the Book's juridical eschatology, the very evidence-bearer of their division: the cross-boast and the sonship-claim alike subpoenaed to answer to the man himself — alive at God's right, returned to the earth, and seated finally in the witness-box of the Day of Resurrection.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:160

> **And for the wrongdoing of those who are Jews, We forbade them good things that had been made lawful unto them, and for their turning many from the way of God —**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Fa-Bi-Ẓulmin min Alladhīna Hādū: The Sentence Clause Fulfilled**

The long subordinate-clause that opened at v. 155 ("then, *for* their breaking of their covenant...") at last delivers its consequence — and the commentators mark the completion of the indictment-architecture: the *fa-bi-mā* of v. 155 and the *fa-bi-ẓulmin* here are one judicial motion: "for the breaking... for the disbelief... for the slaying... for the calumny... for the boast... and for the wrongdoing of those who are Jews" — the verdict arriving as: *ḥarramnā ʿalayhim ṭayyibātin uḥillat lahum* — "We forbade them good things that had been made lawful unto them": *ẓulm* — wrongdoing — the standing comprehensive within the indictment, gathering the prior counts under its canopy (its standing Book-definition: injustice as the putting of things out of their place — and the indictment-file having exhibited precisely a covenant displaced, signs displaced, prophets displaced, honor displaced); and the community-designation *alladhīna hādū* — "those who are Jews" — the standing gentilic of the register (its own usage across the Book: 2:62; 2:111; 2:135; 4:46; 5:18; 5:41; 5:44; 5:64; 5:69; 6:146) — locating the verdict historically in the specific covenant-community whose file has been under review.

**Ṭayyibāt: The Good Things Withdrawn — Food-Laws as Judicial History**

The penalty names its instrument — *Ṭayyibāt* — "good things": the commentators (al-Ṭabarī's standing collection) restrict its reference here by the word's standing usage: pleasant provisions, chiefly *foods* — the pure, the enjoyable (its standing register: 2:172 — "eat of the good things We have provided you"; 5:4-5; 8:69; 16:114; 20:81 — "eat of the good things We have provided you — and transgress not therein"; 23:51; and the manna-quail context of 2:57; 7:160) — the prohibition-verse at hand thereby matching its standing twin-file: 3:93 — "all food was lawful unto the Children of Israel, save what Israel had forbidden for himself before the Torah was sent down" — the baseline of comprehensive permission; and 6:146 — the standing inventory of the specific withdrawal: "and upon those who are Jews We forbade every clawed animal — and of oxen and sheep We forbade them their fat, save what their backs carry or the entrails or what is mixed with bone — thus did We requite them for their insolence — and verily We are truthful": the *jazāʾ*-clause of 6:146 — "thus did We requite them for their insolence (baghyahum)" — naming the same judicial logic our verse installs: the food-restrictions entered not as arbitrary ritual-burdens but as *requital* — a withdrawal of amenity from a rebellious treasury — the standing jurisprudential note developed by the commentators: the ṭayyibāt-forfeiture standing as the *worldly* installment of the counts of vv. 155–159, distinct from the Hereafter's prepared punishment arriving at v. 161's close: two registers of consequence — diet in history, fire beyond it.

**Wa Bi-Ṣaddihim ʿan Sabīli Allāhi Kathīran: The Barring of Many as a Separate Count**

The verse adds a final count to the file — with its own causal particle: *wa bi-ṣaddihim ʿan sabīli Allāhi kathīran* — "and for their turning many from the way of God": *ṣadd* — from ṣ-d-d — barring, diverting, obstructing (its standing register: 4:167 below — "those who disbelieve and bar from God's way"; 5:2 — "let not hatred of a people who barred you from the Sacred Mosque move you to transgress"; 7:45; 8:47; 11:19; 14:3; 22:25; 29:38; 43:37; 58:16) — the barring here reading either as (1) their averting *many others* from God's way — *kathīran* as object: multitudes turned back, the scholars' errant authority deflecting common people from successive revelations (the standing charge-pattern of 9:31; 9:34 — taking their rabbis and monks as lords; devouring wealth) — or (2) *kathīran* adverbially: barring *much/frequently* — obstruction as habitual policy. Both registers converge on the standing dynamic the commentators name: religious authorities who stand at the intersection of their community and God's new address, positioned to escort or to bar — their choice echoing through the multitudes who trust their gatekeeping — 5:63's standing rebuke of the neighbor-file ("why do the masters and rabbis not forbid them from their sinful speech and their consuming the evil is what they used to practice"). The verse thus closes the count-list where it began — *ẓulm* — and the standing structure of vv. 155–161 reads now in full judicial order: charges (breach, disbelief, slaying, the sheathed-heart boast, the calumny against Mary, the execution-boast, wrongdoing, usury-eating, barring of multitudes); historical requital (ṭayyibāt withdrawn); and the standing Hereafter-installment immediately ahead: "We have prepared for the disbelievers among them a painful punishment" (v. 161). The sūrah of the household of faith thereby records, in its last addressed file to its neighboring covenant-community, the total architecture of accountability: the same God who posts watchers over orphans (4:6), spouses (4:34-35), and witnesses (4:135) also audits the ledgers of religious establishments — and where their gatekeepers bar His road, the heavens narrow their tables before the fire narrows their refuge.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:161

> **And for their taking usury, though they had been forbidden it, and for their consuming men's wealth falsely; and We have prepared for the disbelievers among them a painful punishment.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Wa Akhdhihimu al-Ribā: Usury in the Covenant-Community's File**

The indictment hands down its economic counts: *wa akhdhihimu al-ribā wa qad nuhū ʿanhu* — "and for their taking usury, though they had been forbidden it": *ribā* — from r-b-w — increase, growth — the standing name of the usurious increment (its standing full dossier in the Book: 2:275 — "those who consume usury shall not rise save as one rises whom Satan has confounded by his touch — that because they said: commerce is but like usury — yet God has permitted commerce and forbidden usury"; 2:276 — "God blots out usury and augments charities"; 2:278-279 — "O you who believe — fear God and relinquish what remains of usury, if you are believers — but if you do not, then be informed of war from God and His Messenger"; 3:130 — "O you who believe — consume not usury, doubled and many-fold"; 30:39 — the ribā-zakāt antithesis: "what you give in usury, that it may increase upon people's wealth, increases not with God — but what you give in alms, desiring the Face of God — those are the doublers") — the verse's quiet historical precision noted by the commentators: *wa qad nuhū ʿanhu* — "though they had been forbidden it": the prohibition standing in *their own* covenant-code — the prior revelation's standing registers known to the addressed community — so that the count is not *failure to know* but defiance of known law: the covenant-community's own ribā-ban acknowledged, then bypassed by stratagem — the standing report-material in the tafsīr-file describing the evasion-mechanics (sale-constructs designed as loans in costume, the standing ḥiyal-techniques by which increase upon loans was dressed as commerce) — the same engineering of forms the Sabbath-file (4:154; 2:65's standing parallel; 7:163's net-casting on Friday-eve) already registered as the community's standing temptation: law-gaming named among the covenant-counts.

**Wa Aklihim Amwāla al-Nāsi bi-al-Bāṭil: Wealth-Devouring as Established Convict-File**

Then the second economic count — *wa aklihim amwāla al-nāsi bi-al-bāṭil* — "and for their consuming men's wealth falsely": the *akl-bāṭil* formula standing as one of the sūrah's own load-bearing phrases (4:29 — "consume not your wealth among yourselves falsely — except it be commerce by mutual consent"; 4:30's standing consequence-verse; 4:10's own standing archetype — "those who consume the orphans' property unjustly consume but fire into their bellies") — its extension into the covenant-file here registering further specific practices in the comment-canon's standing reports: religious fees for altering judgment; gifts to authorities that functioned as judgments-for-hire; the standing neighbor-charge of 9:34's file ("many of the rabbis and monks consume men's wealth falsely and bar from God's way"); 2:188's standing general prohibition ("consume not your wealth among yourselves falsely, nor proffer it to judges, that you may consume a portion of people's wealth sinfully while you know"); 5:62-63's standing note ("many of them hastening into sin and transgression and their consuming the unlawful — evil is what they used to do"). The commentators mark the phrase's standing anatomy: *bi-al-bāṭil* — "falsely" — the wealth-transfer morally possible (donations! fees! bargains!) yet legally void because its basis is null — and the consuming named *akl* — eating — the Book's standing metaphor of ingestion (as at 4:10): property-wrongdoing digested into the body of the perpetrator — the standing eschatological gloss of 4:10 already installed: such eating is fire-ingestion by stages.

**The Commerce-Question the Jurists Filed Under This Count**

The legal tradition's standing practical deliberation attaches at this verse — and al-Qurṭubī's register preserves its resolution: some early legists, reading this indictment of wealth-practices, deliberated whether *commerce with* the addressed community stood lawful at all; the standing answer derived from two fixed sources: the Book itself — 5:5 — "this day the good things are made lawful to you — and the food of those who were given the Book is lawful for you — and your food is lawful for them" — inter-community food-exchange explicitly sanctified; and the Prophet's standing practice — his own transactions — buying, pledging his armor in pledge (the standing armor-ransom-file: the Prophet's coat of mail mortgaged to a Jewish merchant for provisions, its register in Bukhārī's collections — Bukhārī 2916 and its standing parallels) — establishing the ummah's standing precedent: indictment of corrupt *practices* never annulling the lawfulness of ordinary *intercourse* — a distinction the Jurists enshrined as standing principle: accusation of a party's corrupt modes does not render the party untouchable; only the mode is judged.

**Wa Aʿtadnā li-l-Kāfirīna Minhum ʿAdhāban Alīman: The Prepared Punishment — with Its Standing Exemption**

The sentence seals its consequence with the standing preparation-formula — twice now in the chapter's register (v. 151's *muhīn*; here *alīm*): *wa aʿtadnā li-l-kāfirīna minhum ʿadhāban alīman* — "and We have prepared for the disbelievers among them a painful punishment": *aʿtadnā* — held ready (its standing register: 4:18; 4:37; 4:93; 4:102; 4:151; 5:33; 9:63; 17:10 and the several standing stations) — the punishment pre-fabricated; and the word the commentators seize as the verse's own open window: *minhum* — "*among* them" — the partitive: not the whole community uniformly but *the disbelievers among them* — the standing exemption-architecture of this sūrah's People-of-the-Book-file (v. 155's *illā qalīlan* window; v. 159's universal-belief horizon; and arriving immediately at v. 162: "but those firmly rooted in knowledge among them — and the believers — believing in what was sent down to thee and in what was sent down before thee... unto them We shall grant a great reward") — the file's final division thereby installed: this chapter never indicts a genealogy; it indicts *convictions and practices* — and in the very verses of sentencing it posts the exit-staircase to the rooted-in-knowledge and the believing: punishment prepared for "the disbelievers among them," reward granted to those of the same community who believe the whole revelation — the standing Qur'ānic jurisprudence that has run through the sūrah of the Watcher from its first verse: no party saved or damned by badge, but only by *taqwā and what it does with the covenant it received* — the ṭayyibāt-withdrawal in history and the prepared fire beyond it both pointed, at their standing targets, at conduct — while the door to *ajran kabīran* (a great reward) opens in the very next verse to any of them — and of any community — who will believe and do.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:162

> **But those firmly rooted in knowledge among them, and the believers — believing in what was sent down to thee and in what was sent down before thee, those who keep the prayer and give the alms, and believe in God and the Last Day — unto those We shall grant a great reward.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Lākini al-Rāsikhūna fī al-ʿIlmi Minhum: After the Indictment, the Remnant**

The verdict-file of vv. 155–161 had descended count by count; now the Book executes the turn its every chapter of judgment contains — the adversative of rescue: *lākini al-rāsikhūna fī al-ʿilmi minhum wa al-muʾminūna* — "but those firmly rooted in knowledge among them, and the believers": *al-rāsikhūna* — from r-s-kh — to be firmly rooted, to be set deep and immovable (its standing Qur'ānic technical coinage: 3:7's standing division of the community of scripture — "it is He who sent down the Book upon thee — among it verses decisive... and among it verses ambiguous... and none knows their interpretation but God. And those firmly rooted in knowledge say: we believe in it — all of it is from our Lord") — a commentator-aristocracy whose firmness is precisely their submission: knowledge rooted rather than floating; and *minhum* — "*among them*" — the partitive the whole sūrah has been holding in reserve: the indictment was never ethnic but covenantal — and within the very community so counted stands a corps of the deeply learned whose knowledge issues in full belief — "believing in what was sent down to thee and in what was sent down before thee": two-directional faith: the Torah and its true successors affirmed together (the standing undivided-subscription of 4:152 above; 2:136; 2:285; 3:84; the archipelago standing intact). The standing historical gloss of the commentators (al-Ṭabarī; al-Rāzī; al-Ṭabrisī; al-Zamakhsharī's register) names the earliest bearers of the description: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām and his fellow-learned of Madīnah who, knowing the earlier scripture and recognizing the new, believed in both — the standing files of his conversion in the tafsīr-records and sīrah-literature (Jewish scholars acknowledging the Prophet as described in their own books).

**Wa al-Muʾminūna: One Noun, Two Readings — and Their Consequence**

The second noun — *wa al-muʾminūna* — carries the commentators' standing double-construal: (1) as coordinate-explication of the rāsikhūn among the People of the Book — "and the believers" = those of them who believe — in which case the verse testifies to an astonishing standing possibility: that believing, righteous members of that community, confessing both their scripture and Muḥammad's, receive *a great reward* — their reward-documents distinct from either condemnatory file (its standing parallels: 3:113-115 — "they are not all alike — among the People of the Book is an upright community who recite God's signs through the night... they believe in God and the Last Day"; 3:199 — "among the People of the Book are those who believe in God and in what was sent down to you and what was sent down to them, humble toward God — they sell not the signs of God for a small price — theirs is their wage with their Lord"; 5:65-66; 28:52-54 — those given the Book before it believing in it, recompensed twice); and (2) as a general reference to the Muslim believers set beside the learned of the People of the Book: the rooted of *them*, and the believers of *the ummah* — both registry-lines ending at the same reward (al-Rāzī harvesting both without exclusion). Even the verse's grammar enters the commentary's workshop: *wa al-muqīmīna al-ṣalāta* — "those who keep the prayer" — stands in the *accusative* where syntax expects the nominative — the grammarians and commentators (al-Ṭabarī; al-Ṭabrisī; al-Zamakhsharī) registering the standing resolutions: an accusative of *praise* — the list-shift itself functioning as underlining ("and — especially — those who keep the prayer" — the standing Arabic device of case-shift to signal distinct honor); and a second reading construing it as object of *yuʾminūna* — "believing in... [and in] those who keep the prayer" — the object then read, per reports, as the angels or the prophets themselves (faith extended to the whole chain of worshippers). Both dissolve toward the same standing sum: prayer-keeping and almsgiving singled out as the litmus-habits of the genuinely rooted (29:45 — "prayer restrains from indecency and wrong"; 70:22-25 — the standing profile of the prayer-keepers in whose wealth is a known right).

**Ajr Kabīr: The Reward of the Rooted — and the Standing of Revelation Itself**

The verse ends at its destination — *ulāʾika sanuʾtīhim ajran kabīran* — "unto those We shall grant a great reward": *ajr kabīr* — the standing superlative of wages in the sūrah's own register (its stations: 4:54's "a great dominion"; 4:67; 4:74; 4:95; 4:114; 4:146 — "a great reward" for the believers-tradition; 9:22; 33:29; 48:10; 57:7; 64:15; 67:12) — the great-reward promised now, in the immediate wake of the indictment-file, to the exception-corps — the architecture of vv. 160–162 forming the chapter's standing pattern of balanced scales: prepared punishment for "the disbelievers among them" (161) — great reward for "the rooted among them, and the believers" (162): knowledge, in the Book's economy, judged by its *fruit-direction*: knowledge rooted toward acknowledgment of all revelation ends in reward; knowledge floated toward distortion (5:13, 5:41's standing tahrīf-file; 2:75's standing tamperers) ends in the prepared punishment. Al-Rāzī's standing gloss on the rootedness-name sums the verse's standing anthropology: the rāsikh is the one in whom knowledge has gone *down* — into depth where storms of novelty and contradiction cannot uproot — and the mark of his depth is his expansiveness: the deeper the root, the more of God's successive revelation-received — each new address finding soil rather than surface. The People-of-the-Book movement of the sūrah thereby delivers, before it closes, its final standing portrait: one community, two postures — indictment or reward — and the divider never the blood of the covenant but the bowing of the learned: *those firmly rooted in knowledge... believing* — a profile deliberately drawn so that any scholar of any scriptural tradition may measure himself against it — and the Book immediately lifts its own certificate into the proof of this self-same principle in the next verse: "verily We have revealed to thee as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him" (v. 163) — the Prophet's own revelation enrolled in the same standing chain the rāsikhūn believe — the unity of prophecy as the unity of reward.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:163

> **Verily We have revealed to thee, as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him; and We revealed to Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac and Jacob and the Tribes, and Jesus and Job and Jonah and Aaron and Solomon; and unto David We gave the Psalms —**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Innā Awḥaynā Ilayka Kamā Awḥaynā ilā Nūḥin: The Sunna of Revelation Itself**

The answer to the tablet-demanders of v. 153 now arrives in the form of a certificate-chain: *innā awḥaynā ilayka kamā awḥaynā ilā Nūḥin wa al-nabiyyīna min baʿdih* — "verily We have revealed to thee, as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him": *kamā* — "as" — the comparative particle doing the whole theological work: the revelation to Muḥammad is not a novelty requiring new categories of proof but an *instance* of the standing divine *sunna* of waḥy — the same sending, the same character, the same chain reaching back to Noah — the patriarch-figure deliberately placed as chain-head in the standing List-verses (its register: 2:136; 3:84; 6:83-89's standing extended roster; 19:49-58; 33:7) — the first messenger of the *sent-with-a-code* class in the standing taxonomy (6:84-89; 10:71-72's standing Noah-file; 23:23; 57:26 — "We sent Noah and Abraham and placed prophethood and the scripture among their descendants"). Al-Ṭabarī's and al-Zamakhsharī's standing gloss names the verse's precise polemical address: the demanders of v. 153 had asked for a *separate Book from heaven* as though the present revelation were unevidenced — the answer: the Book they demand *is this recitation itself*, and its method of arrival — waḥy upon a prophet — is precisely the standing method by which every scripture they hold came: no new mechanism is on trial here, only the same old fidelity to what arrives. And the community-reference is double: to the People of the Book, the verse says *your whole canon proves our canon by precedent*; to the believers, it anchors the Prophet's standing within the unbroken succession (42:13's standing roster of the same continuity).

**The Named Roll: From Abraham to Solomon — One Chain, Many Files**
