The verse then unrolls the standing register of names — and the commentators note the selection's arc: *wa ātaynā Ibrāhīma wa Ismāʿīla wa Isḥāqa wa Yaʿqūba wa al-asbāṭ* — "and We revealed to Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac and Jacob and the Tribes": the Abrahamic trunk-line — father, the two sons, the grandson Israel, and the twelve-tribal prophets of his seed (al-asbāṭ — the standing collective for the tribal chieftain-prophets of Jacob's house — 2:136; 2:140; 3:84; 7:160's standing tribal file) — then *wa ʿĪsā wa Ayyūba wa Yūnusa wa Hārūna wa Sulaymān* — "and Jesus and Job and Jonah and Aaron and Solomon": five names spanning five modes of prophecy — Jesus the annunciation-prophet of the Book's own dossier (vv. 156-159 above); Job the patience-prophet — the tradition's standing archive of affliction-endurance (21:83-84 — "and Job, when he cried to his Lord: verily harm has touched me — and Thou art the most merciful of the merciful — so We answered him and lifted what was upon him of harm"; 38:41-44's standing oath-file) — here named, the commentators note, at his *first explicit investiture in the register of prophethood* alongside Jonah (the standing comment-canon observing: the verse is the Book's first explicit numbering of Ayyūb and Yūnus among the prophets — later rosters at 6:83-86 enrolling them explicitly); Jonah — Yūnus — the storm-and-whale prophet, his standing register: 10:98 — "why was there not a town that believed, and its belief availed it — save the people of Jonah — when they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world and gave them enjoyment for a while"; 37:139-148; 68:48-50 — and the standing lesson-figure of the called-yet-fleeing-yet-answered; Aaron — Hārūn — the standing minister-prophet beside Moses (19:53 — "We gave him of Our mercy his brother Aaron, a prophet"; 20:29-32 — Moses' own supplication: "appoint for me a minister from my family — Aaron, my brother — strengthen my back by him, and share him in my affair"); Solomon — Sulaymān — the king-prophet (27:15-44's standing Sulaymān-file; 38:30-40).

**Wa Ātaynā Dāwūda Zabūrā: The Psalms as the Named Scripture**

The verse closes its roll with the one title-station among them: *wa ātaynā Dāwūda zabūrā* — "and unto David We gave the Psalms": *zabūr* — the standing name of David's book (its register: 17:55 — "and unto David We gave the Zabūr"; 21:105 — "We have written in the Zabūr after the Reminder that My righteous servants shall inherit the earth") — the commentators marking the definite-singular (al-Zabūr, tied to David) as the Psalter — the hymnic scripture of prayer and praise — to be distinguished from the plural-file usage (*zubur* — scriptures, documents generally — its standing stations: 3:184; 16:44 — the *bayyināt wa al-zubur* pairing; 26:196 — "verily it is in the scriptures of the ancients"; 54:52 — "everything they did is in the scriptures"). The singular singling-out of David within the roster carries its standing curiosity: among all the named prophets, David alone receives a *named book* in this verse — and the commentators draw the standing implication the verse doubtless intends for the Madīnan demanders: even the Books you know by name — Torah to Moses (implied in v. 164's standing distinction), Psalms to David here, Gospel to Jesus in the standing register (5:46; 57:27) — arrived precisely as this one arrives: *waḥy revealed to a man* — the exception you demand (a book dropping from the sky upon no messenger) is a mechanism God's own canon nowhere employs — even the *tablets of Moses*, the one nearly-physical exception your file prizes, came framed within prophethood-and-conversation (v. 164's standing sequel: kalām) rather than as substitute for it. The verse thereby converts a name-list into an argument: the long succession — Noah, the Abrahamic line, the tribal prophets, Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, Solomon, David — one sunna of revelation, one divine practice — and Muḥammad enrolled within it not at its edge but at its center of gravity: *as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him.*

**The Standing Posture Before the Roll: Belief in All, Preference in Rank**

The commentators close the verse's treatment with its standing balancing-note — the two cords by which Muslim prophetology holds: (1) assent: each name on the roll is binding on the believer's faith — 2:285 — "we make no distinction between any of His messengers" — no messenger refused; (2) honor-gradation: 2:253's standing register in place — "those are the messengers — We preferred some of them over others — among them one to whom God spoke — and He raised some of them in degrees" — the preference of station acknowledged without jealousy or refusal — v. 164 immediately exhibiting the principle with the very name the People of the Book hold dearest: Moses — to whom the Book gives, in the words of the next verse, the standing distinction the tradition ever after inscribed in his honorific: Kalīm Allāh.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:164

> **And messengers We have recounted to thee before, and messengers We have not recounted to thee; and unto Moses God spoke directly —**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Wa Rusulan Qad Qaṣaṣnāhum ʿAlayka min Qablu: The Recounted and the Unrecounted**

The roll of v. 163 opens here upon its own horizon — the Book admitting, with deliberate instruction, that it has not registered the census of prophecy: *wa rusulan qad qaṣaṣnāhum ʿalayka min qablu wa rusulan lam naqṣuṣhum ʿalayk* — "and messengers We have recounted to thee before, and messengers We have not recounted to thee": *qaṣaṣ* — from q-ṣ-ṣ — narration, the telling of accounts (its standing register: 11:100 — "those are the tidings of the towns We recount to thee — of them some are standing, some harvested"; 11:120 — "all that We recount to thee of the stories of the messengers is that wherewith We make firm thy heart"; 12:3; 40:78 — the standing twin-verse: "We sent messengers before thee — among them We recounted to thee, and among them We recounted not to thee") — the twice-stated division (here and at 40:78 — the only two places the Book confesses its own editorial selectivity concerning prophets) forming one of the standing credal-side doors of the religion: the Book names some twenty-six prophets in its pages, yet declares explicitly that the complete roster lies beyond its telling — the tradition's standing figures for it (the reports in the musnad-collections and tafsīr-files naming totals vast beyond enumeration — 124,000 in the standing report, three hundred and fifteen messengers among them, the register in Aḥmad's Musnad through Abū Dharr's question-hadith) — the theological point of the commentators being structural: prophethood is *universal* — God's guidance never geographically or ethnically parochial (10:47 — "for every community a messenger"; 16:36 — "We raised in every nation a messenger: worship God and shun the false gods"; 35:24 — "there is no community but a warner has passed among them"; 14:4 — "We sent no messenger save with the tongue of his people, that he might make things clear to them") — and the unrecounted category preserves the standing humility of revelation-history: what God's Book recounts is didactic selection, not exhaustive registry — the door left open, as the standing comment-canon notes, for sacred figures beyond the addressed horizon to be recognized as among the unrecounted warners of their peoples — without the Book's silence being read as nonexistence, and without speculation being enthroned as certain knowledge: "we know them not — Thou art the knower of the Unseen" — the standing formula by which the commentators pass the unrecounted to their Recorder.

**Wa Kallama Allāhu Mūsā Taklīman: Kalīm Allāh — The Spoken-To**

The verse then plants, at the end of its cadence, one of the Book's most resonant distinctions: *wa kallama Allāhu Mūsā taklīman* — "and unto Moses God spoke directly": *kallama* — Form II of k-l-m — to address in speech — with the cognate-accusative *taklīman* — "a speaking" — the standing intensifier that seals the reality of the event: not allusion, not metaphor, not impression — *speech*: God speaking, Moses hearing — the very phrase from which the tradition coined Moses' everlasting honorific: *Kalīm Allāh* — the One Spoken-To by God — the title entering devotional Islam through this verse and its standing companions (the commentators cross-reading with 2:253's standing gradation: "among them one to whom God spoke — and He raised some of them in degrees" — read in the standing gloss of the majority as pointing precisely to Moses among other distinctions; 7:143-144 — "and when Moses came to Our appointed time and his Lord spoke to him..." — "O Moses — I have chosen thee above men through My messages and through My speech — so take what I have given thee"; 19:52 — "We called him from the right side of the Mount and brought him near in communion"; 20:12-14 — the valley of Ṭuwā: "verily I am thy Lord — so remove thy sandals"; 26:52; 28:30's burning-bush file; 42:51's standing taxonomy: "it is not for any man that God should speak to him, save by revelation, or from behind a veil, or by sending a messenger to reveal by His leave what He wills" — Moses' direct-address placed within, and at the summit of, this threefold classification of divine speech-to-creatures).

**The Honor-Architecture of the Register: Titles in the Standing Tradition**

The commentators (al-Rāzī here with his standing register of distinctions) gather the verse's placement within the Book's honor-architecture — noting how the People-of-the-Book movement of the sūrah arranges its laurels: v. 125's standing Abraham-file just delivered ("and God took Abraham for an intimate friend — khalīlan" — Khalīl Allāh); v. 158-159's Jesus-file just past (raised unto God; Rūḥ Allāh as at v. 171 below — "a Spirit from Him" — and His Word committed to Mary); v. 163's David-station named with the Psalter; and here Moses' kalām-station — each prophet's own standing title drawn from what this very Book confers: the tradition's standing honorifics — Kalīm (Moses), Khalīl (Abraham), Rūḥ (Jesus) — all minted in Qur'ānic vocabulary — the subtle standing apologetic the commentators observe: the Book which the People of the Book are urged by later verses not to *exaggerate* (lā taghlū — v. 171) nor to *attenuate* (v. 150's distinction-making) is itself the deepest grantor of honor to their own prophets — honoring Moses above every Israelite honor-file by naming his distinction from the tongue of God Himself, and honoring Jesus by the loftiest vocabulary while refusing his deification — the balance of the standing balance encapsulated in the sūrah's own ratio: "those are the messengers — We preferred some over others" (2:253) — preference acknowledged, divinity refused, blanket-equality avoided, jealousy silenced.

**Standing Application: The Prophet's Own Reception of This Register**

And the register's standing pastoral note — gathered by the commentators — turns to the recipient addressed in the verse's first person: the Prophet himself, being told *his own* story lies inside this chain ("We have recounted to thee..."), is thereby instructed in the standing posture of all messengers before the unseen ledger of prophethood: there were — and are — worlds of God's envoys whose stories even *he* was not told; the creed stands upon *generic assent* to all (ʾāmantu bi-rusulihi — the standing creed-phrase), while knowledge-by-name remains a grace of selection — the same principle the verse lays upon the community: faith's completeness lives in the undivided assent (4:150-152's standing triptych), not in the completeness of the catalog. The verse thus performs, in one breath, registry and humility: the named roll of v. 163 proved the continuity of the cable; the unrecounted register of v. 164 proves the modesty of the cable's archive; and the kalām-distinction of Moses proves the cable's conductivity at its most direct — God, in prior covenant-history, having *spoken* — and if with Moses He spoke, and with David He psalmed, and with Jesus He spirited-and-worded, then the newest address of the same Speaker asks of its hearers no new category of belief — only the standing act: "we hear, and we obey" (2:285) — the standing response that the chain of messengers, recounted and unrecounted alike, was sent to secure.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:165

> **Messengers as bearers of glad tidings and as warners — that mankind might have no argument against God after the messengers. And God is ever Mighty, Wise.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Rusulan Mubashshirīna wa Mundhirīna: The Two Wings of Every Mission**

The register of revelation now names the *purpose* inscribed on every messenger's commission — a standing double-title that belongs to the Book's standing characterization of prophethood itself: *rusulan mubashshirīna wa mundhirīna* — "messengers as bearers of glad tidings and as warners": *mubashshir* — from b-sh-r — the glad-word already met in its ironically inverted station at v. 138 above ("give glad tidings to the hypocrites of a painful punishment") — here restored to its standing positive office: the announcement of God's mercy, of forgiveness, of the Gardens below which rivers flow; and *mundhir* — from n-dh-r — to warn: the announcement of accountability, of the Fire its fuel is men and stones — the two titles fused as one compound office (its standing register across the Book: 2:213 — "God sent the prophets as bearers of glad tidings and as warners"; 5:19 — "O People of the Book — Our Messenger has come to you after an interval of the messengers, lest you say: no bearer of glad tidings or warner has come to us"; 6:48 — "We send the messengers only as bearers of glad tidings and as warners — whoever believes and makes amends, no fear upon them nor do they grieve"; 11:2; 17:105 — "We have sent thee with the truth, as a bearer of glad tidings and a warner"; 18:56 — "We send the messengers only as bearers of glad tidings and as warners — and those who disbelieve contend with falsehood, that they may refute the truth thereby"; 25:56; 33:45 — "O Prophet — We have sent thee as a witness, and a bearer of glad tidings, and a warner"; 34:28 — "We have not sent thee save as a bearer of glad tidings and a warner to all mankind"; 48:8) — the commentators marking the pairing's standing balance: never gladness without warning (which would produce presumption) nor warning without gladness (which would produce despair) — the prophetic voice holding both because God's own revelation holds both (the standing Qur'ānic self-description: a Book of promise and threat fused — 39:16-20's standing parallel-verses of fire beneath and chambers above).

**Li-Allā Yakūna li-l-Nāsi ʿAlā Allāhi Ḥujjatun: The Removal of the Argument**

Then the verse delivers its standing jurisprudence of responsibility — one of the Book's most consequential purpose-clauses: *li-allā yakūna li-l-nāsi ʿalā Allāhi ḥujjatun baʿda al-rusul* — "that mankind might have no argument against God after the messengers": *ḥujjah* — from ḥ-j-j — to argue with proof, to overcome by evidence: an argument that counts, a legally binding demonstration (its standing register: 2:150 — "that people may have no argument against you"; 6:83 — "that is Our argument which We gave to Abraham against his people"; 6:149 — "unto God belongs the conclusive argument — al-ḥujjat al-bālighah"; 28:75; 40:4 — "none disputes concerning God's signs save those who disbelieve") — and the clause's declared purpose: the sending of messengers extinguishes the defense: after the glad tidings were announced and the warnings sounded, no defendant can stand at the Judgment and plead "I was never told": the standing anticipation-file of the Book making the clause's target everywhere explicit — 20:134 — "and had We destroyed them with a punishment before him, they would have said: our Lord — why didst Thou not send us a messenger, that we might have followed Thy signs before we were humbled and disgraced?"; 5:19 — "lest you say: no bearer of glad tidings or warner has come to us"; 28:47 — the standing companion (the same construction: "lest they say, when a calamity befalls them for what their own hands sent before: our Lord — why didst Thou not send us a messenger"); 16:35 — the standing shirkers' own spoiled argument ("had God willed we would not have worshipped beside Him aught") — answered in the register of 14:10-11; 67:8-9 — the people of the Fire confessing "if we had listened or had reason, we would not have been among the fellows of the Blaze" — every future objection preempted in advance by the very office of the messenger: *baʿda al-rusul* — after the messengers — the ḥujjah extinguished at the level of claim. And the commentators (al-Ṭabarī's chains; al-Rāzī's scholastic register; Ibn Taymiyyah's standing formulation in the fatawa-file) draw the juridical consequence standing across Muslim theology: no one is seized for punishment upon a message that never reached him — the standing rule that God's justice binds the accounting to the arrival of the warner ("We never punish until We send a messenger" — 17:15; "nor were We the punishers until We had raised up a messenger" — its own standing companion-clause at 28:59; 26:208-209 — "We destroyed no town but it had its warners — a reminder") — the principle known in the standing creed-literature as the doctrine that responsibility requires the ḥujjah's establishment — and its widest standing application: the inter-messenger intervals, the unreached peoples, the modern mind far from the signal — all covered by the principle that *ḥujjah* requires reliable delivery — the standing mercy-architecture inside the standing justice-architecture.

**Wa Kāna Allāhu ʿAzīzan Ḥakīman: Might and Wisdom Sealing the Office**

The verse seals with the standing Name-pair already met at v. 158 — and the commentators mark the pair's deliberate recurrence here: *wa kāna Allāhu ʿazīzan ḥakīman* — "and God is ever Mighty, Wise": *ʿazīz* — the Mighty — sealing the *authority* of the sending: the messengers arrive with a writ that heaven enforces — no community that outflanks a messenger outflanks the Sender (the standing register of the Name at passages of divine action: 2:209; 3:4; 5:95; 8:49; 9:40; 22:40; and the several standing stations) — every plot against the envoys scattered by the attribute (the crucifixion-boast of v. 157 scattering before it two verses above); and *ḥakīm* — the Wise — sealing the *design* of the sending: the staggered succession from Noah to Muḥammad, the matched tongues of 14:4, the gladness-and-warning dosage, the very selectivity of the recounted and unrecounted (v. 164) — all Wisdom’s arrangements: nothing of prophecy’s history is accidental, unmeasured, or makeshift. With v. 166 next — "but God Himself bears witness to what He sent down to thee — sending it with His knowledge — and the angels bear witness — and God suffices as a Witness" — the chapter’s certificate-architecture completes: the chain delivered (163), its horizon confessed (164), its purpose defined (165), and its witness posted (166) — the People of the Book addressed with the total standing evidence, so that the clause of v. 165 stands sealed against the very community to whom the sūrah’s final movement speaks: after *these* messengers, in *this* register, with *this* witness — "mankind has no argument against God": the Book’s own legal metaphor closing not in threat but in standing due process: everything was told, everything was warned, everything was witnessed — and upon that completed record the Judgment will rest.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:166

> **But God Himself bears witness to what He has sent down to thee — He sent it down with His knowledge — and the angels bear witness. And God suffices as a Witness.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Lākini Allāhu Yashhadu bi-Mā Anzala Ilayka: The Witness Above Every Demand**

The chapter of certificates reaches its crown: the demanders of v. 153 had asked for a book descending from heaven with visible spectacle — and the Book answers not with spectacle but with *testimony*: *lākini Allāhu yashhadu bi-mā anzala ilayk* — "but God Himself bears witness to what He has sent down to thee": *yashhadu* — from sh-h-d — witnessing, attestation at first hand: the courtroom-word the sūrah has made its own (4:33 — "God is ever Witness over all things"; 4:79 — "God suffices as a Witness"; 4:135's standing witnesses-for-God; 4:159's Jesus-as-witness) — and the Witness here is God Himself: the highest attestation impossible to appeal above — every demand for *further* evidence thereby disclosed not as evidentiary rigor but as refusal (its standing counter-file already installed at 6:111 — "even if We sent down the angels to them, and the dead spoke to them, and We gathered all things before them — they would not believe — unless God wills") — the Book's standing doctrine that evidence complete is evidence refused only by hearts.

**Anzalahu bi-ʿIlmih: Sent Down *With His Knowledge* — The Qualification of the Transmission**

The witness is immediately glossed with a specification the commentators measure with care: *anzalahu bi-ʿilmih* — "He sent it down with His knowledge": the preposition *bi-* carrying its standing double-facing (the standing readings in the comment-canon): (1) *with* His knowledge — the whole revelation wrapped in divine knowing: nothing in it escapes or exceeds the Sender's awareness — its content coextensive with omniscience, no clause accidental, no word unweighed; and (2) by/through His knowledge as standing guarantee: the Book's standing declarations that revelation proceeds from the knowing-source — 12:102's standing tail-note ("that is of the tidings of the Unseen We reveal to thee"); its register: 18:109's exhaustless sea-image ("if the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted before the words of my Lord were exhausted"); 31:27's standing all-the-trees-as-pens file; and the standing creed-principle: God's Speech is His standing attribute — the Qur'ān not created information about Him but His own kalām proceeding from His ʿilm — the verse thereby sealing the revelational chain of vv. 163–165 (waḥy from Noah to Muḥammad, an argument-voiding office) with its standing metaphysical ground: what moves down the chain is Knowledge itself made recitation.

**Wa al-Malāʾikatu Yashhadūn: The Angels in the Witness-Stand**

The attestation spreads to its second register: *wa al-malāʾikatu yashhadūn* — "and the angels bear witness": the standing angelic corroboration of revelation's authenticity (its sister-station at 3:18 — "God bears witness that there is no god but He — and the angels, and those possessed of knowledge — upholding justice") — the commentators glossing the angels' standing stake in the file: Gabriel the conveyor (2:97 — "whoever is an enemy to Gabriel — for he it is who brought it down upon thy heart by God's leave"; 26:193-194 — "the Trustworthy Spirit brought it down upon thy heart"); the the standing general angelic witnessing of the descent — the Qur'ān itself descending amid their ranks (97:4 — "the angels and the Spirit descend therein by their Lord's leave, with every command") and being recited among them in the heavens (the standing report-literature of the celestial mosque — al-Bayt al-Maʿmūr of the night-journey report in Bukhārī's standing register 3207 — where the heavenly recitation-assembly meets the earthly); their testimony thereby the testimony of the entire transmission-personnel: the divine Author witnesses; the courier-host witnesses; and between them the demand for a *spectacle* is answered by the standing tribunal of the actual delivery.

**Wa Kafā Bi-llāhi Shahīdan: The Sufficiency-Formula at Its Highest Post**

Then the formula the sūrah has already planted at v. 79 and v. 132, now in its witness-station: *wa kafā bi-llāhi shahīdan* — "and God suffices as a Witness": the standing sufficiency-architecture — *kafā bi-llāhi...* — whose sūrah-register runs: 4:45 (suffices as Ally and Helper), 4:79 — "trust in God; God suffices as a Guardian"; 4:81 (Guardian); 4:132 (Guardian); and its Book-wide standing stations: 3:173 — the ḥasbunā-cry; 13:43 — "say: God suffices as a Witness between me and you" (the standing parallel-answer to the very context of ours: the Prophet instructed to answer the sign-demanders with this sufficiency-formula); 29:52 — "say: God suffices as a Witness between me and you — He knows whatever is in the heavens and the earth"; 46:8 — "say: God suffices as a Witness between me and you"; 48:28 — "God suffices as a Witness" sealing the Messenger's own mission-file; and 10:29 — "God suffices as a Witness between us and you." The commentators mark the fitting closure: the verse answers the v. 153-demand with the standing tribunal already sitting — God witness, angels co-signing, and the sufficiency-ruling delivered: *no further discovery procedure will be ordered* — the evidence having been, from the beginning, complete: the Prophet need not subpoena heaven when heaven has already filed its testimony. And the verse's own standing echo — 3:18's triple-witness (God, angels, possessors of knowledge attesting the One God) — links this testimony to the testimony of tawḥīd itself: the Book and the Oneness it teaches arriving under the same signatures — 4:166 the certificate of the text, 3:18 the certificate of the doctrine — both sealed: kafā bi-llāh.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:167

> **Verily those who disbelieve and bar from the way of God have gone far astray.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Inna Alladhīna Kafarū wa Ṣaddū ʿan Sabīli Allāh: The Double Charge of the Gatekeepers**

The verdict-resume of the chapter now opens with the standing double charge: *inna alladhīna kafarū wa ṣaddū ʿan sabīli Allāh* — "verily those who disbelieve and bar from the way of God": two verbs in deliberate composition — *kafarū* (they disbelieved: the inward state) and *ṣaddū* (they barred: the outward aggressive act upon others) — the commentators (al-Ṭabarī's standing gloss) marking the full landscape of *ṣadd*: barring ranging across (1) intellectual obstruction — objections manufactured, doubts seeded, the rising generation tutored against the message; (2) social obstruction — the pressure of clan, commerce, and respectability arrayed to make confession costly; (3) physical obstruction — roads watched, sanctuaries policed (8:34-35's standing Meccan file: "what ails them that God should not punish them, while they bar from the Sacred Mosque — though they are not its guardians; its guardians are but the God-fearing — but most of them know not — and their prayer at the House is naught but whistling and clapping"; "they sell the signs of God for a small price and bar from His way"; 5:2's standing counter-command; 22:25 — the barring from the Sacred Mosque declared for the standing pagan file); and (4) self-barring — some readings registering the ṣadd as intransitive-turning: their own feet held back from the road — the standing basic register at 7:45 ("who bar from God's way and seek to make it crooked, and in the Hereafter they are disbelievers"); 11:19; 14:3 — "those who prefer the life of this world to the Hereafter, and bar from God's way, seeking to make it crooked — those are in far astray"; 43:37 — "verily they bar them from the way — while they suppose they are guided"; 47:1 — "those who disbelieve and bar from God's way — He shall render their works vain". The sūrah's own standing indictment of v. 160 ("and for their turning many from the way of God") echoes here generalized: the particular charges (broken covenant, calumny, ribā) now gathered into the master-count — disbelief *plus obstruction*: the private refusal institutionalized as public engineering against the Road.

**Qad Ḍallū Ḍalālan Baʿīdan: The Far Error Seventh Sounded**

The verdict belongs to the sūrah's own standing register — *qad ḍallū ḍalālan baʿīdan* — "have gone far astray": the seventh tolling of the ḍalāl-baʿīd phrase within this one sūrah (its stations: 4:60 — Satan's desire "to lead them far astray"; 4:116 — "whoever associates partners with God has gone far astray"; 4:136 — "whosoever disbelieves in God and His angels and His books and His messengers and the Last Day has gone far astray"; plus its standing pavers at 14:18; 22:12; 34:8; 42:18 — the phrase the Book reserves for total removal from the Road) — and the commentators mark the chapter's own architectural use of it: each tolling names another point of the departure-file — following the arbiter-other-than-God (60), the association-partnership (116), the article-breaking creed (136), and here the obstruction-enterprise (167) — all compass-points of one radius: distance from the Sabīl. *Baʿīd* itself — far — the word of exile-in-extent: error measured not in degrees but in *distance-strata* — and the standing Book-epistemology of roads completes the image: there is *a* way (1:6 — "guide us upon the straight path"; 4:68's standing claimed-performance file — "We would have guided them to a straight path"; 6:153 — "this is My path, straight — so follow it; and follow not the byways") — against which all departures register as *far*: no middle-distance between Road and wild.

**The Standing Pairing With v. 137: From Oscillation to Institution**

The commentators observe the verse's structural rhyming within the chapter: v. 137's waverers (believe-disbelieve-believe-disbelieve) were told "God was not one to forgive them nor to guide them unto a way" — the *individual* file of vacillation; vv. 167–169 now register the *institutional* file: disbelief hardened into the barring-profession — and the coming two verses will deliver its doubled penalty in the same verbal architecture the same verbal architecture (168: "God is not one to forgive them nor to guide them to a path —" 169: "save the path of Hell, abiding therein forever") — the standing comparison the commentators draw: the waverer loses guidance; the bar-keeper loses everything — forgiveness revoked, all guidance revoked save one, the way denied except *the path of Hell* — a sentence structure whose exception-clause is itself the shocking inversion the Book reserves for its darkest verdicts: the only road still open to the obstructor being the road he never wished to travel — *illā ṭarīqa jahannam* (169) — the sūrah of ways (its opening taqwā-way of 4:1; its justice-way of 4:135; its repentance-way of 4:146; its belief-way of 4:152) here mapping the one wayfare that is the sum of all refusal: far astray now, and one-way later. And the standing mercy-file is duly registered by the commentators (al-Rāzī and al-Zamakhsharī's standing note at these non-forgiveness clauses extending through the chapter): every "God will not forgive" of the Book stands upon *persistence* — the door of repentance rehanging every such verse (4:146's own standing exception-architecture; 39:53's standing universal-promise) — so that even the barring-profession, while its perpetrator breathes, retains its standing exit: non-forgiveness as prognosis upon a state, never as a sealed personal destiny — the far error remaining far only for those who keep walking.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:168

> **Verily those who disbelieve and do wrong — God was not one to forgive them, nor to guide them unto a path,**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Inna Alladhīna Kafarū wa Ẓalamū: Disbelief and Wrongdoing Composed**

The verdict-file continues with a second doubled charge — the composition shifting from v. 167's *disbelief + barring* to *disbelief + ẓulm*: *inna alladhīna kafarū wa ẓalamū* — "verily those who disbelieve and do wrong": *ẓalamū* — from ẓ-l-m — wrongdoing, injustice: the standing comprehensive of every thing put out of its place (its standing Book-defining stations: 31:13 — Luqmān's master-axiom — "verily associating partners with God is a tremendous wrong — la-ẓulmun ʿaẓīm"; 2:51; 2:59; 2:229's limits-file; 4:64 above in this sūrah — "they wronged their souls"; 4:110 — "whoever does evil or wrongs his own soul, then seeks God's pardon, shall find God Forgiving, Merciful"; 3:135 — "those who — when they commit an indecency or wrong their souls — remember God and seek forgiveness for their sins" — the double-composition standing across the Book: kufr as the root-wrong, the displacement of God Himself from His centrality; and every derivative wrong as the echoed displacement in creation) — the commentators noting why the sūrah chooses *ẓulm* here at the summit of its indictment: the entire chapter has been one sustained inventory of ẓulm and its remedies — the wronged orphan (4:2-10), the wronged wife (4:19-22; 4:127-130), the wronged slave (4:36), the wronged adversary-before-testimony (4:135), the wronged covenant (4:154-155), the wronged prophets (4:155), the wronged Mary (4:156), the wronged Jesus (4:157): the sūrah of wrong-and-justice thus sealing its indictment with the genus-word that comprehends them all.

**Lam Yakuni Allāhu Li-Yaghfira Lahum: The Non-Forgiveness of a State**

Then the rarest register of the Book again — already met at v. 137 in the waverers' file — *lam yakuni Allāhu li-yaghfira lahum* — "God was not one to forgive them": the durative-negative construction (*lam yakun* + imperfect) declaring a settled divine disposition *against* — not a snapshot verdict but the standing posture of unalloyed Justice toward unrepented confirmed disbelief-with-wrongdoing. The commentators gather the verse into the standing register of the Book's "no forgiveness" files and map the register's boundaries with standing care: (1) 4:48 and 4:116 — "verily God forgives not that partners be associated with Him — but He forgives what is less than that, for whom He wills" — the shirk-exception absolute upon dying-unrepentant; (2) 4:137 above — the progressive disbelievers-unto-death; (3) 9:79-80 — the rider to the mocking-file — "if Thou forgivest them seventy times, God will not forgive them — that because they disbelieved in God and His Messenger"; 63:5-6's twin; (4) 47:34 — "verily those who disbelieve and bar from God's way, then die disbelievers — God will not forgive them" — the standing twin of our verse's own clause with its death-qualifier explicit; and the standing majority-rule of al-Rāzī and al-Zamakhsharī across all five: **every** non-forgiveness verdict of the Book adjudicates a *state* — disbelief-and-wrongdoing confirmed, persisted in, sealed in death — never an announcement that the repentance-door is barred from a living person (4:146's own exception-architecture standing within this very chapter: "save those who repent and make amends" — even of the lowest-depth hypocrites; 3:89's standing counterpart to 3:90's non-acceptance: "save those who repent thereafter and make amends — for God is Forgiving, Merciful"; and 39:53's standing universal-promissory: "say: O My servants who have transgressed against their souls — despair not of God's mercy — verily God forgives all sins — verily He is the Forgiving, the Merciful") — the non-forgiveness of vv. 137, 168, and their Book-companions thus standing as the Book's pronouncement upon the *condition*, while the repentance-door stands as its standing counter-pronouncement upon every *person* still alive to use it.

**Wa Lā Li-Yahdiyahum Ṭarīqan: All Ways Withdrawn**

The penalty compounds: *wa lā li-yahdiyahum ṭarīqan* — "nor to guide them unto a path": the standing guidance-withdrawal completing the non-forgiveness: forgiveness is heavenward amnesty; guidance is earthward direction — both revoked for the state named: the disbelieving wrongdoer sealed in his dispensation wanders without a road *in either world*: no road in this life to felicity (the withdrawing of insight, the sealing-train of 4:155 above — "God has set a seal upon them for their disbelief") and no road in the next save one — which the next verse delivers as the Book's most chilling version of "guidance": *illā ṭarīqa jahannam* — 4:169 — the path to Hell — the only route still signposted for the sealed — the ḥujjah-removal of v. 165 ("that mankind might have no argument against God after the messengers") answering here at its severest pole: to those who had full direction-provision and disbelieved-and-wronged against it, direction stands permanently withheld; and the standing pastoral reading — the commentators indispensable balance — holds the two files together: for the persisting state: no forgiveness, no way; for the returning person: Forgiving, Merciful (4:110 once more — "whoever does evil or wrongs his own soul, then seeks God's pardon, shall find God Forgiving, Merciful") — the sūrah of justice keeping both ledgers open so that none presumes, and none despairs.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:169

> **Save the path of Hell — abiding therein forever; and that is ever easy for God.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Illā Ṭarīqa Jahannam: The Exception That Is the Sentence — The Only Road Left**

The verse completes v. 168 with the Book's most terrible exception-construction: *illā ṭarīqa jahannama khālidīna fīhā abadan* — "save the path of Hell — abiding therein forever": the grammatical exceptive (*illā* — "save/except") performing here its darkest possible office: after the twin withdrawal of v. 168 (no forgiveness, no guidance *unto a path*), the exception should — by every habit of the exceptive form — soften the sentence; instead it *specifies the one withholding still permitted to reach them*: one way only — and it is the way to the Fire. The commentators (al-Ṭabarī's gloss standing first) mark the rhetorical thunder of the construction: God does not withhold *all* paths from them — He withholds all paths but one, and that one He opens — direction itself becoming penalty: guidance now reduced to the road down (its standing structural companions in the Book's register of total-negation exception-clauses: 4:48's pairing above; 4:137's earlier arrangement; and the parallel anatomy at 47:34-35 — "those who disbelieve and bar from God's way, then die as disbelievers — God will not forgive them. So do not slacken and call for peace, while you are the uppermost — and God is with you and will not deprive you of your deeds" — the standing whole-context: the obstructor's way closed to all destinations but the refusal-earned terminus).

**Khālidīna Fīhā Abadan: Permanence Doubled**

The abode-clause doubles perpetuity upon perpetuity: *khālidīna fīhā abadan* — "abiding therein forever": *khālidīna* — from kh-l-d — to abide without departure — the standing adjective of no-exit already drilled through the sūrah's standing register (4:13's Garden-abiding; 4:14's Fire-abiding; 4:57; 4:93; 4:121-122's doubled pair) — followed by *abadan* — everlastingly, without terminus — the standing adverbial doubling the participle (its standing stations: 4:57; 4:122 — "abiding therein forever"; its register across the Book: 2:167; 3:116; 5:37 — "they will wish to exit the Fire — and they will not exit it — and theirs is a lasting punishment"; 9:100's opposite-register; 18:108; 33:65; 43:28; 50:34 — "enter it in peace — that is the Day of abiding"; 64:9; 72:23; 98:6; 98:8) — the commentators (al-Rāzī's standing scholastic note upon every abad-verse) marking that the Book's usages of doubled permanence deliberately foreclose the speculation of termination: not age upon age, but the standing absolute: no exit-clause, no sunrise — and beside it the standing counter-quadrant held through this very chapter: 4:57; 4:122's *khālidīna fīhā abadan* for the believing worker — permanence promised with the identical grammar to the opposite direction — the symmetrical architecture insisting that between the two permanences stands only the road taken here.

**Wa Kāna Dhālika ʿAlā Allāhi Yasīran: The Ease Declared**

The verse closes with the standing ease-formula — and the commentators mark its placement as its meaning: *wa kāna dhālika ʿalā Allāhi yasīran* — "and that is ever easy for God": *yasīr* — from y-s-r — ease, facility: not "light" as trivial, but: *costless to the Doer* — the standing Book-register of the formula at sites of overwhelming divine acts (14:20 — "nor was that difficult for God" — of the removal-and-replacement of peoples; 29:19 — "have they not seen how God originates creation, then repeats it — verily that is easy for God"; 30:27 — "He it is who originates creation, then repeats it — and it is easier yet for Him"; 35:41; 50:44 — "the day the earth splits asunder about them — [they come] hastening — that assembling is easy for Us"; 57:22); — the commentators reading its audience-prepared gravity here in two standing modes: (1) against presumption: let none suppose the sentence upon the obstructor-class arduous to execute, against old ties, tribal immunities, public standing — *easy* — requiring of God no effort, no negotiation, no hesitation: the standing hadith-register of the divine oath at service ("I have made injustice unlawful for Myself..." — Muslim 2577) standing beside this ease: what He reserves to Himself by covenant, He executes by facility; and (2) against presumption's mirror — despair in the opposite audience: for the mercy-files of the Book bear the same ease-vocabulary in their direction (the standing complement at 35:17 — "that is not difficult for God"; 11:4; "the matter of the Hour is but as the twinkling of an eye, or nearer") — the ease-attribute resting beside every announced divine act, so that the reader understands: judgment's execution and mercy's bestowal share the same standing facility — neither is deferred for effort. The verse takes its standing place within the People-of-the-Book movement's two-way register: vv. 162-166 having just delivered the promise-lines (great reward; witness and sufficiency-file), vv. 167-169 now deliver the mirror-file — disbelief-plus-obstruction, disbelief-plus-wrongdoing — no forgiveness, no guidance, no way but one, forever, at no cost to the Judge — the architectural pattern the whole sūrah has kept from its first verses: doors in pairs: the door of the orphan carefully apportioned and the fire for the devourer (4:10); the Garden for the just and the flame for the limit-transgressor (4:13-14); the repentance-door ever open on earth, and the no-exit door beyond it (4:17-18) — 4:169 the bookend of this standing diptych, written not to close hope but to make its remaining corridor unmistakable: every gate beside the one is still open — *now* — and "that is easy for God."

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:170

> **O mankind! The Messenger has come to you with the truth from your Lord; so believe — it is better for you. And if you disbelieve — then unto God belongs whatsoever is in the heavens and the earth; and God is ever Knowing, Wise.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Yā Ayyuhā al-Nāsu Qad Jāʾakumu al-Rasūlu: The Universal Address After the Particular Indictments**

The chapter's final movement widens its address to the widest possible circle: *yā ayyuhā al-nāsu qad jāʾakumu al-rasūlu bi-al-ḥaqqi min rabbikum* — "O mankind! The Messenger has come to you with the truth from your Lord": *yā ayyuhā al-nās* — the standing universal vocative of the Book (its stations across the chapter's own architecture: 4:1 — "O mankind — fear your Lord..."; 4:174 below repeating; the standing register across the Book: 2:21; 2:168; 10:57; 22:1; 22:5; 22:49; 22:73; 31:33; 35:3; 35:5; 35:15; 49:13) — the commentators marking the widening sequence of the chapter's addresses: the believers (4:19; 4:29; 4:43; 4:59; 4:71; 4:135-136; 4:144), the People of the Book (153-171), and now *mankind* — the ceiling of address — every tribunal of the chapter (orphan-file, family-file, justice-file, hypocrisy-file, covenant-file, Jesus-file) folded into a single announcement delivered to *all*: the Messenger's arrival — *qad jāʾakum* — the perfect tense declaring accomplished advent — "has come": the sending not awaited but completed; and the payload defined: *bi-al-ḥaqqi min rabbikum* — "with the truth from your Lord": al-ḥaqq — the standing name of the whole cargo: the revelation itself and the whole fabric of truth it disciplines (its standing register: 2:119; 2:147; 2:176; 5:48; 5:83; 10:47's 17:105 — "We sent thee with the truth"; 13:1; 34:6; 39:2; 39:41; 42:17 — the several standing stations of the rasūl-bil-ḥaqq complex) — and the possessive *rabbikum* — "your Lord" — anchoring the address in the first covenant: the One addressing is not a foreign God but *their* Lord — the standing argument the chapter opened with at 4:1 (rabbukum alladhī khalaqakum) closed with it here: the Lord who created now addresses through His Messenger.

**Fa-Āminū Khayran Lakum: Belief as Self-Interest, Not as Charity to Heaven**

Then the imperative with its standing self-referential motivation: *fa-āminū khayran lakum* — "so believe — it is better for you": *khayran lakum* — from 2:110's standing its standing formula-stations: 2:54 — "turn to your Maker... that is better for you"; 2:110 — "whatever good you send before you for your souls, you shall find it with God"; 5:35; 5:45-46's better-files; 66:5; 73:20) — the commentators (al-Ṭabarī's standing gloss; al-Rāzī's scholastic note expanding) drawing the verse's standing theological reordering of motivation: belief is legislated not as tribute offered upward but as benefit accruing downward — *better for you*: faith assigned to the believer's own ledger of interests — the obedience of the creature an act of self-investment rather than a favor to the Creator — a principle the chapter has already embedded in its ownership-files (4:126; 4:131): everything is His already, so nothing one "gives" God enriches Him; every virtue is rescue of one's own soul (2:286's standing prayer closing the standing pure-theology: "our Lord — take us not to task if we forget or err"; and the standing qudsī-file at Muslim 2577 — "O My servants — you will not attain to harming Me... nor to benefiting Me... it is but your actions that I register for you — then I requite you — whoever finds good, let him praise God — and whoever finds other, let him blame none but himself").

**Wa In Takfurū: The Third Ownership-Declaration — Indifference in Majesty**

Then the disbelief-clause — in the chapter's own familiar indifference-construction: *wa in takfurū fa-inna li-llāhi mā fī al-samāwāti wa mā fī al-arḍ* — "and if you disbelieve — then unto God belongs whatsoever is in the heavens and the earth": the ownership-cadence now tolling its fourth time in the chapter's closing register (its stations herein: 4:126; 4:131; 4:132; and again 4:170-171 — the final verse of the Jesus-file ending with the same cadence) — and the commentators marking the device at its standing summation: your disbelief subtracts nothing from the Estate; your refusal of a deed of property does not unwrite the deed — the standing theological point pressed by al-Rāzī at these clauses: the verse answers the human instinct to imagine that refusal injures the Refused — the Book counter-announcing the standing non-dependence of the Refused Upon the acceptance of tenants: the heavens and earth and all they hold remain His, pledged to His account, traveling to His appointment — with or without the confessor's consent. Its standing Book-kin: 4:131 above; 14:2 — "God — unto Him belongs whatsoever is in the heavens and the earth"; 16:52; 31:26; 34:24; 39:38; 53:31 — the standing estate-roll; and the standing consolation-parallel for the Prophet of "We know indeed that what they say grieves thee..." — the disbelief of the addressed never imperiling the estate nor the address.

**Wa Kāna Allāhu ʿAlīman Ḥakīman: The Knower-and-Wise Seal**

The verse seals with the standing Name-pair of calm omniscience: *wa kāna Allāhu ʿalīman ḥakīman* — "and God is ever Knowing, Wise": *ʿalīm* — the Knower — matching the verse's standing concern: the arrival of the truth *known* perfectly by its Sender, the hidden reception of that truth by every individual hearer *known* without remainder (the standing sūrah-file of this Name-pair — 4:11; 4:12; 4:17; 4:24; 4:26; 4:92; 4:104; 4:111; the recurring ʿalīm-ḥakīm stations); and *ḥakīm* — the Wise — matching the standing design: truth sent as guidance, belief recommended as benefit, disbelief answered with the estate-declaration — every motion of the dance within Wisdom's choreography. The commentators (Ibn Kathīr's standing filing) read vv. 170–171 together as the chapter's own summary-pair: v. 170 to all mankind — "believe; it is better for you"; v. 171 to the People of the Book — "exaggerate not; the Messiah is God's servant and word and spirit; believe; refrain — it is better for you" — the same *khayran lakum* in both — the Book's standing motive-appeal sounded at both universal and particular registers — and then 4:171's own close cadences the chapter's last legal-echo: "unto Him belongs whatsoever is in the heavens and the earth — and God suffices as a Guardian" — the wakīl-sufficiency of 4:132 returning at the chapter's far shore: the estate, the guidance, the guardianship — all His — "and mankind" addressed at last to choose: to believe (better for them) or to refuse (weightless upon Him) — the sūrah of the Watcher keeping, to its final movement, the standing freedom of the human deed and the standing completeness of the divine account.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:171

> **O People of the Book! Commit not excess in your religion, and say not of God aught save the truth. Verily the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, is but the messenger of God, and His Word which He committed to Mary, and a Spirit from Him. So believe in God and His messengers, and say not "Three." Refrain — it is better for you. God is but One God — glory be to Him, above having a child! Unto Him belongs whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is on the earth, and God suffices as a Guardian.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Lā Taghlū fī Dīnikum: Excess Forbidden at the Doctrinal Summit**

The chapter's final direct address to the People of the Book opens with the prohibition that defines the Christian-side error as the Book measures it — the standing counter-charge to the Jewish-side attenuation files above (vv. 150-155: refusal, barring, calumny): *yā ahla al-kitābi lā taghlū fī dīnikum* — "O People of the Book! Commit not excess in your religion": *gh-l-w* — to overshoot, to exaggerate past measure: the commentators (al-Rāzī's standing formulation) drawing the chapter's standing two-error map: the error of the Jews in the Book's file was *deficiency* — refusing prophets sent to them (vv. 155-156; 2:91's standing register); the error of the Christians was *excess* — ascribing to their prophet a station beyond humanity: the two communities erring in opposite directions about the same axis — the status of God's envoys — and the verse opening with the standing prohibition of *ghuluww* itself: excess not as a variant vigor of devotion but as a named sin (its standing hadith-counterpart in the Prophet’s file — his celebrated warning (al-Nasāʾī 3057; Ibn Mājah 3029; the Musnad): “beware of exaggeration in religion — for those before you perished by exaggeration in religion” — with his standing counterbalance: the best of affairs is the middle course); and *wa lā taqūlū ʿalā Allāhi illā al-ḥaqq* — "and say not of God aught save the truth": speech about God confined to the truthful, naming the doctrinal offense as precisely a *qawl ʿalā Allāh* — an assertion upon God (its standing register: 3:94; 4:50 above; 6:93; 7:37; 11:18 — "who does greater wrong than he who fabricates a lie against God"; 16:116; 18:15; 72:4-5) — exaggeration classified not as private enthusiasm but as testimony — testimony unlicensed by the witness of revelation.

**Innamā al-Masīḥu...: The Fourfold Identification of Jesus — Station, Word, Spirit, and Their Measures**

Then the verse's doctrinal core — a fourfold naming of Jesus with the most majestic honorific-vocabulary in the Book, fenced at each end: *innamā al-Masīḥu ʿĪsā ibnu Maryama rasūlu Allāhi wa kalimatuhu alqāhā ilā Maryama wa rūḥun minhu* — "verily the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, is but the messenger of God, and His Word which He committed to Mary, and a Spirit from Him": (1) *innamā* — "only/but" — the restrictive particle opening the definition — the ceiling drawn first: the Messiah is *nothing beyond* what follows; (2) *rasūlu Allāh* — the messenger of God — his standing station: among the envoys of God's choice (v. 163's roll; its standing theological station in the Book: human, commissioned, meal-eating — 5:75 — "the Messiah son of Mary is but a messenger — messengers passed away before him — and his mother was a woman of truth — they both used to eat food"); (3) *kalimatuhu alqāhā ilā Maryam* — "His Word which He committed/cast to Mary": the standing identification of Jesus as God's Word (its Book-register: 3:45 — "the angels said: O Mary — God gives thee glad tidings of a Word from Him — his name is the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary"; 19:34 — "such is Jesus son of Mary — a statement of the truth, concerning which they doubt"); and the commentators' standing double-reading of the *kalimah*: (a) the annunciation-word — the glad tiding delivered to Mary ("a Word from Him" as the message announcing the child — al-Ṭabarī's register); and (b) the creative command itself — the *kun* — "Be!" — by which the fatherless child was formed in the womb (3:59's standing parallel: "verily the likeness of Jesus with God is as the likeness of Adam — He created him from dust — then said to him: Be — and he was") — al-Rāzī gathering both and marking the tradition's ruling insight: though *all* creation issues through God's command, Jesus alone is *named* His Word — the singling-out being honor, not essence-participation: the title distinguishing his *mode of arrival* (word alone, no father) without conferring the nature of the Speaker; (4) *wa rūḥun minhu* — "and a Spirit from Him": the standing rūḥ-identification (its register: 2:87 — "We gave Jesus son of Mary the clear proofs and strengthened him with the Holy Spirit"; 2:253; 5:110; 66:12 — "We breathed into her of Our Spirit") — with the commentators' standing caution-register: the min of *minhu* read as the min of emanation-at-command ("of His creating," as every created spirit is "from Him" — its standing companion at 15:29 — "when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My Spirit"), some earlier readings glossing rūḥ here as mercy (raḥmah) or purity — al-Rāzī gathering the tradition's theological settlement: "from Him" marks origin and honor, never composition — the same diction the Book uses of houses "of God" and camels "of God" (91:13 — naqata Allāh — "the she-camel of God" — belonging, not consubstantiality). The tradition thus enrolled Jesus' honorifics from this verse — Rūḥ Allāh, Kalimat Allāh — the commentators marking what the chapter itself performs: **the Book that refuses deification is itself the deepest honorer of Jesus** — it is the Book that calls him Messiah, Word, Spirit, raised-to-God (v. 158), miracle-working (5:110), eminent in both worlds (3:45) — while drawing the one fence the Christian file crossed: servanthood (v. 172 below sealing: "the Messiah would never disdain to be a servant of God").

**Wa Lā Taqūlū Thalāthatun: Say Not "Three" — the Standing Command of Refrain**

Then the prohibition upon the doctrinal word itself: *wa lā taqūlū thalāthatun — intahū khayran lakum* — "and say not 'Three.' Refrain — it is better for you": *thalāthah* — three — the standing terse reference to the "third of three" file (its standing companion at 5:73 — "those who say: God is the third of three — have disbelieved — and there is no god save One God — and if they refrain not from what they say, a painful punishment shall touch those of them who disbelieve"); and the command *intahū* — refrain! — with the identical self-interest motivation sounded at v. 170 (*khayran lakum* — the standing benefit-clause pointing downward: correct belief as rescue, not as concession). The commentators' standing doctrinal-careful register (al-Rāzī's scholastic discussion most explicit in the file): the verse and its 5:73 companion address the assertion of *three deities* — a triad — an assertion orthodox trinitarian Christians themselves formally disavow ("not three gods, but one"); al-Rāzī acknowledging the claim of three hypostases/aspects within a single Essence, yet pressing the tradition's standing critique that the attribution of full divinity to the human Jesus collapses the claimed unity into effective plurality — and contrasting trinitarian hypostases with the Islamic file of divine Names/Attributes, which are never posited as distinct entities within God — the standing distinction the verse installs pastorally, however, is simpler and prior: *say not "Three"* — speech-discipline upon God — refrain — for the tongue that recites "three" of God has already left the ground in which v. 171's other clauses stand: "believe in God and His messengers."

**Subḥānahu an Yakūna Lahu Walad: The Glory-Formula as Ontology — Against Divine Offspring**

Then the verse's standing crown — the Book's signature formula against offspring: *subḥānahu an yakūna lahu walad* — "glory be to Him, above having a child!": *subḥān* — the standing exclamation of transcendence (its standing register: the Book's glory-formula appearing at passages where false attribution peaks: 2:116 — "they say: God has taken to Himself a son — glory be to Him — nay — unto Him belongs whatsoever is in the heavens and the earth"; 4:171; 6:100; 9:30-31; 10:68; 17:111; 18:4's warning-file; 19:35 — "it is not for God to take a son — glory be to Him — when He decrees a matter, He but says to it: Be"; 19:88-92 — the standing cosmic-recoil verse-file: "they say: the Beneficent has taken a son... the heavens are nearly rent thereat"; 21:26; 23:91; 37:152-159; 39:4; 43:81-82) — the commentators reading the formula's standing logic: offspring in creation-categories presupposes (a) consort and process, (b) composition, (c) need of succession — all denied by the standing perfection-clause that follows: the One who *has no need*, whose attribute is *ṣamadiyyah* (112:2 — the Self-Sufficient upon whom all depend), does not generate dependents — and the verse's own next clause supplies its standing proof-text.

**Lahu Mā fī al-Samāwāti wa Mā fī al-Arḍ: The Estate as Refutation — and the Guardian-Sufficiency**

The rebuttal of sonship is given, in the verse's closing cadence, as estate-declaration: *lahu mā fī al-samāwāti wa mā fī al-arḍ — wa kafā bi-llāhi wakīlan* — "unto Him belongs whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is on the earth, and God suffices as a Guardian": the commentators (al-Zamakhsharī's standing rhetorical note) mark the theology packed in the possessive: sonship-talk imagines a dependent receiving inheritance and essence from a parent; the Book displays instead a King whose *whole estate* — heaven, earth, every candidate for worship, Jesus included — stands under His title: every being related to Him as possession, not progeny — the created-creature file closed against consubstantiality by the title-deed itself. And the final Name-post the sūrah has already planted thrice (4:81; 4:132) — *wa kafā bi-llāhi wakīlan* — "God suffices as a Guardian": the wakīl-file now sealing the Jesus-file, after sealing the family-file (4:132) and the trust-file (4:81): the believer need no son-mediator to stand surety with heaven — God Himself suffices as Guardian — the standing theological completion of the chapter's whole movement: protection, guardianship, estate, and intercession are offices the Book assigns to God in sufficiency — *kafā*. Thereby the sūrah's final theological peak stands: messengers honored (163-165), witness sufficient (166), disbelief-and-obstruction indicted (167-169), mankind summoned (170), Jesus confessed in maximal honor — and fenced from divinity — in the same breath (171), servanthood installed at the summit of rank (172), the Two-Way wages announced (173), proof and light descended (174), mercy-and-bounty and straight-path guidance promised (175) — and the chapter closing on earth with a ruling again: v. 176 — the kalālah-inheritance — law returning after theology, as if to say the Lord of heaven and earth is also the divider of legacies between sisters and brothers — the sūrah of the Watcher watching from Sinai-heights to the minutest estate-file — one Truth, one Guardian, one Book holding both.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:172

> **The Messiah would never disdain to be a servant of God, nor would the angels brought near. And whosoever disdains His service and is arrogant — He shall gather them unto Himself all together.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Lan Yastankifa al-Masīḥu an Yakūna ʿAbdan li-llāh: Servanthood Not Beneath the Messiah**

The doctrinal summit of v. 171 receives its climbing-proof — one of the Book's most polished inversions: *lan yastankifa al-Masīḥu an yakūna ʿabdan li-llāh* — "the Messiah would never disdain to be a servant of God": *yastankif* — from n-k-f — to disdain, to consider beneath one's dignity, to flinch from as degrading (its standing register: 4:172; 4:173's paired response; 21:19 — "those who are with Him are not too proud to worship Him, nor do they weary") — and the particle *lan* — the perpetual never — fencing the whole matter at the level of the person claimed for divinity: the Messiah himself — the very subject of the exaggeration — would never count servanthood beneath him. The commentators (al-Rāzī gathering the standing context-note) record the probable address-scene: the Christian delegation of Najrān, come to Madīnah for their standing doctrinal exchange with the Prophet (the standing reports of the delegation-file in the sīrah-literature), had balked at the Book's designation of Jesus as *ʿabd* — servant, even slave — hearing in it a depreciation of their Lord; the verse answers inside their own scale: ʿubūdiyyah — servanthood-to-God — is not a station beneath greatness but the station *by which* the greatest are great — and the standing counter-witnesses are then offered in the verse's own second clause: *wa lā al-malāʾikatu al-muqarrabūn* — "nor would the angels brought near" — the *muqarrabūn* — the near-stationed (its standing register: 56:11 — "those are the ones brought near"; 83:21; 83:28; 3:45 — "eminent in this world and the Hereafter and of those brought near"; 4:172; 21:19; 37:164-166 — "there is none of us but has a known station — and verily we are the ranged ones — and verily we are the glorifiers"; 66:6's standing non-disobeyer-file) — the highest beings of the Book's cosmology volunteering precisely the posture the exaggerators imagined degrading: if the near-stationed angels and the Word-and-Spirit Messiah both count servanthood as glory, the geography has inverted: the summit of creation is *ʿabd*, and the refusal of it is the sin named next.

**ʿAbd in the Book's Standing Theology: From Taxonomy to Honor**

The commentators expand the term's standing analysis (the standing distinctions gathered across the comment-canon): *ʿabd* marks in its first register sheer created dependence — every creature a servant under the Owner — and in its exalted register the chosen posture of willing submission: servanthood-as-vocation — and the Book's own title-usage honors precisely this word at the peaks of prophetic biography: 2:23's "Our servant" of the Prophet; 17:1 — "glory be to Him who carried His servant by night" — the greatest journey-tribute in the Book paid with the title servant; 18:1; 19:30 — Jesus from the cradle: "verily I am the servant of God — He gave me the Book and made me a prophet" — the standing first-person self-designation already in the Book's own Jesus-file; 25:1; 38:17; 38:30 — "an excellent servant" of David and Solomon; 38:44 — "We found him patient — an excellent servant" of Job; 39:36 — "is not God sufficient for His servant?"; 43:59 — addressing the exaggerators directly of Jesus: "he is but a servant upon whom We bestowed favor — and We made him a sign for the Children of Israel"; 57:27 — his file as messenger-chain; and 72:19 — "when the servant of God stood calling upon Him..." The sūrah's own argument thereby finds its capstone: the Messiah whom the exaggerators would crown as god is in the Book crowned with **servanthood — the very predicate to which the near-stationed angels hold fast** — "the Messiah would never disdain" — and the title trades upward: the greatest name beneath Creator is not "son" or "god" but *ʿabd Allāh* — the name, the commentators note, most beloved in the prophetic biography itself (the standing report in Muslim's register 2132 — Bukhārī's standing reporting of the most beloved names to God: ʿAbd Allāh and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān).

**Wa Man Yastankif ʿan ʿIbādatihi wa Yastakbir: Disdain and Arrogance as One Cord**

The verse then names the refusal and its root: *wa man yastankif ʿan ʿibādatihi wa yastakbir* — "and whosoever disdains His service and is arrogant": disdain of service exposed as *istikbār* — arrogance (its standing Book-dossier: 2:34 — "save Iblīs — he refused and waxed arrogant and was of the disbelievers"; 38:74-76 — Iblīs' own self-elevation: "I am better than he"; 7:206 — "those who are with thy Lord are not too proud to worship Him — they glorify Him and to Him they prostrate"; 16:49-50; 39:72 — "enter the gates of Hell, abiding therein — wretched is the lodging of the arrogant"; 40:60; the standing register) — the commentators marking the psychology of the linkage: to disdain servanthood is not a neutral theology-opinion but the springing of the creature above its created station — the standing first-sin reenacted: Iblīs' refusal of the prostration-command being precisely the refusal of *ʿibādah* out of *kibr* — 4:172 thereby filing the exaggerated-Jesus theologians not under error-of-information but under the family-line of the original disdain — with Jesus himself and the near-stationed angels exhibited as its standing counterexamples: no station in creation is too high for worship — the refusal of worship therefore dignifies no one.

**Fa-Sa-Yaḥshuruhum Ilayhi Jamīʿan: The Gathering to the One Disdained**

The sentence closes with the gathering-verdict: *fa-sa-yaḥshuruhum ilayhi jamīʿan* — "He shall gather them unto Himself all together": *ḥ-sh-r* — the standing eschatological mustering (its register in the sūrah: 4:87 — "He shall surely gather you to the Day of Resurrection — no doubt of it"; 4:140's gatherer-file; and the standing Book-wide stations: 2:203; 3:12; 5:96; 6:22; 6:38; 6:51; 8:36; 10:45; 18:99; the several standing summons-verses) — with *jamīʿan* — "all together" — the totality-adverb sealing the escape-proof: none filtered out; and the participle's own standing irony carried by the commentators: the disdainers of servanthood will yet be gathered — *in service* — to the Master they declined to serve: the posture refused in freedom shall be borne in muster; the summit avoided voluntarily met by summons. The verse thereby plants, at the edge of vv. 173's Two-Way wages, the chapter's final Christological lesson in its purest form: the two highest registers of creation — the Messiah and the near-stationed angels — define honor as *service*, and disdain of service as arrogance leading only to the Gathering: **ʿubūdiyyah is not the floor of the divine household — it is its elevation**: let the exaggerators learn rank from its exemplars.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:173

> **And as for those who believe and do righteous deeds — He shall pay them their rewards in full, and increase them of His bounty. And as for those who disdain and are arrogant — He shall punish them with a painful punishment, and they shall find for themselves no protector or helper apart from God.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Fa-Ammā Alladhīna Āmanū wa ʿAmilū al-Ṣāliḥāt: The Standing Formula and Its Standing Wage**

The Two-Way verdict follows with the Book's most familiar classification-formula — the standing double-classification that is itself the chapter's own moral center of gravity: *fa-ammā alladhīna āmanū wa ʿamilū al-ṣāliḥāti fa-yuwaffīhim ujūrahum wa yazīduhum min faḍlih* — "and as for those who believe and do righteous deeds — He shall pay them their rewards in full, and increase them of His bounty": the *ammā... fa-* construction — "as for... then..." — the standing apportionment-grammar of the Book's judgment-scenes (its register: 2:26; 4:162's own *lākini*; 7:30 — "a party He guided, and a party upon whom error was rightfully due"; 7:42; 30:15-16; 32:18-20; 39:70-73; 45:28-32; 78:31-40 — the standing paired-files of the judgment) — and the content of the first class so familiar to the chapter's ear that its words carry the chapter's whole argument: īmān plus ʿamal ṣāliḥ — the standing pairing sounded over seventy times in the Book (its stations within this sūrah alone: 4:57; 4:122; 4:124; 4:152; 4:162; 4:173) — creed and deed one currency. And the wage is stated in two movements: (1) *yuwaffīhim ujūrahum* — "He shall pay them their rewards in full": *waffā* — Form II of w-f-y — the fullness-verb (its standing register: 3:25 — "the day each soul shall find present what it did of good and what it did of evil"; 3:57 — "as for those who believe and do righteous deeds — He shall pay them their rewards in full"; 3:161; 4:173; 11:111; 16:111; 24:39; 35:30; 39:70 — "every soul shall be paid in full for what it did"; 46:19) — the standing full-payment-verdict — nothing clipped from the account, no arrears, no rounding-down: the standing the standing comment-canon marking the emphatic grammar: God as the Perfect Paymaster — not the purse that rations; and then, beyond the exactness: (2) *wa yazīduhum min faḍlih* — "and increase them of His bounty": the z-y-d of overflow — beyond-wage generosity outpacing desert — the standing doctrine the commentators name under this verse and its kin: God's requiting is not arithmetic parity but *faḍl* — bounty — bounty beyond earning (its standing register: 3:152; 4:67-70's great-reward file; 10:26 — "for those who do good, the best, and more besides"; 24:38; 29:27; 30:39's zakāt-doublers; 35:30; 42:26 — "He answers those who believe and do righteous deeds and increases them of His bounty"; "theirs shall be whatsoever they wish therein — and with Us is more yet") — the two-movement formula thereby setting the standing ratio of requital: exactness first (no laborer defrauded), bounty beyond (no love contained in arithmetic) — and the tradition's standing hadith-gloss (Muslim's register of the qudsī promise — "I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and has never entered the heart of man" — Bukhārī 3244; Muslim 2824) enlarging the *increase* into its standing incomprehensibility.

**Wa Ammā Alladhīna Istankafū wa Istakbarū: The Disdainers' Fourfold Forfeit**

Then the second class — its naming deliberately pairing the two verbs of v. 172 to compose one indictment-word: *wa ammā alladhīna istankafū wa istakbarū fa-yuʿadhdhibuhum ʿadhāban alīman* — "and as for those who disdain and are arrogant — He shall punish them with a painful punishment": *istankafū* — refusing servanthood as beneath them — and *istakbarū* — the arrogance that the refusal grows from and feeds — the commentators (al-Ṭabarī's standing gloss) marking the generalization achieved by the pairing: the verse's polemic completing its movement from Jesus-file to universal law — what began as the correction of one community's exaggeration stands now as the standing condition-name of all who disdain servanthood anywhere: the Christian exaggerator of Jesus' station and the pagan disdainer of obedience meet at one root — istinkāf-istikbār — and receive one fate: *ʿadhāb alīm* — the standing painful-punishment (the phrase tolling through the chapter's doom-register: 4:18; 4:161; the several standing stations across the Book: 2:10; 3:91; 5:36; 9:34; 14:22; 22:25; 31:7; 45:8; 58:5).

**Wa Lā Yajidū Lahum min Dūni Allāhi Waliyyan wa Lā Naṣīran: The Null-Pair Seventh Sounded**

The sentence closes with the chapter's signature annihilation-pair — its seventh tolling in the chapter — the standing double-denial by which every doom-verse of this sūrah has closed: *wa lā yajidū lahum min dūni Allāhi waliyyan wa lā naṣīran* — "and they shall find for themselves no protector or helper apart from God": *walī* — the protecting patron; *naṣīr* — the succoring helper — both *min dūni Allāh* — "apart from God" — the commentators (al-Rāzī's standing note at these paired null-clauses) marking the two-sided foreclosure: alliance-resource and rescue-resource both sought *outside God* and both found *empty*: the standing Book-register of the formula: 4:45 — "God suffices as an Ally — and God suffices as a Helper" — the sūrah's own positive posting of the same two Names for the believers; and its paired-negation file: 4:52 ("whomsoever God curses — thou shalt find no helper for him"); 4:89; 4:123; 4:145 ("thou shalt never find for them a helper"); 4:173; its standing companions at 2:48; 2:107; 2:120; 3:22; 3:56; 9:74; 29:22; 33:17; 33:65; 42:31; 42:46 — the several standing null-stations) — and within this verse the pair performing its standing pastoral office: the disdainer had imagined an address-book of alternatives — networks, patrons, prestige-stations — all filed under *min dūni Allāh* — and the verdict is that the ledger *outside* God reads zero — not diminished, not delayed: *lā yajidū* — they shall not *find* — the verb of search concluding in void. And the verse thereby closes the Jesus-file argument into the opening of vv. 174-176: the exaggerators taught that the Messiah would never disdain service (172), the disdainers measured (173) — and on the other register, the believers-and-workers assigned double-wage security — "He shall pay them their rewards in full, and increase them of His bounty" — the chapter's Two Ways running in parallel to its final legal-verse (176) — servanthood with wage, or disdain with punishment, and *no third estate* — the standing Book-verdict already declared in the triptych of vv. 150-152 and sealed here with the Names of patronage and help: everything under the description "apart from God" — found wanting; everything under the description "God" — sufficient.

---

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:174

> **O mankind! There has now come to you a proof from your Lord; and We have sent down to you a clear light.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**Yā Ayyuhā al-Nāsu Qad Jāʾakum Burhānun min Rabbikum: The Proof Arrived, Not Merely the Report**

The chapter's penultimate doctrinal address opens with the same universal vocative sounded at v. 170 — and the commentators instantly mark the intensification: where v. 170 announced "the Messenger has come to you with the truth," v. 174 announces the arrival of the *proof itself*: *yā ayyuhā al-nāsu qad jāʾakum burhānun min rabbikum* — "O mankind! There has now come to you a proof from your Lord": *burhān* — from b-r-h-n — a word the Book uses sparingly and weightily: the demonstration that compels — not mere evidence (*bayyinah* — the clear sign, its standing general file) but the irrefutable argument that ends debate: the standing *ḥujjah* raised to exhibition (its standing register: 4:174; 12:24 — Joseph's temptation-scene — "she desired him, and he would have desired her, had he not seen the proof of his Lord — *burhāna rabbih*"; 21:24 — "bring your proof — *burhānakum* — this is the reminder of those with me and the reminder of those before me"; 23:117; 27:64 — "produce your proof, if you are truthful"; 28:32; 28:75) — the commentators (al-Ṭabarī's standing gloss; al-Rāzī's scholastic note) identifying the referent by the verse's own placement: the Burhān that has now arrived = the Prophet-and-Qur'ān complex just detailed through vv. 153-173 — the revelation whose chain was established (163-165), witnessed by God and the angels (166), deployed against every file of error (167-173) — the whole preceding People-of-the-Book movement standing under this one noun: the chapter having argued its case, the argument itself is now named: *burhānun min rabbikum* — and the possessive *rabbikum* — "your Lord" — keeping the argument in the standing covenantal frame: the proof comes not from an adversary but from *their* Lord (4:1's standing opening-address answered at the close).

**Wa Anzalnā Ilaykum Nūran Mubīnan: The Clear Light Sent Down — The Qur'ān Named as Illumination**

The second arrival is named in image: *wa anzalnā ilaykum nūran mubīnan* — "and We have sent down to you a clear light": *nūr* — light — the standing Qur'ānic self-designation of the Book itself (its standing register: 5:15 — "there has come to you from God a light and a clear Book"; 5:44; 5:46 — the Torah and Gospel each carrying guidance-and-light; 6:1, 37:117; 42:52 — "thus did We reveal to thee a Spirit from Our command — thou knewest not what the Book was, nor belief — but We made it a light whereby We guide whom We will of Our servants"; 57:9; 64:8 — "believe in God and His Messenger and the light We sent down"; 65:11; and the standing cosmological 24:35 — "God is the Light of the heavens and the earth") — the commentators reading the two arrivals as the standing dyad of divine aid: Burhān in the *mind* — argument that cuts off debate; Nūr in the *heart and conduct* — illumination by which one walks: the proof convinces, the light guides — and *mubīn* — clear, manifest, self-evidencing (its standing collocation through the Book: 2:92 — Moses coming with clear signs; 3:20; 7:73's standing clear-proof of Ṣāliḥ; 12:1 — the Qur'ān as clear Book; 15:1; 26:2; 27:1; 28:2; 43:2; 44:2; and the standing sūrah-file: 4:153's clear-proofs; 4:174's own usage) — the light described by its own shining: not a hidden lantern requiring unpacking but brightness itself, so that the standing sinner-file ("a deep darkness amid the Sea, wave upon wave, and clouds above... when he puts out his hand, he can hardly see it" — 24:40) marks by contrast what has now arrived: a light *mubīn* — needing no mediator to certify that it shines.

**The Standing Address-Architecture: Burhān and Nūr as the Chapter's Two Keys**

The commentators observe the verse's architectural precision within the closing movement: vv. 174-175 standing as the standing key-pair of the whole People-of-the-Book movement: (1) *burhān* names retrospectively the chapter's dialectical achievement — the indictment-file (155-161), the Jesus-correction (156-159), the messengers-register (163-165), the witness (166), the doctrinal summit (171-173) — every argument of vv. 153-173 gathered under one banner-word: the chapter's polemics are not accusation-but-proof, arriving *from their Lord*; and (2) *nūr mubīn* names prospectively what vv. 175 will articulate as its use: those who "believe in God and hold fast to Him" shall be guided "unto Himself upon a straight path" — light becoming movement, illumination becoming locomotion toward God. The standing comment-canon's structural note (al-Rāzī's summary standing at the verse's head) ties the two nouns to the chapter's two audiences: for the People of the Book, the Burhān is the covenant-proof making fidelity to their own revelation lead inevitably to this one (as 4:162's rāsikhūn filed); for the believers, the Nūr is the possession by which the rest of the way is walked (57:28's standing companion-file — "O you who believe — fear God and believe in His Messenger — He shall give you a double portion of His mercy and appoint for you a light in which you walk").
